Description:
URGENT Quotation - Common stormwater repairs at the front of the property

Following our inspection, investigation works and CCTV camera survey, we found the silt arrestor pit below the grassed yard and found the stormwater pit connections have large gaps at the base where the pipes enter, allowing water leak into the subsoil and out the retaining wall into the driveway. CCTV camera surveyed the silt arrestor and located tree root infestations blocking the stormwater outlet pipework for the entire building. We also located sink holes around the stormwater pits in the front yard, where soil has washed away.

This quotation is to re-concrete the base of the stormwater pit, seal around the pipe holes, clean the silt arrestor using venturi pump and use high pressure water jet blaster to remove tree roots from the stormwater outlet to the street.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Isolate stormwater pumps in the lower carpark.
  2. Excavate base of stormwater pit in the front grass area.
  3. Fill sink holes around and under the pit using blue metal aggregate.
  4. Re-concrete the base of the pit.
  5. Use extension ladder to access the silt arrestor pit.
  6. Set up high pressure water jet blaster and equipment and run hoses into the silt arrestor pit.
  7. Clean silt arrestor using venturi pump.
  8. Use high pressure water jet blaster with tree root cutting heads to clear out the outlet pipework to the street.
  9. Render and seal pipework gaps using quickset sand cement.
  10. Turn stormwater pumps in the lower carpark back on.
  11. Clean all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Please attend to site to unblock the drain near the garage
Site Contact is 0406 522 901.
Thanks,
Cherry
Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access and found the driveway strip drain at the garage entrance to be blocked and surcharging when it rains.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster equipment and ran hoses.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and puncture head downstream of the grated drain stormwater piping and could not clear the blockage.

Inspected the stormwater piping at the property and found the common stormwater discharge into the stormwater tank below the garages. 

Cleaned out the surface pit in the middle of the garage, camera surveyed the outlet and found it also discharges into the stormwater tank below the garages. 

Gained access to the garage on the right, lifted lids and inspected the large stormwater tank under the garages. Whilst jet blasting the blocked stormwater drain, we found the grated drain outlet does not discharge into the stormwater tank.

Used CCTV drain camera and found the grated drain outlet pipework connects to an agline under the gravel carspace at the end of the driveway. Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DH7MF

CCTV camera surveyed the agline and found it runs along the building wall and collects ground water from the the gravel carspace at the end of the driveway.

We found both the outlet of the driveway grated drain and the agline under the gravel carspace is not connected to the buildings stormwater system, is blocked and surcharging during rain events.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To rectify the blocked driveway grated drain, we advise to install a stormwater pit within the gravel carspace connecting the agline and grated drain outlet, close off garage for duration of works, saw cut chase and excavate the garage concrete slab from the new pit to the surface pit in the middle of the garage. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:

Description: Please find attached a work order request for Strata Plan 21831. Please attend to the reported side blocked drain and Unit 8. **Please call Brock - 0401 380 002 for for further information.
Invoice Description:
Investigate common sewer blockage near the bins.

Urgently attended the property, gained access and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the front of the building.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively upstream the boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera upstream of the boundary trap, located cracked earthenware pipework and major tree root infestations entering the original 150mm earthenware common sewer pipework in 2 x locations upstream of the boundary trap which was the cause of the sewer blockage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested common sewer pipework downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline approximately 4 meters of tree root infested 150mm common sewer pipework upstream the boundary trap and also reline 2 meters of tree root infested sewer pipework 13 meters upstream of the boundary trap, completely sealing the tree root infested common sewer pipework using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 5's laundry.

5/5 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 5's laundry and found the ceiling to be wet and water damaged.

Cut a hole in the ceiling, exposing the common stack pipe and drainage within the cavity and located water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 3 above.

Gained access into unit 3 and inspected the original bathroom. Found there to be a hole in the original cast iron bath that has been tapped over and drummy tiles, missing grout and seals within the shower recess.

Carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water, bath and shower breach and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 3.

Carried out dye testing of the bath using yellow dye and the shower using green dye. Following dye testing, no dye coloured water leaked into unit 5's laundry ceiling below.

20/5 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 5, 3 & 6. Inspected unit 5's laundry and found only a small amount of water has leaked.

Gained access into unit 6's renovated bathroom and found no water leaks. Undertook dye testing of all waste fixtures and no water leaked form unit 6 into unit 5's laundry.

27/5 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 3 and carried out extensive testing in the original bathroom to locate the leak in unit 5's laundry ceiling.

Drilled a hole in the bath panel, used inspection camera and found water leaking under the bath.

Filled bath up and dye tested the original cast iron bath that has a hole in it. Used inspection camera to find the bath hole is completely rusted through, the temporary tape installed is preventing the bath from leaking.

Blocked off shower waste and flood tested the original shower recess with green dye and following flood testing of the shower recess, green dye leaked under the bath and down into the laundry, confirming the leak.

We found the waterproof membrane in unit 3's original shower recess to have failed causing the leak. We also located a hole in the cast iron bath that is temporary sealed.

Further URGENT Works required to be undertaken in unit 3 by a building contractor - As the waterproofing has failed in the original bathroom and there is a hole in the cast iron bath, we advise the original bathroom is renovated replacing the faulty bath and waterproof membrane.

Once the renovation works are completed in unit 3's bathroom, we advise unit 5's laundry ceiling is repaired and painted.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Thank you,
Esther Ralph
Community After Hours
1300 889 227
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent blockage in unit 6 and urgent water leak/flood into unit 2 below.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 2, found resultant damage and water leaking through the ornate living room ceiling, cornices and walls, also water leaking through the kitchen ceiling and cornice.

Gained access into unit 6, found the toilet and all bathroom waste fixtures to be completely blocked and surcharging when in use causing waste water to leak into unit 2 below and cause resultant water damage. Flow tested the kitchen waste which was also blocked and surcharging when in use.

Inspected the common area outside, removed inspection opening on the common 100mm cast iron sewer stack outside unit 2's bathroom located at the front left of the building connecting unit 6's toilet and found the common sewer pipework in the ground to be blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the 100mm sewer stack with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all infestations entering the common earthenware sewer pipework from the base of the sewer stack downstream to the main boundary trap approximately 5 meters. Please see CCTV video link of tree roots entering the common sewer pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DHIKU

Flow tested unit 6's toilet which is currently clear and in good working order. Please note if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not relined, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur in unit 6. 

We found the common external cast iron sewer waste pipework on the external wall connecting unit 6's shower, basin and floor waste to be completely corroded, blocked, cracked, leaking and required urgent replacement.

Cut out blocked, corroded and leaking common external cast iron waste pipework connecting unit 6's shower, basin and floor waste. Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV downstream the waste stack to clear the common sewer pipework downstream and ensure all clear.

Supplied and installed new PVC pipework, fittings and trap connecting unit 6's shower, basin and floor waste. Installed stainless steel brackets and fixings securing the new waste pipework.

Inspected the external common area and found the common grease pit to be blocked outside causing the blockage in unit 6's kitchen. 

Used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain to clear the blocked grease trap outlet and common sewer pipework downstream. We cleared out a large amount of congealed fat from the common sewer line which was the cause of the blockage. Flow tested all fixtures in unit 6's bathroom and kitchen - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages in unit 6 - We advise to reline the tree root infested common sewer pipework for approximately 5 meters downstream from the base of the common sewer stack outside unit 2 located at the front left of the building downstream to the boundary trap. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further relining works required to be undertaken.

Further resultant water damage repairs and painting required to be undertaken in unit 2 - We advise the resultant water damaged ornate living room ceiling, cornice and walls is repaired and painted. Also the resultant water damaged kitchen ceiling and cornice is repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting in unit 2.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise GK strata engages a cleaning contractor to install fans and dehumidifies in units 2 and 6 to dry out the leak and resultant damage.

Please note on a separate roofing issue- Following our inspection on the roof issue, we found the outlet storm water pipework from the roof to not be discharging into the current rain water head at high level. In heavy rain this is causing water to leak onto the ground in the common area located at the front of the building (photo attached). To rectify we advise GK strata engages a roofing contractor to re-direct the storm water outlet pipework into the middle of the rain water head to prevent further water leaking into the common area during heavy rain.

Relining Quote:
Urgent quotation - Common sewer relining repairs

Following extensive jet blasting and clear out works and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework in 3 x separate locations on the inlet connection to the main boundary trap for the building, tree roots entering downstream the common sewer inspection opening at the top of the stairs and approximately 3 meters of tree roots entering the common sewer piping downstream the sewer stack in unit 10's garage laundry. 

This quotation is to reline 3 x separate sections of tree root infested common original eartanwere sewer pipework on the inlet of the boundary trap, downstream the inspection opening to the left of the boundary trap to the main line and downstream the common sewer stack in unit 10's laundry completely sealing the tree root infested common sewer pipework to prevent further common sewer blockages and floods.

The following works will be undertaken:

Gain access into the common areas and unit 10's laundry. 
Set up safe working area and relining equipment. 
Prepare all common sewer pipework to Australian Standards AS3500.
Clear lines using high pressure water jet, mechanical milling equipment  & CCTV drain camera to prepare lines.
Using CCTV equipment record common sewer pipework before relining.
Pipe relining:
Reline approximately 3.5 meters from the top of the inspection opening next to the stairs downstream to the mainline, sealing 3 x sections where major tree root infestations are entering the dislodged and broken common earthenware sewer water pipework, using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin.
Reline approximately 3 to 4 meters downstream the common sewer stack in unit 10's laundry, sealing the tree root infested and broken earthenware sewer pipework using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin.
Reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested common sewer pipework upstream of the boundary trap, sealing the tree root infested and broken earthenware sewer pipework using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin.
Cure 3 x liners using hot water boiler.
Once 3 x relines have cured, removed relining equipment from the common storm water pipework.
Flow test all relining works undertaken.
Clean all areas where work had taken place.
Remove associated rubbish from the property.
All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

Emergency after hours call out on the 21/5/26 - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 13.

Used drain cleaning equipment downstream the toilet but we were unable to clear the blockage.

Removed inspection opening on the 100mm cast iron sewer stack pipework and found the common in ground sewer pipework to be completely blocked. Please see CCTV video link of major tree roots causing the blockage - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DHQUP

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream the sewer stack pipework to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages in unit 13 - We advise to barricade area and remove plants from the garden, remove pavers from path, dig up and expose the common sewer junction and base of stack for unit 13, cut out and remove tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework replacing with new PVC pipework and fittings, flow test all works carried out, bed pipework, back fill in accordance with AS3500 and reinstate paved area and garden. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

This quotation is to clear out the dirt and debris from the storm water pits within the car park and clear out storm water pipework from the pit to the street with the use of high pressure water jet blasting and CCTV drain camera. 

Please note, to prevent common storm water blockages we advise the works are undertaken every 12 months to ensure the buildings storm water system is in good working order.

The following works will be undertaken.

  1. Advise residents of driveway and car park closure for up to 3 hours so we can park in the driveway and undertake the urgent clear out works. 
  2. Clean out all dirt and debris from the common storm water pits within the car park.
  3. Remove the pit lid grate and use the high pressure water jet blaster to clear out the common storm water line from the pit to the kerb and gutter at the Street.
  4. Use the jet blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out all dirt and debris from the 3 separate storm water lines.
  5. Flow test the pump out line, pit and 3 storm water lines ensuring they are all clear and flowing out of the kerb and gutter at the Street.
  6. If any breaks or faults are found in the 3 storm water lines we will supply CCTV video footage or photos and if required advise on any further repairs required to be undertaken.
  7. Reinstall pit lid grate and clean all areas where work had taken place using the high pressure hose and disinfectant.
  8. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 10 and found water damage and bubbling paint the brickwork wall and common timber service duct.

Within the shower recess, we located missing grout and sealant within the floor tiles and wall perimeter.

Following extensive testing in unit 11, we found the faulty shower recess to be causing the leak into unit 10 next door.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access and inspected the master water meter at the front of the building. 

Following our inspection, we found the water meter to be ticking over slightly and never came to a complete stop.

The buildings master water meter is new and has recently been replaced. 

Walked around the top half of property, looked in gardens, inspected all stormwater pits, hose taps and found no water leaks.

Walked around bottom half of property and found a leak from the pipework under the jetty, an old section of poly pipe has rub marks because the jetty moves with the tide and the floats have barnacles which is causing wear on the pipe.

Replace a section of poly pipe to prevent any further leaks, extended the pipe so it is not stretched when the tide drops.

Returned to the property, inspected the water meter and found it to be slightly ticking over and does not come to a complete stop.

We consider the small amount of usage when it is slightly ticking over could be toilet or taps leaking. We advise a notice is sent out to all residents to advise of any leaking fixtures within their unit.

There is no individual unit hot and cold water meters installed at the property, no common hot water and there are 14 units in total. Estimated usage for a building of this size would be approximately 5-8 KL per quarter.

Inspected the Sydney Water bill provided and found the previous bill has a very small amount of water usage (0.49 KL) and the same time last year had no usage (Nil).

We consider the old meter installed was no longer recording usage and no the new meter is now recording usage.

We advise the next bill is monitored to see if it is excessive or similar cost of the previous bill.

Attended the property to CCTV camera survey the common stormwater and sewer pipes and gain access under the building from the crawl space.

  5. Clean all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
  6. Provide a quotation with a scope of works to rectify the issue.

Following our CCTV camera survey of the common sewer on the left side of the property. we found multiple cracks in the common sewer piping causing tree root infestations. Used yellow dye to flood test the common sewer line on the left side of the building.

Video Links:

https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D59NB
https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D59NY

Following our CCTV camera survey of the common stormwater on the left side of the property we found the 2 x downpipes do not connect into the drainage under the concrete footpath and there are large gaps around the connection. Used green dye to flood test the stormwater line on the left side of the building.

Video Links :
https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D59BH
https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D59B6

Gained access under the building from the crawl space and found the subsoil to be damp, we did not find any dye coloured water leaking under the building from our dye testing of the common stormwater and sewer piping on the left side. This also indicates that previous relining repairs undertaken by another contractor has resolved a leak. 

Inspected the right side of the building where the soil is damp and found water to be trapped in the base of the cavity wall around this area. Inspected the external wall and found large gaps around 1 x hot water heater flue and behind 2 x instantaneous hot water heaters (photos attached) at the front right that is causing water to leak into the cavity wall during rain events.

We also found unit 1's air condition drainage to be discharging from the balcony onto brickwork, into the subsoil contributing to damp soil. We advise the lot owners of unit 1 engages their own plumbing contractor to run the outside air-conditioning condensate pipework to a drain.

Installed sealant over the open ended gas pipes along the right side of the building to prevent water entering the old deleted pipework and leaking out under the building.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken on the common sewer - We advise to use high pressure water jet blaster and clear out the tree roots from the common sewer line. Once the common sewer pipework is clear we can then submit a quotation for relining repairs required to be undertaken. 

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken on the common stormwater - We advise to excavate the concrete path on the left side of the building exposing drainage, cut out base of downpipes, supply and install PVC piping and fittings connecting the base of 2 x downpipes to the earthenware drainage, install inspection opening, backfill and re-concrete the affected area. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent water leaking into the wall cavity on the right side of the building - We advise to erect scaffolding outside the 3 x heaters, gain access to units, cut back flue, re-fit and seal around the wall opening, disconnect 2 x instantaneous heaters removing from the wall, re-point and flash render affected area behind 2 x heaters, re-install heaters and dismantle scaffolding. 

We will submit an URGENT quotation Shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to replace the faulty circulating pump, 2 x isolation valves and non return valve on the hot water return line. We will submit an URGENT quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Could you please attend site as soon as possible to investigate and rectify blocked drain which is
causing a sewage leak out of the laundries of Units 2 & 5
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 2 & 8's laundry, found the common sewer to be blocked and surcharging.

Removed inspection opening lid on the sewer stack pipe in unit 2's laundry and found the common sewer line to be blocked.

Engaged a second plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster and equipment and ran hoses.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found major tree root infestations growing in the earthenware sewer piping approximately 4 meters downstream from unit 2's laundry, causing the blockage. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DHDNQ

Used the high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer piping.

Reinstalled inspection opening lid on the stack pipe and flow tested all fixtures in the laundry - All in good working order.

Walked around the property and found the overflow relief gully to be blocked, used high pressure water jet blaster to remove fat build up from the base of the gully.

CCTV camera surveyed the remainder of the common sewer mainline to the boundary trap and found it to be clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To prevent common sewer, we advise to reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested common 150mm earthenware sewer pipework approximately 4 downstream common sewer stack in unit 2's laundry, sealing all root infested cracked and leaking earthenware joints using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 12/05/26 - Urgent gas leak affecting unit 7

Urgently attended the property after hours at 5.30pm to investigate gas leak near unit 7.

Gained access and found unit 7's gas meter to be turned off. Carried out a drop test and found a drop in pressure. Left the gas meter turned off.

Knocked on unit 7's door and no-one was home at the time to undertake investigation works, so we left a note asking the occupants to contact us.

Used gas detector around the external wall, gas meter and common gas piping and no gas reading were detected.

Returned to the property the following day, inspected the common area outside unit 7 and located a very faint smell of gas.

Walked around and found there to be no access under the building below unit 7.

Knocked on unit 7, but the occupants did not allow us to enter, they advised us they have no gas and the leak is outside. We were given no other information.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access into unit 7 and found there to be no gas smell. We located a faint gas smell in the common areas.

Made a call to Jemena Gas and confirmed the gas meter outside unit 7 was units 7's. As unit 7 has no gas supply or appliances, we disconnected the pipework and capped off the outlet line that goes under the building.

Walked around the property and carried out further testing using the gas detector equipment.

Located a large gas leak on the common gas galvanised steel piping where it goes through the external wall from the bin room outside to the boundary regulator.

Excavated garden bed at the front of the property exposing the corroded, gas mainline and found it to be leaking within the wall.

Please note - As the gas pipework is corroded through the wall cavity, we are unable to undertake any repairs and as this is the main gas supply for the building we are unable to isolate the gas supply.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to isolate the buildings main gas supply, use core hole machine to drill new hole through the common external wall into the bin room, cut out old, galvanised steel pipework and install new copper pipe and fittings where the pipework goes through the wall. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Re-concreted affected area of side passageway.

Inspected the common sewer on the right hand side of the building and found it to be blocked and surcharging from the overflow relief gully.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and equipment and ran hoses. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the common sewer line downstream of the gully outside unit 1.

Following extensive jet blasting, we were unable to clear the blockage from the outside gully. Lifted common sewer lids on the main sewer line up and downstream and found multiple sections of aggressive tree root infestations within the common sewer piping.

Carried out further CCTV camera survey works from the inspection openings and located tree roots downstream approximately 10 meters downstream, upstream approximately 6 meters and also tree roots, cracked piping and collapsed joints from the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to vertical shaft on Sydney Waters main junction approximately 12 meters.

Used pipe locating equipment and CCTV drain camera to locate the common earthenware sewer pipework located under the middle of the road to be completely collapsed. This is causing a sink hole and the bitumen in the middle of road to sink. The Council has been recently patch repaired the road in this area (photos attached). Please see CCTV camera survey on the outlet of boundary trap showing collapsed sewer pipework located under the road - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D55HD

Please see CCTV video link of common sewer line following clear out works on the right side of the building:
Downstream mainline - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D55O3
Upstream mainline - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D55OA

Engaged a second plumber, used high pressure water jet blaster truck with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out tree roots from the mainline on the right side, outlet of boundary trap downstream to vertical shaft and Sydney waters main junction connection under the road.

Once clear, flow tested all fixtures in unit 1 and common sewer pipework outside - All clear and in good working order. 

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Please note: If the tree root infested and collapsed common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages on the right side of the building - We advise to organize Council road opening permits and traffic control, saw cut road surface, excavate the ashfelt and ground, cut out collapsed 150mm earthenware sewer pipework located under the middle of the road, install new PVC pipework, fittings, reline outlet of boundary trap to vertical shaft under the road, reline downstream vertical shaft to Sydney waters main sealing all 150mm common earthenware sewer pipework under the road, back fil trench, temporary reinstate road, advised Council to undertake permeant repairs to the middle of the road.. Also to reline upstream and downstream of the inspection opening on the right hand side of the building sealing all tree root infested common sewer pipework to prevent further blockages. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common storm water pipework

Following the recent clear out works on the common storm water piping we found faulty joints and collapsed broken earthenware storm water piping where tree root infestations are entering the common storm water piping are causing common storm water blockages. 

This quotation is to gain access into garage number 12, reline approximately 9 meters of tree root infested, cracked earthenware common storm water pipework, relining from pit connection 9 meters downstream sealing all cracked and root infested joints finishing back onto earthenware pipework using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin and using robotic cutter reinstate 1 x junction located on relined pipework.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation:
  1. Gain access to Unit 12 Garage area.
  2. Set up safe working area and relining equipment. 
  3. Prepare all stormwater pipework to Australian Standards AS3500.
  4. Clear lines using high pressure water jet, mechanical milling equipment  & CCTV drain camera to prepare lines.
  5. Using CCTV equipment record stormwater pipework before relining.
  • Pipe relining:
  1. Reline approximately 9 meters of tree root infested, cracked common earthenware storm water pipework, relining from pit connection 9 meters downstream sealing all cracked and root infested joints finishing back onto earthenware pipework using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin.
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  3. Once liner has cured, removed relining equipment from the common storm water pipework.

Description:
PLUMBING - PIPE LEAKING
PLEASE SCHEDULE A DATE AND TIME TO ATTEND SITE TO PROCEED WITH THE BELOW
REQUEST :
Please attend site and rectify the leaking pipe in front of unit 8 car spot. (Photos attached).
Site Contact: Bob - 0430 136 590

Frizelle R 0430 136 590 / 0430 136 590
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in carspace 8, below units 3, 7 & 11.

23/4 - Attended the property, gained access and located the leak in car space 8. Inspected and found the kitchen stack pipe leaks from the concrete ceiling.

Gained access into unit 3 above, carried out dye testing to the common kitchen stack pipe and inspected the stack junction within the service riser - No leaks were found.

Knocked on units 7 & 11 above but no-one was home to undertake investigation works, so we left a note asking the occupants to contact us.

30/4 - Retuned to the property and gained access into unit 7 and 11. Cut out kitchen cabinetry in unit 7 and found it to be wet on the concrete slab.

Carried out nitrogen pressure testing in unit 7 and got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply, indicating a leak.

Inspected and found the hot water pipework runs in the concrete slab from the kitchen to the bathroom.

8/5 - Returned to the property with leak detection specialist and gained access into unit 7. Carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing and found the hot water leak had stopped.

Used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water supply in unit 7 from the kitchen to the bathroom.

Leak detection advised us to open up the hot water pipe dropper in the kitchen wall and expose around the hot pipework behind the stack.

Cut out melamine cabinetry and excavated the common wall exposing the hot water dropper and pipework behind the stack. Following our inspection, we found the wall cavity, concrete slab and lagging to be wet.

Carried out extensive testing by running the hot water and nitrogen pressure testing over 1000kpa and still no signs of the hot water leak.

13/5 - Returned to the property and gained access into unit 7. Inspected and found the external wall to be damp around the hot water dropper. 

After running the hot water through the line for a long period of time water started leaking into car space 8 and also from where the hot water pipe drops into the concrete slab.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 7 - As the burst hot water pipe is located within the concrete slab, we advise to re-run the hot water pipework from the kitchen to the bathroom installing new copper pipework and fittings on the external wall, deleting the burst hot water pipe within the slab in unit 7. We will submit a quotation shortly for the URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Please note - Whilst at the property unit 11 advised us of a leak in the kitchen. We inspected and found the dishwasher hose had burst, turned off the water supply to the dishwasher and advised the occupant to contact the appliance service to undertake repairs. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 9/5/26 - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 6.

Urgently attended the property after hours on Saturday, gained access into unit 6 and found the toilet to be blocked and surcharging when other residents use their fixtures.

Inspected the external common, sewer stack and found no inspection openings installed at the base and no access into the common sewer line.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster equipment and ran hoses up scaffolding into unit 6's bathroom.

Disconnected and removed the toilet from unit 6's bathroom.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer stack and sewer piping and found major tree root infestations growing at the base of the common sewer stack pipe and earthenware sewer piping causing the blockage.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to remove the tree roots from the base of the sewer stack pipe and sewer piping.

Once clear, tested the sewer piping with a high pressure hose - All in good working order.

Re-installed unit 6's toilet, sealing it to the bathroom floor tiles. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To prevent common sewer blockages, we advise an inspection opening is installed at the base of the stack and the affected common sewer line is relined. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Attended the property, gained access into garage 5 and located wet concrete slab around the copper stack and cold water riser pipe.

Removed the inspection opening on the common stack and found the in ground common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging. 

Set up high pressure water jet blaster equipment and ran hoses into the garage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with puncture heads to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the blocked sewer line and found building debris, concrete and rubble within the pipework that has caused the blockage. Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D5WX9

Carried out extensive jet blasting using multiple heads, but was unable to remove the concrete/ rubble and the pipework is still partially blocked.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to saw cut and excavate the concrete slab outside garage 5 on the right hand side of the building, excavate the concrete and ground, cut out section of common sewer pipework blocked with concrete and rubble, use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream to clear the common sewer pipework, install new section of PVC pipework and fittings, flow test all works, bed pipework, back fill trench and compact ground and re-instate concrete. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place with the high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common storm water pipework 

Following the recent blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found the common storm water pipework located under the Councils footpath on the Western side of the building to be cracked, dislodged and major tree roots entering the line causing blockages.

This urgent quotation is to reline approximately 3 to 4 meters of cracked, dislodged and tree root infested common storm water pipework located under the Councils footpath upstream from the kerb and gutter using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation: 
  1. Set up relining equipment.
  2. Barricade around work area. 
  3. Using high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera and mechanical milling tool clean sewer lines before relining.
  4. Record sewer lines before relining.
  • Relining repairs:
  1. Reline approximately 3 to 4 meters of cracked, dislodged and tree root infested common storm water pipework located under the Councils footpath upstream from the kerb and gutter sealing all earthenware joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line.
  4. Flow test all relining works undertaken.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 16's bathroom ceiling.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 16 and found water had leaked from the bathroom ceiling.

Went upstairs knocked on unit 23 but no-one was home at the time to undertake investigation works, so we left a note asking them to contact us.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 16 and removed ceiling fan in the bathroom ceiling to inspect inside the ceiling cavity.

Used inspection camera and located water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 23's bath waste pipework.

Gained access into unit 23 above and carried out extensive testing in the bathroom.

Pressure tested the shower and bath breaching pieces and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 23.

Flood tested the bath waste pipework and following flood testing of the bath waste, water leaked through the concrete slab penetration into unit 16's bathroom ceiling below, confirming the leak.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 16 & 23 - To rectify the leak, we advise to cut a larger hole in unit 16's ceiling, excavate the concrete slab, cut out the leaking bath waste pipework, install new bath waste, PVC pipework, fittings and plug & waste through the concrete slab from unit 23 into unit 16 connecting onto existing common waste pipework within the ceiling and flow test all works carried out. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed and we know the full extent of the damage, we will submit a quotation for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property to clear out common sewer and storm water system for the building and undertake a CCTV camera to inspect the condition of the pipework.

  • Common sewer pipework:

Obtained sewer service diagram for the building and located 2 x boundary traps, on the left and right hand side of the building. The outlet of the 2 x boundary traps then run downstream to Sydney Water main located under the road on Ramsgate Ave.

Removed inspection opening lids on the right side of the building, found major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework approximately 1 meter upstream the boundary trap.  Also major tree roots to be entering the base of the original earthenware boundary trap on the right hand side of the building downstream to Sydney Waters main for approximately 8 meters located under the road. 

Removed inspection opening lids on the left hand side of the building, found major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework approximately 3 meter upstream the boundary trap.  Also major tree roots to be entering the base of the original earthenware boundary trap on the left hand side of the building downstream to Sydney Waters main for approximately 8 meters located under the road. 

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework on the left and right hand side of the building. Also clear out all tree roots from the base of 2 x boundary traps on the left and right hand side of the building downstream to Sydney Waters main located under the road.

Flow tested the common sewer pipework for the building which is clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not relined, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Further works required to be undertaken on the buildings sewer pipework - We advise to reline the tree root infested common sewer pipework on the left and right hand side of the building. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

  • Common storm water pipework:

Disconnected and removed the base of the downpipe on the right hand side of the building, used CCTV drain camera downstream the rear right downpipe, found tree roots to be entering the common storm water pipework for 15 meters and junction connecting front downpipe. We found the common storm water pipework to be completely collapsed approximately 15 meters downstream of the rear downpipe to the front of the building before the front retaining wall. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream the rear downpipe to clear out tree root infestations from the common storm water line, but we were unable to get past the collapsed section located at the front right hand side of the building. Used pipe locator to locate the collapsed section under the concrete slab.

Further works required to required the common storm water system on the right hand side of the building - We advise to reline from the rear right downpipe to the front right of the building, saw cut and excavate the concrete slab and Councils footpath, install new PVC pipework from relined section downstream to the kerb and gutter in the street, back fill trench, reinstate concrete and temporary repair Councils footpath using cold mix bitumen. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Disconnected and removed the base of the downpipe on the left hand side of the building, used CCTV drain camera downstream the rear left downpipe and found the common storm water pipework to be blocked.

Used high pressure jet blaster but after extensive jet blasting we were unable to clear the blockage and found the common storm water pipework to be collapsed approximately 8 meters downstream the rear downpipe.

Further works required to be undertaken on the common storm water system on the left hand side of the building - We advise to saw cut and excavate the concrete slab on the left side of the building approximately 8 meters, cut out collapsed and broken common storm water pipework, use CCTV drain camera and high pressure water jet blaster to clear out the common storm water pipework downstream of the collapsed pipework, install new PVC pipework and fittings, flow test all works, bed pipework, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. If further issues are found downstream of the repaired area, a variation quotation will be submitted. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Re-connected the base of the 2 x rear downpipes, re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Investigate water damage in the common hallway ceilings on ground floor.

Used moisture meter to confirm moisture in the common stairs and outside unit 6, indicating a leak.

Cut a hole in the water damaged staircase ceiling, inspected the cavity and located the drainage for unit 12 above. Went upstairs and knocked on unit 12, but we were unable to gain access on our inspection and left and note on their door to contact us.

4/5 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 12 and the occupant advised during heavy rain the unit previously flooding causing water to leak into the hallway below.

Inspected unit 12's balcony drainage and found it runs within the ceiling cavity along to the external downpipe.

Removed inspection opening lids on the external downpipe, used CCTV drain camera to inspect the balcony and downpipe drainage and found it to be blocked with large amounts of solidified calcium.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the external downpipe. Used high pressure water jet blaster to clear the blockage at the base of the downpipe releasing the line.

Following extensive jet blasting and clear out works, we located a large amount of calcium build up within the stormwater aerial drainage within the common ceiling space.

5/5 - Returned to the property the following day, set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the external downpipe.

Carried out extensive jet blasting for over 3 hours, but was unable to clear out all the solidified calcium from the common stormwater arial drainage. Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D5JEN

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - As the calcium blockage cannot be cleared, we advise to cut out the ceilings in units 4 & 5 balcony to access the affected stormwater pipework, cut and replace with new PVC pipe and fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 1/5/26 - Urgent water leak / sewer blockage at the property.

Urgently attended the property after hours, inspected the property and found a large amount of sewage surcharging out of the floor drain in the carpark.

Inspected the common sewer pipework drainage in the lower level carpark and located a blocked common sewer reflux vale that was causing the sewer overflow.

Set up high pressure water jet blasting equipment and ran hoses into the carpark.

Lifted lids on the common sewer pipework and reflux valve releasing the common sewer line.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTVC camera simultaneously to clear the blockage in the sewer piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found congealed fat causing the blockage in the common sewer line. Please see video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D5RMQ

Used the high pressure water jet blaster with CCTV drain camera to clear out the congealed fat from the common sewer piping.

Flow tested the sewer piping with a high pressure hose - All clear and in good working order.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Following our CCTV camera survey of the common sewer line, we located backfall in the pipework which was causing it to hold water and solidified grease waste.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To rectify the backfall in the common sewer line causing blockages, we advise the cut out and replace approximately 6 meters of aerial drainage with backfall in the carpark. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

I’ve now gone back over this matter, again – and the below are my notes/thoughts:
•    9 Jan 2026 – issue a work order to M8 Plumbing
•    8–9 Jan 2026 – committee flags possible ventilation issues in Unit 17 (blinds/windows shut), but agrees to a second investigation to rule out leaks

•    18 Feb 2026 – tenant reports leaks 15–18 Feb and correlates with upper unit laundry usage (can hear water in ceiling pipes)
•    17–18 Feb 2026 – property manager asks for updates; M8 requested to provide a status report
•    25 Feb 2026 – tenant says leak is ongoing

From a technical viewpoint:
The leak seems to correlate “mostly when laundry in the upper unit is being used.” So, I would have thought that this strongly points to:
•    Laundry waste stack / branch (cracked pipe/failed joint)
•    Washing machine standpipe/connection overflow or hose
•    Floor waste / bucket trap issues

Less likely, but nonetheless possible: shower/bath overflows if the laundry discharges into a shared line that’s partially blocked.

The time-based, repeatable nature (during water discharge above) suggests active plumbing leak or intermittent surcharge — not just condensation or ventilation. The Committee’s earlier note about poor ventilation may be relevant to mould/condensation generally, but perhaps doesn’t explain active drip during laundry cycle – so there, we should treat this as a real plumbing issue until proven otherwise.

Suggested next steps:
At this point, it may be prudent to arrange a joint attendance with:
•    Tenant - U17
•    Lot above (20) – when laundry in use
•    Strata plumber (M8 Plumbing)  

Further, in regard to M8’s scope of work, on authorisation from Committee and subject to quote, to perform and document:

4.    CCTV of the laundry/bathroom waste line if drain access exists
5.    Static pressure test of water lines if waste tests are negative
6.    Ceiling inspection cut (if safe/approved) at wettest point to visualise the source and speed up resolution

Isolated the water supply in unit 1, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. Following extensive pressure testing no burst pipes were found within unit 1.

Returned to property, gained access and flood tested the front nature strip with red dye. Following flood dye testing of the grass at the front nature strip, no dye leaked down into the carpark below unit 1.

You are hereby given 14 days notice, in accordance with section 132 of the Local Government Act 1993, that Council intends to serve an order in accordance with the provisions of section 124 (order No. 21) of the Act directing you to repair the pipe facing Bradley Street and to maintain the premises in a safe and healthy condition.
A period of 28 days will be given in which to comply with the order and the Councils order will advise you of your right of appeal.
The reason that Council intends to give this order is that the land and/or premises is not in a safe or healthy condition in that:
• An onsite inspection by a member of Council has disclosed that the pipe is causing a heavy water over-flow at the front of the subject premises onto the public footpath.
• The issue is causing a nuisance to pedestrians passing by.
Invoice Description:
Investigate leaking down pipe facing Bradley Street Randwick is causing water to discharge onto Council’s footpath.

Attended the property, found the downpipe and rain head located on Western facing side of the building to be completely blocked and surcharging onto the Councils footpath during heavy rain.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Gained access onto the roof, could see the rain water outlet to be completely blocked.

Used jet blaster with whippet hose downstream the top of the rain head outlet, but due to the difficult access from the roof we were unable to clear the blockage from the roof after multiple attempts.

Cut a hole in the base of the downpipe, used high pressure jet blaster with whippet hose upstream the downpipe and we were able to clear the blockage after multiple attempts.

Used CCTV drain camera upstream the downpipe - All clear and in good working order.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream of the downpipe to locate a large amount of dirt and debris causing a blockage on the main storm water line.

Used CCTV drain camera from the kerb and gutter outlet and found multiple sections of tree root infestation, dislodged joints and cracked piping between the base of the downpipe and the street. Video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D358D

Used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out all dirt and tree roots from the base of the downpipe to the kerb and gutter clearing the common storm water line.

Repaired the base of the downpipe, flow tested common storm water line downstream to the kerb and gutter in the street - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent common stormwater blockages, we advise the cracked and tree root infested common stormwater line under the council footpath is relined from the base of the downpipe to the street. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Please see attached damp / leak report with photos from Agent and attend to U17 to investigating lifting laundry floor/damp in unit 17.
Site contact: U17 Tenants: Joseph 0411 844 851/ jcataldo75@gmail.com or Jazmin 0468 353 478 / jazmin-green@hotmail.co.uk
PM who report this leak is Andrew Celona 0421 562 225 / andrew.celona@db.rh.com.au
Andrew's email description'We recently had our tradesman investigating lifting laundry floor/damp in unit 17. Our tradesman has advised that a leak from the Common Stack in the laundry with this leak also passing below into unit #14 (U14 owner: Kevin 0414302307 / kevgarber@gmail.com). Please see advise from the tradesman below and attached report.'

 

REPORT:

Attend for complaint of floor lifting under lino squares and also water appearing from under lino as well.
Laundry had not been used prior to our arrival, and shower in the bathroom that backs onto the laundry had also not been used.
We ran water from the laundry tap into the tub to test for any leaks on the waste connections, as well as the side drain for the washing machine hose & also washing machine connections, but after approx 20 minutes of run, no leaks were found.
On inspection, we did notice water beads coming up from between the floor lino squares as this was not apparent prior. We can also confirm this by use of our damp meter before & after with a saturation reading after running water.
Waste connection was noted as running through the side of the tub into a Common wall ducting that houses a stack pipe, running top of the roof to ground floor. We noted that after running water, the wood around the base of this ducting was saturated, which it was not prior. We also noted water damage to rendered walls next to it.

A cable camera was placed into the duct via an access hole, already there, so we could see inside the wall ducting. The tub connection to the stack was found and seen to be dry on the top, as was the wood around it.

A visual inspection directly under the tub connection to stack, looking back up to the connection underside, was not possible due to the angle to look back & up, however we did note that all wood and the base of the duct were damp under this connection.

This indicated that the stack is possibly leaking from the underside of this connection or maybe the base of the stack as it passes through the floor slab.

In order to get a better visual, we were able to access the unit directly below, #14, and see their laundry.
The ceiling of #14, directly under the raised concrete section of floor in unit #17, was soaked and water damaged. The owner confirmed that this leak hadbeen ongoing for approx 6 to 7 months and he had reported it to Strata but was passed off initially as damage from a renovation he had done even though it had been checked by his Builder & Plumber.

Damage to unit #14 ceiling and walls & ducting in unit #17, both appear to be from a leaking Common Stack, as already described.
We recommend referring this to Strata in the first instance so that they can attend and remove the bottom half of the ducting to get a full visual of the issues and cause.
Floor will also need the lino lifted and concrete repairs carried out where the concrete has either lifted or is delaminating.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access and located a water leak in the storage area below unit 3 from the bottom of the common wall.

Inspected the courtyard outside unit 3 and found the common sewer mainline and stormwater piping runs along this wall.

Carried out a CCTV camera survey of the common stormwater line from the downpipe and found no issues that could be causing a leak in the storage area.

Carried out a CCTV camera survey of the common sewer mainline upstream from the boundary trap and found the common sewer mainline to be clear.

Knocked on units 3 & 4 and no-one was home at the time. Left access notes.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 4 and carried out extensive dye testing of the bathroom and kitchen waste fixtures.

Following extensive dye testing of the kitchen waste piping in unit 4, we found yellow dye to be leaking from the bottom of the wall in unit 3's storage area confirming the leak.

CCTV camera surveyed from the external sewer gully outside unit 4 and found the outlet of the gully to be blocked downstream.

Engaged a second plumber, set up high pressure water jet blasting equipment and ran hoses.

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the sewer piping. 

Once clear, CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found major tree root infestations growing in the earthenware to PVC connection causing the blockage and leak.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken- To prevent further common sewer blockages and to rectify the leak, we advise 3.5 meters of common sewer line downstream of the gully to the PVC connection is relined. We will submit a quotation shortly for the URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked stormwater drain in the driveway.

Attended the property, gained access and located the blocked common stormwater pit and grated drain in the driveway at the front right.

Lifted grated lids and cleaned out leaves and debris from the grated drain and the stormwater pit.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream from the pit and found the outlet pipework under the council footpath to be blocked.

Engaged a 2nd plumber and set up high pressure water jet blasting truck, equipment and ran hoses.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster with tree root cutting heads to clear out the common stormwater line under the council footpath.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To prevent further tree root infested blockages, we advise to reline approximately 2.5 meters of broken and tree root infested common storm water pipework located under the council footpath from the kerb and gutter to the stormwater pit completely sealing the pipework to prevent further blockages. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further relining works required to be undertaken on the common storm water pipework.

To prevent flooding in the driveway and common areas during heavy rain, we advise preventative maintenance clear out works on the common stormwater, strip drains and driveway pits at the property are undertaken every 6 months. As we have just completed these works, the next clear out works will be due in October 2026.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Quotation - Relining works on the common stormwater line under the front footpath and driveway.

Following the common stormwater clear out and pipe replacement works at the front of the property and in the council nature strip, we were able to clear out large amounts of tree roots from the common stormwater line which runs under the building to the rear strip drain. Once the tree roots had been cut out, we camera surveyed the piping and found a section of storm water piping under the front footpath and driveway that is letting tree roots into the storm water piping causing blockages. 

This quotation is to reline approximately 4 meters of tree roots infested common stormwater earthenware pipework under the front footpath and driveway.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation: 
  1. Set up safe working area at the front of the property.
  2. Clean stormwater line with high pressure water jet preparation for relining.
  3. Camera Inspect and CCTV record stormwater line before relining.

Relining repairs:

  1. Reline tree root infested section of PVC pipework and fittings approximately 4 meters, using watermark approved liner with 2-part epoxy resin.
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once cured, remove relining equipment from the common stormwater line.
  4. Using Robotic cutter reinstate 1 x  junction located on relined pipework.
  5. Flow test all relining works undertaken.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak at the rear of the building.

Attended the property, gained access to the rear of the building from Ilkka Beach Cafe bar and found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage next to the grease arrestor for the Cafe.

Removed an inspection opening on the common sewer pipework to confirm the blockage was downstream from the arrestor in the common sewer line.

Returned to the property, engaged 2 x plumbers, used extension ladder on both sides of a brick wall, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the rear of the building.

Used high pressure jet blaster extensively downstream the PVC inspection opening from the outlet of the grease arrestor to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate a large amount of congealed fat in the common sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage.

Continued to use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out all congealed fat from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested common sewer pipework which is clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant and high pressure hose.

PLEASE NOTE - We removed the lid for the grease arrestor for the Cafe and found the chamber was full of solidified fat. We advise the Cafe engages their own contractor to clean out the grease arrestor for the Cafe.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate garage flood.

Attended the property, gained access to lower garage and found the common stormwater pit to be full of water and flooded the garage floor.

Used large extension ladder to access the pit and lifted floats to activate pumps and pumped out water from the pit.

Once water was removed from the pit, pump 1 (original pump) would not turn off and the all floats are down, which should turn off at the control panel.

Tested pump 2 (new pump) and found it turns on at the control panel, but the pump does not operate.

Inspected the pump control panel and both pumps are on the same circuit breaker. Isolated the power supply to the 2 x pumps to prevent the new pump from burning out.

Urgently returned to the property the following day, met with our electrical contractor and gained access to the lower carpark. Carried out a series of tests on the 2 x pumps and control panel.

Following testing, we found the original fuse for pump 2 (new pump) on the control panel has blown and caused pump 2 to fail, the stop float switch within the control panel for pump 1 (original pump) has failed which is causing pump 1 to not turn off, and pump 1 (original pump) slowly discharges water from the pit at half capacity of pump 2 (new pump).

Carried out a temporary repair by isolating pump 1 (original pump) and replacing the blown fuse for pump 2 with the fuse for pump 1 so that there is 1 x new working pump.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise the common stormwater pump control panel is upgraded with a new control panel and the original pump 1 and float switches are replaced. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Investigate water leak in 604's garage.

Gained access into G01 above, lifted manhole in the bathroom ceiling and inspected the ceiling cavity. Found water leaking within the bathroom ceiling cavity from the concrete slab.

Stepped out the location of the leak in G01's bathroom ceiling and found it was a separate leak to the garage leak. Gained access into unit 102 and dye tested the bath waste pipework.

Following dye testing in unit 102, we found green dye to be leaking into unit G01's bathroom ceiling confirming a separate leak from unit 102's bath waste.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advised and the works are being undertaken to replace the burst common bath waste pipework where it goes through the concrete slab from unit 102 into unit G01.

Gained access into unit 101, lifted manhole in the bathroom ceiling,  inspected the ceiling cavity and found water leaking within the bathroom ceiling cavity from above.

Gained access into unit 201, lifted manhole in the bathroom ceiling, inspected the ceiling cavity and found water leaking within the bathroom ceiling cavity from above.

Knocked on units 301 & 401 and no-one was home at the time, left access notices.

26/2 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 401, lifted manhole in the bathroom ceiling, inspected the ceiling cavity and no leaks were found.

2/3 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 301, lifted manhole in the bathroom ceiling and no leaks were found to be coming from unit 401.

Cut a hole within the laundry service riser in unit 301 and found water pooling on the concrete slab around the common stack pipe.

Carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and found a drop in pressure on the hot water pipe indicating a burst pressurized pipe within unit 301.

Used pipe location, leak detection equipment and thermal image camera but we were unable to pin point the location of the burst hot water pipework within unit 301.

4/3 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 301 and laid drop sheets in the laundry. Excavated splashback tiles, disconnected and removed the laundry tub.

Excavated the common wall exposing the hot and cold water pipes within the wall. Nitrogen pressure tested the hot water pipework and found a drop in pressure.

Used a listening device and pipe locating equipment to trace out the pipework and found the burst pressurized hot water pipe is located inside the concrete slab from the laundry to the kitchen and is required to be rerun.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the common hot water pipework within the concrete slab in unit 301 is deleted and is rerun from the laundry to the kitchen, we will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 301.

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared within the car park, we located major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework causing sewer blockages in the laundries. 

This quotation is to carry out preventative maintenance water jet blasting and CCTV camera survey works clearing out tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework within the car park to prevent sewer blockages and floods.

Description: No gas to harries cafe
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 21/2/26 - No gas to Harry's Cafe.

Urgently attended the property after hours, engaged one plumber, gained access to Harrys Cafe and found there to be no gas supply to appliances.

Inspected the common gas meter at the rear side passage and found the regulator, gas meter manifold and fittings to be corroded and in poor condition.

Disconnected the gas regulator and found rust particles within the gas pipework which a was causing a blockage, cleared rust and purged the line to get the gas coming through.

Engaged a second plumber who urgently attended plumbing suppliers at Reece Waverley, which was closed and went to additional suppliers in Alexandria to source new gas regulator and safety button.

We found these specific gas parts were not available from any of the plumbing suppliers and they are required to be sourced from the gas company.

Re-connected gas regulator, piping and fittings, purged gas through the line and tested all appliances in the Cafe - Gas was flowing into the cafe and the cook tops were in working order.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty gas regulator with safety button, meter bar, all fittings and safety button is replaced. We advise Harry to contact his gas supplier to see if they will provide these items. Once materials have been sourced from the GAS supplier we can install them.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 21/2/26 - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 7

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 7 and found the toilet to be completely blocked. Sewerage was surcharging when the above units used there waste fixtures.

Flow tested the toilet in unit 7 and still found the common sewer stack to be blocked.

Returned to the property on Monday 23/2/26 with 2 x plumbers.

Carefully cut, excavated and removed bricks exposing common sewer stack pipework.

Cut out the faulty and seized common sewer inspection opening and pipework. Supplied and installed new section of PVC inspection opening and pipework to access the blocked common sewer stack pipework.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera upstream of the common sewer stack pipework to clear out all rust from the original common sewer stack pipework.

Flow tested common sewer stack pipework - All clear and in good working order.

Re-bricked affected area of common wall in the car park and re-pointed using mortar. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose, disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common storm water pipework

Following the recent storm water clear out works undertaken and our CCTV camera survey, we located a collapsed and tree root infested section of common earthenware storm water pipework located under the concrete driveway.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 meters of collapsed, tree root infested and dislodged common earthenware stormwater pipework located under the concrete driveway using watermark approved liner and 2-part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation:
  1. Barricade around work area at the front of the building.
  2. Set up relining equipment in the garden area.
  3. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  4. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Reline approximately 2 meters of collapsed, tree root infested and dislodged common earthenware stormwater pipework located under the concrete driveway using watermark approved liner and 2-part epoxy resin.
  2. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  7. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  8. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  9. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.
