Invoice Description:
Attended the property and gained access to investigate the leak at the front of the building entrance beside the switch room.

Collected keys from Katherine in unit 35 and gained access to the switch room.

Located the common sewer stack in the corner of the switch room adjacent to the where the leak was coming from the wall.

Removed sewer stack inspection opening, CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer drainage and found it to be blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the front of the property and ran hose to the switchboard room.

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream from the inspection opening to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera an pipe locating equipment to locate major tree root infestations entering the cracked and collapsed original common earthenware sewer pipework downstream of the inspection opening lid. Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DSX61

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads extensively and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework, which is the cause of the common sewer blockage.

Once clear, flow tested common sewer pipework downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order.

Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not relined, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages and leaks at the entrance to the building - We advise to reline approximately 3 to 4 meters of tree root infested, cracked and collapsed common earthenware sewer pipework downstream from the switch room sewer stack. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas were work has taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 98.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 98 and located water damage on the internal hallway and bedroom walls adjacent to the shower recess.

Blocked off the shower floor drain and dye tested the shower recess with green dye over 1 hour and following dye testing, no dye leaked.

Isolated the hot and cold water supply and carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the hot, cold and shower breach.

Pressure tested hot water and shower breach - No burst pipes were found on the hot or shower breach. Following pressure testing, we found the common cold water isolation valve does not isolate and we unable to get an accurate pressure test.

Returned to the property, isolated the buildings water supply and drained the water from the line.

Disconnected unit 98's common cold water isolation valve in the kitchen, supplied and installed new cold water isolation valve. Turned the buildings water supply back on testing all works - All in good working order.

Pressure tested cold water supply and found there to be no drop in pressure indicating no burst pipes in unit 98.

Inspected the shower recess and found missing wall & floor grout and stressed tiles. Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DSC6M

We also found faulty sealant around the shower screen. Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DSC6J

Flood tested the shower screen and found water leaks back into the internal wall from faulty shower screen seals and missing internal wall grout, confirming the leak.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 98 - To rectify the leak form the shower recess causing damage to the internal hallway and bedroom wall, we advise the entire original shower recess and 2 x internal walls are re-sealed & grouted and the lot owners shower screen is replaced. We will submit a quotation shorty for the further URGENT grouting and sealing works required to be undertaken in unit 98.

Whilst undertaking testing in unit 98, we removed the toilet cistern lid and cracked the bathroom wall paint. We advise the affected area of bathroom wall above the toilet cistern is repaired and painted.

Addition works: Whilst undertaking the works the owner asked us to inspect other issues:

1. Inspected the bathroom ceiling and found flaking paint throughout the entire ceiling. Gained access into the common roof space and confirmed no water damage to the underside of the ceiling, indicating the paint damage to be caused by poor ventilation in the bathroom when showering. As there is no fan installed inside the bathroom, we advise an electrician is engaged to install a exhaust fan in the bathroom, expelling air outside.

2. Inspected the balcony and found a large crack in the concrete and no waterproof membrane or tiles. We advise a building contractor is engaged to inspect the balcony and undertake repair works.

Once all repair works are completed and we know the full extent of the damage, we will submit a separate quotation for any resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate gas leak in unit 1.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found there to be a gas smell near the fire place.

Used gas detector to identify high readings of gas around the fire place and under the subfloor.

Carried out a drop testing on unit 1's gas outlet pipework and got a drop in pressure indicating a leak.

Engaged a second plumber and climbed under unit 1 from the small crawl space and bubble leak sprayed unit 1's gas supply outlet pipework.

Removed unit 1's gas fire place from the wall and inspected the pipework and connections behind the fire place.

Following testing of unit 1's outlet gas supply, we located a leak on the galvanised steel pipework where it goes up through the floor and connects onto the fire place.

Isolated the gas supply and capped off the service which goes to the fireplace.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - We advise to replace original gas piping up through the floor and re-connect onto the fire place. We will submit a quotation shortly for the URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage on the Cooyoung Crescent side of the building.

Urgently attended the property, found the boundary trap and common sewer line for the whole building to be completely blocked and flooding sewerage.

Set up high pressure jet blaster and equipment.

Removed inspection opening lids and Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream the boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate a broken section of 150mm common sewer pipework on the outlet of the boundary trap where tree roots are aggressively entering the pipework which is the cause of the blockage.

Please see CCTV video link of tree root infestations causing the blockage - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DSEAD

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer line.

Flow tested boundary trap and common sewer line - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise the tree root infested common sewer piping is relined from top of boundary trap (ground level) down over root infested cracked pipework finishing before vertical shaft connection, sealing root infested pipework using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin and reinstate 1 x gully connection using robotic cutter. We will submit an URGENT quotation shortly for the further urgent relining works required to be undertaken.

Description:
investigating 121 Cooper St ceiling leak and suspicious pipe
Hi Team,
As per email Re 121 Cooper st i just sent, please kindly carry out the investigation as engineer's report.
Thank you.
Site contact : 0423778951

As per eningeer comments below Re 121 Cooper St.
Can you please attend and investigate the pipe. I will issue the work order and attach this email. 

I found that the ceiling was dry. I carried out further water testing from the unit above (5/123 Cooper) both on the balcony and on the outside of the building, including some different locations to last time, however this testing did not result in any leaks into the 121 Cooper front bedroom (I cut a small access panel in the ceiling to be able to inspect it directly, and then covered it with a plastic vent - Photo 1 below). The concrete slab and walls that I could see with my inspection camera inside the ceiling were all dry and there were no old water stains.

By inspecting inside the ceiling space this time, I found that there is a pipe running inside the bedroom ceiling above where the mould is occurring - this pipe is wrapped in silver insulation/lagging (Photo 2 below) and there seemed to be some water stains along the underside of that pipe (Photo 3). The 5/123 Cooper balcony drainage outlet pipe connects into it, but I could not determine where the main pipe comes from. It must discharge into the rainhead outside the bedroom window, so I assume it is carrying stormwater from somewhere further up. 

Incidentally this explains why the dropped ceiling extends all the way to the front wall in that corner, and means we can't cut it back as I had originally proposed in my report - but having discovered this pipe it is now my prime suspect.

It is interesting that it is wrapped in insulation - I'm not sure if this was a code requirement, or if the original builder just felt there was a risk of condensation forming on the outside of the pipe and then dripping onto the ceiling. That would certainly be one explanation for why there are mould issues occurring in the bedroom in winter. 

The next step I would recommend is for the plumber to camera inspect this pipe to determine:

1.    What function it serves/where it runs from, and 
If it is damaged and could be leaking into the ceiling.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent after-hours blockage we cleared downstream the toilet and our CCTV camera survey we found the original earthenware pipework to be dislodged on multiple joints causing toilet paper to get stack causing blockages.

This quotation is to disconnect and remove the toilet in the bathroom, reline approximately 9 meters of dislodged and original earthenware sewer pipework downstream the toilet completely sealing the pipework and re-instate all junctions using robotic cutter, re-install toilet and flow test all works carried out.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Set up relining equipment in the bathroom.
  2. Disconnect and remove toilet to access the common sewer pipework.
  3. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  4. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  5. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  6. Reline approximately 9 meters of dislodged and original earthenware sewer pipework downstream the toilet, sealing all root cracked and leaking using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  7. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  8. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  9. Re-instate all junctions using robotic cutter. 
  10. Re-install existing toilet sealing to the ground using high grade flexible sealant. 
  11. Flow test all works carried out.
  12. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  13. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  14. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  15. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  16. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked kitchen waste in unit 3.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found the kitchen sink surcharges sewerage when units above use their fixtures.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the congealed grease fat from the inlet to the gully, upstream to the common sewer stack pipe.

Flow tested the sewer piping with a high pressure hose - All clear and in good working order.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Attended the property, gained access into the underground garage and found water leaking from the concrete wall around the pipe penetration.

Went up above to the common walkway on the right side of townhouse 10 and found the common stormwater pit to be blocked.

Removed pavers to access the lid, lifted pit lid and cleaned out stormwater pit removing build up of sand and debris.

Used CCTV drain camera from the downpipe in townhoues 9's courtyard and found the common stormwater line to blocked.

Cut out common stormwater drainage in the carpark and set up high pressure water jet blasting truck and equipment.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out large amounts of tree roots within the common stormwater drainage.

Please see CCTV video link of major tree roots - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DIJND

Once the tree roots had been cut out, we camera surveyed the piping and found broken section of storm water piping and fitting that is letting tree roots into the storm water piping and water to leak into the subsoil confirming the leak.

Used pipe location equipment to locate the affected storm water piping under the courtyard of townhouse 9.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To rectify further storm water blockages, we advise the broken and tree root infested common storm water piping is relined. We will submit a quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Re-cemented pit lid and pavers outside unit 10, cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.

Investigate urgent sewer blockage.

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the overflow gully located at the front, left hand side of the building.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage in the main line and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment to locate major tree roots entering the original earthenware sewer pipework and inspection opening junction approximately 6 meters upstream from the boundary trap located outside unit 4's garage which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework and junction. Please see CCTV video link after cleared tree roots with high pressure jet blaster - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DIKMP

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the main sewer line from the common boundary trap further upstream and located a separate section of earthenware pipework that has collapsed on the 45 degree bend approximately 11 meters upstream of the boundary trap under unit 4's garage. To rectify, we advise this collapsed section of common eartanwere sewer pipework is relined, completely sealaing the defective pipework to prevent further common sewer blockages.

Flow tested overflow gully and common sewer pipework downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework and junction is not replaced, the tree roots will grow back and further sewer blockages will re-occur.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream the boundary trap to inspect the relined works we previously undertaken under the road, which is in good working order and no faults found.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to excavate the concrete and ground outside unit 4's garage approximately 6 meters upstream from the boundary trap, cut out and replace approximately 2 meters of tree root infested common earthenware sewer pipework and junction with new PVC pipework and fittings, install inspection opening raised to the surface for future clear out purposes, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. Also to reline the collapsed section of earthenware pipework under garage 4 approximately 11 meters upstream of the boundary trap.  We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked stormwater in Townhouse 6.

Attended the property, met with the site contact Stan and gained access into townhouse 6.

Inspected the common stormwater drainage at the rear of townhouse 6 and found that previously, the backyard flooded causing major water damage internally.

During recent heavy rain, the grassed area in the backyard almost flooded again.

Using 2 x plumbers, lifted floating tiles in the backyard to locate surface drains under the tiles. Once we lifted the floating tiles, we found there to be no surface water drainage below.

Carefully re-installed floating tiles.

Used CCTV drain camera and surveyed the common stormwater drain at the rear of townhouse 6 downstream of the common stormwater pit. Following our CCTV camera survey of the outlet to the pit, we found the common drainage to be clear and no blockages.

Next to the common stomrwater pit in the grassed area, we found the soil has sunk adjacent to the floating tiles. We found stormwater water runoff from the grassed area overflows onto the courtyard tiles.

Stan also advised the neighbouring stormwater line has also caused major flooding in the past is currently blocked and is being investigated and rectified.

Returned to the property and gained access, inspected the common stormwater drainage and found an OSD tank at the front left side of townhouse 1 in the rear courtyard.

Inspected the common stormwater drainage in the underground garage and found that townhouse 6's stormwater line discharges into a spoon drain, then into a series of pits within the garage which then gets pumped into the OSD.

Flow tested the basement stormwater pumps, found them to be in good working order and confirmed the OSD is not blocked. We also located an overflow from the OSD tank, which is lower than the level of the grassed area in townhouse 6 to prevent flooding if the OSD blocks.

Further works required to be undertaken in townhouse 6 - To prevent flooding in townhouse 6 during heavy rain, we advise a strip drain is installed along the front of the floating tiles and drainage is installed connected to the grated drain to the common stormwater pit at the rear.  We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in townhouse 6.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common storm water

This quotation is to reline the cracked, original storm water pipework at the front of the property, completely sealing the line to prevent further blockages and ground subsidence 

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation: 
  1. Set up safe working areas at the property. 
  2. Using high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera clean storm water pipework preparation for relining.
  3. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining. 
  4. Carefully move air conditioning unit located in unit 3 courtyard to gain access to the stormwater connection.
  5. Excavate downpipe connection, remove collapsed section of stormwater pipework and install new PVC pipework onto existing stormwater line.
  • Relining Repairs 
  1. Reline approximately 9 meters of crack leaking earthenware pipework relining from downpipe connection in unit 3 courtyard, downstream covering all cracked pipework on mainline finishing at kerb connection using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  2. Reline approximately 7 meters of cracked dislodged earthenware pipework relining from downpipe connection located near garage door, downstream fishing reline at previously relined mainline sealing all cracked dislodged joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 2 meters of cracked leaking earthenware pipework. Relining from down-pipe connection located near entry gate, downstream finishing at previously relined side line sealing all earthenware joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  4. Cure line with a hot water boiler.
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common storm water pipework.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test relined pipework. 
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  9. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.

PLEASE NOTE - We strongly suggest this repair be completed with an approved epoxy resin. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water the leak in unit 30 from unit 32. 

Attended the property, gained access into unit 30 and found bubbling paint in the hallway and master bedroom to the ceiling cornice adjacent to the bathroom. 

Used moisture meter to identify medium readings of moisture within the water damaged cornice. 

Gained access into unit 32, used moisture meter and located high readings along the internal hallway wall adjacent to the shower/ bath.

Inspected the bathroom and found faulty sealant and tiling along the bath edge where water can leak down the wall and under the bath.

We found the bath is not chased into the wall under the tiles and movement in the bath is causing the internal wall seals to crack.

Excavated a hole in the side of the bath and carried out flood testing of the bath waste, internal shower wall tiles and faulty sealant.

Following dye testing of the bath waste, we found no dye to be leaking.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 7's garage from unit 4 above.

19/1 - Attended the property, met with the buildings locksmith and gained access into unit 4.

Inspected unit 7's garage and found water leaking around the plumbing pipe penetration and common stack pipework.

Looked inside unit 4's bathroom ceiling cavity and found the ceiling to be dry indicating the leak to be coming from unit 4.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply in unit 4. Following extensive pressure testing, we found there to be a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 4 causing the leak into unit 7's garage below.

As the occupant in unit 4 was away, we isolated the water supply to prevent further water damage in unit 7's garage below.

23/1 - Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection and gained access into unit 4.

Used pipe locator to trace out the hot water service and listening device to pin pint the burst hot water pipe to be located within the common laundry wall.

Gained access into unit 8 above, carried out a dye test on the common stack drainage and confirmed no leaks were found in unit 4 and 7's garage below.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 4 - We advise to remove the splash back tiles, laundry tub in unit 4, excavate the common wall exposing the burst hot water pipework within the wall, cut out burst hot water pipework, install new copper pipework, fittings and temporary re-install laundry tub. We will send an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed, we will submit a quotation for the resultant damage repairs and tiling in unit 4. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared in unit 1 and our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware common sewer pipework in 3 x locations which was the cause of the blockage and flood. 

Major tree root infestations were entering the junction on the vertical shaft at the rear of the building, major tree roots entering upstream of the boundary trap for approximately 4 meters and also further tree roots entering the common sewer pipework approximately 18 meters upstream.

This quotation is to install 3 x separate relining repairs on the common sewer pipework as a full proof solution to prevent further common sewer blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation: 
  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut downs during the relining works. 
  2. Set up safe working areas around property.
  3. Gain access to all sewer inspection points.
  4. Clean sewer line with high pressure water jet preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.
  6. Measure cut and prepare new liner. 
  • Relining repairs -  3 x Repairs 
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 4 meters of tree root infested sewer pipework, relining from boundary trap connection 4 meters upstream covering all root infested joints finishing reline before gully Junction, using watermarked approved Liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 2-3 meters of root infested sewer pipework., relining over heavily tree root infested joints finishing back onto earthenware pipework, using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  4. Install 1 x 150mm x 150mm x 90 degree satellite Junction repair complete Y section, relining over root infested Junction sealing in to boundary trap outlet, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  5. Cure liner using hot water boiler. 
  6. Once cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line.
  7. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  8. Flow test all relining works undertaken.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  11. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  12. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

- Apply a new waterproof membrane as per Australian Standards
including the use of a flexible bandage (bond breaker) to the perimeter
junctions.

- Supply and fit new 80-100mm metal square floor waste.
- Supply and fit new salmon (tbc) or white 200x200mm floor tiles.

waste and to perimeter junction.

- Apply specialised flexible seal to the wall to wall junctions.

epoxy grout.

due to the age, condition, or design.

walls, timber door frame, plasterboard etc.) surrounding the shower is
not repaired for a minimum of 2-3 months after the leak is resolved.

evaporate.

presuming that there is no timber damage to wall / floor timbers, wall
sheeting / render. If found, a further quote will be provided for repairs.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 15.

5/12 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 15 and found water damage in the laundry and living room ceiling.

Used moisture meter to confirm high readings of moisture indicating a leak.

Gained access into unit 19 above, inspected the laundry and no obvious leaks were found. Carried out pressure testing, flood dye testing, ran washing machine in unit 19 and no leak below.

We left a note on unit 20’s door and collected their contact details to return and undertake further testing.

12/12 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 20 and carried out investigation works in the laundry. Tested washing machine and laundry tub waste, no leaks were found.
Located water on the laundry floor around the floor waste. Found the hot water heater relief valve to discharge over the top of the floor grate but not into the pipework causing puddle on the laundry floor tiles.
Extended the relief drain hose down into the floor waste to allow the laundry floor tiles to dry.

17/12 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 15, used the moisture meter/ thermal image camera and found the water damaged ceiling has not dried and the leak is still active.
Gained access into unit 20, cut holes in the common service riser to confirm the leak is not located in unit 20 or the service riser indicating the leak is coming form unit 19.

5/1 - Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection to carry out further investigation works and testing in units 15 and 19.
Gained access into unit 15, used moisture meter and thermal image camera to locate high readings of moisture within the lounge room ceiling, cornice and wall.
Gained access to unit 19 above, isolated the water supply, used nitrogen to pressure test hot and cold pipework.
Following extensive pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 19.
Used pipe locator to mark out and locate the hot water service to run within the concrete slab and walls in unit 19.
Used listening device and leak detector to locate the highest readings of the burst hot water pipe to be located within the laundry wall.

14/1 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 19 and excavated a hole in the common laundry wall exposing the common hot water pipework.
Carried out further testing and located the burst common hot water pipework to be located within the concrete slab and not within the common laundry wall.
Whilst the laundry wall was open and the water leak exposed, we carried out extensive dye testing in unit 19's original shower recess and no dye was found to to be leaking.
As the burst pipe is located within the concrete slab, we are unable to pin point the location to undertake repairs and an urgent hot water re-run is required deleting the burst hot water pipe within the concrete slab to rectify the leak.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 19 - We advise to re-run a new hot water service throughout the ceiling cornice, from the hot water heater in the cupboard to the hot water pipe already exposed in the laundry and from the hot water heater to the bathroom and kitchen, deleting the burst hot water pipework within the concrete slab. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed, we advise the resultant damage repairs and painting works are undertaken in units 15,19 & 20. We will submit a quotation for all resultant damage repairs after we know the full extent of the damage.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish form the property.

Whilst at the property, unit 15 advised of another water leak in the ground floor fire exit where there is pooling water along the wall and floor joint. Video Link  - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-D1W7Z.
CCTV camera surveyed the common stormwater line directly opposite the wall and no faults were found. We investigated this additional leak several times whilst at the building, also when raining and found it not to be a water leak, but water spilled onto the floor.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

sewer blockage and leakage coming through lower basement car park toilet

0447 983 038
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on 6/1/26 - Urgent sewer blockage in the car park

Urgently attended the property after hours at 8:30pm, gained access into the car park and found the common trades toilet to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in the car park.

Removed inspection opening lid on the common sewer stack outside the common toilet, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework upstream from the main boundary trap which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, flow tested common trades toilet and common sewer pipework downstream to boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur in the car park.

Cleaned all areas where sewerage had surcharged in the car park using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to reline the tree root infested sections of common sewer pipework completely sealing the common sewer pipework to prevent further sewer blockages and floods in the car park. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Description:
AFTER HOURS CALL OUT 29/12/25

Water Leaking from Ceiling from Unit 26 to Unit 16 in the laundry
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 29/12/25 - Urgent water leak in unit 16 from unit 26 above

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 16 and found water damage to the laundry ceiling.

Cut a section of the water damaged ceiling, gained access further up service riser and locating a hot water pipe entering the slab. The common hot pipe had water dripping from lagging.

Gained access into unit 26, dye tested laundry waste pipework and common stack and no leaks were found.

Isolated the water supply and carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply. 

Following nitrogen pressure testing, we got a drop on pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe within unit 26.

Cut and removed service riser panel in laundry found the service riser and we were unable to locate the burst hot water pipework.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to locate the burst hot water pipework in unit 26 - We advise to engage pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water supply in unit 26, use listen device and leak detector to pint point the location of the burst hot water pipework.

Temporary covered hole in unit 16, cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

We were advised by the strata manager Gary, the owners corporation will be engaging another contractor to locate and rectify the water leak.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common storm water pipework

Following the recent common storm water clear out works and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree roots entering the original earthenware sewer pipework for approximately 6 meters upstream from the kerb and gutter located under the concrete driveway.

We have cleared out all tree roots with the use of high pressure jet blaster and the storm water line is flowing, but if repairs are not undertaken the tree roots will grow back and cause further blockages.

This quotation is to reline approximately 6 meters of tree root infested and dislodged earthenware storm water pipework upstream from the kerb and gutter located under the concrete driveway, sealing all root infested and dislodged joints finishing reline back onto PVC pipework using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Barricade around work area at the front of the building.
  3. Set up relining equipment in the garden area.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Reline approximately 6 meters of tree root infested and dislodged earthenware storm water pipework upstream from the kerb and gutter located under the concrete driveway, sealing all root infested and dislodged joints finishing reline back onto PVC pipework using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  2. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  7. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  8. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  9. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

Invoice Description:

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 204 and found water flooding in the kitchen causing water damage to the carpet.

Gained access into the hot water plant room located on level 9, urgently shut down the buildings hot water supply and drained the water from the line.

Put notification up on the building advising a 2nd hot water shut down on the 2/1/26, to undertake permanent repairs when the suppliers were back open.

Returned to the property on the 2/1/26, shut down the buildings hot water supply and drained the water from the line.

Excavated a larger section in the common kitchen wall, cut out burst hot water pipework and installed new hot water pipework and fittings connecting onto existing common hot water supply.

Turned on the buildings hot water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 204 - We advise the resultant water damaged common kitchen wall and service riser is repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 204.

We also advise a carpet cleaning contractor is engaged to steam clean or replace the water damaged carpet in unit 204.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Invoice Description:
Investigate pump alarm in the carpark.

Attended the property, gained access into the carpark and found the sewer pit and sewer pumps to be causing the alarm.

Looked at the sewer pump controller and found pump 2 to be faulting.

Switched sewer pumps over to pump 1 and tested on manual which discharged sewer from the pit, indicating pump 1 is working.

Switched sewer pumps over to pump 2 and tested, which caused the alarm. Isolated pump 2 at the controller.

Returned to the property the following day with 2 x plumbers and gatic lifter to access the carpark sewer pit and pumps.

Lifted sewer pit lid, inspected the 2 x pumps and found pump 1 had been replaced with a newer pump.

Tried to disconnect pump 2, but was unable due to the pump out line being blocked.

Disconnected pump 1, removed from the pit, cleaned pump with high pressure hose and confirmed make and model of pump.

Re-set pump 2, tested and confirmed it does not activate and the pump is causing the alarm.

Re- installed pump 1, cleaned pit and pumps using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty sewer pump 2 is replaced with new sewer pump. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework in unit B3

This quotation is to reline approximately 4 meters of collapsed original earthenware sewer pipework at the base of the sewer stack in unit B3 using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin completely sealing the collapsed pipework to prevent further blockages and smells.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise resident of building water shut down.
  2. Gain access into unit B3 and remove panels to gain access to the stack pipe.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera and sanding paddles in preparation for relining.
  4. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.

- Relining:

  1. Reline approximately 4 meters of dislodged cracked earthenware pipework relining from stack opening finishing at gully connection using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  4. Using Robotic cutter, reinstate 3 x junctions located on relined pipework.
  5. Flow test relined pipework after relining.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 6/12/25 - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 3 and common property. 

Urgently attended the property after hours on Saturday, met with the site contact, inspected unit 3 and found all waste fixtures to be blocked.

We found the common sewer pipework for the entire building to be blocked and surcharging raw sewerage at the front of the building.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the front of the building.

Removed inspection opening on the main boundary trap, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the boundary trap, but after multiple attempts were were unable to clear the blockage and our jet blaster equipment was stuck in the common sewer pipework. We were unable to retrieved our jet blasting equipment from the drain and we were removing a large amount of sand and tree roots indicating the common sewer pipework has collapsed. Used pipe locating equipment to locate the tree root infested and broken section of common sewer pipework under the council nature strip at the front of the building.

Returned to the property on Monday 12/8/25 with 2 x plumbers, excavated the ground in the front nature strip exposing the tree root infested common sewer pipework. We located an inspection opening on the common sewer pipework that was buried and was not raised to the surface which gave us access to the common sewer pipework. Removed inspection opening lid and retrieved our jet blasting equipment from the drain via the inspection opening.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads extensively and CCTV drain camera downstream the inspection opening to clear out major tree root infestation entering the common sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage located under the front council nature strip.

Flow tested the common sewer pipework - All clear and in good working order. Please note - If the tree root infested and broken common sewer pipework at the front of the building is not relined, the tree roots will grow back through the broken sewer pipework and further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Bed pipework, backfilled trench, compacted ground and re-instated area. Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further common sewer blockages, we advise the broken and tree root infested section of common sewer pipework at the front of the building is relined, completely sealing the tree root infested common sewer pipework. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Description:
Annual preventative maintenance on the common sewer pipework 

This quotation is to clear out the common sewer pipework at the building using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV on a preventative maintenance program.

Please note, these works were last undertaken n December 2024 and to prevent common sewer blockages we advised the common sewer lines are cleared every 12 months.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access into the car park with 2 x plumbers..
  2. Removed inspection openings on all common cast iron stack pipes within the car park, used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out each branch line to the main sewer line.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster with 2 x mini reels and CCTV drain camera to clear out the entire main line approximately 100 meters of pipework downstream to the boundary trap.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 6.

Returned to the property and found the water leak in unit 6's laundry and kitchen has continued.

Used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water service, which runs in the concrete slab from the kitchen to the laundry.

Used nitrogen to pressure the hot water supply again, used leak detector and listening device to locate the burst pressurized original hot water copper pipe to be located within the concrete slab which is the cause of the leak.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 9 - We advise the hot water pipework within the concrete slab is deleted and a new hot water service is re-run from the heater into the ceiling space over to the laundry service duct connecting laundry and kitchen.  We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 9.

After the plumbing works have been completed in unit 9 and we know the full extent of the resultant damage, we will submit a quotation for all resultant damage repairs and painting works in units 6 & 9.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak outside unit 7 & 8.

Attended the property, gained access and inspected the water leak at the rear of the property outside unit 7 & 8.

We located water leaking out of the ground into the stormwater pit at the walkway stairs.

Traced water leak back to unit 7’s water meter in the garden bed and found there to be a loud hissing noise coming from the mains cold water pipework.

Inspected the water meter for unit 7 and found it was not ticking over, indicating no leaks from unit 7’s cold water line.

Excavated the garden bed around unit 7's water meter and found the soil to be dry indicating the burst cold water pipe is located on the mains water supply before the meter.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, traced out cold water mains pipework and found it to be located behind the boundary retaining wall.

Used pipe locating equipment, leak detector and listening devise to pin point a burst common cold water pipe behind the retaining wall alongside the common walkway.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to saw cut and excavate the retaining wall and ground next to the walkway and stairs outside unit 7 & 8, turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line, cut out burst cold water copper pipework, install new section of cold water copper pipework and fittings, turn on the buildings water supply and test all works carried out. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once the burst pipe is repaired, we advise a building contractor is engaged by the strata to re-instate the retaining wall along the walkway.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Blocked sewer on the left side entrance walkway.

Urgently attended the property and found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the overflow gully located on the left side entrance pathway.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the blocked sewer gully.

Reinstalled inspection opening lid on the common sewer pipework and flow tested with the high pressure hose - All in good working order. Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify common sewer blockages at the property, we advise the affected areas of common sewer are relined. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed these works with our relining team.

Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent emergency sewer blockage we cleared in unit 7 and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree roots infestations entering the original eartanawere sewer pipework downstream from the toilet approximately and major tree roots entering the junction where the branch line meets the main sewer line.

This quotation is to disconnect and remove the toilet, reline approximately 2 to 3 metes of tree root infested original eartanawere sewer pipework downstream the toilet using a watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. Also to install satellite junction repair where main line connects unit 7's branch line completely sealing the entre junction using a watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin, re-install existing toilet and flow test all works carried out.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Lay drop sheets in unit 7.
  2. Disconnect and remove toilet.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  4. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  5. Set up relining equipment in unit 7's bathroom.
  6. Measure, cut and prepare new liner
  7. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.

  10. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  11. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  12. Re-install existing toilet sealing to the ground and flow test all works carried out.
  13. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  14. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

Description:
Urgent amended quotation - Common sewer excavation and relining works

Following the recent common sewer blockage, we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework in 3 x separate locations on the right hand side of the property. Tree roots were found entering the main earthenware sewer line outside unit 2, tree roots entering the main earthenware boundary trap inlet and major tree roots entering unit 3's common branch line connecting the bathroom which was previously quoted to rectify.

Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DQ3HQ

This urgent quotation is to reline complete boundary trap junction feeding entire apartment block installing 150mm x 150m x 45 degree junction reline, reline approximately 4 meters of tree root infested earthenware sewer mainline outside unit 2 and to excavate and replace unit 3's tree root infested branch line with new PVC pipework and fittings.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Set up relining equipment outside unit 2.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  6. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  7. Reline complete boundary trap junction feeding complete apartment block. Install 150mm x 150mm x 45 degree junction reline. Relining from boundary trap shaft into apartment connecting sealing all heavily root infested joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  8. Reline approximately 4 meters of the sewer mainline outside unit 2. Reining over multiple root infested sections on mainline in-between vertical dropper and unit 2 completely sealing joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  9. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  10. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  11. Excavate the ground in the common area on the right hand side of the building outside unit 3.
  12. Cut out tree root infested common earthenware sewer branch line and junction connecting unit 3's bathroom.
  13. Supply and install new PVC pipework, fittings, junction and inspection opening connecting onto existing common sewer pipework.
  14. Flow test all works carried out.
  15. Bed pipework, backfill trench and reinstate common area.
  16. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  17. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  18. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  19. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  20. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  21. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 3.

Attended the property on the 11/11/25, gained access into unit 3 and found water damage to the gyprock bathroom ceiling. Cut a small hole in the damaged ceiling, inspected the common ceiling cavity and found water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 8 above.

Gained access into unit 8 inspected the renovated bathroom, dye tested the bath waste, toilet and basin pipework. Following extensive dye testing no dye leaked into unit 3 below.

Isolated the hot water supply in unit 8, nitrogen pressure tested the hot water piping and following pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply.

Following nitrogen pressure testing in unit 8, we found the common cold water isolation valve in the kitchen to be faulty, does not completely isolate the water supply and required urgent replacement. 

Put notification up on the building advising a cold water building shut down.

Returned to the property on the 13/11/25, isolated the buildings water supply, gained access into unit 8 and replaced the faulty common cold water isolation valve in the kitchen with new isolation valve. 

Engaged pipe location leak detection to use pipe locator to trace out the hot water supply in unit 8. Following extensive pressure testing in unit 8 on the hot and cold water supply with pipe location leak detection, we found there to be no drop in pressure on the hot or cold water supply and consider the drop in pressure on the hot water supply to be an expansion leak.

Gained access into unit 3 and found the leak has not returned since previous investigation works.

In unit 8's bathroom we found missing sealant where the bath meets the wall tiles. Water can be tracking behind the bath seals when the occupants are using the shower/bath. Further works required to be undertaken at the lot owners cost in unit 8 - We advise the lot owner engages their own contractor to re-seal where the bath meets the wall tiles using high grade flexible sealant.

After unit 8 have undertaken the re-sealing works, we advise the bathroom ceiling in unit 3 is monitored. If no further water is found to be leaking in unit 3, we advise a painting contractor is engaged to repair and paint the resultant water damaged bathroom ceiling in unit 3.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate burst fire service in the driveway.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into the common driveway garages and found there to be a burst 100mm copper fire sprinkler pipe directly above the garage roller door.

Set up step ladder and installed a clamp over the pipe to try and stop the leak.

When the roller door is opened and closed, it touches the 2 x fire service pipes as there is damage to the door and the door has been installed too close to the pipework.

We were unable to get a temporary clamp on the burst sprinkler service and the roller door was required to be removed.

Rang the fire service contractor for the building and he advised there was no isolation valve for the sprinkler service.

Returned to the property the following day and met with the garage door contractor who removed the roller door.

Went to the supplier and picked up a large 100mm stainless steel specialized clamp which is the only clamp that can be used for the temporary repair as the pipework is misshaped and damaged. 

Installed 100mm stainless steel temporary clamp over the burst pipe to stop the leak and prevent any serious damage to common property.

Once we inspected both the fire service pipes after the roller door was removed, we found damage has also been caused to the hydrant service pipework which could burst at any time. 

Returned to the property and met with the buildings fire contractors who turned off the fire alarm.

Isolated the buildings water supply and found that does not isolate the fire service.

Isolated the path valve across the street and found that the path valve isolates both the fire hydrant and sprinkler fire service.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise both the damaged hydrant and burst sprinkler service pipes are cut out and replaced with new copper pipe and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once the repairs have been completed, we advise a new roller door is installed up to 50mm lower that the ceiling pipework to prevent further damage.

We advise the strata engages a roofing contractor to gain access onto the roof and see if there are any faults or dead animals that could be causing a smell above the laundry.

URGENT Quotation - Common sewer repairs in 2 x locations.

Following the water leak in unit 3's garage, we found the common sewer line to collapsed in the garden causing blockages, surcharging and sewer leaks. Also whilst undertaking a CCTV camera survey of the common sewer mainline, we found there to be a large brick stuck in the sewer, both affected common sewer pipes urgently required to be excavated and replaced.

Please note: Unit 3's garage pipework is currently blocked and surcharging sewerage, also the large brick will cause major blockages on the mainline if urgent repairs are not undertaken.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Part A - Collapsed sewer pipe within the garden outside unit 3's garage.
  1. Advised residents of building water shut down whilst the sewer repairs are being undertaken.
  2. Set up barricades around areas of works at the side of the building adjacent to unit 3's garage.
  3. Lay drop sheets and tarps next to areas of works.
  4. Remove any garden plant that will be in the way of dig up and store in tubs and buckets
  5. Excavate the garden bed approximately 1.2 meters deep exposing collapsed section of original earthenware sewer pipework.
  6. Shutdown building water supply and drain the water from the line.
  7. Cut out collapsed section of earthenware sewer pipework.
  8. Supply and install new PVC pipe and fittings connecting onto existing common sewer pipework.
  9. Camera CCTV up and downstream and ensure all clear.
  10. Concrete surround around PVC to earthenware connections.
  11. Flow test all works carried out.
  12. Bed pipework backfill trench and compact as per AS-3500
  13. Re-instate common garden area as best as possible.
  14. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  15. Remove associated rubbish, materials and barricades from the property.

Total cost of works for Part A - $7,850.00 Plus GST

  8. Supply and install new PVC pipe and fittings connecting onto existing common sewer pipework.

  11. Flow test all works carried out.
  12. Bed pipework backfill trench and compact as per AS-3500
  13. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  14. Remove associated rubbish, materials and barricades from the property.

Total cost of works for Part B - $6,450.00 plus GST

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 8/11/25 - Urgent common sewer blockage

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage at the rear of the property.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the rear of the building.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage. Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DO6CW

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested common sewer pipework which is clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, the tree roots will grown back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where sewerage had flooded using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline complete root infested boundary trap sewer line, relining from newly installed plastic pipework located at ground level 4-5 meters downstream finishing at Sydney waters main sewer connection, sealing all root infested cracked and leaking earthenware joints using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin and using robotic cutter reinstate all junctions located on boundary trap shaft. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage on the left hand side of the building.

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked on the left hand side of the building and flooding sewerage onto the street.

Removed inspection opening lid on the boundary trap and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked. 

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment to the rear of the building.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream of the boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework to prevent further sewer surcharging. 

Used CCTV drain camera and located major tree roots entering the base of the original earthenware boundary trap and outlet pipework downstream before the vertical shaft connection to Sydney Waters main. Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DOATS

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out as many tree roots as possible on the outlet of the boundary trap to connection before Sydney Waters main. 

Used pipe locater to locate the top of the vertical shaft in the neighboring property at 61 Abbotsford Rd, Used CCTV drain camera from the vertical shaft and located major tree roots entering the original earthenware pipework in multiple sections within Sydney Waters main. Please see CCTV video link of tree root within Sydney Water sewer pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DOA4U

Flow tested the boundary trap and outlet pipework which is clear and getting away. Please note, if the tree root infested original outlet pipework is not relined, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

We contacted Sydney Water emergency and spoke with the case manager Charles, who advised Sydney Water will send out their crew to CCTV camera survey their sewer main and clear out the tree roots to prevent further blockages.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further common sewer blockages, we advise to reline the tree root infested original earthenware boundary trap and outlet pipework, sealing all tree root infested pipework. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team. 

Please note - We found the neighboring property trees and roots systems at 64-66 Burlington Rd and 61 Abbotsford Rd are causing constant sewer blockages within 68-70 Burlington Rd. We advise an Arborist is engaged by the strata to investigate removal of the trees.

Walked around the property and found all the common stormwater drains, pits, downpipes and gutter pipes to be completely blocked with tree roots, dirt and debris on both sides of the property, front to back.

Removed pit lids and grated drain lids in the driveway and found all pits and grated drains to be full of dirt and debris. Cleared out a large amount of dirt and debris from stormwater pits and grated drains in the driveway.

CCTV camera survey the stormwater piping on the driveway side from the outlet of the pits and found large tree root infestations within the original pipework.

Set up high pressure water jet blasting truck and equipment and carried out clear out works on the driveway stormwater line using the high pressure water jet blaster. Due to the size and amount of tree roots within the pipework on the driveway side, we were unable to clear out the stormwater on the left side of the property.

Returned to the property the following day with the engaged contractor with large jet blasting truck and large tree root cutting heads and equipment.

Using the large tree root cutting heads, we were able to clear out the left side stormwater line under the driveway from the curb and gutter in the street to the pit located behind the boundary fence, then from the front pit to the middle, rear driveway pit.

Upstream of the middle, rear pit we located a large collapse in the stormwater line, where the driveway concrete slab has shifted downwards. To rectify the collapsed pipework, the entire 3m x 3m concrete slab will need to be excavated, stormwater pipework repaired then the entire slab re-poured with rio bars and steel tied into surrounding slab to prevent dropping. Please see video link CCTV camera survey - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DOUGO

Cleared out all left side, downpipe branch lines using the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV camera to the common stormwater pits.

Following our CCTTV camera survey of the stormwater line on the left side, we found tree roots to be entering the system through faults and cracks in the bricked stormwater pits. To prevent further tree roots growing in the common stormwater line on the left side of the property under the driveway, we advise all 3x  bricked stormwater pits are excavated and replaced with GRC concrete pits. 

Inspected the stormwater line on the right side of the property from the 3 x downpipes connections and the street curb and found it to be completely blocked with large amounts of tree roots and soil blocking the entire pipework. This quotation is to carry out preventative maintenance water jet blasting and CCTV camera survey works clearing out tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework on the left, right and rear of the property.

Please note, the clear out works on the common sewer pipework were last undertaken on the 5th May 2025 and as tree root infestations are entering the common sewer pipework in multiple locations, we advise these clear out works are undertaken every 6 months to prevent sewer blockages. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Remove inspection opening lids on the left, right and rear of the property. 
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree roots from the common sewer pipework on the left, right and rear of the property. 
  3. Use CCTV drain camera survey to ensure all tree root infestations have been cut out of the sewer piping.
  4. Use high pressure water jet blaster to clear out the congealed fat from the over flow relief gullies. 
  5. Flow test sewer piping and ensure all clear and in good working order.
  6. Reinstall inspection opening lids and clean all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property to continue investigation to locate the cause of the water leak into unit 106.

Gained access into unit 206, lay drop sheets and excavated a hole in the common wall near the front door to access the void.

Following our inspection in the void we found water to be leaking through the common wall adjoining unit 205's bathroom.

Gained access into unit 205 and inspected the recently renovated bathroom.

Flood dye tested shower, toilet and basin and no leaks were found.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. Following pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 205.

Returned to the property and engaged pipe location leak detection in unit 205.

Used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water supply in the bathroom, used listening device and leak detector to locate the burst hot water pipe to be located within unit 205's common shower wall. The burst hot water pipe located within the common wall is the cause of the water leak into unit 106 below. 

Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DO1PF

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To rectify the burst hot water copper pipework in unit 205, we advise to excavate affected common shower wall tiles and brick wall, turn off the hot water supply, cut out burst hot water pipework, install new copper pipework and fittings, turn on the water supply and test all works carried out. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 205.

PART  B - Common relining sewer repairs under unit 1's bathroom.

Job completed as per variation quotation number 27537 to remove toilet, clean sewer line with jet blaster, use robotic cutting equipment to remove all plastic defected pipework and tree roots causing pipe defects, relining approximately 8 meters from newly installed plastic pipework outside covering all cracked sections finishing reline at furthest toilet connection.

The following works were undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Gain access into unit 1, lay drop sheets in the bathroom and disconnect toilet.
  2. Barricade around work area and set up relining equipment
  3. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.

  5. Install 100x100x45 satellite junction relining from relined mainline into junction branch-line using structural fibre glass liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

  7. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  8. Re-install toilet, clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

  3. Also to reline approximately 1 meter of root infested branch-line in front of the garages, relining from plastic inspection point 1 meter downstream covering root infested material change using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate common sewer blockage between units 14, 15, 16 and carry out the free annual inspection of the relined section we installed in 2022 and report on the condition.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 15 and found the toilet to be blocked.

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer pipework outside and found the common sewer line to be blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework downstream from relining works we undertook in 2022.

Following our camera survey we have found multiple cracks and dislodgement's that are letting major tree roots into the mainline. This mainline picks up units 1 to 16 and is located in front of units 14,15 and 16 before heading to the boundary shaft. Please see CCTV video link showing major tree roots in the common sewer pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DOWW5

Flow tested all fixtures in unit 15 and common sewer pipework outside - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested sewer pipework is not repaired, further sewer blockages will re-occur.

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the relining works undertaken in 2022, which are in good working order and no faults were found,.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to Reline approximately 14 meters of 100-150mm tree root infested cracked earthenware pipework which is located under the front gardens of units 14,15 and 16. Relining from previously relined section on mainline (U15 Junction connection) downstream covering all root infested and cracked joints finishing back onto earthenware using watermarked approved liner and 2 part epoxy resin and using robotic cutter reinstate 4 junction on mainline. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

CCTV camera survey 4 x common roof downpipes at the property.

Attended the property, gained access to the roof and met with the site contact Glen.

We also found overhanging trees, which are dropping large amounts of leaves causing blockages in the downpipe sumps where mesh is installed. - We advise an arborist is engaged by the strata to cut back and remove all overhanging tree branches on the roof.

There are no overflow drains on the roof and when the downpipe sumps block up with leaves, water easily pools on the roof causing flooding. - We advise overflow spigot drains are installed in the roof to prevent flooding prior to waterproofing repair works.

CCTV camera surveyed the back left, square copper downpipe and located a tea tow stuck in the downpipe, 2 x holes approximately 2 meters down from the roof and holes in the copper downpipe sump connection. Please see CCTV video link:

- https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DX5D9

CCTV camera surveyed the front left 50mm galvanised steel downpipe and located rust holes in the metal downpipe sump connection, the galvansied steel downpipe is rusted internally and there are 2 x junction connections 4.5m & 7m down from the roof. Please see CCTV video link:

- https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DX5BZ

CCTV camera surveyed the back right 50mm PVC downpipe and located a large crack within the flanged sump connection. Please see CCTV video link:

- https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DX5BI

CCTV camera surveyed the front right 50mm galvanised steel downpipe and found the galvansied steel downpipe is rusted internally and there are 3 x junction connections 1.5, 4.5m & 7m down from the roof.

- https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DX5BW 

After inspecting all roof downpipes, we found leaves and debris within the pipework at the base.

Further investigation works are required to gain access into the top level units, remove access panels and inspect pipework on all 4 x downpipes where it goes through the roof slab to provide an accurate quotation to replace pipework and sump connections prior to waterproofing repairs. We are required to return to the property with our relining team to provide an accurate quotation for the relining of all internal downpipes and balcony branch line drains. Also prevent leaves from blocking the downpipe sumps, we advise to measure and source 4 x new sump mesh dome covers and install following downpipe repair works. We will provide a quotation shortly for the further investigation works required to be undertaken. 

Whilst at the property we inspected the sewer pumps, unfortunately this is a complicated sewer pump set up and we advise BCS engages a specialist pump contractor such as Prime Water to undertake the sewer pump service works at this property.
