Quotation - Relining works in the common laundry

Following the recent blockage we cleared in the common laundry and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations to be entering the original earthenware sewer pipework under the concrete slab in the laundry.

This quotation is to Install 1.5 meter x 100mm reline from gully upstream to second junction, reinstate 1 x junction, Install 1.5 meter x 100 reline from second junction up to next junction sealing root infested joints an install 2 meter reline from tub connection down to next downstream junction.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Barricade around work area outside the common laundry.

  8. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Further URGENT Works required to be undertaken in unit 4 - To rectify the leak, we advise to disconnect and remove the vanity basin, excavate wall tiles within the common wall exposing the burst cold water pipework, cut out and replace burst pipe with new pipe and fittings, turn the water supply back on testing all works.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 7.

Picked up keys from the managing agent, attended the property and gained access into unit 7.

Located water damage to the internal bedroom wall, skirting, bedroom floors, bathroom ceiling and kitchen floors.

  • Internal bedroom wall and bedroom floor.

Used moisture meter to identify high readings of moisture within the internal bedroom wall and floor substrate.

Carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply for unit 7 and found the common cold water isolation valve did not turn off. Isolated the water supply to the entire building and replaced the common cold water isolation valve for unit 7 on the external wall.

Nitrogen pressure tested the hot and cold water supply and found there to be no drop in pressure indicating no burst pipes in unit 7.

Nitrogen pressure tested the shower breach and found a large drop in pressure. Removed tap coverplates and found water leaking from the cold water shower tap spindle extension within the wall, causing damage to the bedroom walls and floors.

Removed tap spindles and repaired the leak by servicing the cold water shower tap, fibre washers and installing the tap and extension correctly. Carried out further nitrogen pressure testing and no further leaks were found.

Blocked off the shower floor drain and flood/ dye tested the shower recess. Following dye testing of the shower recess, no dye was found to be leaking.

We found the leaking cold water shower tap to be causing the water damage to the internal bedroom wall, skirting and floors.

  • Bathroom ceiling

Used moisture meter within the bathroom ceiling and found there to be no moisture readings, indicating no leaks.

We found the mould within the bathroom ceiling to be caused by poor ventilation when showering and the damaged ceiling to be poor repair and painting works.

  • Kitchen flooring

Inspected the kitchen flooring and found it has buckled and lifted in front of the dishwasher. Used moisture meter to identify no moisture within the concrete substrate.

Carried out extensive testing in the kitchen, tested all appliances, flood tested the kitchen sink waste, pressure tested hot and cold water supply and no leaks were found.

As there was no moisture within the kitchen flooring and no leaks within the kitchen plumbing, we found the damaged kitchen flooring to be caused by a previous leak and the flooring has not been repaired.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 7 by a building contractor -  We advise the bedroom wall and skirting adjacent to the shower recess is repaired and painted, the floating floorboards in the bedroom and kitchen are replaced and the bathroom ceiling is cleaned of mould, damaged gyprock ceiling repaired and the entire bathroom ceiling painted with mould resistant paint.

Returned keys to the managing agent, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked common sewer located under fire stairs.

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging out of the overflow gully located under the fire stairs. We also located a 2nd separate blockage in the common laundry.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream the overflow gully under the stairs to clear out a large amount of congealed fat from the common sewer pipework.

Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the tee junction connecting the blocked gully is faulty as hasn't been correctly reinstated on the relined section on the main line recently undertaken by anther plumber. This junction has only cut out approximately 30% and will need to be cut out further and reinstated properly to allow correct flow (photo attached). We advise the plumbing contractor who undertook the recent relining works returns to the property to re-instate the tee junction correctly to allow the sewer pipework to flow freely.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera, downstream the common external laundry waste pipework to clear out tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework in the ground which was the cause of the 2nd separate blockage. Video Link of tree roots - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DXKPX

Flow tested overflow gully, main line and laundry waste pipework - All clear and in good working order.

Further works required to be undertaken  - To prevent further blockages in the common laundry, we advise to reline the complete laundry line, relining from laundry connection ( above ground) 2-3 meters downstream covering all root infested joints finishing at gully inlet using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Invoice Description:
Investigate no hot water to the building.

Urgently attended the property on the 7/10 at 3.00pm, gained access into the buildings hot water plant room and found no hot water to the building.

The Rinnai hot water heater was faulting with the error code 12 indicating flame failure.

Disconnected water and power supply to the heater, disconnected and removed flame rods. Cleaned flame rods and re-installed, also removed water filter and cleaned.

Reconnected water and power supply to the Rinnai heater and tested. Rinnai heater found to be running for 5 minutes then faulting with error code 10, indicating a fault with the flue.

Inspected the flue and found no blockages. Removed outer flue layer - air intake. Re-set Rinnai heater and found no further fault codes indicating a fault with the flue.

Heater now up to temperature providing hot water to the building.

Returned to the property on the 9/10 and met with Rinnai Service technician. Rinnai Service Team carried out a full service of the hot water unit.

Internal combustion fan was completely blocked, replaced combustion fan, internal unit and combustion chamber was dirty causing obstructions, cleaned internal unit and combustion chamber, removing dirt. Serviced flame rods and relaced flame rod washers.

Re-connected flue piping and secured flue to the ceiling by fixing brackets.

Urgently returned to the property after hours on the 14/10 at 5.00pm, gained access and found no hot water to one of the units.

Inspected the Rinnai hot water heater and found it to be at working temperature 75 degrees. Carried out further investigations and found hot water return line to be cold. Removed return line pump, ran water flow bleeding air from the line. Tested and found the return line up to temperature.

Returned to the property on the 15/10, 8.00 am and found the return line pipework to be warm. Removed pump, ran water flow and there was no air in the line.

Following 2 x separate hot water outages within a few days, we found the Rinnai hot water heater required a complete service, the return line circulation pump is inadequate circulating cold/warm water throughout the building, and the Rinnai hot water heater flue is too long, according to the manufactures specifications.  

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further hot water outages at the building we advise a hot water specialist such as Paul Read or Cervas hot water is engaged to provide an URGENT quotation to completely upgrade the entire hot water plant and equipment at the building.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place

Description:
Urgent variation quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

After completing the quoted relining works we undertook a CCTV camera survey to inspect the common sewer pipework. Following our CCTV camera survey we located the base of the original cast iron sewer stack connecting unit 3's kitchen above to be completely collapsed causing waste water to leak under the subfloor under unit 1.

This section of collapsed pipework is located on a separate section of pipework to the relining works undertaken.

This urgent quotation is gain access to the broken 80mm stack from above unit 3's kitchen and remove rust as much as possible in preparation for relining, install 100mm x 100mm x 45 degree satellite junction repair to give additional length and strength too the junction arm and reline 2 meters from satellite junction repair onto existing common cast iron stack, using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise affected units to not use there waste fixtures.
  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Set up relining equipment.
  4. Gain access into unit 3, clean all sewer pipework with drain cleaning equipment, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Install 100mm x 100mm x 45 degree satellite junction repair to give additional length and strength too the arm using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Install 2 meter section pipe reline repair from the satellite junction repair onto existing cast iron common stack pipework using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  4. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  9. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  10. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  11. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Urgently attended the property gained access to the right side of the property and found the common sewer surcharge gully had overflowed outside unit 2.

Lifted the lid on the common sewer gully and located tree roots at the inlet side of the gully. Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment up to the right side of the building.

Cut out a section of the cast iron sewer stack and used the jet blaster downstream to clear out the inlet pipework to the affected overflow gully. The overflow gully was partially getting away but still blocked. We were unable to clear out the major tree roots from the base of the earthenware gully.

Following extensive jet blasting, we were unable to clear the tree root blockage on the main line without access into unit 2. 

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access into unit 2 and set up jet blasting equipment.

Disconnected the toilet, carried out CCTV camera survey and found a section of the branch line to the main line has been previously relined and no faults were found. We located tree roots entering the mainline, approximately 5 meters upstream from the boundary trap.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Re-installed toilet, flow tested branch line and the main line downstream to the boundary trap which is clear and in good working order.

Flow tested the overflow gully and still found the gully to be partially blocked. After extensive jet blasting we were unable to completely clear the tree roots entering the base of common overflow sewer gully earthenware inlet pipework. Further urgent works are required to excavate and replace with new PVC pipework and fittings to rectify the blockage.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to saw cut and excavate the the concrete slab, excavate the ground approximately 1.3 meters deep, cut out tree root infested original earthenware sewer gully, use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear the inlet and outlet of the gully, install new PVC gully, pipework, fittings and inspection opening raised to the surface for future drain cleaning access, flow test all works, bed pipework, backfill trench, compact ground and re-instate concrete. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further common sewer repairs required to be undertaken.

Please note - There is an air-conditioning unit right next to where the excavation works are required to be undertaken.  Before the excavation works take place, an air- condition contractor will be required to be engaged by the strata manager to disconnect and remove the air-condition unit and return to reinstall the air-condition unit after the works have been completed.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on 23/9/25 - Urgent water leak in unit 13 and separate water leak outside the garages

Urgently attended the property at 8:00pm, gained in unit 13 and found 4 x separate water leaks in the lounge room, bedroom and kitchen.

Following our inspection, we found water damage and swollen skirting board around the floor adjacent balcony below the A/C unit.  Water damage to the common wall in bedroom below window sill, kitchen window sill leaks during heavy rain and the common wall along that shares the balcony wall is damp. Used thermal image camera to locate high readings of moisture within the wall in all these 4 x areas. 

We were unable to gain access into unit 15 on our inspection.

Returned to the property on 29/9/25, gained access into units 15 to carry out further testing and investigation works. 

Found that in heavy downpours, unit 15's bedroom floods causing the carpet to be saturated for days. There is also signs of a water leak in unit 15’s lounge room.

Gained access onto the roof, found cracked pointing on the back of the tiles and a missing flashing. Found missing flashing where the gutter wraps around the roof.

Dye tested unit 15’s balcony and following dye testing a leak was detected coming into unit 13’s balcony running down the downpipe penetrations.

Found that there is a missing flashing where the brickwork meets the slab on each level. This is causing the brick cavity to fill up with water and eventually leak out onto the walls of unit 15 and 13.

Found that they have installed flashings on the right side of the building showing that they’ve had similar issues in the past.

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak into unit 13 - We advise GK strata engages a building contractor to carry out the below repairs:

1. Repair cracked and missing pointing on the back of the roof tiles, and install missing flashings.

2. Install missing flashing where the gutter meets the tiles.

3. Unit 15 balcony waterproofing has failed around pipe penetrations and waterproofing repairs are required.

4. Missing Damp proof flashing along the left side of building.

Investigate separate water leak in front of the garages. Following our inspection, we found a leaking section of common storm water pipework in the garage and found a cracked 90mm PVC square junction that requires urgent repairs. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the cracked and leaking common storm water pipework and junction is cut out and replace with new PVC pipework and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer leak down the common staircase which leads to the road.

Urgently attended the property at 1:30pm, found the common sewer pipework for the building to be blocked, leaking sewerage down the common staircase to the road and into the garage below.

Removed inspection opening lid outside unit 2 and found the common sewer pipework in this area to have been previously been relined by another contractor.  The previous contractors relined straight through the inspection opening and there was no access to gain into the main sewer line outside unit 2.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively upstream the boundary trap but after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage.

Cut out the base of the sewer stack outside unit 2, install new PVC inspection opening and pipework to gain access to the common sewer pipework.

Engaged 2nd plumber, returned the property at 5:00pm, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment outside unit 2.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework. Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree roots entering the common sewer pipework downstream towards the boundary trap and also the tree roots have caused the pipework to crush and squash - Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DQCNG

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested sewer pipework from outside unit 2 downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested and crushed sewer pipework is not repaired, further sewer blockages will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline the tree root infested and crushed common sewer pipework completely sealing the pipework to prevent further blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage at the rear of the property.

Urgently attended the property at 3:00pm on the 25/9/25, found the outlet of the boundary trap for the building to be blocked and surcharging sewerage on the grass area and concrete to the footpath. Please note, the blocked boundary trap is located on the other side of the building to the recent relining and sewer upgrade works undertaken.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment to the rear of the building.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the outlet of the 150mm boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework to prevent further sewer surcharging. 

Used CCTV drain camera and located major tree roots entering the original earthenware pipework on the 225mm vertical connection before Sydney Waters side line connection.

Returned to the property the following day on the 26/9/25 with large jet blaster truck, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out as many tree roots as possible on the outlet of the boundary trap to the 225mm vertical connection before Sydney Waters side line. Please see CCTV video link of tree root entering the sewer pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DQQY1

Flow tested the boundary trap and outlet pipework which is clear and getting away. Please note, if the tree root infested original outlet pipework is not relined, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

We contact Sydney Water emergency who attended the property on Friday night 26/9/25 and cleared out the tree roots and debris from there side line. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further common sewer blockages, we advise to reline approximately 2 meters of root infested earthenware vertical shaft, relining from Sydney main sewer connection 2 meters upstream finishing reline at ground level using Watermarked approved 225 mm liner with 2 part epoxy resin and using Robotic cutter reinstate 1 junction picking up building connection. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Investigate water leak in unit 1 from unit 7 above.Picked up keys for unit 7 from the managing agent,  attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found a large amount of mould on the bedroom concrete ceilings, cornice and external bedroom wall edges low down. Also small

amount has started in the living room ceiling and the bathroom has been cleaned.

Used moisture meter to identify medium levels of moisture indicating dampness in the concrete ceiling slab.

Inspected the bathroom and found no plumbing issues, seals and tiles in the shower are in good conditions. No leaks were found. 

Inspected outside to inspect the external brick walls. Following our inspection, we located a tiled roof cavity above both bedrooms and the bathroom. Until 7 is not directly above.

The roof cavity is above the larger mould growth in into 1 where the concrete ceiling drops down.

Inspected and found faulty flashing and gaps where water can leak into the roof space cavity and onto the concrete slab, transferring moisture to unto 1 below. 

Further works required to be undertaken on the roof - We advise GK Strata engages a roofing contractor to inspect the small tiled roof and flashings above unit 1’s bedrooms and undertake repairs to prevent water entering the roof cavity through holes and faulty flashings. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - We advise a mould cleaning specialist is engaged to clean and remove all the mould within unit 1, then the ceiling and affected walls are sealed and painted with mould resistant paint. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and returned keys to the managing agent.

Description:
Please attend 96 Hall St, Bondi ASAP. Unit 2 is experiencing a serious plumbing issue in their bathroom. The water does not drain properly when we take a shower, which causes the entire bathroom to flood. The second drain outside the shower also does not work, so the water flows out into the room. Sometimes water even rises up from this drain while we are showering.
In addition, the toilet is affected. The water level in the toilet bowl rises, and flushing only makes it worse. During these times, the toilet cannot be used at all. The sink is also impacted - after showering, the water in the sink does not drain, and it takes hours before we can use the sink or toilet again.
We also notice frequent bubbling and gurgling sounds from the toilet, especially after using it.
Also, the other toilet is now blocked and cannot be used.

Site contact is the agent.
Cornell - 0433 997 801
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 2.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 2, inspected the en-suite bathroom and found the toilet, shower, basin and floor waste to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage when in use.

The owners have added a 2nd bathroom in the bedroom. 

Used drain cleaning equipment downstream the floor waste and toilet but we were unable to clear the blockage in the common sewer pipework.

Gained access under unit 2, inspected unit 2's drainage and found there is no inspection openings or access to the common sewer pipework.

Disconnected and removed toilet in the en-suite bathroom to access the common sewer pipework.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in unit 2's en-suite bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage approximately 5 meters downstream from the toilet. CCTV video link  https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DQE8Z

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree roots entering the original earthenware sewer pipework.

Re-installed existing toilet, flow tested toilet, shower, basin and floor waste - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages in unit 2 - We advise to remove the toilet in the en-suite bathroom, reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested in ground earthenware sewer pipework approximately 5 meters downstream from the toilet, sealing the tree root infested earthenware pipework, re-install toilet and flow test all works carried out. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

we have cleared before and used CCTV but no faults were found.

Please investigate further

Also water leak into unit below from shower waste and slab
Invoice Description:
Attended the property to investigate the shower waste blocking in the main bathroom of 104.

CCTV camera surveyed the shower floor drainage and the floor waste gully drainage. Following our CCTV camera survey, no blockages were found.

Ran the shower and found the drainage is slow to drain the fills up. Went downstairs to unit G02 but was unable to gain access.

Returned to the property and gained access into unit G02 & 104.

Cut a hole in the bathroom ceiling cavity of unit G02 to inspect the common waste piping for the shower and floor waste of unit 104 above. Removed acoustic lagging and found unit 104's bathroom drainage to have correct fall and pipe sizing. 

Ran the shower again in unit 104. Once blocked and full of water, we removed the tiled drain insert and found the water easily drains from the shower floor confirming the tiled floor drain insert is causing the blockage.

Removed tiled drain insert, went to supplier, source, supplied and installed stainless steel shower drain grate lid. Flow tested shower for 15 minutes - All clear and in good working order.

Whilst undertaking investigation works in unit G02, we found there to be a leak from the shower waste penetration and concrete slab soaking the acoustic lagging.

Carried out further testing in unit 104, Flood / dye tested the shower recess and found no water leak into G02's ceiling below.

Removed mixer cover-plate and located a large gap around the mixer and the wall tiles. Following flood testing of the shower wall tiles around the shower mixer, we found water leaked into unit G02 below confirming the leak.

Installed sealant around the shower mixer and behind the cover-plate to prevent further leaking from the shower of unit 104 into unit G02's ceiling below.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit G02 - Investigation works has caused resultant damage to the gyprock ceiling in the bathroom. We advise the buildings painting contractor undertakes repairs and painting works to the hole made in the bathroom ceiling. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property to clear blocked common sewer pipework adjacent to the visitors car park.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where sewerage had surcharged using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

We advise a notice is sent to all residents at the building advising to not pour oil down the kitchen sinks to prevent further common sewer blockages.

Description: BLOCKAGE AT THE REAR OF THE BUILDING
Invoice Description:
Investigate common sewer blockage at the rear of the building.

Attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the overflow sewer gully at the right rear of the building.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck in no stopping zone and set up equipment.  

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out bottles, plastic bags and congealed fat from the base of the gully and common sewer which was the cause of the common sewer blockage/flood.

Flow tested the overflow gully and common sewer pipework downstream - All clear and in good working order.

Used the Venturi pump to clean areas  of sewerage that had flooded around the gully, disinfectant and high-pressure hose to remove any leftover grease stuck to the floor. Repeated this process several times to clean areas of works.

We advise a notice is sent to the residents at the building advising to not pour oil down the kitchen sinks to prevent further common sewer blockages and floods.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked and leaking drain at the building driveway entrance on Dangar Street.

Urgently attended the property on 11/9/25, gained access to driveway entrance and found water leaking out of the blocked silt arrestor.

Removed the concrete pit lid and tried pumping out the water with a submersible pump and Venturi pump, but there is too much water we will require to return with more than 1 pump and pump water from the arrestor. 

Returned to the property on the 15/9/25, installed barricades around the silt arrestor and set up submersible pump in the pit pumping out the water from the pit over-night.

Returned to the property on the 16/9/25 after the pit had been pumped out, removed submersible pump from the storm water silt arrestor.

Gained access into the pit and found major tree roots entering the original earthenware inlet and outlet. We also found more than half of the pipe to be blocked with a large amount of sand.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads to clear out as many tree roots as possible from the inlet and outlet to prevent further blockages and floods.

Flow tested the common storm water pit which is clear and flowing.

Please note - There is still a large amount of sand at the base of the pit and within the inlet and outlet pipework of the pit. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DP5EM

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out all sand from the inlet and outlet pipework. Also to clear out all sand from the base of the common storm water pit. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Re-installed pit lid and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework located under unit 1

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found the original earthenware common branch line upstream from the overflow gully under unit 1 to be collapsed and dropped causing sand and debris to enter the pipework.

This urgent quotation is reline approximately 1-2 meters of collapsed and dislodged earthenware pipework, relining from gully inlet upstream covering cracked earthenware joints using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise affected units to not use there kitchen waste.
  2. Barricade around work area outside unit 1.
  3. Set up relining equipment.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 1-2 meters of collapsed and dislodged earthenware pipework, relining from gully inlet upstream covering cracked earthenware joints using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  8. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  9. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  10. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Description: Please attend to the reported blocked drain at the front of the building as per the attached photo.
Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked drain at the front of the building.

Attended the property, found the common storm water drainage at the front right hand side of the of the building to be blocked and surcharging during heavy rain.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the front of the building.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively but after multiple attempts with different jet blasting heads, we were unable to clear the blockage and were only able to get out jet blasting equipment 2 meters downstream under the front of the driveway. Our jet blasting equipment was getting stuck confirming the storm water pipework has collapsed under the concrete.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe location equipment to find the common storm water system for the building to be clear on the left hand side of the building and discharging to the street.

The common storm water pipework has currently collapsed under the front right hand side of the building and requires urgent attention to rectify the blockage.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to notify building of driveway shut down on William St side, saw cut concrete around existing surface drain and then re-run approximately 13 meters to existing clear stormwater on the left side of property, excavate the concrete and ground, supply and install new PVC pipework and fittings from the right hand side to the left hand side of the driveway connecting onto existing common storm water pipework, supply and install new storm water pit, use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear upstream ad downstream, flow test all works carried out, bed pipework, back fill trench and compact using compactor, install steel and re-concrete affected area. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Invoice Description:
Urgently attended the property Friday afternoon 12/9/25, gained access into unit 6 and found the bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked and surcharging out of the floor waste when in use.

Set up electric eel, removed floor waste gully grate and attempted to clear between the outlet of the floor gully and the common branch and common stack pipework, after multiple attempts we were unsuccessful in clearing the blockage and our electric eel cable was starting to kink.

Located the aerial common drainage in the carport below and cut a small hole in the 80mm cast iron pipework to access. Set up jet blasting truck and equipment to clear a large amount of rust in the common cast iron pipework which was the cause of the blockage. Flow tested unit 6’s bathroom fixtures – All clear and in good working order and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Returned to the property on Tuesday 16/9/25, gained access into the car park and cut out faulty section of 80mm cast iron sewer pipework connecting unit 6.

Supplied and install new section of PVC pipework and fittings connecting onto existing common sewer pipework.

Carried out further CCTV camera survey works and found approximately 7 meters of corroded and rusted original 80mm cast iron sewer pipework from the ground level to ceiling that is required to be cut out and replaced with PVC to prevent further sewer blockages.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages - Notify residents of water disruptions, gain access into the car park, cut out approximately 7 meters of corroded and rusted original 80mm cast iron sewer pipework from the ground level to ceiling, install new PVC pipework, fittings, junction, gully and inspection opening for future access, flow test from unit 6, clean all areas where work had taken place. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 1 & 5.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found bubbling paint to the bathroom ceiling bulkhead and access panel above the shower.

Removed the access panel from the ceiling, inspected inside the bulkhead and found it to be dry and no water leaking.

We found the bubbling paint in the bathroom ceiling bulkhead and access panel above the shower to be from moisture when showering and poor painting.

We also found water damage to the internal hallway walls and lifting floorboards in the hallway adjacent to the original shower recess in unit 1.

Nitrogen pressure tested the shower breaching piece and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes.

Blocked off the shower floor drain and flood tested the shower recess wall and floor tiles. Using moisture meter we confirmed faulty waterproof membrane within the original shower recess and first course of wall tiles causing water damage to the internal hallway wall.

We found the floorboards in unit 1's hallway are lifting due to poor installation.

Gained access into unit 5 above and inspected the renovated bathroom, we consider the bathroom has not been "recently' renovated but renovated for some time.

We located bubbling paint to the internal wall in the hallway adjacent to the shower recess.

Blocked of the shower waste and flood dye tested the shower recess, no dye was found to be leaking. Nitrogen pressure tested the shower breaching piece and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes.

Inspected the shower recess and located missing grout within the hob and missing sealant within the shower screen which is causing water to leak int the substrate and outside the shower recess.

Following flood testing in unit 5, we found no water or dye to be leaking into unit 1 below.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - As the waterproof membrane, bathroom floor tiles and first course of wall tiles are original, we advise the shower recess and first course of wall tiles are excavated, re-waterproofed and re-tiled. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 1.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 5 by the lot owner - As the bathroom in unit 5 has been renovated, we advise a re-sealing contractor is engaged by the lot owner to re-grout the shower hob and re-seal the shower screen.

After the repair works have been completed in units 1 & 5, we advise the internal hallway walls are repaired and painted.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property on the 27/8 to investigate water leak in unit 23’s bedroom.

Located the shower recess adjacent to the water damage on the left side bathroom door and bedroom. Carried out investigation and testing works in the shower recess adjacent to the bedroom. 

Nitrogen pressure tested the shower breach, no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes. Flood dye tested the shower recess, used moisture meter to confirm a leak.

Inspected the original, 2 x common and 1 x internal shower wall tiles and located drummy tiles where water is leaking through cracked/missing grout into the substrate and walls.

Returned to the property on Tuesday 9/9, shutdown the building water supply and drained the water from the line.

Cut out small section of cabinetry wall to access the faulty isolation valve, disconnected the leaking common cold water isolation valve and installed new isolation valve. 

Turned the buildings water supply back on testing all works - All in good working order.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken by a building contractor. To rectify the leak in unit 23's bedroom, we advise a building contractor is engaged by the strata to excavate the shower recess, 2 x common and 1 x internal shower wall tiles, install new waterproof membrane and re-tile.

We advise to install an access panel on the cabinetry wall in the bathroom. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 23.

Please accept this work order to carry out a flood test of the courtyard of unit 707 and provide a report

We believe that the waterproofing may have failed
Please contact Fuzz to schedule a time - 0479 144 679
Thanks
Invoice Description:
Flood testing of unit 707's courtyard.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 707 and carried out flood testing investigation works on the upstairs courtyard.

Blocked off all strip drain drainage and flood tested the strip drains, courtyard tiles and waterproof membrane.

Following flood testing on the external courtyard, water leaked into the upstairs bedroom and downstairs kitchen confirming faulty strip drains, sliding doors and waterproof membrane.

Once the strip drain along the bedroom sliding doors was full of water, water filled the internal sliding door track and caused wet carpet in the bedroom indicating the strip drains are not water tight and there are no flashings or seals within the sliding door frames.

We found the internal floor level to be lower (not higher) than the outside tiled floor level and strip drain in the external tiled courtyard. Also there is no hob for the sliding door track to sit on, separating the internal floor and external courtyard.

Video Link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DPRPN

Inspected the courtyard strip drain in the common area adjacent to unit 707 along the sliding doors and located missing sealant and faulty sealant between the tiles, sliding doors and the strip drain, causing water to leak under the tiles and into the substrate/ concrete slab.

We advise a building contractor is engaged by the strata to inspect the courtyard floor levels, strip drains, sliding door frames in unit 707 and the common area adjacent and repairs are undertaken to the waterproof membrane, sliding doors and strip drains on the courtyard level to prevent water leaking internally into unit 707.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 606's bedroom.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 606 and located a damp smell in the bedroom adjacent to the bathroom.

After removing clothes from the bedroom cupboard, we found water damage to the back of cupboard and mould within the internal wall adjacent to the bathroom.

There is also water damage to the floating floorboards in the bedroom at the door and within the wardrobe along the internal wall.

Inspected the bathroom shower recess and located cracked tiles, large amounts of missing wall and floor grout and faulty sealant.

Also the 2 x common show walls are re-grouted and the bath edge along the common wall is re-sealed using high grade flexible sealant. We advise a tiling contractor such as Megasealed is engaged by the strata to undertake these works.

Once all plumbing and tiling repairs are undertaken in the bathroom, we advise the water damaged internal bedroom wall is repaired and painted and the floating floors in the bedroom are replaced.

Investigate water leak in unit 1's bathroom ceiling.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak into the common laundries below the building near the driveway and carparks.

Attended the property, inspected the common laundries and located water coming from the corner of the walls and floor in 2 x locations in separate laundries.

Disconnected sewer lid on the common stack adjacent to the laundry in carpark 3. CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer line and no blockages or collapsed sewer pipes were found.

Monitored the buildings water meter and found it comes to a slow pace almost a stop, indicting a leak from a toilet or tap washers within the building.

Adjacent to the laundry leaks is the retaining wall, grassed area and garden approximately 1.5 meters above floor level. Used moisture meter to identify high readings all the way to the level of the external soil.

Inspected the garden grassed areas and found no stormwater drainage along the external wall. Located the stormwater pit at the bottom picking up the entire roof, 1 x downpipe. The stormwater pit is approximately 800mm deep and there are no agline drainage connected to the pit

Returned to the property on 2 x separate occasions and found the water leak has still not dried up.

Inspected the grass and garden soil on the other side of the laundries and found the soil to still be wet after large amount of rain.

Monitored the buildings water meter on 2 x separate occasions and found it comes to a complete stop indicating no burst pipes.

Further works required to be undertaken by a building contractor - To rectify the leak and prevent further water leaking into the 2 x laundries from the subsoil adjacent to the retaining wall, we advise the soil is excavated along the building down to the base of the wall, aglines are installed connected to the stormwater pit and the external wall is waterproofed, install plastic film, aggregate and geo-tech fabric, backfill compact and re-instate. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place.

Flood tested the shower tray and and located water  leaking out from the shower recess into the hallway and ground floor below, indicating the waterproof membrane in the bathroom has failed.

Located water damage in the first floor bathroom ceiling, went directly above and found the bedroom window.

Inspected the bedroom window and found missing sealant around the window frame on both ends of the window.

Used high grade flexible sealant to re-seal the external window frame to prevent water entering the external wall cavity.

Urgent quotation - Common sewer repairs on the 2nd Boundary trap located on the right side of the property & reline branch line under unit 1's bathroom

Following recent relining works at the building on the left side boundary trap, we undertook a CCTV camera surveyed the second boundary trap located on the right side of the property and found it to be completely full of tree root infestations. We also found the common earthenware branch line upstream the overflow gully under unit 1's bathroom to be badly tree root infested and requires urgent repairs to prevent further sewer blockages in unit 1.

This quotation is to reline from the top of 2nd boundary trap on the right hand side of the building down to vertical shaft inlet just before Sydney Waters main connection, sealing all dislodged earthenware joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin and sing robotic cutter re-instate junction associated with boundary trap. Also to reline approximately 1- 2 meters of bathroom sewer line, relining from gully connection upstream to unit 1 coving all root infested joints, finishing before junction connection using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down during the relining works.
  2. Barricade work area,
  3. Set up relining equipment.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Relining repairs
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline from the top of 2nd boundary trap on the right hand side of the building down to vertical shaft inlet just before Sydney Waters main connection, sealing all dislodged earthenware joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  5. Using robotic cutter re-instate junction associated with boundary trap.
  6. Reline approximately 1- 2 meters of bathroom sewer line, relining from gully connection upstream to unit 1 coving all root infested joints, finishing before junction connection using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  7. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  8. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  9. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  10. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  11. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

committee have request Treat Plumbing attend to inspect both leaks see report from Howards
below:
''Attended the property 16/05/2025 to inspect the leaking pipe on the balcony of U304. Directed to
the area and inspected with the resident - it was raining at this time. Water could be seen leaking
from the penetration where a vertical 100mm PVC bend goes through the concrete slab to the

balcony above, which is part of U304.

edge of the building and collects the roof water from above. Was able to climb over the railing and
inspect around the base of the pipe where water proofing attempts have been made previously.
This is not a leaking pipe but a waterproofing issue. We suggest the builder returns for further
work however, as informed they have made multiple attempts to seal the area.
We recommend 2 men attend with a harness to work on the edge of the building. Remove the
existing water proofing and chop around the penetration and attempt to seal with a water proof
grout, then a water proof membrane. Although it may be obvious that the leak is through the
penetration, the water could be leaking from a crack in the concrete and tracking across to this
penetration. For this reason, we could not guarantee that this will be the solution.''
Thanks,
Cherry

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 13.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 13 and found water leaking from the external wall cavity into the driveway below.

Isolated the hot and cold water supply, carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing and located a drop in pressure on the hot water indicating a leak.

Pulled out dishwasher in the kitchen and found the rendered external wall to be wet at the bottom of the wall..

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, nitrogen tested the hot water and found only a slight loss in pressure.

Traced position of pipework using pipe location equipment and located the copper hot water line in the common kitchen wall behind the cabinetry.

Leak detection advised us to excavate the common kitchen wall where the hot pipe is located to determine if the burst pipe is located in the wall or concrete slab.

Cut out the kitchen cabinetry where the hot water pipework was located, excavated the common wall exposing the hot water pipework. Once exposed, we located a burst hot water tee within the common wall behind the kitchen.

Isolated the hot water supply to unit 13 and attempted to repair the burst pipe using welding equipment. Due to the condition of the pipework we were unable to carry out repairs.

Cut out the burst hot water tee within the wall and connected the hot water supply using fittings and flexible water hose connection as a temporary repair to re-instate the water supply and prevent damage in unit 13.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 13 - We advise to cut out more of the kitchen cabinetry exposing the hot water pipework within the wall, cut out and replace hot water pipework and fittings connecting the kitchen tap and dishwasher. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Following the burst pipe repair works in unit 13, resultant damage was caused to the kitchen cabinets.  Once the repair works are completed and we know the extent of the damage we will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs works required in unit 13.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 117.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 117 and found a large amount of water leaking into the laundry ceiling cavity from the light fitting.

Gained access into unit 123 above and carried out testing in the laundry and bathroom above.

Dyes tested shower recess, bath waste piping and flow tested all bathroom and laundry waste fixtures. In the shower recess, we located no sealant around the perimeter of the shower recess and there are large gaps where water can leak under the tiles. Following testing, no dye leaked.

Isolated the hot and cold water supply in unit 123 and carried out nitrogen pressure testing. Following pressure testing, no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 123.

Excavated a tile on the side of the bath panel and found the bath cavity to be dry.

Following extensive investigation works, we found no water leaking from unit 123 above.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 123 - Whilst undertaking investigation works in unit 123 resultant damage was caused to the tiles on the bath panel, also there is missing sealant and large gaps around the perimeter of the shower recess. We will submit a quotation shortly for the tiling and sealing works required in unit 123.

Returned to the property and gained access into unit 117, the occupant advised once the rain stopped leak slowed down.

Removed downlight in the laundry ceiling cavity and located water damage to the gyprock below the mechanical ducting, the remainder of the ceiling was dry.

Gained access to N block plant room and located water where the ducting penetrates the plant room and roof wall cavity.

Climbed out onto the roof and found small concrete slab roof and hob with no drainage, above the mechanical duct wall cavity, during heavy rain the small concrete roof would flood and surcharge back into the building through the cavity wall flashings.

Further works required to be undertaken on the small roof above N block - We advise to use core hole machine and drill 4 x spigot drains on each side of the hob to prevent flooding on the roof during heavy downpours. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required on N block roof.

Returned to the property and gained access to the pool area.

Installed steel and re-concreted the affected area flush with the floor level ready for the buildings tiler to reinstate the tiles.

Removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 23/8/25 - Urgent sewer blockage in units 1 and 2

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into units 1, 2 and found the bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked.

Removed common external vent pipe, used CCTV drain camera to find the common in ground sewer pipework to be completely blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively and CCTV drain camera to clear the blockage in the common sewer pipework approximately 10 meters downstream from sewer vent.

Following our CCTV camera survey we found the common PVC pipework to be completely crushed by large tree roots which is the cause of the blockage.

CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DCC8C

Returned to the property on Monday 25/8/25, used pipe locating and CCTV drain camera to locate approximately 5 meters of crushed and faulty common sewer pipework located under the pavers in the driveway.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to close off section of the driveway, remove affected pavers, excavate the ground, cut out approximately 5 meters of crushed common sewer pipework and 2 x junctions, install new PVC pipework, 2 x junctions, fittings, bed pipework, back fil trench and re-instate pavers. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property to investigate multiple leaks within units 12, 8 and common hallway below unit 11 during heavy rain.

Gained access into the top level common hallway and found water damage to the Gyprock ceiling and brick rendered wall causing the ceiling to sag.

Gained access into unit 11 above the hallway and located the bricked service riser and internal downpipe for unit 11's roof courtyard above.

Excavated a brick from the service riser and removed lagging around the downpipe, the foam lagging was saturated indicating a leak from unit 11's courtyard above.

Inspected the courtyard above and found sandstone pavers and surface water drain. We were unable to undertake any flood testing at the time as there was heavy rainfall.

Gained access into unit 12 and found water damage to the common wall in the stairwell,  the internal wall adjacent to the bedroom and the window frame in the bedroom.

Inspected unit 12's roof courtyard above and found several issues with the external wall render and flashings. There is also sandstone pavers and surface water drain. We were unable to undertake any flood testing at the time as there was heavy rainfall.

Gained access into unit 8 and found water damage to the gyprock wall below the window. Inspected the external wall and window frame and found gaps in the sealant around the window where water can leak into the wall.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 8 - We advise abseil contractors are engaged to re-seal around the external window frame in unit 8.

Returned to the property on a dry day and gained access into units 11 & 12.

  • Unit 12's bedroom wall, window and stairwell leak.

Cut a hole in unit 12's bedroom cupboard to inspect the common pipe duct, removed lagging to expose the downpipe and found the stormwater downpipe to be dry.

Blocked off 2 x roof courtyard drains and flood tested the waterproof membrane on the roof courtyard of unit 12. following flood testing of the tiles and waterproof membrane no water leaked into unit 12 below.

On the roof, adjacent to the courtyard balcony is the front awning roof and wall flashing. Inspected the awning roof and found the silicone seal along the flashing and rendered brick wall had perished, at the edge of the flashing there is a large gap where water can enter the cavity underneath. Also there are cracks in the rendered wall and rendered ridge capping.

Flood tested the awning flashing and external rendered wall and rendered ridge capping with a hose. Following flood testing, water is leaking through the external wall ridge capping and the internal bedroom wall and window is becoming damp indicating a leak from the wall flashings and rendered wall cracks.

Used high grade flexible sealant to cover the large gap in the edge of the roof flashing and the large crack in the rendered wall to prevent water leaking into the bedroom wall.

  • Unit 12's blocked courtyard drains.

Whilst undertaking investigation works in unit 12's roof courtyard, lifted lids on the 2 x courtyard floor drains and found them to be completely blocked with calcium and debris. The blocked floor drains are causing the tile bed to hold water and flood the small storage room on the roof.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 12 - We advise to cut out and replace silicone seal along the wall flashing, seal and waterproof service penetration below the BBQ table and use high pressure water jet blaster to unblock 2 x balcony floor drains. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 12.

  • Unit 11 leak into the common hallway ceiling.

Removed temporary cover over the bricked service riser in the living room where hole was previously excavated exposing the downpipe.

Blocked off unit 11's roof courtyard drains and flood tested the waterproof membrane on the roof courtyard of unit 11. Following flood testing of the tiles and waterproof membrane we found water leaked around the penetration and downpipe into unit 11's living room then into the common hallway ceiling.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 11's rooftop balcony - We advise to remove affected sand stone pavers around the surface drain and install puddle flange, primer and 2 coats of waterproof membrane to the affected area and install new sand stone pavers. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 11.

Resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in units 8, 11, 12 and common hallway ceiling-  Investigation works has caused resultant damage to the bedroom cupboard in unit 12 and the bricked service duct in the lounge room of unit 11. Also water leaks during the heavy rain has caused damage to the common hallway ceiling, the external wall below the window in unit 8 and the bedroom wall and stairwell wall in unit 12. Once all further works are completed. We can submit a quotation for resultant damage repairs and painting.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish form the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate gas smell in unit 6.

18/8 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 6 and located an intermittent gas smell in the hallway and kitchen.

Investigated the buildings gas supply and located 1 x gas meter for the entire building and pipework in the carpark tee off to risers.

Called Jemena gas to confirm there was only 1 x gas meter at the property, indicating the entire pipework requires to be pressure tested.

Put up gas shut down notices at the building advising residents of gas disruptions.

21/8 - Returned to the property, gained access and isolated the buildings gas supply. Following testing on the entire buildings gas supply we located a drop in pressure.

Isolated the gas valve in the carpark and tested unit 6’s pipework and located drop in pressure indicating a leak.

Gained access into unit 6 and could not locate the gas pipework in the renovated kitchen and the pipework has been covered over.

22/8 - Returned to the property, with pipe location leak detection, cut a hole in the cupboard and located the gas piping bayonet fitting.

Used pipe tracing equipment to locate unit 6's gas piping which rise through the floor in 2 x locations, located pipework in the walls of the kitchen and bathroom.

Once the pipework was located, used gas detector to locate readings of gas below the skirting board and hallway intercom.

To rectify the leak the entire buildings gas supply will need to be isolated as it connects directly to the buildings pipework.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to remove skiting boards and flooring in the hallway, exposing the gas piping, isolate the buildings gas supply, cut out the affected gas piping and repair pipework using new pipe and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water leak in the carpark.

Attended to property, gained access into unit 7 and the common garage.

In the garage we located water leaking through the pipe penetrations on the ceiling where the gas and cold water pipe goes up through the concrete slab into unit 7 and 5's rear courtyard.

Went into unit 7's rear courtyard, blocked off the floor drain and dye tested the courtyard tiles and waterproof membrane. No green dye leaked from the water and gas pipework into the carpark below.

Used drain cleaning equipment and CCTV drain camera downstream the surface drain to clear the blockage in the common storm water pipework. Once we released water from unit 5's courtyard the leak in the carpark below stopped.

Inspected the upstairs rooftop balcony and found water had leaked onto the tiles at the top of the stairs and into door frame indicating the rooftop balcony had also flooded. The balcony floor drain cover had been removed before we got there.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 1.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water leaking from the kitchen gyprock ceiling.

Cut a hole in the kitchen gyprock ceiling to inspect inside the cavity and located the PVC pipe penetration to be leaking through the concrete slab.

Stepped out the location of the leak and went upstairs to unit 1's external balcony above. We found the balcony floor drain to be blocked and the balcony to be holding water.

Lifted floor waste grate on the balcony drain and cleared calcium from the drainage with the use of electric eel, which was causing the blockage.

Once clear, we dye tested the PVC pipework and no dye was found to be leaking into the kitchen indicating faulty waterproof membrane on the balcony.

Inspected the silicone seals around the edge of the external balcony and located faulty seals, gaps and plants growing in the wall joints where water can leak under the balcony tiles into the substrate.

We also inspected the window frames and found the external window track to be full of water and holding water as there are no weep holes.

Please see video link of faulty balcony seals and windows holding water - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DCDWO

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken by a building contractor -  We advise the entire upstairs balcony in unit 1 is cleared of objects and the entire balcony is re-sealed as a temporary solution. As the balcony membrane has failed, a permanent solution would be to excavate all tiles, water proof using 2 x coats of membrane sealant, retile and reseal the entire balcony.

We also advise the windows are inspected and repairs are undertaken to prevent water holding within the external window tracks.

Once the repair works are completed in unit 1, the kitchen ceiling can be repaired and painted.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water leak in unit 11.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 11 and found water leaking under the kitchen floorboards and a small amount of moisture in the kitchen cupboards.

Inspected the original bathroom and located poor grouting within the common shower wall tiles and missing sealant around the bath edge. We also found the shower head to be cracked and leaking badly when in use.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property and spoke with the site contact to go through 3 x separate issues at the building.  1st issue to clear the tree root infested common sewer boundary trap for the building, 2nd issue to install a isolation valve on the common cold water pipework so that the water supply on the irrigation can be isolated in the event of an emergency and 3rd issue to investigate water leaking coming from the neighboring property 19 Hough St.

  • Issue 1 - Blocked common sewer boundary trap located in the garden area at the rear of the property 

Used CCTV drain camera downstream the common sewer boundary trap for the building and found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware boundary trap and common sewer outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DMZGM

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the major tree rot infestations entering the earthenware sewer pipework boundary trap downstream to vertical shaft before Sydney Waters main. Flow tested boundary trap and common sewer pipework - All clear and in good working order.  Please note if the tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework is not repaired/relined, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline approximately 8 meters of heavily root infested cracked pipework, relining from boundary trap 8 meters downstream finishing at vertical shaft connection before Sydney main sewer using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken. 

  • Issue 2 - install isolation valve for water supply for irrigation in the car park area

Excavated the ground and exposed irrigation pipework located in the garden area. 

Isolated irrigation water supply, installed pipework, fittings and raised to the surface an isolation valve so the so the water can be isolated in the event of an emergency or to undertake repairs.

Turned on the water supply and tested all works. Installed box to house new isolation valve, bed pipework and back filled trench.

  • Issue 3 - Leak from the neighboring property 19 Hough St causing water to leak under the fence

Carried out inspection on the building next door number 19 Hough St and found the down pipe located on the right hand side of property is undersized and most likely causing a blockages and water to surcharge and leak into 1-17 Hough St during heavy rain. We also located the overflow sewer gully to be blocked, surcharging when in use and possibly collapsed causing sewerage to leak into the earth.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken at 19 Hough St - We advise the buildings plumber is engaged to upsize the downpipe on the right hand side of the building, clear out blocked overflow sewer gully with the use of high pressure jet blaster and use CCTV drain camera to CCTV camera survey the complete sewer system on the right hand side of the building to ensure no breaks or collapsed sewer pipes are found.  Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DMZGC

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream the common sewer boundary trap for the building and found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware boundary trap and common sewer outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DMZGM

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the major tree rot infestations entering the earthenware sewer pipework boundary trap downstream to vertical shaft before Sydney Waters main. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Excavated the ground and exposed irrigation pipework located in the garden area. 

Isolated irrigation water supply, installed pipework, fittings and raised to the surface an isolation valve so the so the water can be isolated in the event of an emergency or to undertake repairs.

Turned on the water supply and tested all works. Installed box to house new isolation valve, bed pipework and back filled trench.

Carried out inspection on the building next door number 19 Hough St and found the down pipe located on the right hand side of property is undersized and most likely causing a blockages and water to surcharge and leak into 1-17 Hough St during heavy rain. We also located the overflow sewer gully to be blocked, surcharging when in use and possibly collapsed causing sewerage to leak into the earth.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken at 19 Hough St - We advise the buildings plumber is engaged to upsize the downpipe on the right hand side of the building, clear out blocked overflow sewer gully with the use of high pressure jet blaster and use CCTV drain camera to CCTV camera survey the complete sewer system on the right hand side of the building to ensure no breaks or collapsed sewer pipes are found.  Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DMZGC

Description:
URGENT Quotation - Hot water plant and valve repairs in the plant room.

Following our inspection of all hot water plant, we found the hot water temperature on the storage tank to be at 49 degrees, which slowly reached 59 degrees and the instantaneous heater was always heating.

Isolated and removed the flow and return pump, carried out testing and found it to be in good working order.
Inspected the inlet pressure reduction valve and found it to be at 350kpa on the gauge, isolated water supply to the tank and found the pressure gauge fluctuated up and down indicating a fault with the valve.
Inspected the hot water return line pipework after the circulating pump and found it to be cold on the other side of the limiting valve. Found the limiting valve to be installed backwards.
Following our inspection of the instantaneous hot water heater, no faults were found.

To rectify the issue, we advise the 2 x faulty pressure valves on the hot water plant are replaced.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents and isolate the buildings hot water supply.
  2. Source new Adjustable pressure reduction valve and pressure limiting valve.
  3. Disconnect faulty pressure reducing valve (PRV) on the inlet, supply and install new PRV.
  4. Carry out pressure test on the buildings cold water supply and adjust PRV to correct pressure.
  5. Cut out faulty pressure limiting valve (PLV) on the hot water return pipework, supply and install new PLV, pipe and fittings.
  6. Turn the buildings hot water supply back on, commission pumps, hot water heater.
  7. Clean all area where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish form the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak and significant damage to the garage stairwell. 

Attended the property, met with the site contact Kate who showed us where water has been leaking at the base of the fire escape and lower car park entrance for some time. There is also evidence of concrete cancer within the slab ceiling of the fire escape. On our inspection we found water pooling on the floor and dripping consistently from the concrete slab and the light fitting.

Gained access to the common area above and located a planter box. Carried out further investigation works to locate a storm water drain within the planter box located on the opposite side of the water damaged fire escape wall.

Cut out a section of aerial common storm water drainage in the car park next to the main entrance on Moonbie St and found large amounts of dirt and debris causing a blockage within the common stormwater aerial drainage.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment down the driveway entrance. 

Used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the dirt and debris within the stormwater line and the planter box. We found there was a 100 mm PVC riser going through the planter box with incisions cut with a grinder. This is to collect all of the ground water within the planter box.

Flow tested common storm water pipework - All clear and in good working order.

As water is leaking out of the planter box, through the concrete slab into the car park, the waterproof membrane within the planter box has failed and requires replacement.

We also advise a concrete cancer specialist attends and provides a quote to fix all affected affected areas in the carpark.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise BCS engages a remedial building contractor to excavate the dirt from the plant box in the common area above the car park, install new waterproof membrane, re-fill planter box and also repair all affected areas of concrete cancer within the fire stairs.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.
