Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak under unit 2.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2 and inspected water damaged flooring in the living room, bedroom, wet walls and rotten skirting boards.

Climbed under the subfloor of unit 2 through the manhole at the stairs and found the subfloor soil to be wet, which is causing rising damp.

Under unit 2, the floor joists to have no support and the bricked piers have dropped causing a gap. Also, where the joists are supported by the load bearing walls, the joists have dropped and become rotten.

Along the side passage, we found a large hole in the external brickwork wall which has been covered by timber slats, this hole will be allowing a large amount of water to enter under the building when it rains.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers to carry out flood testing under the back deck of unit 2.

We were advised not to remove the decking as they will easily break and we were unable to inspect the external building wall below the decking.

Flood tested the decking with a hose and climbed under the subfloor of unit 2 whilst undertaking the flood test.

Following flood testing of the back decking, water leaked from the external cavity wall into the subfloor under unit 2.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise a building contractor is engaged to inspect the structure of the floor joists under unit 2’s subfloor and carry out repairs and the large hole in the external brickwork along the side passage is re-bricked. Also a qualified contractor is required to lift the decking and a building contractor is engaged to inspect the external cavity wall below the decking and carry put repairs to prevent water leaking into the subfloor under unit 2.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place.

Alternate Site Contact:
Sega
T: + 61 2 9578 6000 | M: + 61 450 635 565
BCS REF # 8396062
Invoice Description:
• Clear all storm water balcony drains in all 21 units.

Attended the property with 2 x plumbers on the 18/7/25 and 28/7/25 to clear all balcony drains in each unit.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck on Coogee Bay Rd and equipment to each balcony.

Lifted balcony drain lids and removed surface calcium from the drain openings to access pipework. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream each balcony drain, clearing out a large amount of calcification, dirt and debris within the drains which is causing blockages.

Following extensive clear out works on unit 12's balcony, we were unable to clear the blocked balcony drain and our jet blasting hose is currently stuck in the drain.

Major tree roots were found in the pipework under the concrete slab and garden bed and jet blasting equipment is currently stuck within the pipe under the garden bed.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 12 and CCTV camera surveyed the blocked balcony drainage to a location under the garden bed. The pipework was completely full of tree roots and unable to be cleared. 

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 12 - We advise to excavate the garden bed, removing trees and soil to locate the drainage under the garden bed and carry out further clear out works on the common stormwater line within the concrete slab, removing tree roots. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 12.

  • Investigate water leak in garage 14.

Gained access into garage 14 and found there was no water to be leaking at the time of investigation.

Inspected the ceiling pipes and plumbing service in the garage and no leaks or faults were found.

Located the hotel units to be above the leak.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the maintenance plumber for the hotel is engaged to investigate the leak into the garage 14, as the hotel is above.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 1.

29/7 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water damage to the timber bulkhead in the kitchen and swelling of the cabinets above the sink.

Inspected unit 2 and confirmed the leak was not coming from unit 2.

Gained access into unit 5 above, removed the access panel under the kitchen cabinetry and found water leaking onto the concrete slab. Knocked on unit 6, but no-one was home at the time. Left access notes.

31/7 - Returned to the property and gained access unit 5 & 6.

Inspected the service duct in unit 6's kitchen adjacent to the leak in unit 5 and found the service duct to be dry. Carried out testing in unit 6's kitchen and no leaks were found. Isolated the hot water supply to unit 5, carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and got a drop in pressure on the hot water indicating a leak.

1/8 - Returned to the property with pipe location leak detection, nitrogen tested the hot water and found only a slight loss in pressure.

Traced position of pipework using pipe location equipment and found the hot water line in the common kitchen wall behind the cabinets adjacent to the service riser in unit 6. Leak detection advised us to excavate the common kitchen wall where the hot pipe is located to determine if the burst pipe is located in the wall.

We also located water leaking from the internal laundry wall adjacent to the shower in unit 5, which is a separate leak. We pressure tested the shower breaching piece and found a drop in pressure indicating a burst shower breaching piece within the internal wall of unit 5.

4/8 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 5 and cut out the kitchen cabinetry where the hot water pipework was located.

Excavated the common wall exposing the hot water pipework. Once exposed, we located a burst hot water pipe within the common wall behind the kitchen.

Isolated the water supply to unit 5 and carried out repairs to the burst pressurized hot water pipe using oxy acetylene welding equipment. Turned the water supply back on testing all works - All in good working order and no further leaks were found.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 5 by the lot owner - Whilst undertaking pressure testing in unit 5, we located a burst shower breaching piece on the internal shower wall. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the lot owners consideration.

Following the burst pipe repair works in unit 5, resultant damage was caused to the kitchen cabinets in unit 5 and there is also damage to the bulkhead and cabinetry in unit 1. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required in units 5 & 1.

REGARDS GLENN
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 2/7/25 - Urgent sewer blockage and flooded lift shaft

Urgently attended the property after hours, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and flooding into the common laundry causing flooding into the lift shaft.

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer pipework in the driveway and found the main boundary trap for the building to be completely blocked, causing sewerage to surcharge into the common laundry and flood the lift shaft.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in the car park.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively and CCTV drain camera downstream the boundary trap to clear out a large amount of wet wipes from the original earthenware sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage.

Flow tested boundary trap and common sewer pipework - All clear and in good working order.

Removed concrete sewer pit lit in the car park and found the reflux valve flap rubber flap has perished and requires replacement. Used CCTV drain camera to inspected the common sewer pipework upstream and downstream which was clear and in good working order.

The lift contractor locked off the lift, hired submersible pump and used a submersible pump to pump out all sewerage from the lift shaft and common laundry area.

Flow tested pump in the common laundry - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening and concrete sewer pit lid, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the 150mm common reflux valve flap is replaced with new reflux valve flap. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

We also advise our relining team attends to inspect the condition of the original earthenware sewer pipework from the top of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters sewer main. If required we will submit a quotation for any further works required to be undertaken

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 7.

Urgently attended the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access into unit 7 and found the leak to be intermittent during heavy rain.

Gained access into unit 11, above unit 7 and no leaks were found, set up step ladder and accessed the roof space from unit 11's laundry.

Following our inspection in the roof space above unit 11 & 7, no leaks were found within the roof space coming from the roof vent seals previously undertaken.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise a roofing contractor is engaged by the strata to replace the missing roof tile and carry out repairs to the roof.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended property, gained access and carried out investigation works and maintenance on stormwater.

Found the box gutter on the roof to be blocked and overflowing down the building, engaged 2 x plumbers, used large extension ladder and accessed the box gutter on the roof.

Removed plastic which was stuck in the outlet and cleaned leaves and debris from the box gutter rainwater sump and outlet.

Lifted pit lid in the garden of 84, cleaned out base of pit removing soil, leaves and debris.

Carried out a CCTV camera survey inspection of the stormwater lines into the pit and identified where they run.

Inspected the rainwater pump and sump pump below the car-stacker to find the pumps were not working and had no power.

Turned on the power supply and found the sump pump was not discharging water from the sump, disconnected pipework and located sand build up in the check valve causing it to block.

Removed debris from the check valve, re-connected pipework and tested the sump pump - All in good working order.

Inspected the rainwater tank and located the downpipe at the rear of the building runs into the tank. We also found no overflow on the rainwater tank, which is causing the downpipe to surcharge at the base connection and leak through the wall under the car-stacker.

As the rainwater tank and pump is no longer in use and there is no overflow which is the causing the drainage leak, we advise to run the downpipe drainage directly to the kerb and gutter, deleting the rainwater tank. The rainwater pump, switch is removed and connected directly to the mains water supply. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property and gained access into unit 8.

Inspected the original bathroom and carried out testing on the shower recess and bathroom fixtures.

Following our inspection of the shower recess, we found faulty floor tiles that are not level, causing the floor grout to wash away. We also located no grout within the wall tiles and no sealant within the tile joints allowing water to leak in behind the tiles.

Blocked off the shower floor drain and flood/dye tested the shower recess with red dye. No dye was found to be leaking.

Invoice Description:
21/7 - We were contacted by the commitee member Ron, who advised of not hot water over the weekend and still flooding in the laundry.

Attended the property and found the common hot water heater plant to be at low temperature.

Re-set the hot water heater and the tank climbed up to temperature, inspected the hot water heater.

Following our inspection, we found the hot water temperature on the storage tank to be at 49 degrees, which slowly reached 59 degrees and the instantaneous heater was always heating.

Following our inspection of the instantaneous hot water heater, no faults were found.

We removed all water from the laundry using the pump.

24/7 - Returned to the property, Inspected the laundry and found water keeps pooling in the laundry, this is due to the heavy rain flooding around the buildings subsoil and eventually filling up the laundry which is lower than the outside ground level.

Gained access and inspected all hot water plant and the hot water heater.

Isolated and removed the flow and return pump, carried out testing and found it to be in good working order, the inlet pressure reduction valve was 350kpa on the gauge, isolated water supply to the tank and found the pressure gauge fluctuated up and down indicating a fault with the valve. The hot water return line pipework after the circulating pump was cold on the other side of the limiting valve, found the limiting valve to be installed backwards.

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the issue with the common hot water heater plant - We advise the 2 x faulty pressure valves on the hot water plant manifold are replaced. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description:

Following the recent CCTV camera survey, we located a crack and break in the original earthenware sewer pipework located at the base of the toilet stack outside unit 1 and 2 meters of the earthenware pipework downstream to be dislodged and dropping. We also found the base of the kitchen stack outside unit 1's kitchen window to have a dislodged elbow, a large break and 3 meters of defective, dropped original earthenware pipework which is causing rising damp in unit 1. Also to excavate the ground in 2 x locations and replace approximately 2 meters of dropped and defective original earthenware sewer pipework with new PVC pipework and 1 meter of faulty pipework on the outlet of the gully to the inspection opening, raise 2 x overflow gullies above ground level to comply with AS-3500.

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.

  7. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • PART A - Urgent relining repairs
  1. Advise residents of a cold water building shut down.
  2. Clear lines using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera.
  3. Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS3500.
  4. Record footage of lines before relining.
  5. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  6. Reline 2 meters of cracked earthenware pipework from newly installed plastic pipework downstream finishing at mainline connection using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  7. Reline 3 meters of dislodged, cracked earthenware pipework from plastic inspection point downstream finishing at gully inlet using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.

  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  11. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.

Total cost of works for PART A - $6,900.00 + GST

Urgent quotation - Relining repairs on the main sewer line for the building

Following the recent relining works undertaken, we undertook a CCTV camera survey on the complete sewer system at the building. Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the common main line for the building to be completely blocked and major tree roots entering majority of the original earthenware main line.  We used high pressure water jet blaster free of charge to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework to prevent further sewerage surcharging. 

This urgent quotation is to reline approximately 17 meters of cracked and tree root infested mainline, relining from plastic inspection point 17 meters upstream covering all root infested joints finishing reline on previously relined section using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin and using robotic cutter reinstate 4 x junctions located on mainline.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Set up relining equipment.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. reline approximately 17 meters of cracked and tree root infested mainline, relining from plastic inspection point 17 meters upstream covering all root infested joints finishing reline on previously relined section using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  5. Using robotic cutter reinstate 4 x junctions located on mainline.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  9. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  10. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  11. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Invoice Description:
Investigate water leaks in the garage below unit 3.

1/7 - Attended the property to investigate 2 x common property leaks into the carpark coming from unit 3 above.

Gained access to unit 3 above, dye tested the shower tray and all waste fixtures in the bathroom - No leaks were found.

Nitrogen pressure tested the hot and cold water pipework and found a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a leak.

9/7 - Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot water supply and found only a slight loss in pressure.

Traced position of pipework using pipe location equipment and found the hot water line drops down in the bathroom behind the vanity and heads across to the kitchen and a separate line to the laundry.

Inspected the lot owners quarter turn shower taps and found them to be faulty, which could be causing the water leak.

Removed taps and temporarily installed new taps so we could pressure test - No drop in pressure was found. Nitrogen pressure tested hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found.

25/7 - Returned to the property, and found the water leak in the garage below unit 3 to have stopped.

We replaced the lot owners taps, sealed gaps behind taps spindles using high grade flexible sealant and charged the lot owner direct for these lot owner repair works.

Spoke with the site contact the following week who advised the water leak into the car park has now stopped.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage outside unit 1 in the common area.

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage in the common area outside unit 1 next to the gas meters. 

Met with the site contact who showed us sewerage leaking into unit 1, which is currently undertaking renovation below ground level.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment outside unit 1.

Removed inspection opening on the sewer shaft located at the bottom of the stairs, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment to locate major tree roots entering outlet of the 2 x original earthenware gully's and earthenware pipework to the vertical shaft at the bottom of the stairs which is the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework.

Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the original earthenware sewer pipework and 2 x overflow gullies to be badly cracked and dislodged in multiple locations causing sewerage to leak into the earth and into unit 1 below.

Flow tested 2 x overflow sewer gully's and common sewer pipework downstream - All clear and in good working order. Please note if the tree root infested and cracked original earthenware pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur and sewerage will continue to leak into unit 1 below.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the tree root infested, cracked, dislodged and leaking common earthenware sewer pipework outside unit 1 is relined completely sealing the defective pipework. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Description:
Quotation - Relining repairs on the common storm water pipework in garage

Following the recent blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey downstream the sewer stack inspection opening in the garage servicing units 1 and above, we located the original earthenware sewer pipework to be badly collapsed, cracked, broken and requires URGENT repairs to prevent further blockages and sewer floods in the garage,.

Please see CCTV video link from our inspection - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DD798

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Set up safe work area around property.
  2. Gain access to garage and inspection points located in the garage.
  3. Prepare plastic pipework with sanding block to AS3500 standards.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  6. Dig down in located area to remove collapsed section of sewer line.
  7. Install new plastic pipework to AS3500.
  8. Backfill area with sand and compact trench as per AS3500
  9. Re concrete affected area.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Reline approximately 12 meters of sewer branch- line, from stack connection 12 meters downstream covering all heavily cracked root infested joints finishing reline at mainline connection. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin. This reline is the complete branch-line. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  4. Using robotic cutter reinstate 2 side line Junction connections on branch-line.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  7. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  8. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  9. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate potential bathroom ceiling leak in unit 9.

Picked up keys from the managing agent for unit 9, attended the property and gained access into unit 9.

Inspected the renovated bathroom and found the gyprock ceiling to be painted. There was no water damage to the bathroom ceiling or bulkhead and no leaks were found.

Located surface mould around the top of the bathroom wall tiles, where it meets the gyprock bathroom ceiling.

Inspected the bathroom and found the shower / bath recess to have faulty sealant along the bath edge where it meets the common wall tiles.

Tested exhaust fan and found it works, lifted cover and found it to be full of dust which requires to be cleaned out. 

Gained access into unit 19 above and found the bathroom to be original. Inspected the bathroom and found the shower recess to have no sealant along the bath edge and behind the taps.

The common wall grout within the shower / bath recess is in good condition, found missing grout on the bath hob on the common wall.

Carried out a test on the shower and found the shower screen leaks from the door joint, down the bath panel onto the bathroom floor tiles, then under the bath. 

Flood tested the bath waste pipework and no leaks were found in unit 9 below.

Inspected the exhaust fan in unit 19's bathroom and found it to be full of dust which requires to be cleaned out. 

We found the mould in unit 9's bathroom wall tiles to be caused by poor ventilation in the bathroom from the blocked exhaust fan, also faulty sealant in unit 19's original shower/bath recess allowing water to leak under the bath and dampen the concrete slab. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 19 at the owners corporation cost - We advise to re-seal shower/ bath recess, behind taps, bath edge and hob using high grade flexible sealant and re-grout hob on the common walls using additive. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 19.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 19 by the lot owner - We advise a new shower screen is installed and the bathroom exhaust fan is cleaned. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 9  at the owners corporation cost - We advise to re-seal shower/ bath recess, bath edge and hob on the common wall using high grade flexible sealant. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 9

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Collapsed and blocked common sewer piping.

Following investigation works at the property, used the pipe locator to locate a collapsed section earthenware sewer piping under the concrete slab along the right side passage approximately 5 meters downstream from the sewer stack in the front garage. We used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to try and clear out the blocked common sewer line, but was unsuccessful.

Investigate water leak in unit 6.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 6 and found water damage in the entrance hallway gyprock ceiling where a hole has formed.

Opened access cover for the air conditioner and inspected inside the ceiling cavity. Following our inspection we located calcium deposits forming from a crack in the concrete slab, metal has been placed under and the leak has been for some time.

Gained access into unit 16 above, located the downstairs shower and common shower wall to be directly above the crack in the concrete slab.

Pressure tested shower mixer, diverter to shower head and shower spray no drop in pressure indicating no burst pipes. 

Inspected the original shower and located cracks in the wall grouting, missing sealant and missing grout in the shower floor tiles. 

Went into the fire stairs and located calcium deposits leaking from the slab level on the opposite side indicating water is leaking under the floor tiles in unit 16’s shower recess. 

Carried out a flood test of the shower floor, 10mm step down and couldn’t get water to leak over 30 min. Carried out extensive flood testing of the shower wall tiles and gaps in the grouting.

Following investigation works, we found calcium deposits leaking from the concrete ceiling slab in unit 6 caused by cracks in the grouting and water leaking under the tiles into the substrate in unit 16's downstairs shower recess.

Further works required in unit 16 to rectify the leak - We advise the downstairs shower recess, floor tiles and 3 x common walls are re-grouted, and the shower recess is re-sealed. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 16.

Further works required in unit 6  - We advise to cut out a section of the water damaged gyprock ceiling, repair and paint the damaged hallway ceiling. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 6.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using the high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Following the recent urgent sewer blockage we cleared at the rear of the building outside the common toilet and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree roots entering the original earthenware branch line for approximately 6 meters downstream the inspection opening outside the common toilet.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent urgent sewer blockage we cleared next to car space 5 and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree roots entering the original earthenware sewer pipework for approximately 7 meters downstream the inspection opening under the driveway and also approximately 2 meters upstream the inspection opening located under the building. 

This quotation is to reline approximately 7 meters of heavily root infested, cracked earthenware pipework. Relining from plastic inspection opening next to car space 5, 7 meters downstream covering all 100mm root infested joints finishing reline before 100/150 diameter change using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin. Also to reline approximately 2 meters of  tree root infested pipework relining from plastic inspection point 2 meters upstream in towards building sealing root infested material change sealing back onto earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Barricade around work area at the rear of the building.
  3. Set up relining equipment.
  4. Clean all sewer pipework with high pressure water jet blaster, milling tool and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.
  • Urgent relining repairs
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 7 meters of heavily root infested, cracked earthenware pipework. Relining from plastic inspection opening next to car space 5, 7 meters downstream covering all 100mm root infested joints finishing reline before 100/150 diameter change using Watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 2 meters of  tree root infested pipework relining from plastic inspection point 2 meters upstream in towards building sealing root infested material change sealing back onto earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  4. Cure reline using hot water boiler. 
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  6. using robotic cutter reinstate all junctions on relined pipework.
  7. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  8. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  9. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  10. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  11. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  
  12. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate hot water issues in units 7 and 10.

Attended the property, gained access into units 7 and 10, found the hot water to be fluctuating and luke warm.

Gained access onto the roof and inspected the common hot water set up.

Following our inspection we found the ball valve on recirculation pump was almost all the way off.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and the occupant advised us water was leaking on the bathroom floor near the bath. 

Tested all fixtures in the renovated bathroom and no leaks were found.

The bathroom floor was dry on the time of our attendance. 

Gained access to the common external wall outside the bathroom and found missing seals on multiple wall penetrations directly above where the water was leaking into unit 1.

Investigation revealed that when it is windy rain water is getting through these penetrations and filling up the cavity wall, then leaking onto the bathroom floor.

Silicon sealed around 5 penetration to prevent further water leaking into the cavity and unit 1.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate rising damp and common sewer gully.

Attended the property, met with the site contact Tom to investigate the reported rising damp in the office space on the basement floor located on Hayden Lane.

Gained access to the ground floor office space and found rising damp behind the skirting boards on two common walls in the main room. Used moisture meter to confirm high readings of moisture within the common external walls.

Inspected the opposite sides of the water damaged walls and found that the bin room walls had a large amount of rising damp and moisture.

Inspected the original earthenware common sewer gully within this area, used aqua vacuum to suck out the sewerage from the base of the gully, used CCTV downstream to locate the base of the the gully and outlet pipework to be completely collapsed and broken. Waste waste is leaking out of the collapsed gully sewer pipework and discharging into the subsoil, causing major rising damp issues into the office space walls adjacent. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DJODO

Walked around the property, inspected all common sewer gully's and boundary traps. We located a second gully within the rear side passage close to the collapsed gully which was blocked with a large amount of grease build up from the kitchen line entering the gully.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster equipment and ran hoses to the blocked gully.  Removed inspection opening lids and used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear the blockage in the overflow relief gully.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping downstream and identified the line discharges into an old bricked grease trap with a bitumen lid. Attempted to lift the bitumen lid from the original grease trap, but was unable to remove without breaking.

Flow tested the outlet of the second gully with a high pressure hose and found it to be in working order and no further blockages.

Please note - Due to the faulty bitumen lid on the old grease trap, we were unable to inspect the quality and advise the original grease trap is removed.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place in the rear side passage with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further URGENT works are required to be undertaken within to rectify the 2 x affected gully's and original grease trap - We advise to saw cut the concrete within the rear side passage, excavate the concrete and ground, cut out the collapsed earthenware sewer gully, original grease trap and second gully, install new PVC pipework, 2 x gully's, delete the original grease trap and faulty lid, back fill trench and reinstate concrete. We will submit an URGENT quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Carried out further investigation works for the rising damp and located an original cast iron downpipe chased into the external wall within the small council laneway adjacent to the rear side passage.

Following investigation works, we found large holes in the external brickwork / chase where the downpipe offsets out of the wall at head height. Along with poor brickwork pointing, these large holes are causing water to leak into the external wall cavity.

Removed pot plants along the council laneway exposing the council footpath and sandstone guttering, we found the downpipe connection at the sandstone gutter is faulty, which is causing a large amount of roof rainwater to leak under the council footpath into the soil. Also the fall in the council laneway and the poor quality of sandstone gutter is allowing excess runoff from the road to enter the subsoil and track under the building.

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the leaking, original common downpipe chased within the eternal wall and gutter connection - We advise to cut out and replace the cast iron downpipe within the wall chase, cement holes in the external brickwork behind, install new PVC downpipe within the chase, install a new metal gutter connection within the sandstone gutter and seal the common wall chase with metal coverplate.  We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further common storm water downpipe works required to be undertaken.

Whilst at the property, we also located holes in the guttering and large amounts of faulty brickwork pointing. We advise a roofing contractor is engaged by the strata to gain access to the roof, inspect guttering, flashing and roof and carry out repairs. A building contractor is engaged by the strata to inspect the external walls and pointing and carry out repairs. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DJICX

We also advise the local council is contacted by the strata to rectify the poor quality of sandstone guttering within the council laneway which is allowing water run-off to leak under the building. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DJICM

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak into the laundry.

1/7 - Attended the property, gained access into the common laundry and basement below the building.

Due to heavy rain at the time, we found the entire basement and laundry to be flooded, we also found gutters to be overflowing and the entire backyard to be waterlogged, indicating the stormwater system is inadequate.

We were unable to investigate the addition leak into the basement due to the large amount of rain.

3/7 - Returned to the property when the rain had stopped, gained access into the laundry and located water leaking from the right side of the building under the footings, below the outside ground level.

Disconnected the common sewer pipework in the front garage and installed an inspection opening for CCTV camera survey and jet blasting clear out purposes.

Obtained a sewer service diagram from Sydney water, located the common boundary trap at the rear yard and CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer pipework upstream. Following our camera survey, we found the outlet of the boundary trap and the mainline within the rear yard to be clear.

Following our CCTV camera survey from the newly inspection opening installed in the front garage, we found the sewer line along the side passage to be blocked.

Engages 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran equipment int the front garages.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to try and clear out the common sewer line, but was unsuccessful.

Used the pipe locator to locate a collapsed section earthenware sewer piping, under the concrete slab along the right side passage approximately 5 meters downstream from the sewer stack in the front garage.

As the sewer piping is currently blocked and collapsed, this is causing the additional leak in the laundry under the building.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise the collapsed section of earthenware sewer piping under the right side passage concrete is excavated and replaced with new PVC piping and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Whilst undertaking the common sewer works at the property, we found the common stormwater pit and pump at the front garages to be blocked, preventing it from removing water from the basement and front garages.

Set up venturi pump and used the high pressure water jet blaster to remove dirt, debris and leaves from the base of the pit, washed down from the front strip drains during the heavy rain, which caused the pump to fail.

After testing the pump in the lower driveway in front of the garages, we found a large amount of stormwater to be discharging into the sewer system which is illegal and requires to be rectified urgently.

Whilst at the property during the heavy rain event, we were able to identify several issue with the common stormwater causing flooding. Once we have gone through the works with our team, we can provide a quotation to rectify issues with the current stormwater which is causing flooding.

Cleaned all areas and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water leak in the garage.

19/6- Attended the property, gained access into the garage and located water leaking from the common pipe stack and riser below unit 4.

Gained access into the building and left access notices on units 4 & 11 as no-one was home at the time.

25/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 4 and removed the common service riser panel on the bathroom wall, inspected the common hot water pipework within the service riser and located the leak to be coming from above.

Did a door knock on unit 18, gained access, removed the common service riser panel on the bathroom wall, inspected the common hot water pipework within the service riser and located the leak to be coming from above.  

Made contact with unit 25 and organized to return to the property.

2/7 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 25 and located a large amount of mould on the bathroom concrete ceiling and water stains coming from the top of the common service riser panel.

Removed service riser panel causing damage, exposed the common hot water pipework and located water dripping through the concrete slab from the roof above.

Gained access onto the roof, cut out the PVC lagging where the pipework goes into the concrete slab and located a burst pressurized pipe on the common hot water return line.

Installed a temporary clamp over the burst pipe to stop the water leak and put notices up at the building advising residents of water disruptions.

3/7- Returned to the property the following day, shut down the buildings hot water supply and drained the water from the line.

Cut out burst hot water copper pipework and installed new section of copper pipework and fittings.

Turned on the buildings hot water supply, bleeding the air from the line and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Commissioned and tested common hot water heaters - All in good working order.

Installed high grade flexible sealant around the common hot water PVC pipework lagging on the roof to prevent water leaking and supplied and installed new hot water lagging.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further resultant damage repair works required to be undertaken in units 4 & 25 - Following the burst pipe investigation works, there is resultant damage to the common service riser panels in the bathroom of units 4 & 25, we advise a building contractor is engaged to inspect and carry out repairs and painting works in unit 4 & 25.

Please note - The burst pipe we located and repaired on the roof is a new burst pipe in a separate location to the previous burst pipe we repaired and invoiced for. The building has old copper pipework throughout the property and the common hot water pipework on the roof is concealed in PVC lagging which is difficult to locate when burst pipes occur.

Invoice Description:
Investigate why the spa jets are not working.

25/6 - Attended the property, gained access to the common pool and spa area.

Tested the spa jets and found only the left side jets are working and the right side jets are not pushing air.

Inspected the air intake and found calcium to be blocking the pipework.

Made contact with the buildings spa service technician who advised high pressure water jet blasting or hydrochloric acid wont affect the pipes.

2/7 - Returned to the property, gained access to the common pool and spa area. Set up high pressure water jet blaster in the carpark and ran hoses up to the spa.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster equipment to clear out a large amount of solidified calcium from the vertical section of spa jet pipework.

We were unable to clear out the blockage which goes further around the base of the bend with the high pressure water jet blaster.

Used submersible pump to pump out water from the spa and emptied the spa.

Poured hydrochloric acid down the pipework to break up the solidified calcium and left it within the pipe for a long period of time.

Used wet vac simultaneously to try and remove calcium within the pipework but was unable to clear.

3/7 - Returned to the property the following day after using the acid to break up the solidified calcium.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster in the carpark and ran hoses up to the spa.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster, gurney gun and chain cutter over 3 hours, but was unable to clear out the solidified calcium from the spa jet pipework.

Further works required to be undertaken - As the blockage cannot be cleared, we advise to excavate tiles and concrete around the affected spa pipework, cut and replace with new pipe and fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further work required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Unit 1 / 237 Leaking shower: Can you please refer to the attached report on pages 7-10 and arrange to attend and diagnose a leak from Unit 1/237 shower and quote to repair?
Site Contact Person : Rui Miguel Melo
Phone : +61 417060090
Email : ozbreaker@gmail.com

FROM THE REPORT: 
Observations
On 23 June 2025 the owner of Unit 1/237 Cope St (Rui) reported that a water leak onto the common area stair behind the Unit 1 northern wall was suspected to be coming from their shower.
On 25 June 2025 I attended the property and I observed that there was a point at the base of the timber stud frame behind the shower (visible from the common area stair as the wall lining is being replaced on that side) that was heavily water stained and the wall paint below was damaged (Photo 12).
I peeled back the carpet outside the bathroom doorway and found that the carpet nailing strips were not water affected (Photo 13).
I inspected the bathroom outlet pipes through the slab soffit below from the driveway but did not observe any evidence that they have been leaking, either before or during my testing (Photo 14).

I carried out water testing in the shower with the following results:
 Running the shower resulting in a minor leak from the above location after only a few minutes.
 The shower has a “rain” shower head which is not adjustable, so I water tested the taps using the garden hose, however there was no leak (Photo 15).
 Rui removed the shower head and I ran the shower, there was no leak (Photo 16). I observed that the sealant around the shower head pipe has peeled away.
 I water tested the penetration around the shower head pipe by directing the garden hose against the opening in the wall tiles, and water leaked into the foyer almost immediately (Photo 17).

Conclusions and Recommendations
I did not find evidence to confirm that the shower recess waterproofing membrane is leaking. Therefore, the leak into the common area may not be due to water leaking through the membrane.
As a leak occurred quickly when the shower was running, but not when the shower head was removed, it appears that water can track back along the threaded section of pipe and penetrate behind membrane.
It is also possible that the shower pipe work could be leaking.
If the bathroom membrane itself has failed then a full shower renovation would be required at a minimum, if not a full bathroom renovation.

I therefore recommend the following staged approach:
1. Engage a plumber to pressure test the shower pipework and confirm that it is not leaking.
2. Engage NRG to perform the following localised repair to the shower head (variation costing to be provided for approval):
a. Grind a larger opening in the tile around the shower head to be able to access the area around the shower head threaded pipe.
b. Remove the existing sealant and determine the existing membrane type.
c. Completely seal the pipe penetration to the existing membrane using Ardex CA 20 P Plus in accordance with the manufacturer’s specifications.
d. Locally apply a compatible Ardex liquid membrane around the pipe penetration from the existing penetration onto the pipe thread.
e. After the repairs have cured, water test the penetration using the garden hose for 5 minutes.
f. If the leak does not re-occur, install a matching cover plate to cover the opening in the tile and reinstate the shower head.
g. Re-test by running the shower for 15-20 minutes.
3. If further leaks occur contact BWRA to carry out further testing.
This will likely involve spray testing the taps after removing the
cover plates, and dye flood testing the shower recess.

Investigate leaking isolation valve located under the building and fluctuating hot water supply.

Attended the property, gained access under the building and found the common cold water isolation valve located under unit 1 to be leaking and required replacement.

Put notification up on the building advising a cold water building shut down.

Investigated fluctuating hot water supply to the building.

Gained access into the hot water heater room, found the common Rinnai 28i instantaneous hot water heater to show error code 10 on the control panel. Removed the air intake fan and removed large build up of dust and debris causing blockages. Cleaned out all dust and debris and re-installed. Tested common hot water heater and after 5 minutes the hot water heater would still cut out and error 10 code would appear on the control panel.

Returned to the property, engaged a hot water specialist contractor and carried out further investigation works to locate the fault.

We found the heater leaking in fault error 10; related to blocked flue. Dismantled flue to clean as well as terminal and fan internals; some build up but nothing overly excessive - Tested heater and it went into fault error 12; relates to flame failure; gas, supply pressure tested okay. 

Inspected and cleaned flame rods, again only not minor build up; tested to same error. Continued through heater diagnostic and found that the internal computer settings were set for use with a long flue (over 7 metres), this flue is only 2-3 metres long. We have changed the settings and the heater has fired up without fail for over 20 minutes. Due to incorrect settings, the fan would be too powerful for the flue length and it was likely causing uneven flame across the burner tray and flame rods.

Left heater on and rising in temperature; this incorrect setting is an obvious fault and is the likely cause of the recent issues. No other apparent causes have been identified during the service.

Shut down the buildings water supply and drained the water from the line.

Gained access under the building, disconnected faulty common isolation valve located under unit 1 and installed new isolation valve. Turned on the buildings cold water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

PLEASE NOTE - We advise the common hot water heaters at the building are serviced on a preventative maintenance plan every 6 months. We will submit a quotation shortly for preventative maintenance works required to be undertaken.

Scope: Investigate and resolve Leak in U107 from bathroom upstairs (Unit 207)
Please contact:
Unit 207: Lachlan Murray
Mobile: 0411836895

Unit 107:
Diego Varese+61 466 550 809
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 107.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 107 and found water leaking through the ceiling through the toilet and laundry penetrations.

Gained access into unit 207 above and tested all fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Gained access into unit 206 next door, removed tile on the front face of the bath and found water pooling under the bath.

Pressure tested shower breaching piece, hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found,

Flood dye tested the bath waste pipework and no leaks were found.

Flood tested the seals where the bath meets the common wall tiles and found water leaking under the bath confirming the leak.

We found a large amount of movement within the bath and the tiles on the common shower wall to be drummy.

Returned to the property, removed 2 x drummy tiles from the common shower wall and found the shower walls to be completely rotten and requires urgent replacement.

Installed 2 x new tiles under the taps, cut out faulty sealant where the bath meets the wall tiles, installed new high grade flexible sealant where the bath meets the common wall tiles and re-grouted affected wall tiles using additive as a temporary repair until the shower/bath has been upgraded. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 206 - As the original bathroom tiles are drummy and the shower walls are water damaged behind the tiles, temporary sealing repairs will not rectify the leak. We advise the wall tiles around the bath are excavated, the gyprock shower walls are replaced, a new bath is chased into the wall and 3 x walls around the bath are re-waterproofed and re-tiled. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the sewage leak, we located a cracked joint on the common sewer pipework high up on the garage wall which is leaking sewage down the wall into the carpark.

This quotation is to block off driveway and lift Sydney water manhole lid, install scaffolding to gain access to inspection opening, reline approximately 4 - 5 meters of 225mm pipe from inspection opening downstream of boundary trap to Sydney water main using our watermark approved epoxy relining system, flow test all works, dismantle and removing scaffolding from the property.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.
  2. Close off the driveway and erect scaffold to safely access the common sewer pipework.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to prepare lines to AS-3500.
  4. Record common sewer pipework before relining.

- Relining work:

  1. Bock off driveway and lift Sydney water manhole lid.
  2. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  3. Install scaffolding to gain access to inspection opening.
  4. Reline approximately 4 - 5 meters of 225mm pipe from inspection opening downstream of boundary trap to Sydney water main using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Dismantle and remove scaffolding from the property.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  9. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  10. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

Total cost of works -  (Day Works) 9:30AM-5:00pm - $11,850.00 Plus GST

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate re-occurring sewer smell in the Dentist.

Attended the property, gained access into the Dentist and could smell a strong sewer smell.

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer inspection opening at the front right hand side of the building and used CCTV drain camera and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked with congealed upstream from the boundary trap located at the right rear of the building which is the cause of the blockage/ sewer smell in the Dentist.

Due to the pipework being over 2 meters deep and the access extremely difficult to the only way to excavate and replace the faulty sewer pipework would be with the use of a Hydro vacuum excavation truck. To prevent further common sewer blockages at the building, we advise the ground is excavated  approximately 11 meters at the rear of the building, cut out defective common sewer pipework, install new PVC pipework, fittings, flow test all works, encase the new sewer pipework with concrete to prevent further dropping, back fill trench and re-instate area. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the major sewer repairs.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 5.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 5 and found water damage and water leaking through the bedroom ceiling.

Gained access into unit 8 above, inspected the bathroom and flood dye tested the shower recess and all waste fixtures in the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. After extensive pressure testing, we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 8.

Returned to the property and engaged pipe location leak detection.

Nitrogen pressure tested hot water and found only a 10 KPI loss in pressure. It appears this leak stops and starts.

Used pipe locator to trace position of pipework and found line drops down in the kitchen and head across to the bathroom where it turns up behind the vanity in the corner of the bedroom.

Returned to the property, laid drop sheets in the bedroom and excavated large hole within the bedroom wall exposing the hot water copper pipework as advised by leak detection. 

After we opened up the bedroom wall and exposed the pipework no burst hot water pipe was found within the wall and the burst hot water pipe was found to be located within the concrete slab.

As the burst pipe is located within the concrete slab, we are unable to pin point the location to undertake repairs and an urgent hot water re-run is required deleting the burst hot water pipe within the concrete slab to rectify the leak.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 8 - We advise to re-run a new hot water service from the hot water heater in the laundry to the hot water pipe that is already exposed in the bedroom deleting the burst hot water pipework within the concrete slab. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed, we advise the resultant damage in units 5 and 8 area repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation for all resultant damage repairs after we know the full extent of the damage.

Gained access into unit 8 above, inspected the bathroom and flood dye tested the shower recess and all waste fixtures in the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. After extensive pressure testing, we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 8.

Returned to the property and engaged pipe location leak detection.

Nitrogen pressure tested hot water and found only a 10 KPI loss in pressure. It appears this leak stops and starts.

Used pipe locator to trace position of pipework and found line drops down in the kitchen and head across to the bathroom where it turns up behind the vanity in the corner of the bedroom.

Returned to the property, laid drop sheets in the bedroom and excavated large hole within the bedroom wall exposing the hot water copper pipework as advised by leak detection. 

After we opened up the bedroom wall and exposed the pipework no burst hot water pipe was found within the wall and the burst hot water pipe was found to be located within the concrete slab.

As the burst pipe is located within the concrete slab, we are unable to pin point the location to undertake repairs and an urgent hot water re-run is required deleting the burst hot water pipe within the concrete slab to rectify the leak.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 8 - We advise to re-run a new hot water service from the hot water heater in the laundry to the hot water pipe that is already exposed in the bedroom deleting the burst hot water pipework within the concrete slab. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed, we advise the resultant damage in units 5 and 8 area repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation for all resultant damage repairs after we know the full extent of the damage.

Description:
Quotation - Reline sewer vertical shaft

Following our inspection at the property, we carried out a CCTV camera survey of the common sewer pipework and located tree roots on the sewer main riser before the connection to Sydney Waters sewer main.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2-3 meters of tree root infested vertical shaft sewer line, relining from plastic on vertical shaft down to Sydney main sewer connection sealing all root infested joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin and reinstate junction using robotic cutter.

After this section has been relined any further sewer blockages in this area will Sydney Waters cost to clear. The scope of works will permanently seal all the joints the before he boards main connection point.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise resident of building water shut down.
  2. Set up safe working areas at the property
  3. Gain access to common sewer inspection points at the rear of the yard.
  4. Use high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera and sanding paddles in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework before relining.

- Relining:

  1. Reline approximately 2-3 meters of tree root infested vertical shaft sewer line, relining from plastic on vertical shaft down to Sydney main sewer connection sealing all root infested joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  2. Cure liner using hot water boiler. 
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  4. Reinstate junction using robotic cutter.
  5. Flow test relined pipework after relining.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate water leak in Unit 7.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 7 and found water damage to the bathroom ceiling, cornice and wall above the bath.

Cut a hole within the bathroom ceiling to inspect inside the ceiling cavity, found the wall high up close to the concrete ceiling to be damp.

Gained access into unit 8's bathroom, nitrogen pressure tested the shower and bath breaching pieces, hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 8

Dye tested the bath waste piping with yellow dye and the shower recess with red dye and no leak was found in unit 7's ceiling below.

Flood tested the shower walls and along the bath edge within the shower recess and after extensive flood testing of the shower, no water leaked below.

Splashed water onto the vanity basin and located water leaking down the back of the vanity onto the bathroom floor, from faulty sealant where the basin top meets the wall tiles

Flood tested unit 8's bathroom floor and eventually water leaked from the wall in unit 7's bathroom ceiling cavity, indicating faulty waterproof membrane in the original bathroom unit 8.

Installed sealant where the vanity basin meets the wall tiles to prevent further water leaking onto the bathroom floor and advised the occupant.

Further works required to be undertaken by a building contractor in unit 8 - As the water proof membrane has failed within the original bathroom causing water to leak into 7 below, we advise the entire bathroom floor is excavated, re-waterproofed and retiled to replace the faulty waterproof membrane. 

Following these repair works, we advise the water damage bathroom ceiling, cornice and wall in unit 7 is repaired and painted

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer pipework and found the downstream mainline junction has tree root infestations, used locating equipment to locate the mainline junction.

As the common sewer gully is collapsed and the mainline junction has tree root infestations and the pipework is still blocked, urgent excavation works are required to replace the collapsed pipework and mainline junction within the common sewer the line.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the collapsed common sewer pipework -  We advise to excavate the ground at the rear right of the building, cut out collapsed common sewer gully and mainline junction, use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear the common sewer line up and downstream from the collapsed pipe, install new PVC pipework and back fill trench. We will submit an URGENT quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place with the high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Please note - This is a separate blockage to the recent common sewer gully we cleared outside unit 6.

Description:
Urgent Quotation -  Common Gas Upgrade.

Following our inspection at the property, we found the majority of the common gas pipework to be original galvanized steel pipework which is rusting in multiple locations and in very bad condition, the original lead outlet piping does not comply with Australian gas standards AG-5601. To rectify further gas leaks, the common gas meter set up and manifold on the left hand side of the building is required to be upgraded.

This urgent quotation is to replace and upgrade the original galvanised steel, common gas main and meter manifolds to copper, install meter bars and remove non-approved lead outlet piping.

The following works will be undertaken: 

  1. Notify residents and isolate the gas supply to the building. 
  2. Excavate the front garden in unit 4, from the front left gas regulator down to the front of the building.
  3. Excavate and trench to allow for new copper pipework within unit 4's front garden, excavate through the building wall into the subfloor.
  4. Supply and install new 40mm copper gas main within unit 4's front garden and under the subfloor to the rear left side meter manifold location.
  5. Secure pipework under the building using brackets and fixings.
  6. Install new gas meter bars securing the meters and regulators to the wall. 
  7. Install new gas ball valves on the inlet manifold. 
  8. Cut out and remove galvanised steel inlet manifold pipework at the rear left side meter manifold and replace with new copper piping and fittings.
  9. Install new copper pipe and fittings connecting from the outlet of the meter to the first thread after the lead on the outlet pipework and previous replaced copper outlet piping.
  10. Turn the gas supply back on, test and commission the new gas supply pipework.
  11. Perform a drop test on the outlet pipe work for each meter. If we find any further leaks on the outlet pipework we will report back with our findings.
  12. Bed pipe, back fill and compact ground as per AS 3500.
  13. Reinstate common areas.
  14. Remove barricades and clean all areas where work had taken place.
  15. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 1's bedroom.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water damage to the internal bedroom wall and cornice adjacent to the bathroom.

Used moisture meter in unit 1's bedroom to confirm medium readings within the wall and cornice where the water damage appears and low reading throughout. 

Gained access into unit 4, inspected the internal wall in the bedroom and located water damage adjacent to the shower and bath taps and also along the bath edge.

Used moisture meter in unit 4's bedroom wall and located high reading of moisture along the bath edge and low readings behind the shower and bath taps.

Pressure tested the shower and bath breaching pieces and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 4.

Inspected the internal shower / bath walls and found cracked sealant where the bath meets the internal wall tiles. We also found movement in the bath which is causing the seals to crack and the bath is not recessed into the wall.

We have carried out re-sealing works around the bath edge previously in unit 4 and the seals are cracking indicating re-sealing works will not stop the water leak.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 4 as a permanent repair - As the bath is not recessed into the wall and there is movement in the bath causing the seals to crack, we advise the bath and first course of wall tiles around the bath are excavated and a new bath is installed, chased into the wall, the first course is re-waterproofed and re-tiled. We will submit a quotation shortly for the works required to be undertaken.

Once the repair works have been completed in unit 4, we advise the resultant water damaged bedroom ceiling and cornice in unit 1 and the bedroom wall in unit 4  is repaired and painted.

Description: unit 7 - Blocked balcony drainage and flooding
Invoice Description:
Investigate flooding in unit 7.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 7 and found the balcony sliding door track to be full of water.

Lifted the stainless steel drain grate out from the grated drain which runs along the balcony in front oof the sliding doors.

Found the drainage to be clear and in good working order.

Inspected the grate and found it covers the weep holes for the sliding door track, causing water to stay within the track.

As it was heavy rain at the time, we removed the drain grate which has allowed the track to release water into the drain through the weep holes to prevent further flooding.

Returned to the property, gained access and cut out stainless steel grate where the weep holes for the sliding door track are located.

Re-installed grate, tested the sliding door frame and found the weep holes are no longer blocked.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water leak in unit 12.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 12 and found peeling paint on the original timber ceiling in the bathroom.

Cut 2 x holes in the original timber ceiling to inspect inside the ceiling cavity. Found moisture, but none of the copper pipes to be leaking within the ceiling cavity.

Went outside to the right side passage and inspected the external wall outside the bathroom of unit 12 & 16.

Following our inspection of the external wall, we located a large water stain behind the common stack pipe indicating a leak from the stack branch where it goes through the wall.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in the common garages.

Attended the property after hours on Sunday 25/5 at 3.30pm, gained access into the common garage and found water dripping into carspace 33, through the concrete slab around the pipe penetrations and service duct for units above.

Stepped out the location of the leak and found unit 94 to be above, no-one was home at the time so we left a note on the door.

Returned to the property once the occupant was home at 5.30pm, gained access into unit 94 and located the laundry service riser directly above the garage leak.

Pulled out washer and dryer from the laundry to access the common stack duct, removed service riser panel and inspected the common service duct.

Found water pooling at the base of the concrete slab and water leaking from the hot waterpipe lagging where it goes into the concrete slab.  

Isolated the hot water supply to unit 94 to prevent further water damage and advised the occupant.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection to try locate the burst hot water pipe within unit 94.

Nitrogen pressure tested the hot water pipework and found a drop in pressure.

Used a listening device and pipe locating equipment to trace out the pipework and found the burst pressurized hot water pipe is located inside the concrete slab.

Excavated gyprock and tiles from the laundry service duct, cut out copper piping and performed a pressure test on the hot water pipework which is run within the concrete slab to kitchen. Following testing we confirmed the hot water pipework from the laundry to the kitchen within the concrete slab is burst and is required to be rerun.

Cut out and capped off hot water tee feeding the kitchen line to isolate the leak and prevent further water leaking through the concrete slab.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the burst pressurized hot water pipework within the concrete slab in unit 94 is deleted and is rerun from the laundry to the kitchen service duct. We will send an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed in unit 94, we advise the resultant damage repairs are carried out in unit 94. We will submit a separate quotation for these works after the plumbing works have been completed an we know the full extent of the repair works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

As discussed on the phone, please attend onsite to the property to unblock the sewerage for the complex.
Unit 1 (Ground Level) has sewerage coming up from her shower and can see it blocked outside her bathroom window. She arranged for a plumber to attend today who advised it was a strata issue linked to the main sewer.
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours sewer blockage in unit 1 on Friday night on the 23/5/26.

Urgently attended the property after, gained access into unit 1, found all the bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked and flooding sewerage out of the overflow sewer gully outside the bathroom in the common area.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment outside unit 1's bathroom. 

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate the original common sewer pipework to be broken, dislodged and major tree roots entering the pipework which was the cause of the blockage. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DGHSW

Used high pressure jet baster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree roots from the common sewer pipework. 

Flow tested all fixtures in unit 1's bathroom and common sewer pipework outside  - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where sewerage had flooded using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the tree root infested section of common earthenware sewer piping is relined, completely sealing the tree root infested pipework as a permeant repair. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further relining works required to be undertaken.
