Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out, Friday 23/5/26 - Urgent flood in unit 13.

Urgently attended the property after hours on Friday night and found unit 13's balcony drainage to be blocked, surcharging during the heavy rain and flooding the bedroom causing major damage to the carpet.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and drain cleaning equipment downstream from unit 13's balcony drain but after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage.

Located where the pipework goes into the ground on the left hand side of the building in the garden. Excavated the ground in this area and found a 100mm PVC storm water pipe.

Used reciprocating saw to cut out the pipework and found major tree root infestation which was cause of the blockage/flood in unit 13. 

Used jetting equipment to partially clear the blockage and have made the drainage pool out onto the garden floor for now, as a temporary repair and to prevent further flooding in unit 13.

Please see video link from Friday night - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DGHEY

Returned to the property, gained access and inspected the common stormwater pipework in the garden. Following our inspection, we found the common stormwater drainage to be completely full of tree root infestations. 

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - Due to the location and depth of the blocked common stormwater pipework, we advise the common stormwater drainage is re-run, deleting the tree root infested pipework within the garden. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Whilst at the building, we also found most of the common stormwater pits, pipework and drains around the property to be blocked with debris and require urgent cleaning to prevent blockages and floods at the property. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further stormwater clear out works required to be undertaken.

We advise a carpet contractor is engaged to steam clean or replace the water damaged carpet in unit 13's bedroom.

  4. Thermann boiler 2 - Redirect condense water via plastic pipe
  5. Test all works carried out,
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework under the laundry floor for units 9 and 14.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 to 3 meters of root infested original earthenware sewer laundry line, relining over heavily root infested section finishing back on to earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to units 1 & 3 and reviewed the engineers report.

Unit 1 - Found rising damp throughout the entire unit and in the common hallway next to the front door.

Lifted floor grate on the shower waste drain and inspected the waterproof membrane and found there to be no vissable water proof membrane, turn-down, seal or puddle flange installed into the drain. 

Located large gaps in the shower wall and floor grouting and poor sealant within the shower recess, allowing water to leak into the substrate.

Carried out extensive pressure testing on the shower breaching piece, hot and cold water pipes and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 1.

Unit 3 - Gained access into unit 3, which is located above unit 1.

Blocked off the shower floor drain and filled the shower tray with green dye to a level of the shower screen.

Following flood/dye testing of the waterproof membrane in unit 3, no leaks were found.

Carried out extensive pressure testing on the shower breaching piece, hot and cold water pipes and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 3.

Went outside to inspect the external wall and located missing bricks, gaps in the pointing and large holes on the external wall where water can leak into the cavity.

Following investigation works and testing, we found the rising damp in unit 1 to be caused by:

1. Poor waterproofing within the renovated bathroom of unit 1 - We advise the lot owner engages their contractor to rectify the waterproofing issues in the renovated bathroom. 

2. Poor external brickwork - Pointing, holes and missing bricks - We strata engages a remedial building contractor to undertake repairs.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Quotation - Common sewer plumbing repairs

Quotation request number QR439162

  • Issue 1: Cracked common sewer pipe in unit 2's garage.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of water disruptions and isolate the water supply.
  2. Gain access into unit 2's garage.
  3. Excavate concrete and expose around faulty cracked earthenware pipework.
  4. Cut out earthenware pipework from the cracked fitting to the base.
  5. Supply and install new PVC pipework connecting the common sewer stack.
  6. Secure pipework where required.
  7. Turn the water supply back on and flow test all works.
  8. Clean all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish.

Total cost of works for issue 1 - $2,480.00 + GST

  • Issue 2: Replace collapsed common sewer gully

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access, lay drop sheets and install barricades within the side passage.
  2. Carefully remove pavers around the collapsed common sewer gully, approximately 2m2
  3. Excavate concrete and ground exposing original earthenware sewer gully and branch line junction.
  4. Cut out collapsed earthenware sewer gully, pipework and fittings.
  5. Supply & install new PVC gully, pipework, fittings connecting onto existing common sewer pipework, raising gully above ground as per AS-3500. 
  6. Flow test all works carried out.
  7. Bed pipework, back fill trench & compact ground as per AS-3500,.
  8. Install rio bars, and steel in preparation for concreting. 
  9. Re-concrete affected area.
  10. Re-instate existing pavers.
  11. Remove associated rubbish from the property,
  12. Clean all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose once concrete has cured. 

Total cost of works for issue 2 - $7,950.00 + GST

Looked at the rainwater head and found there to be leaves collecting on the mesh guard covering the rainwater head.

Urgently attended the property, gained access to unit 2 and found the kitchen sink waste and the basin waste to be blocked.

Tried to plunge the kitchen sink, but we found the common waste stack piping to be blocked.

Disconnected the kitchen waste pipework and used electric eel extensively to clear the blockage in the common stack pipework. We removed a large amount of congealed fat from the common sewer pipework which was causing the blockage.

Reconnected kitchen waste piping and flow tested kitchen waste piping - All clear and in good working order.

Disconnected the basin waste pipework and used an electric eel downstream to try and clear the blockage, but after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage in the common waste pipework.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to the external side passage outside of unit 2.

Removed inspection opening lids on the common sewer gully outside the bathroom used a high pressure water jet blaster upstream to clear the blockage in the sewer piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found major tree root infestations growing in the earthenware sewer piping and junction connecting unit 2's basin line causing the blockage (photos attached).

Used the high pressure jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the sewer piping.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids on the common sewer gully and tested all fixtures in the bathroom of unit 2 - All in good working order.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the tree root infested common sewer pipework connecting unit 2 is relined. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Variation Quotation - Cut out and replace hot water and gas pipework within the common service riser and under the bath hob.

Whilst undertaking the quoted works and excavating the common brickwork within the service riser and additional excavation of the bath hob, we located the burst common, hot water pipe and tee within the common wall under the bath hob.

Whilst excavating, we exposed the burst pressurized pipe and found the common hot, cold and gas pipework originally laid on top of each other and covered in bricks and render. When excavating the brickwork and render, we hit the hot water pipework and gas pipework, causing damage. As the pipework was all bundled together and not been able to be cut out and replaced, we have patch repaired the burst common, hot water pipe under the bath hob using welding equipment and isolated the leak to prevent further damage.

This variation quotation is to excavate a larger hole in the bath hob and common wall, service riser, cut out and replace the common hot water and gas pipework located under the bath hob and within the common wall and service riser.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access into unit 8 and lay drop sheets in the main and ensuite bathrooms.
  2. Excavate a larger hole in the common service riser, bath hob and common wall chase exposing the hot, gas and cold water pipework.
  3. Isolate the hot, cold and gas supply to unit 8 and drain the water from the line.
  4. Cut out hot water and gas pipework under the bath hob, within the common service riser and wall chase.
  5. Supply and install new hot water and gas copper pipework under the bath hob and common service riser.
  6. Turn water supply back on testing all works.
  7. Install temporary cover over the ensuite shower wall tiles and on the bath hob until repairs are carried out.
  8. Clean all areas where work has taken place.
  9. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

AFTER HOURS BLOCKAGE

Blocked toilet at the rear - Shop and wine bar
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours sewer blockage on Sunday night located at the rear of the property.

Urgently attended the property after hours at 6:30pm pm on Sunday night, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage at the rear of the property.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment to the rear of the building.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate tree roots entering the original common sewer pipework which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet baster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree roots from the common sewer pipework. 

Flow tested the common sewer pipework - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where sewerage had flooded using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty section of earthenware sewer piping is excavated and replaced with new PVC piping and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Quotation - Common sewer relining & repairs

Quotation request number - 00185293

Following our inspection at the building, we found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework on the main sewer line for approximately 10 meters on the Western side of the building.

As the main sewer pipework has been run in the ground very shallow and the access is easy, it is more cost effective for the building to excavate the ground, cut out 10 meters tree root infested sewer pipework and install new PVC pipework and fittings rather than relining the main line. Please note, the sewer pipework on the Eastern side of the building has already been excavated and replaced with new PVC pipework. 

We also found tree root infestations entering upstream from the northern, middle & southern overflow sewer gully's that require relining repairs which is located under the concrete and building.

Please see below scope of works we recommend as a permeant repair to prevent further common sewer blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • PART A -  URGENT WORKS - Excavate the ground, cut out 10 meters of tree root infested main line sewer pipework and install new PVC pipework and fittings on the Western side of the building
  1. Advise residents of building water shut down. 
  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Excavate the ground exposing approximately 10 meters of tree root infested main sewer line.
  4. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  5. Cut 10 meters of tree root infested main line sewer pipework and fittings,
  6. Supply and install new PVC pipework and fittings connecting onto existing common sewer pipework.
  7. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  8. Bed pipework, back fill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

Total cost of works for PART A - $5,800.00 + GST

  • PART B- Excavate, replace 3 x faulty flat bottom earthenware sewer gully's and reline upstream 3 x branch lines towards the building
  1. Barricade around 3 x separate work area.
  2. Excavate the ground, exposing 3 x original earthenware sewer gullies.
  3. Cut out 3 x original earthenware sewer gullies and pipework.
  4. Supply and install 3 x PVC gullies, pipework and fittings.
  5. Connect inlets to 3 x gullies.
  6. Set up relining equipment on the Western side of the building.
  7. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  8. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  9. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  10. Reline approximately 5 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework located upstream of the middle sewer gully, sealing tree root infested earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  11. Reline approximately 4 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework located upstream of the Southern sewer gully, sealing tree root infested earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  12. Reline approximately 5 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework located upstream of the Northern sewer gully, sealing tree root infested earthenware pipework using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  13. Cure 3 x separate liners using hot water boiler.
  14. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  15. Flow test all works carried out.
  16. Bed 3 x new gully's and pipework, back fill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500.
  17. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  18. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  19. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  20. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer.
  21. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We strongly suggest this repair be completed with an approved epoxy resin. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Common sewer repairs on the right hand side of the building

Following the preventative maintenance sewer clear out works and our CCTV camera survey, we found the base of the 2 x common sewer stack pipes on the right hand side of the building to be badly collapsed and major tree root infestations are entering the original common sewer pipework which will cause continual sewer blockages. We have cleared the tree roots from the pipework, but if repairs are not undertaken the tree roots will aggressively grow back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur. As the original earthenware pipework has collapsed at the base of 2 x common sewer stack, sewerage is leaking into the ground and eroding the subsoil which will create further problems to the building. 

This quotation is to saw cut the concrete slab and exarate the ground outside unit 3, cut out tree root infested/collapsed original earthenware sewer pipework work at the base of the stack, junction and approximately 2 meters of pipework, install new PVC pipework and fittings, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. Also to reline the base of the sewer stack outside unit 1 completely sealing the collapsed and tree root infested original earthenware pipework. As the affected stack runs through the concrete stairs, relining would be the most cost effective solution to rectify this section of common sewer pipework.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Sewer stack on the right hand side outside unit 3
  1. Notify residents of excavation works required on the right hand side of the building & water disruptions. 
  2. Install safety barricades around work area.
  3. Excavate trees within the garden bed.
  4. Saw cut concrete approximately 2 meters, excavate concrete using jack hammer and ground exposing the tree root infested/collapsed section of earthenware sewer piping and fittings.
  5. Turn off water supply and drain the water from the line.
  6. Cut out approximately 2 meters of tree root infested and collapsed section of earthenware sewer pipework, junction and fittings.
  7. Supply and install new PVC piping, fittings, junction connecting onto existing common sewer piping and install inspection opening at the base of the stack.
  8. Use CCTV drain camera downstream and ensure all clear.
  9. Turn on the water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  10. Bed pipework, back fill trench and compact fill as per AS 3500.
  11. Re-concrete affected common area.
  12. Remove associated rubbish, materials and fill from the property.
  13. Clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.
  • Reline the base of the sewer stack on the right hand side of the building outside unit 1

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise affected residents of water disruptions. 
  2. Set up relining equipment on the right hand side of the building. 
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  4. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  5. Measure, cut and prepare new line. 
  • Relining works
  1. Advise affected units to not use their waste fixtures. 
  2. Reline the base of the collapsed and tree root infested sewer stack outside unit 1 covering all root infested joints, using water marked approved liner with 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  8. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  9. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken. 

PLEASE NOTE -  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our relining products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate urgent water leak in unit 5.

Urgently attended property, gained access to unit 5 and found water leaking from the bulkhead ceiling in the bathroom, running down the shower wall.

We will send an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed and we know the extent of the damage, we will submit a quotation for all resultant damage repairs, painting and tiling works in unit 5 & 8. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property, gained access into the basement carpark and found water leaking through the carpark walls all the way along the Curlewis St side.

Inspected the buildings main water meter at the front and found the dials were not ticking over and come to a complete stop, indicating no water leaks from the main cold water pipework.

Outside there is heavy rain, 2 extremely large downpours and the main stormwater pump in the carpark has pumped out 2 x times onto the road and gutter whilst at the property. 

On the Curlewis streetscape, heavy rain is being absorbed into the grass, it is not ponding and water is flowing straight into the basement car park below. 

Inspected the common stormwater drains in the basement and they are flowing towards the main stormwater pit.

We found the water leaking into the basement is caused by the rain outside, filtering down to the basement through the grass and sand in the nature strip.

Investigate urgent gas smell in the Float Centre shop.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak outside units 1 & 2.

Attended the property, gained access into the common hallway and found wet carpet at the front entrance to unit 2.

Gained access into unit 2, lifted the carpet at the front door and found the concrete slab to be dry underneath. Adjacent to the leak is unit 1.

Gained access into unit 1 and located the bathroom to be adjacent to the leak, carried out extensive flood/dye testing of the bathroom fixtures and found no water to be leaking into unit 2 from our testing.

Advised the occupants in unit 2 to monitor the leak and advise if any dye penetrates the hallway wall.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 1 and carried out extensive pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply. Following testing we located a drop in pressure indicating a leak.

Removed shower mixer cover-plate, took apart the mixer and found the cartridge to be leaking back into the common wall causing the leak in unit 2.

Went to the supplier and picked up a new mixer cartridge matching the existing, isolated the hot and cold water supply and installed the new mixer cartridge. 

The common cold water isolation valve for unit 1 does not completely isolate and requires to be replaced.

Following testing, we found the new mixer cartridge we installed is also leaking. Carried out a static pressure test on the common cold water pipework and found it to be 700kpa which is too much pressure for the mixer. 

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - To rectify the leak, we advise a new shower mixer is installed and a pressure reduction valve is installed on the cold water pipework in the common meter cupboard. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 1.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage down the driveway. 

Urgently attended the property, gained access into garage 5, removed inspection openings on the common sewer stack within the garage and found the common sewer line to be completely blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran equipment into the garage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole the blockage and release the common sewer line.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found major tree root infestations growing in the earthenware sewer piping from the base of the sewer stack downstream to main line for approximately 15 meters causing the blockage.

Please see CCTV video link of tree roots entering the original earthenware pipework in multiple locations - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DFEM1

Used the high pressure jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer piping.

Flow tested common sewer line - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested sewer pipework is not repaired, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages will re-occur. 

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise the tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework is relined downstream the common sewer stack in the garage as a permeant repair. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Removed ceiling tile and inspected inside the ceiling cavity. Following our inspection, no leaks were found to be coming from the common drainage pipes within the ceiling cavity.

I’m hoping you might be able to provide a quote for a plumbing repair at 7/21 Maroubra Rd, Maroubra. Below is the report received from the initial attending plumber with some photos attached. We understand that the leak is currently running externally rather than into the unit below. Would there be any cost in having you provide this quote?

I called to the property on Monday, 19 March and  investigated the water leak above the bathroom window of unit 3. I initially believed that the leak was the result of a cracked bath breech and leaking taps in unit 7 bathroom. I installed a new stainless steel seat in the bath breech and repaired the hot and cold bath taps.

I returned to the property on Friday, 21 March to confirm that the leak had stopped. The repair had not stopped the leak. I pressure tested the bath breech in unit 7 and installed new hot and cold bath taps and extenders.

I returned to unit 7 on Wednesday, 26 March when it was apparent that the previous repairs had been unsuccessful. I pressure tested the water service and confirmed that we had a burst cold water pipe in the bathroom. I opened the bathroom wall and exposed the cold water pipe that supplies the bath and shower (photo 1). The burst appears to be located below the bath and shall be very difficult to access without doing extensive damage to the bathroom. 

The best option is to connect to the cold water service on the external wall, extend the pipe to the front wall of the building, drill into the shower wall to supply the bath and shower, and drill into the vanity to supply the basin tap. This will effectively disconnect and by-pass the burst water pipe below the bath. The proposed by-pass line is indicated in red in photo 2.

Whist this is the fastest and most cost-effective way to fix the leak, I'm concerned about the condition of the pipes that we are connecting to inside the shower wall. The pipes feel thin and fragile. Whist I'm confident that the repair will be successful, I'm worried that further burst pipes may occur in unit 7 bathroom.

The only way to safeguard against further burst pipes is replace all hot and cold pipes in shower wall as marked in red in photo 5. We would then need to run a new hot water pipe from the kitchen to the front of the building to supply the bathroom (marked in red in photo 6). This would eliminate all existing hot and cold pipes in unit 7 bathroom. On the downside, it would add considerable cost to the plumbing repair and require more extensive restorative work in unit 7 bathroom It would also add visible pipework to the external wall of the building.

Kind Regards,
Matthew Butcher
Licensed Real Estate Agent & Strata Manager

Invoice Description:
Investigate 2 x plumbing issues at the building.

Attended the property, gained access into the common foyer outside unit 8 and found stained carpet and a damp smell along the external wall.

Went upstairs to the front walkway at the entrance and found the downpipes have been removed, leaving a hole in the walkway floor and exposed brickwork where the previous downpipe penetrates the walkway concrete.

Used a hose to flood test the walkway and wall where the downpipe was removed.

Following testing, we found water leaks into the external wall and into the foyer causing wet carpet.

Used sand cement to patch render the brickwork where the downpipe was removed to try and prevent water leaking into the wall.

Found the concrete base of the sewer drainage to be cracked, causing an air gap where the sewer downpipe joins the drainage pipework.

Removed cracked concrete and used sand cement to re-seal the common sewer joint where the 2 x pipes meet at the floor.

Returned to the property after the sand cement re-seal had set and no further sewer smells were found by garage 24.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

SUBJECT
Leak from pipe into basement party shop
JOB DESCRIPTION
November 20th
Whilst on site, DA Fire reported to the BM that there was a leak inside the party shop in the basement
coming from above. The carpet was soaked and it appeared to be a sewerage leak
Work order issued to Treat Plumbing to investigate
Treat Plumbing attended on the same day and reported the following
"Inspected and found a copper stack which goes up through the floor and is leaking above. Stepped out the
leak and located the affected copper stack to be in between the Ugg shop and watch shop. There is an access
panel inside the watch shop ceiling that we were unable to open today as it is above the glass cabinets and
they were not aware of us attending."
The BM arranged for Treat to return on Thursday the 28th
The BM advised both the Tudor shop and the Ugg shop. The manager of the UGG shop confirmed that the
28th was ok.
Tudors response: We would need to know the location on where you are planning to investigate inside our
Tudor store. Will also need to confirm in advanced whether you require to access or not at least 2 days before
so we can organise security. Please also confirm you are happy to compensate the security cost.
Treat Plumbing reattend on the 28th and only inspected inside the UGG store. After the investigation they
reported the following
Attended the property, gained access into the ground floor UGG shop, cut a hole in the gyprock wall and
found we were unable to access the common stack pipework from the UGG shop side. We confirmed that an
opening must be made in the wall of the Tudor shop to access the leaking common pipework. Please see
attached photo of where the first hole will be made in the Tudor watch shop. Please see a previous photo,
before the shop renovation of common stack pipework located behind the Tudor shop wall. We need to
schedule to return (possibly after hours) to access the pipework from the Tudor watch shop - Please advise
when we can return to undertake the further works. We advise that an access panel be installed in the Tudor
watch shop at this location for future maintenance.
Whilst on site Treat stopped water leaking from one of the toilets in the basement
December
The BM contacted the Tudor store who advised that security would be required to man the store from 6pm to
9am on the night that the plumbers attend. A quote for the security was provided and was approved. The
owners corporation will arrange the make good repair work & inspection openings etc.
Invoice received from Treat (1270512)
March
The BM emailed the SC the information and approval was received to proceed with the necessary repairs
Work order issued to Treat Plumbing on the 27th of March

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked balcony in unit 11.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 11 and found the balcony drain to be blocked and surcharging in heavy rain.

Lifted drain covers and used electric eel, milling tool, camera CCTV and wet vac to clear out the branch line picking up unit 11 balcony drain.

Following this, we found building material in the branch line. It started raining really heavily and water started bubbling up from the floor drain indicating a blockage downstream in the common drainage.

Gained access to the front right side garden and located a 90mm PVC drain connected to the balcony drains, cut a section of pipe and relieved water to prevent unit 11's balcony from surcharging.

Set up jet blasting equipment and used jetting heads downstream of the downpipe to clear the blockage in the ground. We were unsuccessful and our jet blasting equipment was getting stuck.

Re-turned to the property, set up jet blasting equipment and used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear the common stormwater pipework downstream of the downpipe. Cleared out a large amount of dirt and tree root infestation from the common storm water drainage.

Used large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera from the curb and gutter upstream and removed a large amount of sand, and debris from the line indicating a collapse in the pipework.

Excavated in the front garden area and found the 90mm PVC stormwater pipework under the ground to be badly collapsed and broken, causing sand and tree roots to enter the pipework causing blockages.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to gain access to the front garden, excavate the ground exposing the collapsed, tree root infested common storm water pipework, cut out and remove tree root infested pipework, use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear the common storm water pipework downstream, supply and install new storm water pipework, flow test all works, back-fil trench and re-instate the garden. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further URGENT works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked laundry for unit 2.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2’s laundry located under the building and found the laundry sink to be blocked and surcharging when in use.

Removed trap, used drain cleaning equipment downstream, but were unable to clear the blocked common laundry waste pipework.

Used CCTV camera upstream of the overflow gully outside and found major tree root infestation entering the inlet of the original earthenware pipework which was the cause of the blockage.

Video link -- https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DREDI

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high-pressure water jet blaster with large tree cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree infestation entering upstream of the inlet of the overflow gully.

Re-connected laundry waste pipework and flow tested - All clear and in good working order.

Following our CCTV camera survey of the branch line connecting to unit 1's laundry waste, we located tree root infestations where the PVC waste connected to the earthenware drainage under the building. To prevent blockages in unit 1's laundry waste pipework, we are required to gain access under the building via the small man hole, cut out laundry 1's laundry waste pipework, remove the tree root infestations from the common waste pipework and re-connect drainage for unit 1's laundry waste.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages in unit 2's laundry - We advise to reline the tree infested original sewer pipe upstream from the overflow gully under the stairs, completely sealing the tree root infested pipework as a permanent repair to prevent further blockages. Also to gain access under the building via the small man hole, cut out unit 1's laundry waste, remove tree root infestations from the waste pipework and re-install pipework. We will submit an urgent quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - This is a completely separate issue to the previous reline we undertook to reline approximately 6 meters of 150mm root infested earthenware pipework from PVC section on boundary trap shaft to vertical shaft down to boards main sewer connection.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 6.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 6 and found water damage to the timber flooring in the living room.

Unit 4 also advised the water leak is currently causing water damage to the bathroom ceiling, cornice and wall (photos attached).

Isolated the water supply in unit 6, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply.

Following extensive pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the cold water supply indicating a burst cold water pipe in unit 6 which is the cause of the leak.

We also used pipe locator to trace out the cold water service on the common/external balcony wall which is located adjacent to the bath.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 6 - We advise remove affected external brick work from the balcony adjacent to the bathroom existing burst pressurised cold water copper pipework, turn off the water supply, cut out burst cold water copper pipework and replace with new copper pipework. fittings, turn on the water supply and test all works and repair brickwork on the external wall. We will submit urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the burst pipe has been repaired in unit 6, we advise the resultant water damaged bathroom ceiling, cornice and wall is repaired and painted. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting in unit 4.

We also advise a building contractor is engaged to repair or replace the resultant water damage timber flooring in unit 6.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in the car park.

Attended the property, gained access into the car park and found water leaking through the concrete slab below units 3 and 5.

Gained access into units 3, 4 and 5, found all the balcony spitter pipes to be completely blocked, causing water to pool in the courtyard. 

Returned to the property, engaged 2 x plumbers, set up high pressure water jet blaster and equipment.

Gained access into unit 3, used high pressure water jet blaster with whippet hose to clear the blocked spitter pipes causing water to leak under the bench seat.

Gained access into unit 4, used high pressure water jet blaster with whippet hose to clear the blocked spitter pipes causing water to leak on the tiles.

Gained access into unit 5, after using extensive drain cleaning equipment we were unable to clear the blocked spitter pipes.

We tried to excavate a hole through the existing spitter pipe with a jack hammer but we were unsuccessful. The blocked spittrer pipes are causing water to pool and leaking through the tiles under the timber bench and into the car park below.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 5 - We advise to core drill 2 x new holes through the external wall, install 2 x new spitter pipes. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Over flowing releif gully

Sewer blockage
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Sunday 23/3/25 - Urgent sewer blockage

Urgently attended the property after hours, found all bathroom fixtures to be blocked and surcharging sewer outside.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed decking to access the common sewer inspection opening, used high pressure water jet blaster and drain cleaning equipment but after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage.

Returned to the property on Tuesday 25/3/25 and Wednesday 26/3/25, engaged 2 x plumbers and set up high pressure water jet blaster truck.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment to locate a 2nd inspection opening buried under the front nature strip on the street.

Excavated the ground locating inspection opening, removed inspection opening and used high pressure water jet blaster with multiple large jet blasting heads.

Following extensive jet blasting for a further 8 x hours and with the use of CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment, we found major tree roots entering through the original earthenware vertical dropper to Sydney Waters sewer mains. This is located in the middle of Old South Head Rd. 

We’ve attempted to clear out all tree roots, but the roots are so large it takes up 1/2 of the diameter of pipework. There is also sand coming into line indicating the sewer pipework located under Old South Head Rd has collapsed.

We contacted Sydney Water emergency who advised they will urgently attend the property to inspect the issue. Sydney water reference number - 94490787

Sydney Water urgently attended the property, inspected their assets and advised the Sydney Water sewer main under the road is not blocked or affected by the tree root within the branch line, they attempted to clear out the large amount of thick tree toots but were unable to clear the blockage. As the branch line is owned by the property owner up to the point of connection to the Sydney Water system, this is a lot owners cost to repair.

As the tree root infested pipe work is located deep under Old South Head Road, we are trying to get Sydney water collapse services to undertake excavation and pipe work repairs to the sewer pipework under the road. 

Sydney Water require CCTV video evidence showing the tree root infested pipework under the road before taking any liability for repairs. As the sewer line is completely blocked under the road we cannot see anything on our CCTV drain camera.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise the owners of the house do not use any waste fixtures,  use aqua vacuum to suck out all sewerage from the blocked sewer pipework located under the road, so we can then undertake a CCTV video to show video evidence to Sydney Water of the collapsed and tree root infested pipework located under the road. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Please note - We have left the inspection opening open on the nature strip to prevent further blockages occurring inside the property and then cleaned the area where works took place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations to be entering the original earthenware sewer pipework and junction downstream from the common trades toilet on the ground floor.

This quotation is to disconnect and remove the common traders toilet to access the common sewer pipework, reline approximately 5 to 6 meters of tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework downstream the toilet, re-instate junctions with the use of robotic cutter and install satellite junction repair on the tree root infested main line junction connecting common trades toilet branch line, re-install existing trades toilet and flow test all works carried out.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.
  2. Gain access into the common trades toilet.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster, milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to prepare lines to AS-3500.
  4. Record common sewer pipework before relining.
  5. Set up relining equipment into the garage.
  6. Measure cut and prepare liner. 

- Relining work:

  1. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 5 to 6 meters of tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework downstream from the common trades toilet, using a watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  3. Install satellite junction reline repair on tree root infested junction on the main line connecting trades toilet branch line, using a watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  4. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  6. Re-instate junctions with the use of robotic cutter.
  7. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  8. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  9. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  10. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  11. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  12. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree roots to be entering the original earthenware sewer pipework on the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main sewer. 

We also found a contractor has drilled a Condit pipe through the common sewer pipework located under the footpath. We advise the relining works are undertaken after the pipe has been repair under the footpath, completely sealing the entire pipework to prevent tree roots entering. . 

This quotation is reline 21 meters of tree root infested 150mm diameter original common earthenware  pipework from the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main junction located on the road, using our watermark approved epoxy relining system and reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.
  2. Gain access into lot 3.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster, milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to prepare lines to AS-3500.
  4. Record common sewer pipework before relining.
  5. Set up relining equipment into the garage.
  6. Measure cut and prepare liner. 

- Relining work:

  1. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline 21 meters of tree root infested 150mm diameter original common earthenware  pipework from the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main junction located on the road, using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  5. Reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  9. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Common hot water heater service.

Whilst on the roof we found 1 out of the 2, common 265 litre heavy duty Rheem gas hot water heaters to be turned off. We tried to re-start the heater multiple times, but after multiple attempts we were unable to get the heater working. We left faulty common hot water heater turned off and the building is currently running off 1 x common hot water heater.

This quotation is to service the 1 x faulty 265 litre Rheem heavy duty gas hot water heater in the rooftop plant room.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Visual Inspection (for any damage/leaks/rust/faults etc) of system in plant room area that is related to the Hot Water System.
  2. Test that the hot water system is at the correct temperature (both in storage and ring main).
  3. Test thermostat settings and differentials.
  4. Test that the hot water is circulating back to the boilers/storage tanks at the correct flow rate.
  5. Test the water pressure is correct for that particular hot water service (that is not too high or too low).
  6. Test for leaks on Pressure Relief Valves (PRV) and/or Temperature and Pressure Relief Valves (TPRV).
  7. Test for correct operation and sequencing.
  8. Removal and cleaning for dust and debris in all applicable areas of hot water system (inside burner, control box, wiring etc).
  9. Visual inspection of all areas of wiring for hot spots, loose connections etc.
  10. Test for faulty sensors (flame, temperature, flow etc.)
  11. Test that the all-isolation valves are in working order.
  12. Test for correct inlet gas pressures.
  13. Test for correct gas burner pressures.
  14. Test for correct operation of gas solenoids.
  15. Test for correct operation of air switches (where applicable).
  16. Removal and cleaning of burner train, sensors and ignition system.
  17. Testing of flue dampeners (where applicable)
  18. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
Invoice Description:
Common hot water heater service.

Job completed as per quotation number 25841 to service the 1 x faulty 265 litre Rheem heavy duty gas hot water heater in the rooftop plant room.

The following works were undertaken:

  1. Arrived to heater 1 not working and heater 2 at 75 degrees.
  2. Heater 1 required a new pilot.
  3. Supplied and installed new HSI IGNITOR and heater now functions; brought up to temperature and reintroduced.
  4. Both heaters serviced and in working order; temperatures brought down to 70 degrees.
  5. Tested all works caried out - all in good working order.
  6. Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Removed associated rubbish from the property. 

PLEASE NOTE - Following the hot water servicing and investigation works, we found heater 1 is due for a relief valve replacement and the return water was not hot, pump was very hot; found to be a bad impeller bearing and a replacement pump is required. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework.

Following our CCTV camera survey, we found a 4-5 meter section of common sewer piping to be holding sewage with backfall due to the pipes dropping over time.

This quotation is to reline approximately 4-5 meters of dropped sewer mainline using a watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  2. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  3. Set up relining equipment, measure, cut and prepare new liner.
  4. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  5. Reline approximately 4-5 meters of dropped sewer mainline, relining from stack junction on mainline downstream covering all dropped sewer mainline pipework finishing back onto earthenware pipe using a watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin
  6. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  7. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  8. Flow test all works carried out.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  11. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  12. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer.
  13. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We strongly suggest this repair be completed with an approved epoxy resin. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500. Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Also to install a satellite junction repair where unit 7's branch line connects to the main line completely sealing the tree root infested pipework as a full proof repair. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Investigate water leaks in the carpark.

13/2 - Attended the property, gained access into the carpark and met with the site contact.

Inspected the building plan provided and walked around the carpark to identify leaks from the carpark ceiling and pipe penetrations up through the concrete slab.

Following our inspection on a dry day, we confirmed the majority of the leaks are caused by rain leaking through the surface water drainage, downpipe penetrations and construction joints indicating faulty waterproof membrane from the courtyard above.

  1. Leak from downpipe penetration outside entrance to block 18.
  2. Leak from hole in the concrete slab above carspace 81. 
  3. Leak from existing PVC drip tray outside entrance to block 7.
  4. Leak from cable penetration within carspace 51.
  5. Leaking drip tray within carspace 35 collecting water from construction joints.
  6. Construction joints within the concrete slab leaking within carspace 25.
  7. Water leak from downpipe penetration outside entrance to block 3, carspace 16.
  8. Leak from sewer stack penetration below units 114 & 116.

Whilst inspecting the leaks, we also altered common cold pipework in the bin room extending the hose tap and copper pipework past the wall which was being removed installing new pipe and fittings.

21/2 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 114 & 116, carried out extensive flood testing to all waste fixtures and found no water to be leaking into the carpark from the common stack piping connecting the bathrooms of unit 114 & 116.

Sealed flashing with high grade flexible sealant and installed waterproof membrane over the flashing, vent and roof penetration to prevent water leaking.

Further works required to be undertaken by a building contractor - As a full proof solution to prevent water leaking into the carpark, we advise a building contractor is engaged to remove pavers in the courtyard and carry out waterproofing repairs to prevent water leaking during rain events.

Further works required to be undertaken by Treat Plumbing - As a temporary solution, we advise new drip trays are installed to catch the water leaking from pipe penetrations, holes in the slab and construction joints discharging water onto the carpark floor and the existing drip tray are re-sealed. Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked and leaking common toilet.

Attended the property, found the common toilet to be constantly leaking and blocked. 

We found the inlet valve and outlet valve to be faulty and the entire faulty toilet cistern required replacement. 

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer stack in the garage and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked in the ground. 

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in the car park.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream from the common sewer stack to clear out major tree roots within the original earthenware junction on the main line connecting the common toilet branch line.

Flow tested the toilet and still found the toilet waste pipework to be blocked. After multiple attempts we were unable to get our jet blasting equipment upstream the common branch line junction.

Returned to the property, disconnected and removed the common toilet to access the common sewer pipework. Please note, we carefully removed the toilet but the toilet broke as it was originally concreted to the ground.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in the common toilet.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the common original earthenware branch pipework.

CCTV video link downstream from common toilet - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DNJQK

Supplied and installed new toilet and new cistern, connecting water and waste sealing to the ground using high grade flexible sealant.

Flow tested common toilet and common sewer pipework outside - All clear and in good working order. Please note - If the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Removed broken toilet and broken cistern from the property. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken on the common sewer pipework  - We advise the tree root infested original common sewer pipework downstream from the common toilet is relined, completely sealing the tree root infested pipework as a permeant repair to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 504.

Attended the property to investigate the water leak in 504's bathroom and separate toilet ceiling. Inspected the ceiling cavity and found water dripping through the ceiling penetrations.

Gained access into unit 604 above, carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 604.

Performed dye testing on the bath waste pipework, shower recess and toilet waste and no dye was found to be leaking into unit 504. 

Inspected the shower recess in unit 604 and found cracked wall tiles within the first course allowing water to leak under the bath. This was not causing the leak into unit 504 below.

Inspected within the ceiling cavity and located water leaking through the common stack penetration from unit 704 above.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 704, undertook a nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water pipes and found a drop in pressure on the hot water pipe indicating a burst pressurized pipe within unit 704.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection to try locate the burst hot water pipe within unit 704.

Nitrogen pressure tested the hot water pipework and found a drop in pressure. Used a listening device and pipe locating equipment to trace out the pipework and found the burst pressurized hot water pipe is located inside the concrete slab from the laundry to the kitchen and is required to be rerun.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the common hot water pipework within the concrete slab in unit 704 is deleted and is rerun from the laundry to the kitchen, we will send an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 704.

Once the plumbing works have been completed in unit 704, we advise the resultant damage repairs are carried out in units 504, 604 & 704. We will submit a separate quotation for these works after the plumbing works have been completed an we know the full extent of the repair works required to be undertaken.

Following dye testing in unit 604, we found the common shower recess to have cracked tiles within the first course of wall tiles and faulty waterproof membrane causing water to leak under the bath. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 604.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Friday 14/2/25 - Urgent sewer blockage in lot 15

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into lot 15, found the toilet to be completely blocked and surcharging when in use.

Used drain cleaning equipment downstream from the toilet but we were unable to clear the blockage in the common sewer pipework.

Returned to the property the following day on Saturday 15/2/25, engaged 2nd plumber and set up high pressure water jet blaster truck, equipment and 2 x mini reels to access the bathroom in lot 15 at the rear of the property.

Carefully disconnected and removed the toilet to access the common sewer pipework.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the toilet to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment to locate major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework approxitemely 8 meters downstream from the toilet under the large trees. The common sewer pipework has cracked and broken allowing tree roots to enter the pipework.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework.

Re-installed toilet sealing to the ground and flow tested - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages in lot 15 - We advise the tree root infested and broken section of common sewer pipework approxitemely 8 meters downstream from the toilet is relined completely sealing the pipework as a full proof solution to prevent further blockages, We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leak from the front awning.

24/1 - Attended the property, gained access and located water damage and water leaking from the access panel in front awning outside the Thai Massage shop.

Set up step ladder and gained access onto the awning roof above the Thai Massage shop. Found some leaves blocking the outlet to the box gutter causing the box gutter to hold water.

Removed the leaves, opened the access panel below and tested the drainage. Following testing, we found the drainage to be in good working order and no leaks were found.

28/1 - Returned to the property, gained access onto the awning roof with 2 x plumbers and inspected the water leak. Opened access panel and confirmed the leaks were coming from the awning roof and flashings and not the drain.

Where the wall flashing meets the brickwork, the flashing has come off the wall and there are cacks in some of the surrounding sealant above the affected area.

Used high grade flexible sealant to cover all affected areas of flashing and applied 3 x coats of waterproof membrane to the box gutter join.

29/1 - Returned to the property, gained access and opened the access panel to inspect the leak. Once the access panel opened water leaked from the awning.

Tested the awning flashing by pouring buckets of water over the wall and water leaked below through the access hatch.

Dried the area and applied more sealant to try and eliminate the source of the leak.

31/1 - Returned to the property, gained access, opened the access panel to inspect the leak and found water leaking after last nights rain.

Gained access onto the roof with 2 x plumbers and inspected the awning.

Following our inspection on the awning roof, we found water could be leaking from the flashings, joins or screw holes and the entry point will be difficult to locate.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to gain access onto the awning with 2 x plumbers and install waterproof membrane covering all joins, flashings and screw holes within the entire section of awning roof above the Thai Massage shop. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 12's carspace.

Attended the property, gained access into the common garages and found water had leaked into unit 12's carspace.

Inspected and found water leaks from the common stormwater drainage and concrete slab penetration below unit 10 garden.

Gained access into unit 10 and located the stormwater downpipe in the garden, disconnected the downpipe drainage and flow tested the common waste pipework.

Following testing, we found the carpark drainage to be faulty and the pipework to have an air gap which is not sealed causing a leak from the drainage.

Poured some water around the pipe penetration and also found water leaks through the concrete slab around the pipework indicating the waterproof membrane in the unit 10's garden has failed.

CCTV camera survey of the downpipe drainage and found it to be partially blocked, used drain cleaning equipment to clear out debris from the pipework.

Carried out a temporary repair to the common drainage in the carpark by sealing the air gap with high grade flexible sealant.

Description:
URGENT LEAK INTO HOSPITAL (BM Advised UPS/Battery room)

RELIEF bm IS EMAILING ADDITIONAL DETAILS.
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 22/1/25 - Investigate urgent water leak in the private hospital.

Urgently attended the property after hours, met with the building manager and inspected the water leak in the Private hospital, Level 6 UPS room.

Found water leaking through a crack within the concrete ceiling slab below units 701 and 702.

Gained access into unit 701, isolated the cold water supply and carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the cold water supply and no drop in pressure was found. Turned the water supply back on to unit 701 and pressure testing has caused low water pressure in the toilet and 3 x basin taps.

Knocked on unit 702, but was unable to gain access at the time.

23/1 - Returned to the property the following day with 2 x plumbers, inspected the water leak in level 6 private hospital and found it has come to a slow drip now and the hallway floors are dry.

Gained access into unit 701, carried extensive pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes.

Cut a hole within the gyprock service riser wall outside unit 702 in the common hallway and found the wall cavity to be dry.

Disconnected the washing machine and dryer within unit 701s laundry, cut a hole within the laundry wall and found the wall cavity to be damp and wet.

Cut a series of holes within the laundry wall to open up the damp cavity and could not find the source of the leak.

24/1 - Returned to the property, gained access to the private hospital on level 6 UPS room and installed a temporary drip tray to catch residual water leaking and prevent further water damage. 

Gained access into unit 701, carried out further investigation works and no water leaks were found. 

Disconnected the basin tap mixer and found perished rubber blocking the cartridge filter causing low water pressure to 3 x basin taps.

We found the water leak in the private hospital on level 6 UPS room has to come to a stop and has not returned. We consider this to be a one off water leak. We advise the leak is monitored and re-inspected if the leak returns. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 701 - Isolating the water supply from the mini taps under the basin has caused debris to block the filters on the mixer cartridge. We advise 3 x blocked mixer cartridges are replaced. We have sent some photos to our supplier and are awaiting a response to whether the cartridges can be replaced or the entire mixer need to be replaced. Once we have received the information from the suppliers, we will submit a quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

Following the investigation works, there is resultant damage to the common hallway wall outside unit 702 and to the laundry walls within unit 701. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

Investigate 2 x separate water leaks in the garages.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty common sewer pipe work is relined. After all works have been completed in unit 12, we advise the resultant water damaged kitchen ceiling and vent in unit 8 is repaired and painted. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 8.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent after hours sewer blockage we cleared in lot 5 and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree roots to be entering the original earthenware sewer pipework approximately 8 meters and 13 meters downstream from the inspection opening in lot 5.

This quotation is to reline 6 meters of tree root infested original earthenware pipework approximately 8 meters downstream from the inspection opening in lot 5, using a watermark approved epoxy relining system. Also to install satellite junction reline repair upstream from the boundary trap in lot 12, sealing over the tree root infested junction connecting lot 5 and 6 using a watermark approved epoxy relining system.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.
  2. Gain access into lots 5 and 12.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster, milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to prepare lines to AS-3500.
  4. Record common sewer pipework before relining.
  5. Set up relining equipment into the garage.
  6. Measure cut and prepare liner. 

- Relining work:

  1. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline 6 meters of tree root infested original earthenware pipework approximately 8 meters downstream from the inspection opening in lot 5, using a watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  3. Install satellite junction reline repair upstream from the boundary trap in lot 12 cover sealing over tree root infested junction connecting lot 5 and 6, using a watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  4. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  9. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  10. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  11. Investigate 2 x water leaks at the property.

Attended the property, gained access into the car park and found water leaking through the concrete slab around the air conditioning pipes under unit 6.

We were unable to gain access into unit 6 on our inspection and left a note on their door to contact us.

Investigated 2nd water leak, causing water to leak down the councils footpath.

Carried out investigation works to locate a leaking irrigation pipe causing the leak and also high water bills for the building. As advised by the site contact, we capped off the leaking irrigation pipework to isolate the water leak.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 6, found water damage to the internal wall adjacent to the toilet.

Jack hammered a hole within the badly water damaged wall behind the in wall cistern and found water to be constantly leaking. Video link of cistern leaking in unit 6 - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DYWK9

Inspected the original bathroom and found the in wall toilet cistern to be constantly leaking.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken 6 - We advise the faulty inlet valve within the in wall toilet cistern is replaced with new inlet valve. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Whilst in unit 6, we investigated a 2nd leak from the bathroom ceiling. Another contractor has cut a hole within the gyprock ceiling to investigate this leak.

Gained access into unit 4 and inspected the original bathroom.

Flood dye tested the shower waste pipework and found dye leaking into unit 6 below. Following extensive testing we found the waste pipework in the outlet of the strip drain and waterproof membrane to have failed and requires replacement.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 4 to rectify the water leak - We advise a building contractor is engaged to remove the tiles within the shower recess, 1st course of wall tiles, install new drainage connecting strip drain, install new waterproof membrane and re-tile the shower recess and 1st course of wall tiles.

After the works have been completed in units 4 and 6, we advise the resultant water damaged wall in unit 6 accent to the toilet is repaired and painted. Also the resultant water damaged bathroom ceiling in unit 6 is repaired and painted. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken on the common storm water pipework.

Whilst in the car park we found sewerage leaking out of the common sewer stack inspection opening located next to the visitors car space.

CCTV video link of sewer branch line - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DYEWA

Flow tested sewer stack and common sewer pipework downstream - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockage - We advise the tree root infested branch line from the base of the sewer stack to the main line is relined, completely sealing the pipework as a full proof repair.  We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Sunday 13/1/25 - Urgent blockage in unit 7's bathroom

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 7 and found the toilet to be completely blocked and flooding sewerage when in use.

Removed inspection opening on the sewer stack on the external wall and found the in ground common sewer pipework to be blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment outside unit 7''s bathroom.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework and junction just before the previously relined main line. We found another plumbing company has undertaken a patch reline downstream the sewer stack outside unit 7's bathroom but has not sealed the tree root infested junction or base of stack. 

Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DYM9W

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer pipework.

Re-installed inspection opening, flow tested toilet and all fixtures in unit 7's bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

Please note, if the tree root infested junction and pipework is not relined, further blockages will re-occur in unit 7's bathroom. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify further sewer blockages in unit 7 - We advise to reline the tree root infested junction and pipework connecting unit 7, completely sealing the pipework as a full proof repair using a watermark approved epoxy relining system. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
