Job Issued By: Taylor Ashkar (Strata Manager)
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in units 206 and 207.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 206 and found water damage to the common living wall and skirting adjacent to unit 207.

Used moisture meter to locate high readings of moisture within the common living room wall.

Gained access into unit 306 above, cut a small hole in the kitchen cabinetry to inspect the common riser and no leaks were found.

Flood dye tested all waste fixtures in the bathroom and kitchen - No leaks were found in unit 306. 

We were unable to gain access into unit 207 on our inspection.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 207 and found water damage to the skirting in the bedroom adjacent to the bathroom.

Inspected the original bathroom, flood dye tested the bath waste, left under test for 30 minutes and found dye leaking from under the face of the bath confirming the leak.

Removed affected tiles on the front face of the bath and used aqua vacuum to suck out the water from under the bath.

Following our inspection under the bath, we found the bath waste to be encased with concrete and we were unable to locate where the original bath waste pipework is leaking.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 207 to rectify the water leak - We advise to remove further tiles and excavate section on the front face of the bath, carefully excavate concrete encased around waste pipework and bath, cut out leaking bath waste pipework, replace with new, test all works, temporary cover hole on the front face of the bath, We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed, we will submit a quotation to repair and paint the resultant water damaged living room wall in unit 206,  repair and paint the resultant damaged bedroom skirting and re-tile the front face of the bath in unit 207. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Description:
AFTER HOURS BLOCKAGE - Blocked laundry and flooding in use

manager Isabel Windosr

Booked 11-12 4th
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 5/1/25 - Urgent sewer flood in lot 5

Urgently attended the property after hours on Saturday, gained access into lot 5, found the ground floor toilet, laundry and floor waste to be blocked and flooding when in use.

Gained access into the car park below, removed inspection opening on the ariel common sewer drainage and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the inspection opening in lot 5's courtyard to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer pipework.

Used CCTV drain camera and found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework approximately 8 meters and 13 meters downstream which was the cause of the sewer blockage. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DYRGF

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all the tree roots from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested all fixtures in the bathroom and still located a blockage. 

Returned to the property the following day on Sunday 5/1/24, carried out further investigation works to locate the main boundary trap for the building to be located in lot 12's courtyard.

Used CCTV drain camera upstream from the boundary trap and located a 2nd major tree root blockage on the sewer junction connecting lots 5 and 6. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-DYRJ7

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment into lot 12's courtyard. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera upstream the boundary trap to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer junction connecting lots 5 and 6.

Flow tested all fixtures in lot 5 downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note - If the tree root infested common sewer is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise the tree root infested common sewer pipework is relined as a full proof repair and prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining ream.

Description: 4&7/22 flood bondi - leak through laundry ceiling - Chloe manager
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 3/1/25 - Urgent water leak in unit 4 from unit 7 above

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 4 and found water constantly leaking through the laundry ceiling. 

Removed access vent on the ceiling and found water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 7 above.

Gained access into unit 7, flood dye tested the bath waste with yellow dye. Following dye testing we found yellow dye to be leaking through the laundry ceiling in unit 4 below.

Removed affected tiles on the front face of the bath and found a large amount of water pooling under the bath.

Following testing and our inspection under the bath, we found the bath waste pipework and floor waste located under the bath to be completely blocked, surcharging when is use which was the cause of water penetration into unit 4 below.

Removed original cast iron inspection opening on the common waste pipework within unit 4's bathroom ceiling cavity, connecting unit 7's blocked bath above.

Used electric eel extensively to clear the blockage in the original common branch and stack pipework.

Re-installed inspection opening lid, flow tested bath and all fixtures in unit 7's bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

Sucked up water from under the bath using aqua vacuum to prevent further water damage to unit 4 below.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further resultant water damage repairs and tiling in units 4 and 7 - We advise the resultant water damaged laundry ceiling is repaired and painted. We also also the front face of the bath is repaired and tiled in unit 7. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Emergency after hours call out on Tuesday 31/12/24 - Urgent sewer blockage in the driveway

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer stack at the rear of the building, used CCTV drain camera downstream to also locate major tree root infestations entering the earthenware pipework downstream the driveway. 

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree root infestations from the rear sewer stack downstream the driveway to the previous reline undertaken by another contractor. 

Re-installed inspection opening and flow tested common sewer pipework from the rear of the property to the boundary trap located at the front left of the building  - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disincfeacnt. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise the tree root infested 150mm earthenware sewer pipework on the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney waters sewer main is relined completely sealing the pipework as a full proof repair. Emergency after hours call out on Boxing Day 26/12/24 - Urgent sewer flood in unit 8

Urgently attended the property after hours at 10:00am, gained access into unit 8, found the bathroom waste fixtures to be completely blocked and sewerage flooding out of the floor waste when the bathroom fixtures were in use.

Removed floor waste grate lid, used electric eel extensively downstream but was unable to clear the blockage in the stack pipework. We were removing a large amount of tree roots from the base of the stack. 

Inspected around and under the building and we were unable to locate any inspection openings on the stack pipework as the stack has been run internally within the brickwork.

Engaged 2nd plumber, setup high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment into unit 8's bathroom on the 2nd level.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with whippet hose but we were unable to get our jetting blasting equipment downstream the stack as it was hitting the back of the square junction.

After 6 hours of clear out work with the use of electric eel, flex shaft and jet blasting equipment we were unable to clear the blockage.

Spoke with an owner in unit 12 to explain the further works required to try and clear the sewer blockage and prevent further sewerage flooding in unit 8's bathroom.

Returned to the property the following day on the 27/12/24, removed bricks from the external wall exposing the original cast iron stack pipework within the wall.

Cut out a small section of the sewer stack pipework, used high pressure water jet blaster downstream and found the base of the stack to be completely collapsed and tree root infested.

After extensive jet blasting we were removing a large amount of sand, our jet blasting equipment was getting stuck and we were unable to clear the blockage.

We have left the hole open at the base of the stack to prevent further flooding in unit 8's bathroom.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken by the strata plumber for the building - We advise to saw cut the concrete, excavate the concrete and ground located at the back right side of property, remove bricks on the external wall to allow new pipework to run through wall, cut out the common stack and install new PVC pipework and fittings from stack to main sewer pipework, flow test all works, back fill trench and re-instate concrete.

Description:
Variation Quotation - Common hot water re-run from the bathroom to the kitchen in unit 1a.

Removed the shower wall tiles and excavated the internal wall to expose the hot water pipework where leak detection had advised us of the loudest noise coming from the burst hot water pipe. After undertaking the excavation works, exposing the hot water pipework in the shower wall, we found the burst pipe was not within the shower wall. Carried out further testing by capping off the line within the concrete slab which runs to the kitchen tap and found a drop in pressure on the hot water pipework within the concrete slab.

Cut out a section of copper pipework in the shower wall just below the tee and installed a cap to isolate the hot water supply to the kitchen tap, deleting the hot water to the kitchen and to stop the water leak.

This quotation is to rerun the hot water pipework from the shower wall to the kitchen installing new copper pipework and fittings, deleting the burst hot water pipe within the slab in unit 1A.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access into unit 1a and lay drop sheets in the bedroom and kitchen.
  2. Excavate internal wall in the bedroom wardorbe and drill a hole through the concrete slab into the carpark.
  3. Use extension ladder to access the landing above the foyer entrance outside unit 1a's kitchen and drill a hole through the external wall into the kitchen cabinetry.
  4. Surface mount copper pipe and fittings to the underside of the concrete slab in the carpark, through the external wall up to the landing into the kitchen.
  5. Install brackets and fixing securing the pipework to the concrete slab and external wall.
  6. Isolate the hot water supply to unit 1a and drain the water from the line.
  7. Connect hot water copper pipework withing the shower wall and install new hot water point and mini tap under the kitchen sink connecting the kitchen sink mixer.
  8. Turn the water supply back on testing all works.
  9. Paint pipework on the external wall matching existing paint colour as close as possible to match.
  10. Patch render shower wall in preparation for tiling.
  11. Install primer and 2 x coats of waterproof membrane to the shower wall.
  12. Re-tile affected area of internal shower wall matching existing tiles as close as possible to match.
  13. Grout affected area using additive.
  14. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate sewer leak in the driveway.

Urgently attended the property on the 12/12/24 at 3:00pm, removed sewer inspection opening lid in the rear left driveway and found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Set up large high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively upstream and downstream of the inspection opening lid in the driveway to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera and found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework from the inspection opening in the driveway downstream to the boundary trap and also upstream under the driveway. Used CCTV drain camera downstream the boundary and found the base of the boundary trap and outlet pipework to Sydney waters main to be completely blocked with tree roots. We also found a large amount of sand at the base of the boundary trap indicating the boundary trap has collapsed. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera for 3.5 hours to clear out as many roots from the common sewer pipework as possible, upstream and downstream of the inspection opening in the driveway. After extensive jet blasting there was still a large amount of tree roots in the base of the boundary trap and outlet pipework that required further clearing.

Returned to the property the following morning, used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the original 150mm earthenware boundary trap and outlet pipework downstream to Sydney waters main.

We located 2 x previous reline patch relines located downstream of the inspection opening in the driveway where tree roots are aggressively entering the joins where the reline meets the origainal earthanwere pipework.

Flow tested common sewer pipework which is clear and getting away. Please note, if the tree root infested common original sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline the tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework and boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main as a full proof solution to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

  3. Using robotic cutter Reinstate 3 x Junction connection located on boundary trap shaft.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common storm water line locate at the front left of the building

Following the recent preventative maintenance works and our CCTV camera survey, we located 2 x sections of collapsed and tree root infested original earthenware storm water pipework located at the front left of the building that requires urgent attention.

This quotation is to reline approximately 5 meters of collapsed and tree root infested original earthenware storm water pipework, completely sealing the line to prevent further blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation: 
  1. Set up safe working areas at the front left of the building. 
  2. Using high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera clean storm water pipework preparation for relining.
  3. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining. 
  4. Measure, cut and prepare new liner. 
  • Relining Repairs 
  1. Reline approximately 5 meters of collapsed and tree root infested earthenware storm water pipework at the front left if the building sealing all root infested and collapsed  joints, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 
  2. Cure line with a hot water boiler.
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common storm water pipework.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test relined pipework. 
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  7. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  8. Carry out free annual inspection of the relining works undertaken. 

PLEASE NOTE - We strongly suggest this repair be completed with an approved epoxy resin and not a non approved silicate resin that has been previously used. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Sunday 1/12/24 - Urgent storm water flood 

Urgently attended the property on Sunday, gained access into lot 10a found the common courtyards at the rear to be blocked and flooded with mud and dirt caused by the building site next door. Due to the large rain a large amount of mud and dirt has washed into the buildings drainage, this caused all levels and the walkways drainage to be completely blocked and the entire common storm water system for the building to be blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, removed all mud and dirt from the common areas, the base of the common storm water pit and strip drain using buckets and disposed of the mud into the skip bin at the front of the property as requested.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment to the rear courtyard of 10a.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively removing a large build up of mud, sand and debris. After extensively jet blasting we were able to get the storm water system flowing but there was still a large amount of mud and debris in the pipework that required clearing to prevent flooding in any further rain occurred. 

Returned to the property the following day with 2 x plumbers on 2/12/24, cleaned out common stormwater pits at the top level, strip drains and surface drains at the rear of 10a, and the surface drains at the back of 10. 

Used the high-pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear the common storm water mainline drainage on both sides of the property to the kerb and gutter at the street to get the storm water system for the building flowing and clear. 

Returned to the property 4/12/24 & 5/12/24, set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses, pressure cleaned all mud and dirt from the spiral staircase, courtyard tiles and all common areas. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

- Labour (normal working hours 8 hours x 2 plumbers @ $160 per hour) - $2,560.00 + GST

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 1104 - To rectify further water leaking under the bath, we advise the bath is removed, and a new steel bath is installed and recessed inside the wall.

After the bath replacement works are completed, we advise that the water damaged common area hallway outside unit 1104 is repaired and painted.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework - STAGES 1 & 2

Following our CCTV camera survey on the common sewer lines, we located tree root infestations to be entering majority of the original earthenware sewer pipework which requires relining repairs to prevent further common sewer blockages and floods.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of a building water shut downs.
  2. Gain access to building sewer inspection openings around property.
  3. Gain access to all stack base connections located on ground floor.
  4. Gain access to shop toilet/bathroom.
  5. Using high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles, milling tool and CCTV drain camera clean complete sewer line preparation for relining.
  6. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  • STAGE 1 - Reline approximately 2 meters outlet of main boundary trap - Green line 
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Measure, cut and prepare liner.
  3. Install approximately 2 meter sectional pipe reline on the outlet of the main boundary trap using watermark approved liner with 2 part epoxy resign.
  4. Cure liner using hot water.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. Provide CCTV video of relined works to the owners corporation.
  • STAGE 2 - Reline approximately 16 meters from common sewer stack downstream to boundary trap inlet - Red line
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Measure, cut and prepare liner.
  3. Reline approximately 16 meters downstream the common sewer stack to the boundary trap inlet using watermark approved liner with 2 part epoxy resign. 
  4. Cure liner using hot water.
  5. Re-instate all junctions using robotic cutter.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. Provide CCTV video of relined works to the owners corporation.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked storm water drains in the car park.

Attended the property, gained access into the car park and found the common storm water pits to be completely blocked.

Engaged 2 x plumbers, set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the lower garage.

Lifted all common stormwater pit lids in the lower garage and found the common stormwater pits and drains to be full of solidified, cement and sandstone.

After inspecting all the common stormwater lines, we found them to be completely blocked which was causing the perimeter spoon drains to overflow.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera and drain cleaning equipment to remove large amounts of cement/sandstone from the common stormwater lines unblocking the stormwater drainage to the large stormwater pit.

Installed PVC pipe and fittings and connected the drainage from ceiling to spoon drain with air gap, behind car-space 10 & 11.

Returned to the property, set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the lower garage. Used the high pressure water jet blaster to continue removing the remaining debris from the common stormwater lines.

Once clear, we flow tested the common stormwater drainage in the carpark and it is now clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

After the common stormwater repair works at the property had been completed, we returned to the property on several occasions following dry weather and found the water runoff in the garages to be slowing down and the water level around the retaining walls on the higher level carpark is drying up.

Inspected the buildings main water meter and found it comes to a complete stop at intervals indicating no burst pipes on the common cold water supply or fire hose reel line for the building. Carried out pressure testing on the fire hydrant service and no drop in pressure was found indicating the buildings water supply pipes which run along the retaining wall are not the cause of the water leaking.

There is still water flowing from the retaining walls in the lower carpark, which is decreasing over time and dry weather. We consider the amount of water that circulated and discharged from the stormwater tank whilst the street works were taking place has drained into the subsoil along the Curlewis Street, causing a large pool of water to be trapped behind the basement retaining walls. This may take some time to drain away.

Description:
Quotation - Common sewer stack replacement and external wall seal.

Whilst undertaking the works, we were asked by the committee member Frank to inspect the rendered wall and common stack pipework on the left side of the building that is causing water ingress, as the wall is not completely sealed by the render. There are gaps and cracks where the render meets the original cast iron stack allowing water to leak into the wall substrate during rain events. We also found the original cast iron stack pipework to be corroded and in bad condition. 

To rectify the water ingress and seal the wall, we advise the entire stack is cut out, the wall is re-rendered behind the stack sealing the wall, and the common cast iron stack is replaced with PVC.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1.  Advise residents in affected units of work and water disruptions.
  2. Install barricades around the work area.
  3. Erect scaffolding to access the external wall and common stack pipework.
  4. Excavate brickwork exposing 100mm waste pipe within the external wall.
  5. Cut out common cast iron stack pipework from base of stack to eaves and branch line within the wall. 
  6. Patch holes and gaps in the brickwork, re-render the external wall behind.
  7. Supply and install new PVC pipework and fittings connecting onto existing branch lines.
  8. Flow test all works carried out.
  9. Secure the PVC pipework to the wall using stainless steel brackets and fixings.
  10. Repair external wall around waste pipe penetration.
  11. Paint pipework and external wall to match existing paint colour as close as possible to match.
  12. Dismantle and remove scaffold from the property. 
  13. Clean all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leaking rainwater tank at the rear of the property.

Attended the property, gained access to the rear visitor carspace and found water leaking from the common rainwater tank.

Removed rainwater tank lids and inspected inside the tank, found the tank to be full of water up to the inlet and overflow pipework.

Opened the hose tap to drain the rainwater tank to a level and carried out dye testing to confirm if the rubber bladder insert was leaking.

Returned to the property the following day and found no dye to be leaking from the rainwater tank and the leak to have dried up indicating the rubber bladder insert is not leaking.

Emptied the tank completely, removing the dye coloured water and left hose tap open as rain was expected over the next few days.

Returned to the property and gained access. Found after the tank was drained to a level below the inlet and overflow pipes the leak has not returned.

Supplied and installed PVC flanges over the inlet and overflow pipework entering the tank and sealed flanges to the rubber insert using high grade flexible sealant.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Coudl you please arrange to attend the building urgently following sewerage overflow onto the back tiled area after the storm yesterday.
Jo - 0423 338 494
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the overflow relief gullies at the rear of the property.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream of the common sewer inspection opening at the rear of the building next to the overflow gully to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the common sewer line approximately 15 meters from the inspection opening downstream to the boundary trap, which was the cause of the common sewer blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations from the original common earthenware sewer pipework from the inspection opening to the boundary trap.

Once clear, flow tested the common sewer line downstream to the boundary trap - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Please note - If the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To rectify further common sewer blockages, we advise the affected tree root infested common original earthenware sewer pipework is relined from the inspection opening at the rear of the building downstream to the boundary trap approximately 15 meters and re-instate junction using robotic cutter. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leak in electrical room.

Attended the property, gained access into the basement level electrical room and hallway outside the common laundry.

Found water to be leaking from the 65mm common cold water copper piping. Dried the pipe leak and found water droplets on the pipe returns after several minutes.

The water leak is caused by condensation leaking off the common cold water mains piping.

Inspected the common laundry located a few meters away, which has minimal ventilation and contains dryers that are frequently in use, contributing to the basement humidity levels.

After inspecting the water leak caused by condensation, we can confirm that it has not caused the power outage.

We have advised the caretaker Glen to leave the doors open in the common area to improve airflow and reduce humidity levels around the pipework when the laundry driers are in use.

Description:
Urgent Ceiling Leak LOT 42 SP 42232 - 57/17 Elizabeth Bay Road, Elizabeth Bay

Team,

Please see below and contact Thomas for access to unit 57. Unit above is Unit 67 which Ron Danielle real estate should have access to onsite.

Thanks

Zac Marshall
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 57.

Picked up keys from the managing agent, urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 57 and found water leaking from the bathroom ceiling.

Cut a hole in the double layered water damaged bathroom ceiling, inspected inside the ceiling cavity and located water leaking through the concrete slab and bath waste penetration for unit 67 above.

As the bathroom ceiling in unit 57 was double layered we found there to be a large amount of water trapped in between the 2 x sheets of gyprock ceiling, causing a large amount of water damage.

Gained access into unit 67, found the shower and bath taps to be constantly leaking down the shower wall.

Pressure tested the bath breaching piece, hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 67. Dye tested the bath waste piping with yellow dye and no leak was found in unit 57 below.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the common sewer pipework on the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main located on the left hand side of the building in he driveway. 

The tree roots are aggressively entering through an existing Silicate resin reline undertaken by another plumbing contractor (photos attached).

This quotation is to use robotic cutter cut out and remove defective reline on vertical shaft, use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV to clear out the pipework in preparation for relining, reline approximately 3-4 meters of root infested vertical shaft, relining from vertical shaft connection down shaft finishing at Sydney water main connection sealing all root infested joints and previous defective Reline, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation:

 

  1. Advise residents of a building water shut down.
  2. Set up safe working areas around property 
  3. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property. 
  4. Using robotic cutter cut out and remove defective reline on vertical shaft.
  5. Using high pressure water jet clean sewer system preparation for relining.
  6. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining. 
  • Relining Repairs 
  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 3-4 meters of root infested vertical shaft, relining from vertical shaft connection down shaft finishing at Sydney water main connection sealing all root infested joints and previous defective reline, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 
  3. Cure line with a hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test relined pipework. 
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  8. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  9. Carry out free annual inspection of the relining works undertaken. 

PLEASE NOTE - We strongly suggest this repair be completed with an approved epoxy resin and not a non approved silicate resin that has been previously used. All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework downstream the sewer stack in unit 4's garage

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework downstream the sewer stack in unit 4's garage causing the kitchen and laundry fixtures in unit 4 to block up and surcharge.

This quotation is to reline approximately 7 meters of  tree root infested common sewer pipework, relining from inspection opening on stack in unit 4's garage downstream covering all root infested joints, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. Using robotic cutter reinstate 1 x Junction on the common sewer line.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Set up relining equipment in unit 4's garage.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations and debris in preparation for relining. 
  4. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  • Relining works
  1. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 7 meters of root infested common sewer pipework relining from inspection opening on stack downstream covering all root infested joints, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  5. Using robotic cutter re-instate 1 x Junction on the common sewer line.
  6. Turn on the buildings cold water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  9. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  10. Carry out free annual inspection of the relining works undertaken. 

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual CCTV inspection of the relining works undertaken. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Attended the property and gained access into units 1 & 2.

Used moisture meter to confirm there are no water leaks in unit 2.

Inspected the external window frames outside units 1 & 2's kitchen and found gaps around the wall openings where water can leak into the wall cavity. 

Further works required to be undertaken by a building contractor - We advise the kitchen windows for unit 1 & 2 are re-sealed to prevent water leaking to the wall cavity.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - After the windows have ben sealed, we advise a building contractor is engaged to replace the water damaged kitchen cabinetry and a flooring contractor is engaged to repair the timber floors.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Emergency after hours call out on the 13/11/24 -  Urgent water leak in unit 12 from unit 14 above

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 12 and found water damage to the bedroom wall and the carpet to be damaged in the bedroom adjacent to the bathroom.

Returned to the property on the 18/11/24, engaged pipe location leak detection to undertake further testing to locate the burst hot water pipe in unit 14.

Used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water supply within unit 14, used listening device and leak detector to pin pint the burst pressurized hot water pipe to be located within the internal bathroom wall behind the bath.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak in unit 14 - We advise to excavate the bedroom wall to expose the burst hot water pipe located behind the bath, turn off the hot water supply, cut out burst hot water pipework and install new copper pipework and fittings.  We will submit an URGENT shortly quotation for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 14.

After the plumbing works have been completed and we know the full extent of the resultant damage, we will submit a quotation for the resultant damage repairs and painting in units 12 and 14.

We also advise the water damage carpet in unit 12's bedroom is steam cleaned or replaced. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

The following works were undertaken:

  1. Gain access and set up high pressure water jet blaster and equipment.
  2. Remove metal square downpipes on the right side of the building to access the common storm water line.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster downstream from the downpipes to clear out the common storm water line that runs to the rear of the property.
  4. Use CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear and map out the common stormwater pipework to the rear of the property.
  5. Following our CCTV camera survey if any faults are found we will report back with our findings.

Following the stormwater clear out works on the right side of the property, used high pressure water jet blaster to clear out a large amount of debris from the stormwater line under the driveway from the front downpipe to the rear, used CCTV drain camera and found the condition of the original pipework down the driveway is in good condition and good working order.

Approximately 2 meters away from the rear concrete slab that has been excavated and replaced, the stormwater line holds water and an absorption trench has been installed within the excavation (next to where the tree was removed), to allow stormwater from the right side pipework to discharge into the ground.

Cut out the base of the rear, right downpipe and following clear out works and CCTV camera survey on the branch line to the main line, we found at the base of the downpipe to be collapsed where it  joins the earthenware pipework and branch line.

Installed PVC pipe and inspection opening at the base of the front right downpipe for future clear out purposes.

Further works required to be undertaken on the right side stormwater - We advise a collection pit is installed within the stormwater line before the absorption trench and the collapsed branch line from the rear right downpipe is excavated and replaced.

CCTV camera surveyed the left side stormwater line from the middle downpipe to the grated drain branch line and found the majority of the stormwater pipework at the rear to be cracked, collapsed and root infested for approximately 20 meters due to the large Jacaranda tree.

Further works required to be undertaken on the left side stormwater - We advise the jacaranda tree is removed by an arborist, approximately 20 meters of common stormwater line under the tree is excavated and replaced, a collection pit and large absorption trench is installed at the rear car-space to allow stormwater from the left side pipework to discharge into the ground.   

We will organise a meeting with the committee and once we have gone through all the stormwater works required, we can submit a quotation to rectify the stormwater at the property.

  10. Testing of all works carried out.

  12. Compact ground and re-instate pavers.

  14. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  15. Remove all rubbish from the property.

After excavating, exposing and replacing the collapsed stormwater pipework adjacent to the front downpipe and under the council footpath, we tested the stormwater drainage at the side passage from the rear surface pit and found the current stormwater pipework under the pavers has back- fall, also the top level of the pit and walkway pavers is lower than the level at the kerb, this is causing the pit to hold water and the drainage under the pavers to hold water to the front downpipe.

To rectify this issue, we advise the rear downpipe which discharges into the pit is surface mounted on the buildings wall and connects to the front downpipe where the drainage has been replaced to the street with fall. As the level of the pavers and top of pit is lower than the outlet at the street, the surface pit will never drain properly and always hold water. Once the rear downpipe is connected to the front downpipe, we advise the surface pit is deleted and the hole filled in with sand, compacted and re-paved. We will submit a quotation shorty for the further works required to be undertaken to prevent further issues with the common stormwater pipework.

Whilst undertaking the works, we were also asked by the committee member Frank to inspect the rendered wall and common stack pipework on the left side of the building that is causing water ingress, as the wall is not completely sealed by the render. There are gaps and cracks where the render meets the original cast iron stack allowing water to leak into the wall substrate during rain events. To rectify the water ingress and seal the wall, we advise the entire stack is cut out, the wall is re-rendered behind the stack sealing the wall, and the common cast iron stack is replaced with PVC. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent leak in unit 89.

Whilst undertaking works on Thursday 31/10 we were notified of an urgent leak in unit 89.

Gained access into unit 89, removed downlight in the bedroom ceiling and allowed water to drip into a bucket.

Inspected the ceiling cavity and found water leaking through a crack in the concrete slab.

Went upstairs to unit 95 above and turned the water supply off to the unit.

Returned to the property the following day, gained access into unit 89 and found the leak in the bedroom ceiling cavity had stopped.

Gained access into unit 95 above and found wet carpet in the middle of the bedroom directly above.

Carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water pipes and shower breaching piece for unit 95 and no leaks were found.

Flood / dye tested the shower in unit 95 and only found a leak to be coming from the shower screen.

After extensive testing in unit 95 and inspecting the ceiling cavity in unit 89 for over 3 hours, we found no water to be leaking.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Made a follow up call after 4 days and found the leak has not returned.

We advise to monitor the leak in unit 89 and if the leak returns further investigation works are required.

Description:
Private job - possible burst in internal wall

Please see report from Howard

Attended on 30/08/2024. Accessed U16 kitchen. There is water on the tiled kitchen floor just near the doorway to the laundry. Paint has bubbled above the skirting tile on the wall backing onto the shower. There is water droplets on the top of the skirting tile. The laundry wall and the adjacent wall in the kitchen both back onto the shower in the bathroom.

Tried to isolate the hot water duo valve for pressure testing, however it was faulty. Removed the valve and installed a new duo valve. This is an owner issue. Removed the shower mixer dress fittings to find no water leaking from the cartridge. Pressure drop tested the shower recess tee which held. Reinstalled the dress fittings.

The cold water control valve is located in the laundry. This valve is old. Turned the valve off and on to find it was working well. Pressure drop tested the cold water which also held. Set up the nitrogen and pressure tested the hot water which dropped pressure. Repeated - the hot water pressure dropped again. There appears to be a burst hot water pipe in the internal wall between the shower in the bathroom and the kitchen. This is an owner issue.

Inspected under the kitchen sink to see the hot and cold water pipework goes into the wall.

The bathroom is original, however, the shower area is not. Believe the original shower/bath combination was removed and converted into a shower. New wall and floor tiles have been installed over the top of the original tiles. Used a thermo gun to try and get a reading, however, due to the extra thickness of the 2 layers of tiles on the wall, it did not pick up a reading. We believe that tiles will need to be removed from the shower wall to expose the pipe and find/repair or replace. The pipe is likely closer to the wall surface in the shower than in the kitchen wall.
Invoice Description:
Investigate burst pipe in unit 16.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 16 and found water leaking from the internal wall in the kitchen and laundry adjacent to the shower recess.

Isolated the hot water supply and carried out a nitrogen pressure test. Following pressure testing, we located a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst pipe in unit 16.

Inspected the water damage and found bubbling paint on the internal walls in the laundry and kitchen adjacent to the shower recess.

Returned to the property and carried out leak detection on the hot water piping to pin point the burst hot water pipework.

Nitrogen pressure tested the hot water pipework and used listening devise to find and locate a burst hot water pipe within the internal shower wall.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to excavate the shower wall to expose the burst hot water pipework, repair burst hot water pipework, patch render the shower wall, re-waterproof and re-tile. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Variation quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent quoted relining works undertaken and our CCTV camera survey, we located a further 12 meters of tree root infested original common earthenware sewer pipework that requires relining repairs to prevent further sewer blockages.

This quotation is to reline approximately 12 meters of mainline sewer line, relining from driveway inspection opening downstream covering all root infested earthenware joints finishing reline past outside inspection opening. This will completely seal all the earthenware mainline running through the middle of the building, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin and using Robotic cutter reinstate 2 x Junctions. 

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of works being undertaken on the sewer pipework.
  2. Set up relining equipment.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  4. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  • Relining works
  1. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 12 meters of mainline sewer line, relining from driveway inspection opening downstream covering all root infested earthenware joints finishing reline past outside inspection opening. This will completely seal all the earthenware mainline running through the middle of the building, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Using robotic cutter reinstate 2 x Junctions. 
  4. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  6. Flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  9. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  10. Provide free annual CCTV camera inspection to inspect the relining works undertaken. 

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate sewer smell  in unit 1's downstairs bathroom.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found there to be a sewerage smell in the downstairs bathroom.

Carried out a CCTV inspection of the common sewer line for unit 1 and downstream - No sewer blockages were found. Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the recent relining works upstream of the boundary trap to be in good condition an no faults were found with the common sewer pipework.

Returned to the property the following day, gained access into unit 1, installed a new floor waste grate seal within the floor waste drain in the downstairs bathroom. We advised the occupant they need to pour water down the dry floor waste grate every few weeks to prevent the trap running dry.

Invoice Description:
Investigate low hot water pressure and water hammer noises.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found low hot water pressure and water hammer noises on the hot water supply.

After pressure testing, we found when the hot tap is used in unit 3 on the ground floor, the hot water pressure dropped to 150kpa and unit 11 has no water coming out of the hot taps.

Gained access into the hot water plant room and found a pressure limiting valve on the buildings common hot water supply which is not required due to the buildings water pressure.

Put up water shut down notices at the building advising of hot water disruptions and went to the supplier and picked up materials.

Returned to the property, gained access into the hot water plant room and isolated the buildings hot water supply, cut out the pressure limiting valve and removed it from the hot water manifold.

Following testing, we still found low water pressure. Also when turning on the buildings hot water supply, the water hammer noise was heard to be coming from the hot water manifold and instantaneous hot water heater.

Inspected the hot water plant, instantaneous and storage heater, circulating pumps, valves and manifold pipework for the buildings common hot water supply.

Following our inspection of the hot water plant and manifold piping, we found the low water pressure and water hammer noises to be caused by manifold piping, valves and circulating pumps which have been installed incorrectly.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To rectify the low hot water pressure and hot water hammer noises effecting the buildings common hot water supply, we advise the hot water manifold pipework is altered and reconfigured to the correct installation requirements. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 8 and inspected mould in the living room.

Used moisture meter and found high readings of moisture in the living room wall adjacent to the balcony. We also found water stains to the outside balcony dividing wall.

Following flood testing of the balcony in unit 17, we found the waterproof membrane to be faulty causing water to leak around the downpipe penetration, through the concrete slab into unit 15's wall below.

Following testing of the roof above unit 17's balcony using the water hose, we found water leaks from the roof and wall flashings, down the balcony dividing walls. After inspecting the awning roof above unit 17's balcony, we found faulty flashings which are causing the leak from the roof.

Inspected the buildings roof from the balcony of unit 17 and found all the gutters are completely blocked with leaves and debris.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken by a building contractor in unit 17 - As the water proof membrane on the balcony has failed, we advise the balcony floor and faulty waterproof membrane is excavated, re-waterproofed and re-tiled. Also, the roof flashings on the awning roof are replaced with new flashings to prevent water leaking from the roof down the balcony walls.

Once the repairs works are completed in unit 17, we advise the resultant water damaged walls in unit 8's living room are repaired and painted.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken by a roofing contractor - We advise all gutters at the property, are cleaned removing leaves and debris.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line and branch line affecting unit 2

Following the recent emergency sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer branch pipework and junction downstream from unit 2's toilet.

This quotation is to reline approximately 4-5 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from downstream from the toilet to the mainline junction covering all root infested joints using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. Also Install 150x100x45 satellite junction (Complete Y section) relining from common mainline into unit 2's branch-line, sealing heavily root infested cracked junction.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Gain access into unit 2.
  3. Disconnect and remove toilet to access the common sewer pipework.
  4. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean sewer line preparation for relining.
  5. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 4-5 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from the downstream from the toilet to the mainline junction covering all root infested joints using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Install 150x100x45 satellite junction (Complete Y section) relining from common mainline into unit 2's branch-line, sealing heavily root infested cracked junction.
  4. Cure liner using hot water.
  5. Once liner has cured remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  6. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test relined pipework after relining.
  7. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining.
  8. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  9. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  10. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  11. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.

Please note - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Please note - If repairs are not undertaken, the tree roots will grow back into the original earthenware sewer pipework and further blockages will re-occur.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line on the left hand side of the building

Following the sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework downstream approximately 3 meters from the overflow sewer gully on the left hand side of the building

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 meters of  tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework approximately 3 meters downstream from the overflow sewer gully, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of water disruptions. 
  2. Set up relining equipment.
  3. Barricade around work area.
  4. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  5. CCTV record storm water pipework before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 2 meters of  tree root infested common earthenware sewer pipework approximately 3 meters downstream from the overflow sewer gully, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. completely sealing the sewer pipework as a full proof repair.
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common storm water drainage.
  5. Flow test all works carried out.
  6. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  10. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.

Please note - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

This quotation is to install 1 x sectional reline approximately 2 meters of cracked and broken section of common sewer pipework, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of works being undertaken on the sewer pipework.
  2. Set up relining equipment.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining.

Investigate rising damp in unit 1.

11/10 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water damage along the common wall in the kitchen and living room. Inspected the water damage and found it to be low down along the base of the wall at low level.

Inspected all plumbing fixtures on unit 1's kitchen and no leaks were found.

Gained access into unit 4 above and found no water damage, inspected all plumbing fixtures in the kitchen, tested the kitchen sink waste and no leaks were found to be coming from unit 4.

Gained access into the carpark and found the sandstone walls below unit 1 to be very wet and leaking into the stormwater pit.

Walked around the neighbouring property and no leaks were found, plumbing services are located on the opposite of the building.

15/10-  Returned to the property and gained access into unit 1, used thermal image camera to identify moisture along the base of the wall indicating rising damp behind the gyprock. Cut a small hole in the affected gyprock and confirmed damp brickwork behind. 

Covered the hole using core flue and cleaned all areas where work has taken place in unit 1.

Gained access into the carpark to inspect the perimeter walls and common stormwater causing the sandstone to be wet resulting in rising damp.

Following inspection and testing of the common stormwater at the property we found 3 x issues contributing to rising damp and wet walls within the carpark.

1. Common stormwater pit located on the left side of property at the front pedestrian entrance is cracked, soil below the tiles and concrete has washed away around the pit, the cracks in the pit is allowing water to leak underground into the carpark below. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NHAT6

2. Stormwater drainage inlets to the front left stormwater pit are lower than the outlet piping to the council drains. When we investigated the inlet drains to the front left pit, they are connected to the front courtyard drains for the ground floor units along Curlewis Street. As the outlet is higher, the pit will fill to a level, causing the drainage line within the carpark for the courtyards to fill up and become charged. We followed the drainage in the carpark and found it is capped off at low level, no where to discharge and required to be run into the stormwater system. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NHA1O

Removed the cap on the pipework in the carpark to prevent the courtyard drains from overflowing, causing the front pit to leak into the subsoil.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken on the left side common stormwater - We advise the courtyard drainage line in the carpark is connected to the carpark downpipe, which drains to the main stormwater pit on B2 and the cracked stormwater pit under the tiled walkway entrance is replaced with new GRC stormwater pit. 

3. Common stormwater pit on the right side of the property at the top of the driveway is still overflowing after the works have been carried out on the footpath causing the pit to overflow and leak underground into the carpark below. The council has raised the pit (which is leaking from the joins) and installed the larger square metal outlet, however the flow of water from the pump out pipework is much greater that the flow to the street, casing the pit to still overflow within the property. Please see video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NHAUB

Further urgent works required to be undertaken on the right side common stormwater - We advise to install a GRC stormwater pit and connect the pump out line and council outlet to allow more direct flow to the street.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 8/10/24 - Urgent water leak in the carpark

Urgently attended the property after hours, inspected car space 27 and found water leaking out of the common wall and ceiling below unit 22.

Gained access into unit 22 and located the kitchen to be above the leak. Tested all plumbing fixtures in the kitchen, pulled out the dishwashers and no leaks were found.

Isolated the cold water supply to carry out nitrogen pressure testing and found the common cold water isolation valve does not isolate the water supply and requires replacement.

Isolated the hot water supply from the heater in the bathroom, pressure tested the hot water and no pressure loss was found.

9/10 - Advised residents of a building cold water shut down, returned to the property the following day and isolated the buildings cold water supply and drained the water form the line.

Disconnected the faulty common cold water isolation valve and installed a new isolation valve, turned the water supply back on testing all works.

Carried out nitrogen pressure test on the cold water supply for got a drop in pressure indicating a burst cold water pipe causing the leak.

Advised the residents how to isolate the water supply when not in use to prevent further water damage.

11/10 - Returned to the the property, gained access into unit 22, isolated the hot and cold water supply, removed the dishwasher from the kitchen cabinets and excavated the common wall to locate cold water pipes within the kitchen above where it is leaking. After exposing all the common pipework within the kitchen wall, we found the cold water pipework is leaking out of the concrete slab.

Engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe locating equipment to trace out the cold water line from the kitchen to the bedroom wall and leak detector to locate the burst cold water pipe to be within the concrete slab.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 22 - To rectify the water leak, we advise to cap off and delete the burst pressurized cold water pipe within the concrete slab and re-run a new cold water service from the kitchen to the bathroom. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the works required to be undertaken.

Re-installed dishwasher, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate common hot water pump and heater on the roof.

9/10 - Attended the property, gained access to the roof and found the common hot water pump making a loud noise.

Tested the hot water supply and found warm water from the taps in unit 26.

Following testing we found the hot water heater would only activate if the hose tap on the inlet to the heater is turned on indicating the non return valve on the inlet supply is faulty.

Went to the supplier and picked up materials to replace the to replace the faulty non return valve and also install a new one on the hot water heater.

14/10 - Returned to the property, gained access to the roof and isolated the water supply to the common hot water heater and pump.

Disconnected the faulty 32mm non return valve and supplied and installed a new non return valve.

Cut out copper piping on the inlet to the heater and supplied and installed a new non return valve on the inlet to the heater.

Turned the water supply back on to the common hot water heater and pump, tested all works and found there to be no more warm water in unit 26.

Whilst testing the common hot water pump, we found a loud noise and the pressure to be less than when we previously replaced the pump. As the pump is exposed on the roof, we consider the rain and outdoor weather elements has caused the failure of the pump.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty hot water pump is urgently replaced and a custom made cover is installed over the pump to protect it from the rain. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Inspected the shower recess wall and floor tiles and located faulty grouting, which can cause water to leak in behind the tiles into the substrate.

Further works required to be undertaken at the lot owners cost in unit 5 - As the shower walls with faulty grouting are on internal walls, we advise to re-grout the internal shower wall tiles and re-seal the shower screen. Further works required to be undertaken at the lot owners cost in unit 9 - We advise to re-seal behind the shower taps and the shower screen. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the lot owners consideration in unit 9.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Pipe location leak detection advised us, if the burst pipe was not found in the common laundry wall further investigation works are required.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

'Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to gain access into units 4 & 9 and carry out pressure testing on the hot water supply, inspect all hot water valves and pipework in the below ground floor hot water plant room to determine what is causing the restricted and fluctuating hot water pressure at the property.

Site contact:
U9 owner on OC - Mark Dyson 0410 486 002 / mark@darkhouse.com.au

Invoice Description:
Investigate hot water pressure.

Attended the property and gained access into unit 4 & 9.

Ran all bathroom fixtures testing the hot and cold water supply and found the hot water supply has less flow.

Carried out a pressure test and found the hot and cold water supply to be around 200 kpa, indicating the buildings water pressure.

Gained access to the hot water plant room, inspected all valves and pipework and found it to be in working order.

Followed the cold water line from the heaters, back to the main feed and found the main isolation valve to be half on.

Turned the valve on full way and the water flow in unit 9 improved.

Below the isolation valve is a pressure reduction valve. As the buildings water pressure is 200kpa, the pressure reduction valve is restricting pressure and is not required.

Went to the supplier and picked up materials. 

Returned to the property, isolated the water supply to the common hot water, cut out and removed the pressure reduction valve and installed pipework and fittings.

Turned the water supply back on and testing all works - All in good working order.

Following testing, we found the hot water supply, pressure and flow has improved.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Hi Team,
BCS REF # 7925959
Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access into unit 18's garage and found water leaking from the concrete ceiling around the service riser penetration.

Gained access into unit 12 and located the bathroom to be above with the common service duct built out in the corner behind the toilet.

Tested the toilet and found the flush pipe to be leaking on the floor. Dye tested the toilet waste piping and common stack pipework and no dye leaked into the garage.

Carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and found a drop in pressure on the hot water indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 12.

Excavated a tile low down on the service riser duct within unit 12's bathroom to expose the pipework and we were unable to locate the burst pressurized hot water pipework.

Returned to the property the following day, carried out pipe location leak detection and located the burst pressurized hot water pipework within the common wall high up high behind the common stack.

Excavated wall tiles and cut out the common service riser in the bathroom to expose the burst hot water pipe.

Isolated the hot water supply and repaired the burst hot water pipe using welding equipment.

Turned the water supply back on testing all works - All in good working order and no further leaks were found. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 12 - Following the burst pipe plumbing repair works there is resultant damage to the common service riser and wall tiles in the bathroom. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and tiling works required to be undertaken.

Please note - This is the second burst hot water pipe in unit 12 in different locations and the copper piping is in poor condition. If burst pipes continue to occur, we advise the entire hot and cold water piping is rerun in unit 12.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

This quotation is to reline approximately 4 to 5 meters of root infested earthenware pipework relining from newly installed plastic pipework down to previously relined mainline, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin (unit 2's branch line).

The following works will be undertaken:

  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the common sewer line in preparation for relining.

- Relining repairs:

Invoice Description:
Investigate further leaking in the common hot water plant room.

23/9 - Urgently attended the property, gained access into the hot water plant room on the roof and located a burst hot water tee on the hot water outlet pipe manifold for the heaters to be leaking onto the floor.

We also found the isolation valves for the burst hot water heater to be faulty causing water to fill up the tank and continue to leak.

Disconnected the inlet supply to the burst heater and capped off the pipework after the valve to prevent further leaking from the burst heater tank.

We tried to install a clamp over the burst hot water pipe but due to the location of the burst on the tee, we were unable to undertake a temporary repair.

Set up a catch tray under the burst hot water tee to divert water leaking into the drainage and ran a hose from the tank drain into the floor waste.

Put up water shut down notes to advise residents of URGENT hot water disruptions the following day.

Gained access into unit 710 and found water damage to the ceiling at the front entry behind the door, dripping water into a bucket.

24/9 - Sourced materials from the suppliers and picked up materials.

Returned to the property, gained access to the hot water plant room on the roof, isolated the buildings hot water supply and drained the water form the line.

Cut out burst copper tee and piping on the outlet manifold for the heaters and installed new copper pipe, tee and fittings.

Supplied and installed 2 x new isolation valves on the inlet and outlet pipework manifold where the burst common hot water heater has been disconnected.

Turned the buildings water supply back on and tested all works - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Please note - We advised the building manager Peter, there are now only 2 working, common hot water heaters in the hot water manifold of 5. See attached video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N5IX3

Description:
Quotation - This quotation is to undertaken 6 monthly preventative maintenance on the common hot water heaters - Building 7, 9, 11 & 13. 

These works were last undertaken in March 2024 and to prevent any hot water faults, we advise the common hot water heaters are serviced every 6 months. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access to the hot water plant room in building 7, 9, 11 & 13.
  2. Building 7 -  Carry out service to 6 X Rinnai Demand Duo HD 28 315L (Model: REU-VCM2837WC-AK).
  3. Building 9 - Carry out service to 11 X Rinnai Demand Duo HD 28 315L (Model: REU-VCM2837WC-AK)
  4. Building 11 - Carry out service to 1 X Raypak Hot Water System (Model: B0280NCO).
  5. Building 13 - Carry out service to 7 X Rinnai Demand Duo HD 28 315L (Model: REU-VCM2837WC-AK)
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.

Please see below procedures:

- Visual Inspection (for any damage/leaks/rust/faults etc) of system in plant room area that is related to the Hot Water System.

- Test that the hot water system is at the correct temperature (both in storage and ring main).

- Test thermostat settings and differentials.

- Test that the hot water is circulating back to the boilers/storage tanks at the correct flow rate.

- Test the water pressure is correct for that particular hot water service (that is not too high or too low).

- Test for leaks on Pressure Relief Valves (PRV) and/or Temperature and Pressure Relief Valves (TPRV).

- Test for correct operation and sequencing.

- Removal and cleaning for dust and debris in all applicable areas of hot water system (inside burner, control box, wiring etc).

- Visual inspection of all areas of wiring for hot spots, loose connections etc.

- Test for faulty sensors (flame, temperature, flow etc.)

- Test that the all-isolation valves are in working order.

- Test for correct inlet gas pressures.

- Test for correct gas burner pressures.

- Test for correct operation of gas solenoids.

- Test for correct operation of air switches (where applicable).

- Removal and cleaning of burner train, sensors and ignition system on a yearly basis.

- Testing of flue dampeners (where applicable)

This quotation is to reline approximately 3 meters of vertical shaft sewer line, relining from plastic on vertical shaft down to Sydney main sewer connection sealing all root infested joints using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
and reinstate 1 x Junction connection feeding boundary trap using robotic cutter.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Remove inspection openings to access sewer line.
  2. Clean sewer pipework upstream of inspection opening using jet blaster and CCTV drain camera preparation for relining.

  4. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  5. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  6. Reinstate laundry junction using robotic cutter.
  7. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  8. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  11. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken to the owners corporation. 
  12. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.
