Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Saturday 7/9/24 - Urgent common sewer blockage

Urgently attended the property after hours, found the common sewer pipework to be completely blocked and surcharging sewage onto the driveway.

Setup high-pressure water blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection lids and high-pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the common sewer pipework on the right hand side of the building to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering into original earthenware sewer pipework in multiple locations causing the blockage.  The earthenware pipework has cracked, broken and major dislodgements causing the tree roots to enter the pipework.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree investigations from the common sewer pipework. 

Removed inspection opening on the common stack pipework in the car park, used high pressure jet blaster  and CCTV drain camera to clear further tree roots entering the original earthenware sewer pipework approximately 13 meters downstream.

Flow tested the common sewer pipework downstream to the boundary trap which is flowing and in good working order. Please note, if the tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and clean all areas where WORK had taken place using high-pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further urgent works to prevent further blockages - We advise the original common tree root infested pipework is relined as a full proof solution to prevent further blockages. We will submit urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the work relining team.

Description:
Relining repairs on the common sewer pipework

Quotation request number 015560

Following our inspection at the building and our CCTV camera inspection of the sewer line, we have identified multiple tree root intrusion on 3 x separate sections of the sewer, 1 x 7m section under unit 3 courtyard, 1 x 6m section under unit 2 courtyard and 1 x 1m section leading into unit 2 bathroom line. We have been asked to quote on a comparable scope but on camera inspection the highlighted diagram shows 12 meters under unit 2 courtyard we only measured 7 as the remaining line is in plastic and looks in good condition. We have identified 6 meter section leading under unit 2 courtyard this could be the comparable to the 12 meters being asked for.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

1. Gain access into unit 2 and 3 courtyards.
2. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property.
3. Set up safe working area around property.
4. Clean complete sewer main line preparation for relining.
5. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Reline approximately 7 meters of root infested earthenware pipework. Starting Relining on plastic pipework located under unit 3 courtyard 7 meters downstream covering all root infested joints finishing back onto plastic pipework. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  2. Reline approximately 6 meters of root infested earthenware pipework. Starting Relining on plastic pipework located under unit 2 courtyard 6 meters Upstream covering all root infested joints finishing before gully/vent connection. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Using robotic cutter reinstate 1x Junction connection.
  4. Reline approximately 1 meter of root infested material change from plastic to Existing Reline. Relining from plastic inspection opening upstream and finishing on previously relined bathroom line feeding unit 2 bathroom. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  5. Flow test pipework after relining.
  6. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining
  7. Supply all video of the relining works after completion.
  8. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  9. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on unit 1's common sewer pipework

Following our CCTV camera survey we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework under unit 1's bathroom in 2 separate locations with tree roots entering the shower branch line and the toilet branch line.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2.5 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from the middle bathroom floor drain downstream, finishing on plastic pipework before gully connection outside using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin and reinstate 1 x junction connection to the shower. Also to reline approximately 1.5 to 2 meters of root infested earthenware toilet branch line, relining from plastic pipework in unit 1 over material change and root infested earthenware pipework, finishing back onto plastic pipework outside using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 

Re-run basin line approximately 1 meter in PVC pipework, fittings and connect into common sewer stack pipe located outside of unit 1. This will eliminate all underground pipework and is cheaper to re run this section than it is to reline.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Gain access to unit 1 and lay protective sheeting on the floor leading to the bathroom.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean sewer line preparation for relining.
  3. Maxi mill and sand all plastic pipework to AS3500 standards.
  4. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Prepare, measure and cut liner to correct length. 
  2. Turn off the water supply to unit 1 and drain the water from the line.
  3. Reline approximately 2.5 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from the middle bathroom floor drain downstream, finishing on plastic pipework before gully connection outside using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  4. Reline approximately 1.5 to 2 meters of root infested earthenware toilet branch line, relining from plastic pipework in unit 1 over material change and root infested earthenware pipework, finishing back onto plastic pipework outside using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  5. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  6. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line. 
  7. Using robotic cutter Reinstate 1 x junction connections for the shower line.
  8. Re-run basin line approximately 1 meter in PVC pipework and connect into common stack pipe located outside of unit 1
  9. Turn on the water supply to unit 1 and flow test relined pipework after relining.
  10. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining.
  11. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  12. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  13. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  14. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.
  • All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Total cost of works - $9,850.00 + GST

Please note - Following our CCTV camera survey no faults were found with the junction connecting the floor waste picking up the shower/laundry and do not consider repairs to be necessary at this time. 

Additional cost as an option to to install 1 x satellite junction repair (complete T section) Relining from newly installed relined floor waste line relining into shower/ laundry branch line completely sealing junction and finishing new reline on plastic pipework in branch-line, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin. 

Cost of works if approved with scope of works $3,300.00 + GST
Cost of works if taken at a later date $3,950.00 + GST

following this branch line we found it elbows up and picked up the planta box drain on the opposite side of the leak at the top of the stairs. After extensive flood tested of the planter box, no water leaked.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 11.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 11, removed cupboard, inspected the common service riser adjacent to the bathroom and located a burst common 25mm cold water copper pipe.

We found the common cold water copper pipework to be in very bad condition and multiple previous patch repairs on the cold water pipework. Video link of burst cold water pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N4FIZ

Turned off the buildings cold water supply and drained the water from the line. Repaired burst section of cold water copper pipework as a temporary repair, to isolate the water leak and prevent further water damage to unit 11.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 11 to prevent further burst cold water pipes - We advise to notify the building of water shut down and sewer works, gain access to unit 11 and remove cupboard located in front of service riser, cut out and remove 100mm cast iron stack to access the faulty cold water copper pipework, turn off water supply, cut out 25mm copper pipework, replacing tee for cold water isolation valve and re running to isolation valve, install new 100mm PVC pipework for sewer stack, test all works carried out and clean all areas where work had taken place. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Whilst in unit 11 we also found water damage to the carpet outside the shower. Flood tested the original shower recess with red dye and following testing we found the red dye to be leaking out of the shower recess confirming the waterproof membrane within the shower has failed and requires replacement. Video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N4FHB

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 11 - We advise to remove the tiles from the shower recess, 1st course of wall ties and hob, install new sand cement bed with correct fall, install primer, 2 coats of waterproof membrane and re-tile the shower recess and 1st course of wall tiles. We will submit a separate quotation shortly to re-build the leaking shower recess in unit 11.

After all works have been completed in unit 11, we advise a carpet contractor is engaged and the water damaged carpet is steam cleaned or replaced.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework at the property.

Following the recent sewer clear out works and our CCTV camera survey, we found tree roots entering the common sewer pipework in multiple different locations. We have cleared out these tree root infestation with the use of high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera, but the tree roots will grow back and cause further blockages if not repaired.

This quotation is to reline 4 x sections of tree root infested sections of original common earthenware sewer pipework at the building as a full proof repair to prevent further blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

Preparation -

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property.
  3. Gain access into garages and laundry rooms.
  4. Set up safe working areas around property.
  5. Using high pressure water jet and CCTV drain drain clear the complete sewer system before relining.
  6. Camera Record each line before relining.

Relining Works & excavation works:

  1. (Blue section on diagram) Dig down in garden bed area (located front right of property to gain access into the sewer line.
  2. Make correct access into the sewer line for the reline repairs to be completed.
  3. Backfill hole with existing sand and leave area clean and tidy.
  4. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  5. (Red section on diagram) Install 1x 100x100x45 Junction repair ( Complete Y section ) Relining cracked root infested junction. Relining from earthenware mainline into branch-line feeding into garage 17, Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  6. (Green section on Diagram) Reline approximately 14 meters of root infested, cracked earthenware joints relining from stack connection (ground level) in Laundry room 8. 10 meters downstream cover all badly broken and root infested joints, Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  7. Using robotic cutter reinstate 4 junction on mainline.
  8. (Purple on diagram) Reline approximately 3 meters of laundry room branch-line sealing all root infested joint using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  9. (Yellow section on diagram) Install approximately 1-2 meters of structural fibre glass liner. relining over cracked displaced earthenware joints on main line finishing back onto earthenware pipework, Using watermarked approved line with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  10. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test and commission all relined pipework.
  11. Reinstate all access points made at stack bases around property.
  12. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  13. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  14. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  15. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  16. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  17. Supply updated sewer diagram showing newly relined sections.

Please note - On the day of inspection we have look at approximately 80% of the sewer line. we was unable to gain access into garages 11 and 18. we was also unable to check the sewer line that runs across the front garden due to limited access.

All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to the roof hot water plant to inspect the faulty circulating pump.

Found the common hot water circulating pump to be switched off at the power and the pump to be isolated.

Turned on the power to the pump, which caused the power point to trip at the main power switch in the laundry indicating a faulty pump.

Removed the circulating pump cover and found moisture within the electrics causing the fault.

Poured a bucket of water over the awning roof above the heaters and caused the roof to leak, we found the roof never leaked directly onto the pump.

Inspected the hot water heater flues and found them to be close to the awning roof which is trapping the hot air under the roof canopy causing condensation.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty circulating pump is replaced and to prevent moisture affecting the new circulation pump, we advise the common hot water circulating pump is relocated. We Will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 17.

Urgently attended the property on the 20/8/24, gained access into unit 17 and found the carpet outside the bathroom to be badly water damaged.

We were unable to pressure test the hot and cold water supply as the hot and cold water isolation valves failed and required urgent replacement.

Put notification up on the building advising a building water shut down.

Returned to the property on the 22/8/24,  shut down the buildings water supply and drained the water from the line.

Gained access into unit 17, disconnected the faulty common cold and hot water isolation valves. 

Installed new hot and cold water isolation valves in unit 17. Turned on the buildings water supply and tested all works carried out.

Carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing in unit 17 and following pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst pressurized hot water copper pipe in unit 17.

Engaged pipe location leak detection after hours, used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water supply in the concrete slab and bathroom walls.

Used listening device and leak detector to pint point the burst hot water pipe to be located within the internal shower wall which is the cause of the leak.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 17 - We advise to remove affected tiles and excavate the internal shower wall,  cut out burst hot water copper pipework, install new copper pipework, fittings, test all works, patch render wall, install waterproof membrane and re-tile using tiles as close as possible to match. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed, we advise a caret contractor is engaged to steam clean or replace the water damaged carpet in unit 17.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leaking stormwater above unit 3's garage.

Attended the property, gained access and found the common stormwater pipework above unit 3's garage to be broken and blocked causing water to leak into the garage.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to common area above the garages. Used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear multiple blockages in the common storm water piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the storm water piping and found tree root infestations are entering the original earthenware storm water piping. 

Used the jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and the drain camera simultaneously to clear out the storm water piping from the base of the downpipe to the vertical junction and from the drain above the garages clearing the vertical dropper and stormwater lines.

Following our camera survey, we located tree roots entering the common stormwater pipework from multiple breaks in the branch line connecting the downpipe approximately 10 meters and from the downpipe junction and vertical dropper approximately 3 meters. 

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak into garage number 3 below - To prevent further tree roots entering the common stormwater pipework causing blockages, we advise this section of common stormwater pipework is re-lined. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our re-lining team.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 3 and leak in garage 3. 

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found water leaking through the ceiling and cornice outside the bathroom. We also found water damage to the bathroom wall.

Gained access into unit 7 above and located a burst lot owners hot water heater which was the cause of the water leak into unit 3.

Isolated the water and electrical supply to the burst hot water heater to prevent further water damage to common property. We have organized with unit 7 to replace the burst hot water tomorrow at the lot owners cost.

Inspected garage number 3 on the left hand side of the building, found the common sewer line to be blocked and leaking out of the inspection opening within the garage.

Removed boundary trap lid in front of the garage and found the boundary trap to be completely blocked.

Returned to the property the following day once the occupant cleared the goods out of the garage, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream the boundary trap to clear the blockage at the base of the shaft. Used CCTV drain camera to locate the base of the boundary trap to be collapsed and another collapsed section of original earthenware sewer pipework under the road.

Flow tested common sewer pipework and boundary trap which is clear and flowing. Please note - If the boundary trap and outlet pipework downstream to Sydney waters main is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur. 

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had  taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the collapsed and defective original earthenware boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main under the road is relined as a full proof solution to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

We also advise the resultant water damage in unit 3 is repaired and painted. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting required to be undertaken in unit 3.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 10/08/2024 - Urgent flooding in the basement fire stairs.

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access and found the fire stairs adjacent to the lift shaft in the carpark to be flooded.

Removed the pit lid to the common stormwater pumps in the lobby, inspected the pumps and found the water level to be full within the pit, overflowing and the high level alarm to be activated.

Adjusted the float switches, activated the 2 x pumps but found the pumps were only slightly working and not removing water quickly.

Walked around the property and identified a bust water main on the street which is causing the water to leak into the carpark stormwater system.

As the the common stormwater OSD detention pit was full, the  common stormwater pumps were not in working order and there was a large amount of water flowing into the OSD tank from the burst, we were required to urgently re-attend the property with 2 x plumbers and pump out the large OSD retention tank to prevent flooding into the common lift shaft and switchboard room.

Returned to the property after hours with 2 x plumbers and 2 x submersible pumps, hoses and drop sheets.

Removed the pit lid, set up 2 x submersible pumps within the common stormwater pit and ran hoses on drop sheets through the lobby, out to the curb and gutter in the street.

The 2 x submersible pumps took approximately 4-5 hours to completely drain the large OSD retention pit and flooded water in the fire stairs.

CCTV video link of water leaking into the pit of the burst pipe - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N3MTI

CCTV video link of faults found within the float switch - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N3MTS

Once all the water was removed from the common stormwater pit, we climbed down into the pit and found 200mm of sand and debris at the base of pit which is required to be cleaned out and removed.

Tested the float switches and found them to be faulty, not always activating the pumps when lifted.

Set up submersible pumps within the fire stairs and removed flood water from the fire stairs and common areas.

Further URGNT works required to be undertaken - We have already called and advised A-line pumps to urgently return to the property and repair the common stormwater pumps and float switches, so the water from the burst main in the street cannot cause any further flooding at the property.

We also advise the common stormwater pit is cleaned out AFTER HOURS using a sucker truck, to remove the 200mm build up of sand and debris at the base of the pit which can cause blockages to the stormwater pumps - We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended property and found the over flow sewer gully located on Chambers St to be blocked.

Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line and branch line affecting unit 1

Following the recent emergency sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework and mainline junction downstream of unit 1's toilet.

This quotation is to reline approximately 6-7 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from the stack base connection downstream to the mainline junction covering all root infested joints using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin, reinstate the 1 x junction connection on mainline using robotic cutter. Also Install 150x100x45 satellite junction (Complete Y section) relining from common mainline into unit 1s Branch-line, sealing heavily root infested cracked junction.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Gain access into garage 7 sewer access point OR remove toilet in unit 1.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean sewer line preparation for relining.

  2. Reline approximately 6-7 meters of root infested sewer line, relining from stack connection located in garage 7 downstream, finishing reline at main line junction using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

  4. Install 150mm x 100mm x 45 degree satellite Junction reline (Complete Y section) relining from common mainline into unit 1s branch-line, sealing heavily root infested cracked junction.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test relined pipework after relining.
  6. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer line after relining.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework on the outlet of the boundary trap where the pipework changes from 150mm to 225mm diameter which was the cause of the common sewer blockage.

This urgent quotation is to reline over root infested material change before Sydney's main sewer connection, relining from plastic pipework after boundary trap sealing 150mm x 225mm diameter change and finishing reline before Sydney main sewer connection, using watermarked approved liner with 2 Part Epoxy resin. 

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Gain access to sewer inspection openings located on property garden.
  3. Gain access to Sydney waters main sewer chamber located on property.
  4. Using high pressure water jet blaster clean sewer line before relining.
  5. Maxi-Mill Plastic pipework to AS3500 Relining standards.
  6. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline over root infested material change before Sydney's main sewer connection, relining from plastic pipework after boundary trap sealing 150mm x 225mm diameter change and finishing reline before Sydney main sewer connection, using watermarked approved liner with 2 Part Epoxy resin. 
  3. Cure liner using hot water boiler.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  5. Flow test all works carried out and commission all relined pipework.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS 3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  10. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.

Please note - By relining this section of pipework it covers the last connection owned by the building. The reline will completely seal the material change from plastic to earthenware and guarantee no future roots enter on this section again in the future.

All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the . duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate water leak into the next door neighbour number 11 Fletcher St.

We were only able to partially clear the blockage and the common boundary trap for the building is still blocked and requires URGENT repairs.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the common sewer blockage - We advise to remove affected pavers, excavate the concrete and ground next to the large tree located at the rear left of the building, turn off the water supply to the building, cut out collapsed 150mm earthenware boundary trap, supply and install new 150mm PVC boundary trap, pipework, fittings, turn on the buildings water supply, test all works, bed pipework, back fill trench, compact ground and reinstate concrete. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

  • STAGE 5 - Reline 4.5 meters of tree root infested original sewer pipework

Whilst undertaking stage 2 and our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations entering approximately 4.5 meters of original earthenware pipework. Please location on drawing marked in purple.

This quotation is to reline approximately 4.5 meters of earthenware sewer line. Relining from top of vertical shaft down finishing on previously relined pipework, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property.
  3. Set up safe working areas around property.
  4. Using high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera, milling tool and sanding paddles to clear the complete sewer system before relining.
  5. Camera Record each line before relining.

- Relining:

  1. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 4.5 meters of earthenware sewer line. Relining from top of vertical shaft down finishing on previously relined pipework, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Cure reline with hot water.
  4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test and commission all relined pipework.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  10. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.

Please note - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty

Description:
Quotation - Preventative maintenance jet blasting & CCTV camera survey works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared at the rear of the property and our CCTV camera survey, we located multiple areas where tree root infestations are entering the original earthenware main sewer line causing sewer blockages at the property.

This quotation is to use a high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree root infestations from the common main sewer line to the boundary trap on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months to prevent sewer blockages and floods at the property. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Remove inspection opening lids on the main common sewer line. 
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out multiple tree root infestations from the earthenware sewer piping from the rear of the property to the main boundary trap.
  3. Flush out all overflow relief gullys using high pressure water jet blaster. 
  4. Use CCTV drain camera to ensure all tree roots have been cut out of the sewer piping. Following our CCTV camera survey if any broken or collapsed sewer pipes are found we will report back. 
  5. Flow test common sewer pipework to the main boundary trap. 
  6. Reinstall inspection opening lids and clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant. 
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate basement leak and blocked sewer.

Attended the property, gained access and found the common sewer piping to be completely blocked and surcharging.

Removed inspection opening lids on the common boundary trap and found it to be completely blocked.

Set up the jet blaster and ran hoses, Used jet blaster with tree root cutting heads to try and clear out the common sewer pipework to Sydney Waters main.

Lifted lids on the Sydney water main and found the main to be blocked.

Called Sydney water and lodged an urgent job with them, who advised they will attend within approximately 4 hours - Reference number: 9235 5604

Returned to the property the following day after Sydney Water attended and found the common sewer and outlet of the boundary trap still fully blocked.

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads downstream of the boundary trap and upstream from Sydney Water manhole to clear out the tree roots from the sewer piping.

After extensive jet blasting, we cleared out all tree roots from the common sewer piping on the outlet of the boundary trap to Sydney Waters main.

Flow tested the sewer piping with a high pressure hose - All clear and in good working order.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent common sewer blockages on the outlet of the boundary trap to Sydney Waters main caused by tree root infestations, we advise the common sewer pipework is relined. Once we have reviewed these works with our relining team, we will submit an urgent quotation for the further relining works required to be undertaken.

Investigate water leaks in the carpark.

8/7 - Attended the property, gained access into the basement garages and located a water leak from the concrete slab and electrical conduit outside garage 4. Also located a second leak from the light fitting and conduit in the fire escape.

Both water leaks appear below the junction box and new electrical conduit for the carpark lights, where the conduits penetrate into the concrete below the external garden area above.

Gained access to the common garden area above, stepped out the leak and could not find where the conduit's turn-up within the grassed area.

Excavated down to the concrete slab, cleaned and primed all areas on the concrete slab surrounding the conduit penetrations and piping.

Sealed all electrical conduits, breaks and pipework where it goes into the concrete slab using high grade flexible sealant.

Applied 2 x coats of waterproof membrane over the affected areas of concrete slab and penetrations in the garden.

Backfilled and compacted the area, reinstated as best as possible installing pavers and pot plants.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - Following the conduit sealing works in the external garden area, we advise the leak in the garages is monitored and if the leak returns further investigation works are required.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent after hours sewer flood in unit 1's kitchen and our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework located under the concrete driveway.

This quotation is to install a sectional reline repair relining over the tree root infested section of earthenware sewer pipework under the concrete driveway, using watermarked approved line with 2 part Epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation:
  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property.
  3. Set up safe working areas around property.
  4. Using high pressure water jet blaster, CCTV drain camera, milling tool and sanding paddles to clear the complete sewer system before relining.
  5. Camera Record each line before relining.
  • Relining works:
  1. Turn off the buildings cold  water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Install sectional reline repair sealing over the tree root infested and dislodged common earthenware pipework located under the concrete driveway, using watermarked approved line with 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Cure liner using hot water.
  4. Once the reline has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test and commission all relined pipework.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.
  10. Carry out free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee.

Please note - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate blocked sewer causing gurgling in unit 1.

Attended property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging from the overflow gullies on the left side of the building causing the blockage in unit 1.

Removed inspection opening lids on the common sewer stack and used a high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the b lockage and release the common sewer line. 

Used CCTV drain camera to locate multiple areas of tree root infestations entering in the original earthenware sewer piping on the left hand side of the building.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages - We advise the tree root infested original earthenware common sewer pipework on the left side is relined as a full proof solution to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

If the building does not have the funds to undertake the relining works, we advise the tree root infestations are cleared out of the common sewer line on a preventative maintenance program. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the preventative maintenance option.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent urgent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework downstream the common sewer stack in unit 5's garage causing the sewer blockage/flood in unit 5's downstairs bathroom and laundry.

This urgent quotation is to reline approximately 6 meters of cast iron and earthenware pipework, relining from cast iron inspection opening located in garage 5, 6 meters downstream covering cracked root infested joints and dislodgement's finishing reline before mainline, using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise affected units to not use their waste fixtures when relining works are undertaken.
  2. Gain access to unit 5's garage in preparation for relining.

  2.   4. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  5. Flow test all works carried out and commission all relined pipework.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS 3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 406.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 406 and found water damage to the carpet in the living room, behind the kitchen bench.

Pulled back the carpet and found water within the concrete chase where the hot water pipework was previously re-run.

Isolated the hot an cold water supply and carried out nitrogen pressure testing and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 406.

Removed the base panel below the kitchen sink to access the skirting cavity and found the chipboard timber supports for the cabinetry to be wet within the skirting.

Returned to the property the following day, gained access into unit 406.

Cut a hole in the kitchen cabinets and used the inspection camera within the void to rule out any leaks from the benchtop joints - No leaks were found.

Pulled out the dishwasher and found it to be dry underneath, carried out testing by running a cycle on the dishwasher and instantly water leaked from the clip securing the hose, down the back of the cabinets. Please see video link of leak - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NZCIB

Isolated the water supply to the dishwasher and advised the occupant not to use until it is replaced or serviced by the lot owner of unit 406.

Re-concreted the chase in the living room floor, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish form the property.

Urgent quotation - To replace the leaking common shower recess & re-grout the shower walls in unit 6.

This quotation to excavate the shower recess floor tiles, hob, first course of wall tiles, install new waterproof membrane and re-tile shower recess floor tiles, hob, first course of wall tiles and to re-grout 2 x internal shower wall tiles.

  3. Remove the entire shower recess floor tiles and 1st row of shower wall tiles.
  4. Repair base of shower walls.
  5. Seal penetration through the concrete slab and install puddle flange.
  6. Cork all corners using sealant. 
  7. Apply hydrepoxy primer and  two coats of acrylic polyurethane membrane as per BCA .
  8. Installation of sand cement bed falling to the drain.
  9. Re tile shower recess and first course of shower walls using tiles as close as possible to match existing.
  10. Installation of high grade flexible sealant within the shower recess, vertical wall and behind the tap spindles.

  13. Clean all areas where work has taken place.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages in the out house toilet - We advise the tree root infested sewer pipework is relined as a full proof solution.

Invoice Description:
Investigate gas smells at the property.

21/06 - Attended the property and investigated the gas smell at the front of the building.

Used gas detector and located readings of gas within the front garden, grassed area where the gas piping goes through the retaining wall.

To confirm the gas leak, we are required to isolate the buildings gas supply and pressure test the common gas piping from the gas meter manifold to the path valve. As the common gas line is high pressure the gas is required to be isolated to carry out investigation and repair works.

Put up notices around the building advising resident of gas disruptions on Wednesday the 26th June between 9am and 3pm.

26/06 - Returned to the property and carried out pressure testing on the gas piping from the path valve to the meters and on the individual gas meter outlets at the property.

Following testing, we identified the buildings main gas piping to be in good working order and no leaks were found from nitrogen pressure testing the main gas line.

After drop testing the outlet piping from the meters, we located a large drop in pressure from unit 5’s outlet gas piping to their fixtures within the unit.

As there was a large drop in pressure, we have isolated the gas supply to unit 5 and left an access request note on their door advising the occupant their gas supply has been turned off and to call Treat plumbing.

Whilst at the property, we have contacted Jemena Gas Network and advised them of the leak on their service before the path valve. Reference number 403057424

27/06 - Returned to the property the following day on the 27/06, gained access into unit 5 and found gas piping to the BBQ on the balcony and the fire place in the living room.

Used gas detector and bubble leak spray on all accessible pipework within unit 5 and no leaks were found. Disconnected the BBQ, tested and found the BBQ is not causing the gas leak.

Used gas detector and bubble leak spray around the piping on the external wall near the gas meter and found a burst copper gas pipe at low level above the gas meter.

Cut out the burst copper gas pipe at low level and installed new copper pipe and fittings. Turned the gas supply back on and found the meter ticking over constantly indicating additional leaks.

Inspected the copper gas pipework for unit 5 on the external wall and found rusted brackets and fixings in sections securing the pipework approximately 8 meters high to where it goes into the roof eaves.

We consider unit 5's external copper gas pipework on the external wall has rusted in several location where clipped and caused the copper pipe to burst. As there is still a gas leak and the pipework is not accessible, we have left the gas supply off to unit 5 until the pipework on the external wall is replaced.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To rectify the gas to unit 5, we advise unit 5's common gas pipework on the external wall is replaced with new copper pipe, copper saddles and stainless steel fixings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further work required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 902.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 902 and found water damage to the internal wardrobe wall in the bedroom adjacent to bathtub.

Used moisture meter to confirm high readings of moisture within the internal wardrobe wall.

Inspected the seals around the bath and found the silicone seals had cracked and the bath had become separated from the wall. 

Cut a hole in the bath panel, inspected under the bath and found water to be pooling under the bath.

Dye tested the bath waste and the silicone seals where the bath lip meets the wall tiles. From dye testing we found the faulty seals around the bath edge causing water to leak under the bath.

Used aqua vacuum and removed build up of water under the bath and covered the hole made in the side of the bath.

Returned to the property and gained access into unit 902.

Cut out faulty sealant where the bath meets the common wall tiles and vertical wall, cleaned and primed affected areas in preparation for resealing and installed new high grade flexible sealant to all affected areas in the shower bath area and vertical wall.

Installed metal vent covering the hole made in the side of the bath panel, cleaned all areas where work had take place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Due to movement in the bath and as the bath is not recessed inside the wall, we consider the resealing works carried out to be a temporary repair.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 902. To rectify further water leaking under the bath, we advise the bath is removed, and a new steel bath is installed and recessed inside the wall.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

To arrive and set up jet blasting equipment through the side passage and over the fence.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blockage in unit 10.

Urgently attended the property, removed inspection opening on the common sewer stack located on the external wall connecting unit 10's bathroom and found the common in ground sewer pipework to be completely blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment through the side passage and over the fence.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the sewer stack to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the base of the sewer stack and original earthenware sewer pipework for approximately 6 meters downstream which was the cause of the blockage in unit 10.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree root infestations from the common sewer pipework.

Flow tested common sewer pipework - All clear and in good working order. Please note if repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested original earthenware pipework further sewer blockages and floods will re-occur in unit 10.

Reinstalled inspection opening lid and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages in unit 10 - We advise to reline the tree root infested original earthenware pipework downstream from the stack outside unit 10 down the side passage for proximately 6 meters and reinstate junctions using robotic cutter. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 502 and found water leaking from the common stack penetration in the ceiling cavity above the toilet.

We will send an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed, we will submit a quotation for the resultant damage repairs and tiling in unit 602. 

Pipe location leak detection advised us, if the burst pipe was not found in the laundry wall of unit 602 then the burst pressurized pipe is located inside the concrete slab and is required to be rerun.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
AFTER HOURS BLOCKAGE

Unit 2, laundry and bathroom fixtures blocked.
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on Sunday - Blockage in unit 2's bathroom

Urgently attended the property after hours on Sunday, gained access into unit 2, found all the bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked and flooding out of the floor waste causing water damage to the carpet outside the bathroom.

Used electric eel downstream the floor waste but we were unable to clear the blockage.

Disconnected and removed toilet to access the common sewer pipework. Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment into unit 2's bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework downstream which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree roots from the common earthenware sewer pipework.

Flow tested all fixtures in the bathroom - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if repairs are not undertaken the tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework further sewer blockages will re-occur in unit 2's bathroom.

Returned to the property on Monday 17/6/24 when the suppliers were open, re-installed toilet connecting water and waste, sealing to the ground using high grade flexible sealant.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages in unit 2 - We advise the tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework downstream from unit 2's toilet is relined as a full proof solution to prevent further blockages and floods in unit 2. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

We also advise advise the water damaged carpet outside the bathroom is either steam cleaned or replaced.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in B1 carpark below units 2,8 & 13.

6/6 - Attended the property, gained access into the carpark on B1 and found water leaking from the water pipe penetrations below units 2, 8 & 13.

Gained access into units 2, 8 and 13. Inspected and located the water services behind the riser boxed out in the kitchen.

Removed service riser panel in unit 13 and found there to be no leaks within the common pipework and the cavity was all dry.

Unit 8 had no service riser access, excavted holes high up in the gyprock and besablock walls and a made holes in the kicthen cabinetry removing the gas meter, cutting melamine and excvating gyprock and besa block walls. Found high up in the common service riser around the pipes to be dry and the concrete slab at floor level to be damp.

Gained access into unit 2, excavated a hole high up in the gyprock and besablock walls and located water leaking from the ceiling concrete slab and pipe penetrations indicating the leak is between levels 2 & 8.

Carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply in unit 8 and found the cold water isolation valve to be faulty causing a drop in pressure.

Advised the building manager the cold water isolation valve in unit 8 requires replacement and organised water disruptions notifying residents.

11/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 8, isolated the buildings cold water supply and installed new isolation valve in the hallway cupboard. Turned the buildings water supply back on testing all works.

Carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot, cold and tempered water supply in unit 8 and no drop in pressure was found.

12/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 2 & 8.

Excavated a tile on the side of the bath in unit 8 to inspect the cavity under the bath but found it was all dry and the leak was not coming from the bathroom.

Made a larger hole in the common service riser under the kitchen cabinets and used inspection camera to inspect all common pipes within the service duct at concrete slab level.

From our inspection with the camera, we located water leaking from the hot water lagging at concrete slab level from the common hot water pipework servicing unit 8, before the hot water meter. The pipework is located at the back of the riser behind the buildings main hot water and sewer stack risers.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 8 - We advise a large hole is made within the kitchen cabinets, removing the gas meter and excavating the melamine and besablock walls, isolate the buildings hot water and the hot water riser is cut out to gain access to the common hot water pipework behind, and the burst common hot water pipe is repaired using copper pipe and fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Covered holes made using core flue, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water damaged bedroom wall in unit 1.

6/6 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water damaged skirting and wall in the bedroom adjacent to the bathroom.

Isolated the hot and cold water supply in unit, carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the shower breach, hot and cold water pipework and no drop in pressure was found, indicating no burst pipes in unit 1.

Dye tested the shower recess with yellow dye and no dye was found to be leaking into the bedroom from the wall.

Inspected the basin waste penetration below the vanity, tile cut out and found water underneath the tile bed around the basin waste indicating water leaking under the tile bed.

The carpet in the bedroom was dry to touch and there was no water leaking into the carpark through the penetrations.

13/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 1 and used thermal image camera to insect the bedroom wall. Found the highest reading of moisture behind the vanity basin. Thermal image camera identified no moisture beside the column and window frame where the previous leak was identified.

Carried out extensive testing in the bathroom fixtures. Flood tested the basin waste and found no water leaking under the tile bed below the basin waste penetration tile cut out. Tested the toilet several times and no water leaked under the tile bed below the basin waste penetration tile cut out.

Inspected the internal shower wall tiles and found a vertical crack in the grouting from floor to ceiling. Removed the shower head and carried out extensive flood testing of the shower wall tiles and vertical grout crack and found water to leak from under the tile bed below the basin waste penetration tile cut out. 

Used thermal image camera to confirm the highest reading of moisture within the bedroom wall where water is trapped underneath the tile bed and along the wall, below the basin.

After extensive flood testing of the bathroom, we found there to be no water leaking into the carpark below, the rising damp wall is caused by water leaking into the tile bed from the cracked grout in the shower recess. 

The thermal image camera indicated the leak from the cavity wall and window frames has been resolved.

Removed mouldy skirting in the bedroom to try and allow the wall to dry, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 1 - We advise the cracked grouting on the shower wall is sealed by a professional sealing contractor to ensure the crack does not return, we consider re-grouting will not prevent the crack from re-appearing.

Once the repairs have been carried out in unit 1's shower, we advise the thermal image camera is used to determine if the leak has been resolved.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 07/06/2024 - Investigate gas smell in unit 3.

7/6 - Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 3 and found the gas to be turned off.

Turned on the gas supply at the meter, used gas detector inside unit 3 and no gas smells were present.

Bubble leak sprayed all gas fittings and pipework within unit 3 and on the external wall and no gas leaks were found.

11/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 3 and found a strong gas smell in the kitchen and lounge room.

Carried out a drop test on the gas piping for unit 3 and found a small drop in pressure to be coming from the faulty gas regulator.

Carried out a drop test on unit 9's meter and original galvanised steel pipework and found a large drop in pressure indicating a common gas leak. 

Isolated the gas supply to unit 9 to prevent further gas leaks and left a note with unit 9.

12/6 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 9 and inspected gas appliances in the kitchen and living room.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 9 - We advise to re-run a new copper gas service from the outlet of the gas meter outside connecting unit 9's gas cooktop, hot water heater and bayonet deleting the burst pressurized gas pipe under the building. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 9.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 3 - We advise the faulty gas meter regulator is replaced. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 3.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 2.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2 and found water damage to the internal bedroom wall adjacent to the bathroom.

Used moisture meter to locate high readings of moisture within the internal bedroom wall.

Inspected the original bathroom, isolated the water supply and carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the shower/bath breach, hot and cold water supply. Following extensive pressure testing no burst pipes were found in unit 2.

Carefully removed 1 x tile and excavated a small hole on the front face of the bath and found water pooling under the bath.

Flood dye tested the bath waste and toilet and no leaks were found.

Flood tested where the bath meets the internal shower/bath wall tiles and found water leaking under the bath confirming the leak.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken at the lot owners cost in unit 2 - We advise to cut out the faulty sealant where the bath meets the internal wall tiles and re-seal using high grade flexible sealant. We will submit a quotation shortly for the lot owners consideration in unit 2.

After the sealing works have been completed, we advise the lot owner engages a painting contractor to repair and paint the resultant water damaged internal bedroom wall in unit 2.

Gained access into unit 6, inspected all fixtures in the renovated bathroom above and no leaks were found.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Description: richard (ec) - blocked upstairs toilet. affecting unit above - suspect stack
Invoice Description:
Investigate sewer blockage in the common area and slow draining toilet in unit 3.

Attended the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked on the right hand side of the building and surcharging out of the overflow relief gully. 

Gained access into unit 3, tested the toilet and found the waste pipework to be slow draining and blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening on the original cast iron sewer stack on the right hand side of the building, used high pressure water jet blaster downstream to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework approximately 12 meters downstream.

Used high pressure jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree roots from the common sewer line.

Flow tested common sewer line - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

As a full proof solution and to prevent further sewer blockages we advise the original sewer pipework is relined. We will return to the property with our relining team to provide a quotation for all relining works.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property today and inspected the pool leak and our cold water switch installation.

Our previous installation included altering of the cold water copper pipework and installation of a control and float switch.

After inspecting the faulty pressure pipework which was not altered or installed by us, we found it to be hanging loosely with no clips or support.

There is no weight on the pressure pipework which could cause this to crack.

To prevent any further pipework from dropping we supported the pipework using a brick on the ground.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the pool plumber is engaged to repair the cracked pressure pipework and secure it using brackets and fixings.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 7D.

3/6 - Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 7d and found wet carpet in the hallway outside the bathroom door.

Flood tested the shower recess and no blockages or leaks were found. 

Isolated the water supply carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply.  

Following pressure testing we found a small drop on the hot water supply and were unable to get an accurate pressure test on the cold water supply as the common isolation valve is faulty and requires replacement.

Put up water shut down notices around the building advising residents of water disruptions.

7/6 - Returned to the property, isolated the buildings water supply and drained the water form the line.

Disconnected the faulty common cold water isolation valve and installed new isolation valve.

Turned the buildings cold water supply back on testing all works.

Engaged pipe location, leak detection and carried out extensive pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply in unit 7D. No burst pipes were found in unit 7D.

Flow tested the shower and found the common waste pipework to be partially blocked in the common stack pipework. 

Removed grated drain in the shower and used electric eel to clear out the common shower waste drain to the common stack.

We were unable to access the bathroom floor waste as it is located under the vanity basin. If further blockages reoccur the vanity basin, is required to be disconnected and temporarily removed to access the common bathroom floor waste.

Flood tested the shower floor drain and no further blockages were found.

We found the water leak and wet carpet in 7D to be caused by the blocked shower drain. No further plumbing works are required.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 7D - We advise the wet carpet in unit 7D is either steam cleaned or replaced.
Inv Description: Service call, Labour, Materials & Eectric Eel.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked kitchen sink, bathroom waste pipework in unit 3 and inspect tap in the bin room.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 3, found the kitchen waste to be completely blocked. We also found the bathroom floor waste next to the toilet to be blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used extension ladder, disconnected kitchen waste pipework on the external wall, used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the blockage in the common kitchen waste pipework. 

Re-connected kitchen waste pipework on the external wall and flow tested unit 3's kitchen - All clear and in good working order.

Ran hoses into the bathroom, used high pressure water jet blaster and aqua vacuum extensively downstream from unit 3's dry floor waste in the bathroom and after extensive jet blasting we were unable to clear the blockage. We were removing a large amount of rust from the original cast iron internal waste pipework which is the cause of the blockage.

Gained access into the bin room and supplied new vandal key for the hose tap.

Returned to the property, gained access into units 1 & 3, to continue to try clear the blockage in the galvanized steel waste pipework.

Cut a small hole in unit 1's bathroom ceiling and could not find any common waste pipework within the ceiling cavity.

Gained access into unit 3's bathroom, used mechanical milling tool downstream the dry floor waste and after extensive clear out works we were unable to clear the blockage.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the blocked floor waste in unit 3's bathroom - We advise to lay drop sheets in unit 3, disconnect and remove the toilet, remove affected tiles and excavate the floor, core drill new hole through the external wall, install new PVC pipework, fittings discharging out of the external wall, re-concrete bathroom floor, install new waterproof membrane and re-tile affected area matching existing tiles as close as possible to match. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 3. 

We advise the resultant water damaged bathroom celling in unit 1 is repaired and painted. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Quotation - Reline the corroded and defective original internal cast iron kitchen stack connecting units 6 and 11

Following the recent blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we found the original 80mm cast iron stack pipe connecting units 6 and 11's kitchen to be badly corroded and requires repairs to prevent further common blockages.

This quotation is to gain access into units 6 and 11, use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS- 3500 before relining, cut out junction in unit 11 and install new plastic junction which will pick up kitchen lines, cut out section of plasterboard in unit 6 to gain access to junction, cut out and replace with new PVC junction, gain access to roof space above unit 11, cut out section of cast iron pipework to connect on 80mm PVC which can currently let water leak into the roof space, reline 12m of 65mm diameter pipework using our watermark approved epoxy relining system, reinstate 2 x junctions with the use of robotic cutter, re-plumb pipework in unit 6 and 11 and plumb vent pipe to newly relined pipework in roof space.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise affected units of water disruptions. 
  2. Gain access into units 6 and 11.
  3. Lay protective sheeting on floors to work space areas.
  4. Clear lines using high pressure water jet.
  5. Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS3500.
  6. Record footage of lines before relining.

- Pipe relining

  1. Cut out junction in unit 11 and install new plastic junction which will pick up kitchen lines.
  2. Cut out section of plasterboard in unit 6 to gain access to junction. cut out and replace with new PVC junction.
  3. Gain access to roof space above unit 11. cut out section of cast iron pipework to connect to PVC which can currently let water leak into the roof space.
  4. Reline 12m of 65mm diameter pipework using our watermark approved epoxy relining system
  5. Reinstate 2 x junctions with the use of robotic cutter. 
  6. Re-plumb pipework in unit 6 and 11.
  7. Plumb vent pipe to newly relined pipework in roof space.
  8. Flow test all works carried out.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
  10. Provide CCTV of the relining works to the owners corporation. 

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate water leak in unit 13 and the common hallway.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 13 and found water damage to the living room bulkhead ceiling and water stains on the walls.

Inspected the common hallway outside unit 13 and found water stains on the gyprock ceiling adjacent to the lift shaft.

Accessed the roof from the fire stairs and found 2 x blocked surface drains near the lift shaft and a blocked box gutter on the higher roof.

The 2 x roof drains were blocked with calcium build up within the grates causing the water leak in unit 13 and the common hallway. Removed calcium from the grates and cleared the drain openings.

Removed the basket ball inside the box gutter and foam particles which was blocking the drain, causing it to fill up with water.  Cleaned box gutter and released the build up of water flow testing the drains.

Identified faulty joints within the box gutter that can leak when the box gutter is holding water. Applied 2 x coats of water proof membrane over the affected joints within the box gutter to prevent any further leaking. 

The blocked floor drains on the roof has caused water damage to the bulkhead ceiling in unit 13 and the common hallway ceiling on level 1. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

We also advise the roof and gutters are cleaned on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months and the common storm water drains are cleared with the use of high pressure water jet blaster. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the preventative maintenance works required to be undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - Whilst on the roof, we located a burst hot water heater which requires urgent replacement . Access through unit 19 is required to replace the burst common hot water heater on the roof. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Urgently attended the property after hours Saturday night, located all bathroom fixtures to be blocked and surcharging out of the floor waste when in use.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment in the bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream from the floor waste but we were unable to clear the blockage.

Returned to the property the following day on Sunday 9/6/24 with 2 x plumbers, tried to jet blaster down the floor waste using an aqua vacuum but the blockage was too thick and the bathroom was filling up with water.

We could not locate the boundary trap shaft, we excavated the ground at the rear right of the property exposing boundary trap shaft.

Used CCTV drain camera upstream to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware branch line connecting the floor waste in the bathroom causing the blockage.

CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NSMDT

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the sewer pipework.

Flow tested all fixtures in the bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages - We advise the tree root infested sewer pipework is relined downstream from the floor waste.

My builder Alan was called to U134 as the floor showed signs of lifting in the kitchen.  Concerningly, Alan has found that there is considerable water under the floor.  

The tenant has today reported that from time to time, after a shower he has noticed that water has appeared to trickle out from under the cabinetry in the kitchen on the bathroom side (not the sink side). We weren’t previously aware of this.  Alan checked all the plumbing that he could access in U134 (bathroom and kitchen) and he says it all looks good (Treat did all the plumbing). The property has an original bath which has no effective waterproofing beneath it so perhaps the problem is coming from there or elsewhere and tracking into the kitchen.

I’d be most grateful if you could also inspect and carry out dye tests to determine the source.  It has been like this for some weeks but we did not realise that it was a water issue.

While there is no evidence of water on the ceiling of U134, Alan thought he would check upstairs in U144 (you did the plumbing there too).  He said it also all looks good there.  He brought to my attention that the bathroom ceiling of U144 has core flute sheeting (which he explained to me is a type of plastic) which must have been installed many years ago (it certainly predates the fire detection system which was installed on top of it). He observed that there is an area that has yellowed which suggests that water must have come from U154 at some stage.  This may have been rectified some time ago of course but Alan flagged the possibility that water may be coming from U154 hitting the core flute sheeting and tracking into a cavity and reaching U134 that way.

As yet, I’ve been unable to reach Kelly by phone to issue a WO (Kelly, would you please issue a WO ) but I’d be most grateful if you could attend to determine the problem as there is a fair bit of water present and we wish to avoid further damage within U134 and prevent damage to U124 below before it occurs. 

Probably best to start the investigation in U134’s bathroom, then its kitchen and if that’s not the problem you may need to access U144 and U154.

Investigate water pooling in the garage.

22/5 - Attended the property, gained access into the carpark and found the concrete slab to be completely dry and there was no residual water from the leak.

Invoice Description:
Investigate 2 x water leaks in unit 7.

Attended the property and gained access into unit 7.

Bathroom ceiling leak - Found water leaking from the bathroom ceiling and downlight.

Cut a hole in the gyprock bathroom ceiling and inspected inside the ceiling cavity.

Directly above the ceiling, we found a large gap in the roof tiles where light was shining through into unit 4.

Used a ladder and climbed onto the tiled roof above unit 7.

Inspected the roof tiles above the bathroom and found the front capping tiles have lifted / not installed correctly, creating a large gap in the tile mortar.

Lifted the roof tile beside the capping and found holes in the sarking below the tiles where we can see directly into the bathroom below.

Bedroom leak near front balcony - Found water damage to the ceiling and cornice in the bedroom adjacent to the balcony.

Used moisture meter and identified low - medium readings.

Cut a hole in bedroom ceiling and found damp timber joists and mould directly above within the ceiling cavity.

Used a ladder, gained onto the roof above the front bedroom and inspected the tiles above the leak.

Found there to be a cracked tile which was previously sealed with silicone. The tile had moved, shifting downwards and the crack was not sealed towards the top end of the tile.

Applied additional silicone over the crack and previous silicone with high grade flexible sealant to try and prevent any further water leaking during rain events.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise a roofing contractor is engaged to carry out repairs to the roof tiles and sarking above unit 7.

Once the roof tile repair works are carried out, we advise the resultant damage holes cut in the bedroom and bathroom ceiling are repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation shortly for the repairs and painting works required in unit 7.

Covered holes made in the ceiling using core flue, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.
