Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework 

Following the recent after hours sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found tree roots entering the original earthenware common sewer pipework in multiple different locations within the driveway. We have cleared out these tree root infestation but if repairs are not undertaken, the tree roots will grow back and cause further blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down whilst the relining works are being undertaken.
  2. Gain access to all sewer inspection openings around property.
  3. Set up safe working area around property.
  4. Using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera clear out all tree roots and debris in preparation for relining.
  5. Camera inspect and record sewer line before relining.

- Relining Work

- PART B - This includes all part A with additional 10 meters on sewer mainline.

  1. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 8 meters of heavily root infested sewer line. Relining from boundary trap connection (located rear left of the property) 8 meters upstream covering all heavily root infested joints sealing back onto plastic pipework. Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 10 meters of root infested sewer mainline. Relining from plastic inspection opining on mainline 10 meters upstream finishing on plastic pipework sealing all root infested joints. Using watermarked
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE: All Relining works comes with a 25 year Installation Guarantee with a Product Life Expectancy of 50 Years. We also back the 25 year guarantee with a free Annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We strongly recommend using an EPOXY Resin over a SILICATE Resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the area. We only use Epoxy resins.

Turned the gas supply back on to all buildings and tested all works carried out.

Further works required to be undertaken on the shared gas main in the driveway - As advised by Jemena emergency crew, we advise the shared cast iron main in the driveway requires an upgraded. This cost should be shared with the 4 x buildings that it services.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware sewer pipework and junction connecting unit 1.

This quotation is to reline approximately 13 to 4 meters of root infested earthenware mainline, relining from plastic section on sewer line downstream covering all earthenware joints finishing back onto plastic pipework at boundary trap shaft connection and using robotic cutter reinstate 3 x junctions on main line. Also to install a satellite junction repair to root infested junction closet to upstream inspection opening connecting unit 1.  We recommend this repair to seal the inspection opening junction to ensure no blockages come in around the liner at this point where the junction is robotically cut open.

The following works will be undertaken:

  • Preparation
  1. Advise residents of building water shut downs.
  2. Using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera clean all sewer pipework before relining.
  3. Maximill all plastic pipework to AS3500 preparation for relining
  4. Record sewer line onto USB before relining.
  • Relining works 
  1. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 13-14 meters of root infested earthenware mainline, relining from plastic section on sewer line downstream covering all earthenware joints finishing back onto plastic pipework at boundary trap shaft connection sealing all root infested joints, using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Heat cured Epoxy resin.
  3. Using robotic cutter reinstate 3 junctions on mainline.
  4. Install satellite junction reline repair (complete Y junction) sealing the tree root infested junction connecting unit 1's bathroom, using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Heat cured Epoxy resin.
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.
  8. Provide CCTV video of the relining works undertaken to the owners corporation. 

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

I have received the below email and photos from the tenants of 4/3 Lowe Street.

They have reported leaks coming through the tops of the windows and also potentially from the unit above.

Can you please organise for these to be attended to?

It also looks like there is some water ingress from the external walls.
Have any other units in the building reported similar?

Chloe Henriques
Senior Property Manager
McGrath Estate Agents - Company Owned
M 0408 505 288
W www.mcgrath.com.au 

 

Hi Chloe, 

I hope you’re having a good week and staying dry! 

We are having some pretty severe leaks at the flat at 4/3 Lowe St Clovelly. With all this rain we have seen the window seals leaking from the top. It has soaked through multiple towels in the night (in our attempt to protect the walls and carpet from damp) and soaked through to the carpet. This has been occurring in both the main bedroom and living room. The window seals are brand new and only installed under 2 years ago I believe. We’ve had someone come to plug up the holes in the railing (which worked), but the leaking from the top of the window seal is new. There is an excessive amount of water which will lead to moulding of the carpets (which was also newly installed in July prior to us moving in). This issue might be under warranty? It would be worth checking. Photos attached. 

The ceiling has leaked in both the bedrooms. Over the course of a few hours it soaked through the carpet in both bedrooms. It leaks onto our main bed and has been dripping on us whilst we are sleeping. I’m not sure where this water could be coming from, perhaps the flat upstairs? The water in the second bedroom is a yellow colour which is likely very unhygienic. It has occurred during heavy rainfall. Photos attached. 

Also, we have noticed an increase in mould/bubbling coming through the walls. There is black mould on the outside of the building (wall of our bedroom). We are noticing effects on the inside of the wall - the paint is peeling (it was only painted in July before we moved in) and also some black mould is starting to creep in, in small amounts. Photos attached. 

The paint is also cracking/bubbling in the bathroom (it was also only painted in July before we moved in). The walls and ceiling around the shower are becoming flaky and the ceiling fan fell out of the ceiling (due to decaying wood). We have screwed this back in place. We attempt to get air flow through the bathroom as there is no exhaust fan but this does not seem to stop the damp rising. Photos attached. 

We are attempting to keep the flat as dry as possible with regular air flow. If the leaks continue it will result in a pretty unhealthy living environment as well as long term maintenance problems for the owners. 

Thanks
Steph

Out of business hours: 0423 144 958

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 2's bathroom.

10/5 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 2 and found the water leak in the bathroom had stopped.

Carried out pressure testing on the hot water supply and found a drop in pressure on the hot water pipework.

Used the thermal image camera within unit 4's bathroom but could not identify where the leak is located.

Put up water shut down notices around the building advising residents of cold water disruptions to replace the cold water isolation valve in unit 4.

13/5 - Returned to the property, isolated the buildings water supply and drained the water form the line.

Disconnected the faulty cold water isolation valve in unit 4 and installed a new isolation valve. Turned the water supply back on testing all works.

Engaged leak detection and traced out the hot water supply pipes in unit 4. Leak detection advised us to excavate the wall in the laundry where the hot water copper tee is located.

Excavated the laundry wall, exposed the pipework and found the wall and cavity to be dry. Whilst the wall was opened up, we pressure tested the hot water supply in unit 4 and no pressure drop was found.

We advised unit 4 to leave the hot water on to try re-create the burst hot water pipe.

27/5 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 2 and found the leak had stopped.

Gained access into unit 4, carried out pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and no pressure drop was found. Inspected the wall cavity in the laundry and found the wall to be dry.

Cut a hole in the gyprock ceiling in unit 2's bathroom and found there to be a leak coming from a burst, common, copper waste pipe within the ceiling cavity.

Applied high grade sealant over the burst, common, copper waste pipe as a temporary repair within unit 2's ceiling cavity to stop the leak.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 2 - We advise a larger hole is cut in unit 2's bathroom ceiling and the burst copper waste piping is cut out and replaced with PVC pipe and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 2.

Once the plumbing repair works are carried out in unit 2, we advise the resultant damaged bathroom ceiling, cornice and wall in unit 2 is repaired and painted. Also to repair and paint the resultant damaged laundry wall in unit 4. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the repairs and painting works required in unit 2 & 4.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description: Sewer still blocked after syd water celared out the weekend
Invoice Description:
Sydney water emergency contacted us after hours to advise that after they cleared the blockage in their sewer main, the boundary trap for 4 Military Rd was still blocked.

Returned to the property, found the common sewer pipework to be blocked and surcharging sewerage outside unit 7.

Removed inspection opening lids and used a high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found relining resin at the base of the boundary trap causing the blockage in the common sewer piping. Please see CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NITZJ

Used the jet blaster and drain camera simultaneously to clear as much resin as we could to prevent further sewer surcharging outside unit 7.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the contractor who carried out the common sewer relining repairs, returns to the property and removes the relining resin from the boundary trap causing the blockages.

Following our CCTV camera survey we also found the outlet of the original 150mm boundary trap to be cracked and broken. We will return to the property with our relining team to provide a quotation to reline the cracked and broken original earthenware sewer pipework.

We strongly recommend using an EPOXY Resin over a SILICATE Resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the area. We only use Epoxy resins.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked toilet in unit 4.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 4, found the toilet to be gurgling and blocked.

Removed inspection opening lid on the common sewer stack outside unit 4, used CCTV drain camera to locate the common original earthenware sewer pipework to be blocked with major tree root infestations. CCTV camera surveyed upstream unit 4's toilet junction and found major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware branch line under the bathroom.

Laid drop sheets in unit 4 and removed toilet to access the common branch line.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran equipment into unit 4's bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera downstream the toilet waste to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware common branch line under unit 4's bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original eartanwere sewer pipework at the base of the sewer stack outside unit 4's bathroom, tree roots entering the inlet junction connection to the overflow gully next to the stack and tree roots entering approximately 2 meters of earthenware pipework on the main sewer line downstream.

Re-installed toilet sealing to the ground using high grade flexible sealant.

Flow tested toilet and common sewer line outside - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested common earthenware pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will reoccur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further sewer blockages in unit 4 - We advise to remove affected pavers outside unit 4's bathroom, saw cut and excavate the concrete slab, ground, cut out tree root infested earthenware pipework at the base of the stack, overflow gully, install new PVC pipework, fittings, gully and inspection opening raised to the surface in preparation for relining. Reline approximately 3 meters of tree root infested pipework downstream from unit 4's toilet using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin and also reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested pipework on the main line using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin, back fill trench, re-instate concrete and pavers. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent blocked sewer in unit 1.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found the bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked.

Gained access into the backyard and located the common boundary trap, removed bricks on top of the boundary trap and found the boundary trap to have no lid.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to the common sewer in the backyard. Used a high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the blockage upstream of the boundary trap.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping upstream towards the building from the boundary trap and located tree roots entering the pipework approximately 1 meter from the shaft on the 45 fitting causing the blockage. 

We also found a hole in the vertical shaft of the boundary trap shaft causing dirt/debris to enter the base of the boundary trap and cause blockages. 

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the sewer piping upstream from the boundary trap clearing out the mainline.

CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer piping from inside unit 1 on the stack inspection opening and found the sewer line to be all clear after jet blasting.

Tested the common sewer piping with a high pressure hose - all in good working order.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent common sewer blockages at the property caused by tree root infestations, we advise the common sewer pipework is re lined. Once we have reviewed these works with our relining team, we will submit an urgent quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining & excavation works on the common sewer line

Following the recent blockage we cleared outside unit 3's courtyard and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer line and the outlet of the overflow gully to the stack junction. 

This quotation is to saw cut concrete stairs, excavate the concrete and ground, cut out tree root infested overflow gully and pipework downstream to the stack junction, install new PVC gully, pipework and junction on the common stack, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. Then reline approximately 11 meters of root infested earthenware sewer pipework, relining from the sewer stack inspection opening downstream to vertical shaft connection sealing all root infested and dislodged joints, using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin and reinstate 1 junction using robotic cutter.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation & excavation: 

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  3. Record sewer line before relining.
  4. Saw cut concrete stairs.
  5. Excavate the concrete and ground exposing tree root infested common sewer pipework. 
  6. Cut out tree root infested overflow gully and pipework downstream to the stack junction.
  7. Supply and install new PVC gully, pipework and junction on the common stack.
  8. Bed pipework, back fill trench, install rio bars and form up stairs in preparation for concreting.
  9. Re-instate concrete stairs.

- Relining work

  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 11 meters of root infested earthenware sewer pipework, relining from the sewer stack inspection opening downstream to vertical shaft connection sealing all root infested and dislodged joints, using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Reinstate 1 x junction connection using robotic cutter.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. We will re-submit the quotation sent for the further common hot water servicing required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
23/4 - Attended the property and met with Gabriel to inspect the car stacker and pump.

From our investigation works we found the sump at the base of the car stacker is not low enough to catch all the water.

To provide an accurate quotation, we are required to return to the property with and outside slab scan contractor to scan the concrete below the car stacker to see if the sump can be lowered by excavating and saw cutting the concrete and steel.

2/5 - Returned to the property, gained access to the garage and under the car-stacker.

Used submersible pump to remove all the water from the base of the car stacker to enable slab scans.

Engaged a slab scan contractor and scanned the concrete slab below the car-stacker for rio bars and power.

Inspected the base of the car-stacker and found the new pump cannot be installed inside the original sump pit in the centre, as the car-stacker level finishes 40mm above the slab and there is no height to install a pump and pump out pipework. If we were to lower the level of the middle sump by excavating, we risk breaking through the concrete and ground water constantly entering at the base of the car-stacker.

Inspected the location of the new sump and pump close to the lift shaft wall and consider this is the best possible location to install the new pump and lower the sump level. Slab scanned the concrete in this area and found rio bars, but no power.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the concrete slab under the car-stacker is saw cut and excavated approximately 100mm deeper where the new pump will be installed against the lift shaft wall, the concrete floor is chased from the old, middle sump towards the new sump to remove all the water at the base of the car-stacker and the old sump is re-concreted so it doesn't hold water. We will submit an amended quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description: Urgent water leak into electrical room and out to the street
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak into electrical room.

Urgently attended the property, located water leaking into the electrical room and discharging out of the common storm water line to the kerb and gutter in the street.

Inspected the main water meter for the building and found the water meter to be ticking over at a very fast rate indicating a burst cold water pipe.

Inspected the garden area on the east side of the building and found water leaking out of the ground next to the hose tap. We found water to be leaking out of the electrical conduits in the electrical room.

Met with the buildings electrician, excavated the ground exposing main copper cold water and followed line but we were unable to locate the burst cold water copper pipework.

We isolated the buildings cold water supply so that the electrician was able to complete their works to make safe.

Engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe locating equipment to trace out the cold water supply from the outlet of the cold water meter at the front of the property and under the concrete slab within the car park.

Used leak detection equipment to confirm the burst pressurized pipe on the common cold water supply. After extensive with the use of listening device and leak detector we were unable to locate the burst cold water copper pipe as the burst pipe is located within the concrete slab.

To rectify the urgent leak, a cold water re-run is required deleting the burst pressurized cold water copper pipework within the concrete slab.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken  - We advise to saw cut and excavate the concrete slab in the car park exposing cold water tee, excavate the ground in the front garden area into garage 11, core drill hole through the wall into the electrical room, turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line, cut out cold water copper pipework on the outlet of the cold water meter, re-run new cold water copper service from the outlet of the water meter, through the front garden into garage 11, surface mount to the wall connecting onto existing cold water tee under the concrete slab, turn on the buildings cold water supply, test all works, back fill trench at the front of the property and re-instate the concrete in the car park. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent gas leak at the property.

Urgently attended the property, gained access and found a gas smell at the top of the stairs outside the building entrance.

Inspected the gas piping in the driveway and located the main gas regulator for buildings 60, 60a, 60b and 60c, we also found the other buildings have completed gas upgrade works.

Used gas detector to locate the highest reading of gas below the stairs outside 60A.

Returned to the property with, leak detection pipe locating equipment and located all the common gas pipework under the driveway, stairs and wall at the front of the building.

Located the common gas piping under the stairs and under the driveway retaining wall, which then goes under the building into the garage/ store room and meter room to the gas meter manifold.

Also a path valve is installed in the driveway to isolate the gas supply to unit 60A only in the event of an emergency. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

CEILING REPORT
Date: Thursday 28th March, 2024
Attendees: Dean, Kathryn
Report: Upon inspection we have noted the paint is failing on the kitchen ceiling.
We noted that this area of the ceiling had recently been repaired due to water damage from above.
This lead me to believe underlying issues may still be persistent.
To investigate this further I got a moisture meter out and took a reading of the ceiling.
The meter returned a reading of 12.5% confirming their is still a large amount of moisture being held in the ceiling.
Due to this moisture reading we believe this doesn’t fall under our warranties.
We are happy to come back and fix the ceiling for a fee.
However we recommend that further investigation is undertaken before we do our repairs to ensure the water issue has been totally rectified.
If this issue isn’t resolved the coatings are likely to fail again in another 6-12 months.

 

CEILING REPAIR QUOTE
Scope of Works:
- Scrape back kitchen ceiling to a hard edge (roughly 1-3m2)
- ReSkim Ceiling to hard edge using cornice cement
- One coat of oil based undercoat or watertite zinzer
- Two coats of ceiling paint
IMPORTANT NOTE: We recommended further investigation is undertaken to identify cause of moisture in ceiling. If this issue isn’t resolved before repairs are undertaken coatings may continue to fail in the future.
Exclusions:
- Any items not listed above
- Any ceiling other than kitchen ceiling
- No walls
- No electrical

- No air conditioning

"I then inspected underneath Peta's kitchen sink, and I found that the gas hot water pipe is leaking onto the cabinetry under the sink. There was water actively dripping down the inside of the cabinetry from this pipe. Judging by the scummy build up and mould under this tap, it appears that this leak has been ongoing for a long time. Please see Photo 6 below.

This source of water ingress would explain the damage that has occured along the base of the shared wall between Steve's and Peta's kitchens which has been repaired by Carbon. As this leak has continued water appears to have run all the way along Peta's kitchen to the back of the wall to the living room and now penetrated under the wall, appearing in the corner with the damaged and mouldy carpet.

The potential for leaking kitchen pipework in No. 115 was raised in our original report, where it was recommended that this area be inspected and repaired if needed, but it doesn't look like anyone has done this until now.
Based on the above, I strongly recommend that a plumber be engaged to repair this leak. The plumber should also investigate whether there may be any leaks occurring within the wall behind the No. 115 kitchen, or if it is only occurring on the outside of the wall, below the kitchen sink.

Once this No. 115 kitchen leak has been addressed, if it is the only source of water ingress into the No. 115 living room (which it appears to be at this stage), the living room carpet and walls should dry out and the damage should stop spreading."

Description:
This building has a problem when it rains very heavily, in that the section of the roof over the main communications riser leaks. This allows water to enter the smoke alarms within the riser, setting them off.

There is a plan to either replace the membrane on the section of roof above, or to install a Colorbond canopy roof over this section, which contains all the plant for the building. Either of these options is going to take quite some time.

In the interim I am hoping we can get a drip-tray fabricated and installed to catch this leak and divert it to somewhere less problematic, perhaps even a bucket that can be emptied when needed.  I don’t think the volume of water is all that great and it only occurs in driving heavy rain. I have attached a photo showing where the water is coming in, with mould growing on the parts that are affected.

Are you able to assist with this?  I remember your guys did a great job with a drip-tray they had made for a garage ceiling at 39 O’Brien St.

This is a security building.  The on-site contact is Roy in unit 1, on 0416 084 637.
Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access onto level 2 and inspected the communication cupboard.

Inspected inside the ceiling cavity and measured up size of drip tray to catch the water leaking from faulty membrane on the roof.

Please note, there is no place to run the drain for the drip tray, so the drain will have to be installed into a bucket which is emptied when full.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise a custom made drip tray is installed within the ceiling cavity to catch the water leak and run the drainage into a bucket. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 12.

3/4 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 12 and found water bubbling paint on the internal wall in the living room adjacent to the kitchen.

Inspected the kitchen cabinetry under the sink and found water damage to the back panel from the underside of the benchtop.

Tested the kitchen taps and found the cold water tap is leaking back into the internal wall and down the wall underneath the sink, also located faulty sealant along the top of the benchtop and the wall tile joints causing water damage to the internal living room wall adjacent.

Turned off the water supply form the 2 x common isolation valves under the sink and found the isolation valves to be leaking and did not isolate the water supply.

Put up water shut down notices around the building and advised resident of water disruptions for the 5/4/24 to replace the leaking common isolation valves in unit 12.

Whilst in unit 12, the occupant also pointed out a separate leak in the living room from the ceiling access panel.

Removed the access panel and found the bath waste penetration within the ceiling cavity.

Went upstairs into the bathroom and dye tested the bath waste with green dye, found no dye coloured water to be leaking from the common waste piping under the bath.

Pressure tested the shower and bath breaching pieces and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found, indicating no burst pipes in unit 12.

Identified large cracks in the shower / bath wall tiles on the common wall below the window. Flood tested the shower / bath wall tiles below the window and found water to leak through the bath waste penetration into the living room below.

5/4 - Returned to the property, isolated the buildings cold water supply and drained the water from the line.

Disconnected the 2 x leaking, faulty isolation valves in the kitchen and installed 2 x new isolation valves.

Turned the buildings cold water supply back on and tested, all in good working order.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken by the lot owner of unit 12 - We advise the lot owner of unit 12 engages their own plumbing contractor to repair the leaking cold water tap in the kitchen and also seal the kitchen benchtop along the internal wall.

Once the kitchen taps repairs and sealant works have been completed by the lot owner, we advise the internal living room wall is repaired and painted.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 12 - To prevent water leaking from the access panel in the living room, we advise the cracked wall tiles in the upstairs bathroom on the common wall are excavated, the wall is re waterproofed, new tiles are installed, re-grouted and the bath edge along the common wall is re-sealed using high grade flexible sealant. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once the upstairs bathroom common wall tiles are repaired and the bath edge is re-sealed, we advise the living room ceiling is repaired and a new access panel is installed. We will submit a separate quotation for the repairs and painting works required in unit 12's living room ceiling.

Re-installed access panel in the living room, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 3.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found the toilet to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Removed external inspection opening lids and found the common sewer line to be fully blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the common sewer stack outside unit 3's bathroom to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate a large amount of tree root infestations entering the base of the original stack pipework in multiple sections within the original earthenware main sewer line downstream which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Flow tested unit 3's toilet and common sewer line downstream - All clear and in good working order. Please note if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will reoccur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further blockages, we advise the tree root infestations are cleared out of the common sewer line on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

We will also provide a quotation to reline the tree root infested common earthenware sewer pipework as a full proof repair to prevent common sewer blockages. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 1.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found a large amount of water damage to the kitchen ceiling & shelving, hallway service riser cupboard & ceiling outside bathroom, bathroom walls & ceiling.

Removed the light fitting above the shower, inspected inside the ceiling cavity and found water dripping from the concrete slab. Opened up the service riser timber adjacent to the shower and found the water leaking from above. 

Gained access into unit 4, dye tested the shower recess with green coloured dye and no dye was found to be leaking in unit 1 below.

Isolated the water supply and carried out a nitrogen pressure test on the hot an cold water supply and got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst pressurized hot water pipe in unit 4.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection and traced out the hot water supply in unit 4. Used listening device and leak detector to pin point the burst hot water pipe to be located within the shower wall.

Excavated the shower wall tiles, exposing the hot water pipework and located 2 x burst pipes on the hot water piping below the shower breach within the shower wall.

Isolated the hot water supply to unit 4, cut out the affected area of burst copper piping and installed new copper piping and fittings.

Turned the hot water supply back on bleeding the air from the line, testing all works carried out - All in god working order.

Installed temporary core flue over the affected tiles in the shower recess, cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 4 & 1 - We advise the affected shower wall tiles in unit 4 are re-tiled using white wall tiles and unit 1's kitchen ceiling & shelving, hallway service riser cupboard & ceiling, bathroom walls & ceiling are repaired and painted.

We will return to the property with our repairs and painting team and submit an accurate quotation for the repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 1 & 4.

Installed a temporary cover over the service duct, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 26 and inspected the balcony drainage.

The occupant in unit 26 has a lot of plants and garden on the balcony which is being watered regularly and the water runoff goes to the balcony next door in unit 27.

- Test that the hot water is circulating back to the boilers/storage tanks at the correct flow rate.

- Test for leaks on Pressure Relief Valves (PRV) and/or Temperature and Pressure Relief Valves (TPRV).

- Test for faulty sensors (flame, temperature, flow etc.)

- Test that the all-isolation valves are in working order.

- Test for correct inlet gas pressures.

- Test for correct gas burner pressures.

- Test for correct operation of gas solenoids.

- Test for correct operation of air switches (where applicable).

- Removal and cleaning of burner train, sensors and ignition system on a yearly basis.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent after hours sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware main sewer line located under the courtyard and also major tree root infestations entering the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested and cracked earthenware pipework located under the courtyard and to reline approximately 7 meters of root infested earthenware pipework from the plastic section after inspection opening down to vertical shaft located under the road. sealing all root infested joints

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of building water shut downs whilst the relining works are undertaken.
  2. Using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera remove all tree roots from sewer line preparation for relining.
  3. Clean the complete sewer line.
  4. Apply for DBYD plans
  5. Investigate heavily Cracked Junction on main line.
  6. Record sewer line before Relining

- Relining:

  1. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 2 meters of Root infested and cracked earthenware pipework. Relining over root infested elbow and crack penetration in earthenware pipework, using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 7 meters of root infested earthenware pipework. Relining from plastic section after inspection opening down to vertical shaft located under the road, sealing all root infested joints. Using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. CCTV record footage of both relines and provide to owners corporation. 
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove asscoiated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Remove associated rubbish from the property. 

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared in unit 1, we found major tree root infestations entering the inlet to the main boundary trap and outlet pipework downstream to Sydney Waters main under the road. 

As advised by committee member at the building, we also undertook a full CCTV camera survey on the rest of the common sewer pipework. We found a further 12 meters of original earthenware pipework near the common laundry at the rear of the building that requires repairs.

  • Part A - URGENT WORKS - Reline from the top of the boundary trap to Sydney main sewer (Vertical shaft) under the road

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Engage pipe locating contractor to trace out the services under the road.
  2. Obtain Dial Before You Dig services search.
  3. Make application to council for road opening permit, includes a traffic management plan.
  4. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  5. Safely barricade the work area. 
  6. Using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to remove all roots, sand and debris from the common sewer line in preparation for relining. 
  7. Using CCTV equipment record sewer line before relining.
  8. Saw cut and excavate the road exposing vertical shaft to gain access to top vertical shaft.
  9. Raise vertical shaft to ground level in preparation for relining.
  10. Bed pipework, backfill hole with 10mm blue metal and compact ground as per AS-3500 
  11. Re-instate road using hot mix.
  12. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  13. Reline approximately 18 meters from the top of the boundary trap (located near side gate) down to vertical shaft located in the road Sealing all dislodged and root insisted joints, using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part heat cured Epoxy resin installed to AS3500.
  14. Using robotic cutter reinstate 1 junction.
  15. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  16. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property. 
  17. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation for the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE: Our Relining works comes with certificate of warranty with 25 year Installation guarantee with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee

Total cost of works for PART A - $17,950.00 + GST

Investigate water leak in the lower ground car park area.

Attended the property, gained access into the car park and located sewerage leaking out of the base of the common sewer stack pipe. We found the concrete around the base of the stack pipe was cracked and broken allowing sewerage to leak out of the pipework.

Removed inspection opening lid on the common sewer stack pipe, used CCTV drain camera downstream the stack to locate major tree root infestation in the common sewer line at the base of the stack, downstream in the main line and a large amount of congealed fat which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively to clear out the tree root infestations from the base of the stack, downstream in the main line and congealed fat from the common sewer line.

Flow tested downstream from the affected stack in the car park - All clear and in good working order.

Re-concreted around the base of the stack pipework.

Removed 150mm inspection opening lid located furthest from the entrance at the top of carpark, used CCTV drain camera to find a further thick tree root infestations and congealed fat blocking the common sewer line.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To rectify further blockages, we advise the tree root infestations and congealed fat is cleared out of the common sewer line near the entrance at the top of carpark, using of high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further clear out works required to be undertaken.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Attended the property to carry out CCTV camera survey and investigation works on the faulty common storm water pipework at the building.

Following our CCTV camera survey and investigation works we located 2 x faults with the common storm water pipework that require urgent repairs.

  • Section 1 - Install new PVC pipework from the outlet of the rear strip drain to the curb and gutter at the rear of 563 Victoria Road.

Used CCTV downstream from the outlet of the strip drain and we were only able to push our drain camera approximately 1 meter downstream. We found the common storm water pipework to be completely blocked with dirt and sludge.

To rectify this issue, we advise to notify both buildings (561 and 559) of driveway disruptions, saw cut and excavate concrete driveway, excavate ground, cut out collapsed section of 100mm earthenware pipework, install new section of PVC pipework, fittings, inspection opening raised to the surface for future clear out access, back fill trench, compact ground and re-concrete driveway.

We also found missing drain grates on the strip drain and the base of the strip drain to be blocked with leaves and dirt. To rectify further blockages, we advise to clean out the dirt and leaves from the base of the strip drain and replace missing grate lids.

We will submit a quotation shortly for the common storm water repairs required to be undertaken.

Phone : +61 404624328
Email : marilyn.forbes@hotmail.com

 

W.O. Issued by : Bettina Hoffman
Email : Sophia.Lentros@Somervilles.com
Invoice Description:
Attended the property on the 8/3/24, gained access to the car park, found water leaking on the concrete slab and into the storm water pit.

Unit 3 gave us access to the garage and we found water seeping through from the bottom of the common brick wall and into a spoon drain. This spoon drain then discharges into the common storm water pit.

Inspected the common area above and found the isolation valve for the properties water supply. Following our inspection no visible water leaks were found in the common area above.

Following testing, we found  there to be a burst common cold water pipe causing water to seep out of the common brickwork and leak into the car park below.

Returned to the property o the 13/3/24, engaged pipe location leak detection to use pipe locator to trace out the cold water supply in the common areas, use listening device and leak detector to try pin point the exact location of the burst pipe.

Following extensive testing, we pin pointed the burst common cold water copper pipework to be in the ground in the common area next to the tiled walkway.

Excavated the ground exposing the burst common cold water copper pipework. Due to the location we were unable to carry out a temporary repair over the burst cold water copper pipework.

Put notification up on the building advising a cold water building shut down.

Returned to the property on the 14/3/24, excavated the ground further exposing burst cold water copper pipework.

Shut down the buildings cold water supply and drained the water from the line.

Cut out burst section of copper pipework, installed new section of copper pipework and fittings connecting onto existing cold water supply.

Turned on the buildings water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order. Bed pipework, backfilled trench and re-instated common area.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent blocked sewer in the Shop Atrium.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into the shop atrium and found the common sewer overflow relief gully to be blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran equipment into the shop atrium.

Removed inspection opening lids and used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear the blockage in the overflow relief gully and common sewer piping downstream.

CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer piping, found congealed fat and major tree root infestations downstream in the common sewer line which was the cause of the blockage.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the congealed fat and tree root infestations from the common sewer piping.

CCTV video link downstream inspection opening to main boundary trap - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NTHUO

Flow tested the sewer piping with a high pressure hose - All clear and in good working order.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockage and floods in the Shop Atrium - We advise the tree root infested section of common sewer pipework is relined as a full proof solution repair. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Investigate water damage in townhouse 10.

Attended the property, gained access into townhouse 10 and found water damage to the common service riser duct in the bathroom.

Set up step ladder in the common hallway and gained access into the roof cavity.

Found the common stack vent goes up through the roof tiles, above where the common service duct is located.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent common sewer blockage we cleared downstream from unit 2's toilet and our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations to be entering the original common sewer pipework for approximately 3.5 meters downstream from the toilet to the main line junction. We used CCTV drain camera upstream from the boundary trap and located tree root infestations entering the main earthenware sewer line upstream from the boundary trap. 

This quotation is to remove unit 2's toilet, reline approximately 3.5 meters of tree root infested pipework from pan connection downstream to next junction, completely sealing the line using our watermark approved epoxy relining system and reinstate 1 x junctions using robotic cutter and re-install existing toilet. Also to used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out further tee root infestations from the common sewer line upstream from the boundary trap.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Lay drop sheets in unit 2.
  2. Disconnect and remove the toilet to access the common sewer line.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster, sand paddles, mechanical milling equipment and CCTV drain camera to prepare lines to AS-3500.
  4. Record common sewer pipework before relining.
  5. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the main line upstream from the boundary trap. Complete further investigation into main lines and how to enable better servicing and repairs due to no mainline access

- Relining works:

  1. Reline approximately 3.5 meters of tree root infested pipework from pan connection downstream to next junction, completely sealing the line using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  2. Once cured remove relining equipment from the common sewer line.
  3. Reinstate 1 x junction using robotic cutter. 
  4. Re-install existing toilet and seal to the floor using high grade flexible sealant.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video of relining works undertaken to the owners corporation.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

NEED THERMAL CAMERA

check wall - is wet after pulling back carpet.
Invoice Description:
Investigate leak continued in unit 201.

23/2 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 201 and found the timber flooring in the hallway has been removed.

Used thermal image camera to identify high readings of moisture along the base of the common hallway wall adjacent to unit 202's bathroom and kitchen.

Gained access into unit 202, used thermal camera and located wet carpet underlay in the living room next to the dishwasher.

Pulled out dishwasher and found water pooling on the vinyl floor underneath the dishwasher and under the kitchen kickboards.

Tested the dishwasher and no leaks were found. As there was a large amount of water under the dishwasher, we isolated the dishwasher for further testing.

Dried the floor and removed water using the wet vac.

Returned to the property on the 28/2, gained access into unit 202 and found the kitchen skirting and back of dishwasher to be dry.

Gained access into unit 201, used thermal image camera and found high readings along the hallway wall indicating the leak is still going and has not dried.

Turned on the air-condition in unit 202 and found water leaking from the hallway wall into unit 201.

Inspected the tundish drain under the laundry tub in the bathroom and found the air-condition drain to be sealed and waterproofed into the floor drain.

Excavated around the floor drain removing sealant and water leaked up from the floor tiles onto the bathroom floor indicating a blocked drain.

Removed waterproofing and tile grout from around the aircon drainage under the laundry tub in the bathroom and found water surcharging up through the floor onto the tiles. 

Used electric eel downstream from the tundish under the laundry tub to clear the blockage in the common pipework to the floor waste.

Once clear, we tested the air-condition in unit 202 and no further blockages were found.

Dried up the floor in unit 201 using the wet vac , excavated the common wall down low and released residual water build up within the block wall.

Returned to the property on the 6/3 - Knocked on unit 202 and found the air-condition unit has been used almost every night since the drain was cleared.

Gained access into unit 201 and found the hallway wall and floor has dried and the leak hasn’t returned after we cleared the blockage. 

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 201 - We advise the common hallway wall is repaired and painted by the buildings repair contractor and the timber flooring is replaced by a flooring contractor.

Please note - We inspected under the bath in unit 201 and found water pooling under the bath caused by faulty seals around the bath edge. To prevent further water damage in unit 201, we advise the bath is removed, and a new steel bath is installed and recessed inside the wall.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

We also advise to remove affected tiles on the front face of the bath, cut out leak bath waste, install new bath waste, asscoiated pipework, fittings, repair front face of the bath and re-instate tiles. We will submit a seperate quotation shortly to replace the leaking bath waste.

Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line under unit 2's bathroom

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared in unit 2 and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware branch line under the bathroom causing the blockage.

This quotation is to reline from the plastic pipework located under unit 2 under foundation and finish back onto plastic covering all earthenware branch-line pipework and sealing all root infested joints on this line, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin

Re-lining products are seamless, high strength, single length pipe without any joins which will create one complete pipe. Once cured, they are tested to provide a 50 year life span and are covered with a 25 year installation warranty.

The following works will be undertaken:

-Preparation:

  1. Gain access into unit 2.
  2. Lay protective floor sheeting on floors towards bathroom.
  3. Clean sewer line using high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera before relining.
  4. Camera inspect and CCTV record sewer line before relining.
  5. Maxi Mill plastic pipework preparation for relining.

- Relining repairs

  1. Reline from the plastic pipework located under unit 2 under foundation and finish back onto plastic covering all earthenware branch-line pipework and sealing all root infested joints on this line, using water marked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin
  2. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line. 
  3. Flow test all works carried out.
  4. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  5. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  6. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  7. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty..

These tree root infestations cannot be cleared out and the faulty common storm water piping is required to be excavated and replaced with new PVC piping and fittings.

We excavated the common storm water piping close to to unit 1 and have disconnected a plumb quick fitting to temporarily let the storm water drain into the garden and prevent flooding on unit 1's balcony until pipe repair works have taken place.

Investigate loud bangs in the carpark hot water heater room.

Gained access into the carpark and inspected the hot water heater and electrical room.

Found the heavy duty gas hot water heater up to temperature. 

Released the pressure valve on the hot water heater and found it leaks when in use.

Checked the buildings water pressure from the common heater and found no air locks in the water pipes that could cause a bang noise. 

We found the common gas hot water heater to be in good working order.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leaks and blockages in building 13 after heavy rain.

20/2 - Attended the property, gained access and inspected the 4 x leaks and blockages at the property.

1. Gained access and located blocked drains at the rear of the building flooding the fake grass area.

Lifted grated 2 x drain lids and removed foam and debris blocking the surface drain. There are additional drains under the fake grass which we could not find as it was heavy rain at the time.

2. Gained access into unit 2 and found water leaking through the cavity wall in the bedroom causing wet carpet. Adjacent to the cavity wall is the tiled courtyard and we found the surface drain to be blocked causing flooding.

Cleared out the blocked drain of debris to stop the flooding and release the water from the courtyard. We rescheduled with unit 2 to return on a dry day and carry out testing on the external wall to determine where the leak was coming in.

3. Inspected the leak on level 12 fire stairs which is leaking down to level 9 within the fire stairs. Found the leak to be coming from the external roof access area caused by cracks in the silicone seals and flashings around the door frame.

4. Gained access to the balcony on level 12 and found it to be flooding and the drain to be blocked. Removed grated lid and cleared the drain using drain cleaning equipment.

29/2 - Returned to the property on a dry day.

1. Gained access to the fake grass area at the rear of the building. Cut out a section of fake grass and removed the plastic underlay to locate the blocked drain causing flooding.

Lifted the grated lid and cleared out dirt and debris from the grate and base of the pipework using drain cleaning equipment. Once clear we tested the drain and found it in good working order and flowing to the stormwater pit at the rear.

2. Gained access to the courtyard of unit 2, inspected the base of the wall cavity and located cracked seals and missing tiles where the courtyard meets the wall.

Flood tested the affected area and after 3 hours, we found water eventually leaked into the bedroom from the external cavity wall seals and tiling.

3. Gained access to level 12 fire stairs and external roof area, flood tested the faulty roof flashings and silicone seals around the access door. After extensive testing we were unable to replicate the leak into the fire stairs.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 2's courtyard - We advise to re-seal the cracked silicone wall joints along the external wall, also to waterproof and retile the missing corner tile and seal along the tiled skirting and wall adjacent to unit 2's bedroom. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 2's courtyard.

Further works required to be undertaken on the external roof area on level 12 - We advise to re-seal all external cracked silicone joints and flashings around the door frame and along the external wall to prevent water leaking into the fire stairs. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken on the external roof area on level 12.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property to investigate 3 x separate leaks from the common external downpipe and roof outside the first stairs, off Stanley Street entrance.

Leak 1 -  We found the 45 degree elbow on the downpipe at high level outside the level 5 landing rail to be leaking during heavy rain. Engaged 2 x plumbers, used safety harness and ladder to access and temporary repair the 45 degree bend using t-rex sealant and tape to prevent water leaking from the joint during heavy rain. We spoke with the building manager James, who advised the building would like a quote to cut out and replace the entire metal downpipe and slip fittings with new PVC pipework and glued fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly to cut out and replace the entire downpipe on the first stairs.

Leak 2 - During heavy rain water was leaking out of the external downpipe at the base and splashing from the storm water pit grate onto the wall, causing water to leak from the garden bed onto the walkway tiles outside the stair entrance on ground floor. We cut out the base of 2 x downpipes, installed offsets and 45 degree bends at the base of the 2 x downpipes to discharge water into the pit and not splash onto the wall outside the pit and into the garden bed. 

Leak 3 - We found water leaking through the ceiling joint on level 5, where the building meets the stair joint and walkway. We advise the buildings waterproofing contractor is engaged to inspect the waterproof membrane on the roof which is causing the leak through the construction joint.

Whilst at the property we were also asked us to clean the level 2 entrance awning roof. Used extension ladder to gain access onto the roof, then cleaned the roof, sump and mesh guard of leaves and debris. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared in unit 11's garage and our CCTV camera survey, we located the original earthenware sewer line to be broken and collapsed causing tree root infestations to enter the common sewer line which was the cause of the blockage.

This quotation is to reline approximately 3 to 4 meters of broken, collapsed and tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework downstream from the stack in unit 11's garage and to re-instate 1 x junction with the robotic cutter.

Re-lining products are seamless, high strength, single length pipe without any joins which will create one complete pipe. Once cured, they are tested to provide a 50 year life span and are covered with a 25 year installation warranty.

The following works will be undertaken:

-Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of building water shut downs during the relining works. 
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool and CCTV drain camera to clean the earthenware pipework in preparation for relining. 
  3. Camera Inspect and CCTV record sewer pipework.

- Relining repairs

  1. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 3 to 4 meters of broken, collapsed and tree root infested earthenware sewer pipework downstream from the stack in unit 11's garage, completely sealing the defective pipework using Watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin.
  3. Once liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer line. 
  4. Re-instate 1 x junction using robotic cutter.
  5. Turn on the water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty..

Invoice Description:
Clear common storm water line with the use of high-pressure jet blaster, use CCTV drain camera to ensure pipework is all clear and use pipe location equipment to locate and trace where the storm water pipework runs.

Attended the property and gained access to the lower laundries and toilet at water level.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran the hoses and extension reel down to the water level.

  • Downpipes.

Inspected the common downpipes and found 3 x downpipe has been sleeved top to bottom with 50mm PVC connected to the roof sump and the other 1 x downpipe is original square copper connected to the roof sump.

Cut out the base of the 2 x downpipes closest to the front entrance to access the drainage and used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV camera to survey the common stormwater pipework under the slab at water level.

We found the 1 x original copper downpipe is in good working order and discharges into the water and the other 1 x sleeved 50mm downpipe has been offset at the base to discharge onto the concrete slab outside the laundries deleting the original stormwater pipework in the slab.  

The other 2 x 50 mm sleeved downpipes closest to the water are also clear and in good working order discharging to the water.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster downstream of the 50mm sleeved downpipe closest to the front entrance to clear out the original drainage under the slab and found after 1 meter the drainage is collapsed causing water to surcharge from the ground behind the laundries.

After extensive jet blasting with the high pressure water jet blaster in the allocated timeframe, we were unable to clear out the collapsed stormwater pipework downstream from the sleeved 50 mm downpipe.

  • Floor drain behind the laundries

Cleared out leaves and debris from the surface drain at the back of the laundries in front of the retaining wall and found the pipework to be completely blocked.

Camera surveyed the inlet pipework to the gully and found it connects to a deleted sewer stack indicating the gully is original sewer pipework.

After extensive jet blasting, we found the sewer gully did not surcharge but we were unable to locate where the pipework runs and what it is connected to. We found the original sewer gully has been deleted when the sewer pipework has been rerun to the sewer pump.

  • Roof drains

Gained access to the roof and flood tested the original copper roof drainage downpipe at the back left.

After flood testing the original copper downpipe from the roof, we found it did not leak. We blocked off the roof sump outlet, flooded the sump and found water had leaked around the downpipe to the lower levels.

Cleaned all leaves and debris from the roof and at the back of the wall behind the laundries and removed from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - As we could not clear out the stormwater drainage from the downpipe end, further jet blasting is required at low tide to clear rocks from the pipework at the waters edge and use the high pressure water jet blaster upstream towards the downpipe to try and clear out the original stormwater pipework under the concrete slab. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 16.

Attended the property on the 7/2/24, gained access into unit 16 and found water leaking within the kitchen cupboard where the common kitchen stack is located.

Inspected the common service riser and found water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 4 above.

Gained access into unit 4, removed section of access panel and could see water pooling under the bath. Flood dye tested bath pipework and no leaks were found.

Returned to the property on the the 7/2/24, isolated the water supply and carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on shower breaching piece, hot and cold water supply within unit 4.

Following extensive pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe within unit 4.

Returned to the property on the 12/2/24, engaged pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water supply within the kitchen and bathroom.

Used listening devise and leak detector to locate the burst pressurized hot water pipe to be located within the concrete slab.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak - We advise to delete the burst pressurized copper pipework within the concrete slab, excavate and remove tiles within the bathroom, re-run new hot water line from hot water heater through kitchen cupboards, connecting kitchen sink, shower/bath and basin. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

After the plumbing works have been completed and we know the full extent of the resultant damage, we will submit a quotation for all resultant water damage repairs, painting and tiling in units 4 and 16.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Description:
Quotation - Further relining works on the common storm water line

After cleaning the lines ready for relining we cleared the adjoining lines completely also. Once cleaned to relining standards more issues became apparent. I have marked a picture to try and show which way the pipework runs. the yellow line is what we have relined and the red/blue is what still needs to be lined. The relined pipe meets a square junction which is being root infested from the top, it then drops down into a bad connection made by one pipe being smashed to insert the next pipe. This is also root infested. the line this vertical shift feeds into is approx 1.8m deep under the laundry line area. The pipes are cracking and showing signs of deteriation. There is a large tap root growing through this pipe that our jet couldn't remove. our recommendation is to use our robotic cutter to trim back the earthenware pipe and cut out the large tap root. We can then core on top of the vertical shaft and raise a pipe up to surface which will also remove the roots growing in from the top. We can then line the t section at the bottom of the vert where the main meets the riser sealing this faulty section. Our final line is the option to line and seal the main stormwater line from the pit up which is starting to crack and move quite a lot.

The following works will be undertaken:

 - Preparation:

  1. Clear lines using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera.
  2. Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS3500.
  3. Record footage of lines before relining.

- Relining repairs:

  1. Core down on top of vertical shaft with 150mm core bit and excavate down to top of vertical shaft around 0.6m remove cap and tree roots.
  2. Install new riser with 5" finishing collar level with ground and concrete around pipe.
  3. Install 150 x 100 x 90 junction satellite repair over root infested vertical shaft base sealing onto PVC riser.
  4. Cut out lateral connection using robotic cutter
  5. Reline 7m of 150mm diameter pipework from pit upstream to vertical shaft junction using our watermark approved epoxy relining system.
  6. Flow test all works carried out.
  7. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. Provide CCTV video of the relining works undertaken to the owners corporation.
     

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the blockage main common storm water pipework picking up the storm water for the entire building - We advise to excavate the ground next to the driveway, cut out tree root infested section of common earthenware storm water pipework, use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the pipework downstream, install new section of PVC pipework, fittings, flow test all works carried out, backfill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further common storm water repairs required to be undertaken. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Quotation - Relining works on the common storm water line

Following the recent storm water blockage we cleared from the downpipe in the upper level carpark storage room, we found major tree root infestations to be entering the original cracked and dislodged earthenware storm water line which was the cause of the blockage.

This quotation is to reline approximately 10 meters of cracked dislodged earthenware pipework relining from newly installed plastic section on stack 10m downstream to vertical shaft connection located in outside garden (where washing Lines are located) Using watermarked approved liner with 2 part epoxy resin and using robotic cutter reinstate junction on stormwater line

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Gain access into storeroom located next to lift.
  2. Cut into stormwater stack preparation for underground pipework to be relined.
  3. Using high pressure water jet clean complete stormwater line from all roots and debris.
  4. Install new plastic section on stack preparation for relining.
  5. Camera inspect and CCTV record stormwater line before relining.
  6. Investigate junction located on line prior to relining if we find this junction do be in working order this will be reinstated.

- Relining repairs: 

  1. Reline approximately 15 meters of 100-150mm cracked, dislodged and root infested earthenware pipework.
  2. Relining from the garden pit to the downpipe dropper on the mainline sealing all earthenware joints using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Using robotic cutter reinstate junction on stormwater line
  4. Flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property. 
  7. CCTV record footage of reline and provide to owners corporation.
  8. PLEASE NOTE, On camera inspection we have also identified some issues on the main line. On the day of repairs we will do a complete clean on this line and identify where this line goes and what this line feeds we will supply a full condition report after we have identified and cleaned this section.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate water hammer in house 104.

Attended the property, gained access into house 104 and located water hammer noises when the shower, bath and kitchen taps are in use.

Inspected the newly installed cold water pipes and found them to be clipped secure and no movement which could be causing water hammer.

Isolated the water supply and replaced washers for the shower and bath taps, replaced the original cold water isolation valve and cut out loose unnecessary pipework under the laundry tub, turned the water supply back on testing all works and still found water hammer.

Inspected the original hot and cold water pipes on the external wall in the rear yard outside the kitchen, bathroom and laundry and found there to be loose, unclipped, crossed over water pipes causing vibration and movement in the hot and cold pipes when all taps are turned on and off.

Installed brackets securing pipework on the external wall where there were no clips installed over a long distance and found the pipework still moves and shudders in all of the old/original pipes.

To rectify the water hammer noise in house 104, we advise all the original hot and cold water pipework on the external wall is altered, where they cross over installing new pipes, all unclipped pipes are secured at correct intervals and water hammer arrestors are installed to prevent backpressure. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.
