Description: Gas and HW inspection Hi team, The gas bill for the plan has been doubled this financial year. The committee ask to investigate and find out why. Please attend and investigate if this is a issue that can be resolved. (5 out of 6 units have hot water system with gas, please check that as well). Please ensure all work order updates get sent directly to sydney.admin@picagroup.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate high gas bill at the property.

Attended the property, gained access and located the common gas meters on the left side passageway.

Inspected all 7 x common gas meters and found the dials are not ticking over when no gas is being used.

Gained access to the hot water heater plant and found the heaters at temperature. Whilst at the building, we found the Raypak gas heater only turned on when required and the gas meter dial stopped when it stopped heating.

Carried out an inspection of the remaining 6 x common gas meters over the course of 1 hour and found they did not move when no gas was being used.

Performed a drop test on unit 5's meter as it did move a few digits but no gas leaks were found.

We also found unit 5 & 1's gas meter has recently been replaced, unit 5 most recent.

It is possible when Jemena gas replaced the gas meters they have adjust the new bill to suit previous usage which was not metered.

We advise the next gas bill is monitored to see if it is reduced or back to the approximate cost of the previous bill.

As no gas leak was found, no further works are required to be undertaken.

WORK ORDER: Two Blocked Downpipes
Good Afternoon,
Please attend to unblock two downpipes on south side of the building. One is connected to rooftop guttering and the other to a double carport. If repair
costs will exceed $2,000 please provide a quote for the full cost. Kindly issue all quotes, invoices, correspondence, updates, etc to
sydney.admin@picagroup.com.au.
Thank you!
Invoice Description:
Investigate 2 x blocked common downpipes located on the south side of the building.

Attended the property, found the common storm water line to be completely blocked on the right hand side of the building causing water to flood near the carport on the right hand side of the building.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively for 6 hours and we were unable to clear the blockage in the common storm water line.

Following our CCTV camera survey, we found major thick tree root infestations entering through the entire original earthenware storm water line on the right hand side of the building.

Following extensive jet blasting we were able to get the common storm water line on the right hand side of the building slowly draining.

Returned to the property the following day, cleaned all dirt and sludge from the common area using high pressure water jet blaster.

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the blocked and tree root infested original earthenware storm water line on the fight hand side of the building - We advise to obtain council road opening permit,  cut out and delete 2 x downpipes at the right hand side of the building, surface mount new 100mm PVC pipework and fittings to the external wall on the right hand side of the building picking up the 2 x downpipes, saw cut and excavate approximately 12 meters of the driveway and footpath using road saw, excavate the concrete and ground, install new PVC pipework, fittings discharging to the street, re-concrete affected area of driveway, carry out temporary bitchuman repair to the councils footpath, clean all areas, remove associated rubbish and advise council to undertake permanent repairs to council footpath. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description: Store room flooding from heavy rain.
Invoice Description:
Investigate storage room flooding during heavy rain.

Urgently attended the property, gained access to the upper carpark level storage room below ground floor and found water leaking from the wall cavity and up from the slab. 

Cut a hole at the base of the galvanized steel downpipe, used the hole saw to cut through the pipe and found the common earthenware storm water piping downstream of the downpipe to be blocked.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran hoses into the store room.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV to clear out multiple blockages in the common storm water main line from the base of the downpipe to the garden pit.

CCTV camera surveyed the storm water piping and found multiple areas where  major tree root infestations are entering the original earthenware storm water piping.  CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NQ1C1

Used the jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and the drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree root infestations from the common storm water piping.

Once majority of the tree roots had been cut out we camera surveyed the piping and found dislodged joints and cracks with large gaps that are allowing tree roots to enter the earthenware storm water piping in multiple areas within the main line to the storm water pit.

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify further storm water blockages in the carpark level store room, we advise the tree root infested, cracked and broken common earthenware storm water piping is relined. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

Sealed hole in the downpipe and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.

Description:
URGENT BURST WATER MAIN
PLEASE ATTEND SITE TO UNDERTAKE THE FOLLOWING:
Burst Water main. Kindly attend urgently and rectify and make safe.
Site Contact: Jenny Brown 0413 084 394
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 9/1/24 - Urgent water leak in the carpark.

Urgently attended the property after hours and found water constantly leaking out of the concrete slab in the car park. Video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NQCD7

Inspected the main cold water meter and found the meter to be ticking over at a very fast rate indicating a burst pressurized common cold water pipe under the concrete slab.

Returned to the property the following day on the 10/1, saw cut and excavated the concrete slab within the car park and located a burst pressurized cold water pipe and collapsed sewer pipe at the base of stack and riser.

To repair the collapsed sewer pipework, we were required to excavate and remove bricks around the common service riser.

Isolated the buildings water supply, cut out the burst main cold water pipe and installed new copper pipe and fittings connecting the cold water supply riser.

Cut out the collapsed section of earthenware sewer pipework and installed new PVC pipe and fittings connecting the common sewer stack.

Turned the buildings cold water supply back on testing all works carried out - All in good working order.

Backfilled the excavation in the carpark with sand and compacted around the cold water pipe and common sewer drainage.

Closed off the area in the carpark with danger tape to prevent access.

Returned to the property on the 12/1, installed rio bars and mesh within the excavation in preparation for concreting.

Re-concreted the affected area of carpark and installed new brickwork at the base of the service riser.  

Removed excess bricks, rubble and fill from the property and disposed of.

Returned to the property on the 15/1, used the high pressure water jet blaster to clean the concrete, washed down the affected area in the carpark and removed danger tape.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Flow tested pump - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Unit 3 - One of the drains on the patio is blocked. Water pooling.
Can you please attend to clear.
Access - Owner - Jenny - 0433 316 924
Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked balcony floor drain in unit 3.

4/12 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found the back balcony floor drain to be blocked.

Used the electric eel to try and clear the blockages in the balcony drainage but we were unable to clear the solid debris in the pipework.

Camera surveyed the pipework and found large chunks of bark and rocks blocking the pipework.

Set up the high-pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses up to the top floor balcony of unit 3. Used the high-pressure water hose to clear out the blockage but was unable to due to the large bark and rocks blocking the pipe.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and scheduled with unit 3 to return for further jet blasting and to locate the blockage.

8/12 - Returned to the property, gained access into the garage, cut out the the base of the PVC stormwater downpipe and installed an inspection opening to allow CCTV access to the common stormwater drainage and downpipe below units 3 & 4.

Gained access into unit 3 and the garage simultaneously and ran hoses up to the balcony of unit 3. Used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV camera to survey the common stormwater drainage pipework and located the blockage to be approximately 4 meters downstream from the balcony floor level, within unit 4. 

CCTV camera surveyed the common downpipes from the inspection opening installed in the garage and could not locate the blockage as our equipment was unable to reach from the garage and access is required into unit 4 below to locate.

19/12 - Returned to the property and gained access into unit 3 & 4. Used CCTV camera to survey the common drainage and located the blockage to be within unit 4 behind the internal shower wall at slab level. 

22/12 - Returned to the property with the large jetting truck and the pipe milling tool to try and clear the blockage. Gained access into unit 3, used drain cleaning equipment and the pipe milling tool to try and clear out the solid blockage in the balcony drainage.

After several attempts with the milling tool and the large jetting truck, we were unable to clear the blockage.

Used aqua wet vac to remove water from the pipework and CCTV camera surveyed the pipework to find a large amount of concrete causing the blockage in the common stormwater pipework. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NQRY3

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to remove the inbuilt wardrobe in unit 4, excavate the internal wall void between the bedroom and the bathroom shower and use core hole machine to access the common downpipe, cut out drainage and use internal pipe cutting tool to remove the solidified concrete within the pipework. Once the concrete is removed using the internal cutting tool, repair downpipe within the void. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent common sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the inlet junction to the boundary trap and approximately 14 meters of 150mm earthenware sewer pipework upstream towards the building.

This quotation is to install a 150mm x 150mm x 90 degree junction satellite repair relining inlet junction to the boundary trap, reline approximately 14 meters of 150mm diameter pipework from boundary trap upstream to PVC section using our watermark approved epoxy relining system and reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter. 

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  3. Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS3500.
  4. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Turn of the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Install a 150mm x 150mm x 90 degree junction satellite repair relining inlet junction to the boundary trap, sealing all cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 14 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework from boundary trap upstream to PVC section, sealing all cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  4. Reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter. 
  5. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate 3 x separate issues.

Attended the property, met with the building manager Alex and inspected 3 x separate issues.

  • Leak 1 - Building 13, level 10 fire exit.

Gained access to building 13, level 10 and found the floor to be dry close to the fire exit. Investigated the ceiling and confirmed there was no water leak.

Inspected water pooling on the floor on ground level below units 8 & 15. Identified the water to be residual water from the urgent leak in units 8 & 15.

  • Leak 2 - Building 11, level 2 ceiling adjacent to unit 11.

Gained access to building 11, level 2 and found water damage to the gyprock ceiling and wall.

Gained access to the roof space directly above the water damage and found water pooing on the floor below the air-conditioner condenser unit and ducting.

Inspected where the ducting penetrates the tiled roof and located large gaps and cracks in the flashing which seals the roof and prevents water leaking.

We are unable to safely access the rood due to the large pitch and height of the roof.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise a roofing contractor is engaged to inspect the roof above building 11, level 2 and carry out repairs to the flashings where the air-condition ducting penetrates the tiled roof. 

  • Job 3 - Building 11 - Pool Area bathrooms.

Tested the common drainage in the pool bathrooms and found the floor waste was blocked and surcharging waste water when the fixtures are being used.

Removed floor waste grate lid and used electric eel to clear the blockage in the common drainage pipework. 

Flow tested all waste fixtures within the pool bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

Reinstalled floor waste grate lid and cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 5/1/23 - Urgent blockage in unit 201's shower

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 201 and found the shower to be completely blocked and flooding when in use.

Removed drain grate and used electric eel extensively but we were unable to clear the blockage in the common waste pipework.

We advised the occupant to not use the shower and to only use the bath as the bath waste piping is currently clear and in good working order.

Returned to the property the following day, used mechanical drain cleaning milling tool but we were again unable to clear the blockage in the common waste pipework.

Further urgent works are required to be undertaken - We advise to gain access into unit 101, cut a hole within the bathroom ceiling, cut out unit 201's shower waste pipework, use electric eel to clear the common waste pipework downstream, install new PVC pipework, fittings and temporary cover unit 101's bathroom ceiling. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once the plumbing works have been completed and we know the full extent of the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken to unit 101's ceiling, we will then provide a separate quotation for the repairs and painting works in unit 101.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Please note - We have advised the occupants in unit 201 to not use the shower and to only use the bath until the blockage has been rectified.

Description: AFTER HORUS - Blockage in common area
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 24/12/23 - Blocked common sewer piping flooding into the rear of the property.

Urgently attended the property after hours, inspected the common sewer piping near the rear door and found the common over flow relief gully to be fully blocked and caused a large sewage back up which flowed under the rear door and into the property.

Used drain cleaning equipment to partially clear the blockage and release the common line.

Returned to the property in the morning on the 25/12/23 - Set up the high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to the rear gullies.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera, found a large amount of congealed fat in the common earthenware sewer pipe work and over flow relief gully which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out congealed fat from the common sewer line.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Description: Blocked toilet, overflow at the rear of the property
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent sewer blockage in shop 98D.

Urgently attended the property after hours on the 30/12/23, found the common toilet outside shop 98D to be blocked and sewerage to be surcharging at the rear of the property.

Removed inspection opening lid on the common stack pipework and found the common sewer line to be completely blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment at the rear of the building.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera, found major tree root infestations entering multiple sections and a collapsed section of original earthenware pipework which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out all tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Whilst at the building we also located 2 x blocked overflow sewer gullies. Used high pressure water jet blaster to partially clear out the 2 x overflow gullies. We found both overflow sewer gullies to be collapsed and large amount of sand in the base of the gully causing the blockage.

Flow tested the toilet in 98D and common sewer line downstream - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested common sewer pipework and 2 x overflow gulls, further blockages and floods will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages - We advise the tree root infested and cracked earthenware sewer pipework is relined and the 2 x collapsed overflow gullies are excavated and replaced with new PVC pipework and fittings.

Description: After hours blockage unit 2
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent sewer blockage outside unit 2

Urgently attended the property after hours on the 27/12/23, removed inspection opening lids and found the common sewer line to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the overflow gully outside unit 2 when in use.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to located major tree root infestations entering majority of the original earthenware sewer line downstream to the boundary trap. Used pipe locating equipment to locate the boundary trap be covered by a large shed located at the rear right of the common garden area.

Used high-pressure water, jet blaster with large tree roots, cutting heads and CCTV Drain Camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the main sewer line.

Following the clear out works on the main line, we still found the overflow sewer gully outside unit 2 (rear right) and the overflow sewer gully (front right) to still be be blocked.

Return to the Property the following day on the 28/12/23, used Aqua vacuum to suck out the sewerage and sand from the base of the 2 x overflow sewer gullies..

Used high-pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream the gully to partially clear the blockage. We found the 2 x common earthenware sewer gullies to have collapsed causing a large amount of sand to enter the common sewer pipework.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further blockages we advise the 2 x collapsed earthenware overflow sewer gullies outside unit 2 and at the front right of the property is urgently excavated and replaced with new PVC pipework and fittings.

Cleaned all areas where work had place using the high pressure hose and disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description: Please attend and repair a burst pipe in Unit 7 that is causing a waterfall leak into Brown Sugar below. Contacts: Yann - Unit 7 - 0402 426 027 Peta - Brown Sugar - 0421 222 928
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 26/12/23 - Urgent water leak in Brown Sugar Restaurant

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into Brown Sugar and and found water leaking through the ceiling from unit 7 above.

Gained access into unit 7 above and located a burst pressurized cold water copper pipe within the bedroom cupboard adjacent to the bathroom.

Turned off the cold water supply to isolate the leak and prevent further water damage to Brown Sugar below.

Turned on the buildings cold water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 7 - We advise the damaged cabinetry is replaced in the bedroom. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 7.

Please note - No water damage was found to Brown Sugar when we inspected the property. We advise the occupants to monitor the ceiling and contact us if any resultant water damage occurs to the ceiling.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, found the common hallway wall outside unit 204's bathroom to be water damaged.

Installed access cover on the front face of the bath, cleaned all areas where work had take place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Due to movement in the bath and as the bath is not recessed inside the wall, we consider the resealing works carried out to be a temporary repair.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 204. To rectify further water leaking under the bath, we advise the bath is removed, and a new bath is installed and recessed inside the wall. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 213.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 213, found water damage to the common wall in the bathroom adjacent to unit 212.

Used moisture meter to confirm high readings of moisture within the wall.

Gained access into unit 212 and found the silicone seals around the bath had cracked and the bath had become separated from the wall. 

Cut a hole in the bath panel, inspected under the bath and found water to be pooling under the bath.

Dye tested the bath waste and the silicone seals where the bath lip meets the wall tiles. From dye testing we found the faulty seals around the bath edge causing water to leak under the bath.

Used aqua vacuum and removed build up of water under the bath and covered the hole made in the side of the bath.

Returned to the property and gained access into unit 212.

Cut out faulty sealant where the bath meets the common wall tiles and vertical wall, cleaned and primed affected areas in preparation for resealing and installed new high grade flexible sealant to all affected areas in the shower bath area and vertical wall.

Supplied and installed new access cover where the hole was made in the side of the bath.

Cleaned all areas where work had take place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Due to movement in the bath and as the bath is not recessed inside the wall, we consider the resealing works carried out to be a temporary repair.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 212. To rectify further water leaking under the bath, we advise the bath is removed, and a new bath is installed and recessed inside the wall. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

  • Unit 3B - Cut out the water damaged bulkhead, supply and install new bulkhead to the bathroom ceiling, prepare, paint bulkhead matching existing paint colour, replace the water damaged wall mirror cabinet and vanity basin.
  1. Gain access into unit 3B and lay drop sheets in the bathroom.
  2. Cut out and remove entire water damaged bulkhead from the bathroom ceiling.
  3. Re-build bulkhead and install gyprock to the entire bulkhead.
  4. Plaster and white set bulkhead ceiling.
  5. Sand back and prepare all areas for painting.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to the landing on top of the garages at the front and found the surface drain to be blocked.

Following our CCTV camera survey, we located a large cracks, dislodged sections of earthenware pipe and tree roots entering the pipework for approximately 10 meters from the surface drain in the driveway to the curb and gutter in the street.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further blockages and floods occurring, we advise the common storm water pipework is relined from the garage drain to the curb and gutter in the street approximately 10 meters. We will submit a quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 28/11/2023 - Investigate main gas supply at the building shut off.

Urgently attended the property after hours and found the gas supply to be turned off by Jemena Gas. The main gas valve and Boundary regulator is located at the rear middle fence off Kennedy Lane.

Used gas detector to locate high readings of gas within the rear common area and laundry's.

Traced pipework and excavated the garden area in Kennedy Lane and found the main common gas supply pipework goes under the ground.

Excavated around the main gas supply piping in the ground but was unable to locate the leak.

Returned the property the following day with 2 x plumbers, disconnected the boundary regulator, and undertook leak detection works nitrogen testing equipment to pressure test the main gas pipework and found a large leak on the gas supply.

We excavated more of the garden in Kennedy Lane to expose more of the gas piping and use our testing equipment to try and locate the leak.

After excavating, we exposed a large leak on the galvanised steel fitting where it connects onto the large Gold line piping. Video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NC7IU

Used Denso tape to wrap the leaking galvanised steel pipework under the ground to temporarily stop the large leak.

We have turned ON the gas supply to the property and then carried out further testing using the gas leak detector and found multiple leaks on units 14,16,& 18 outlet piping which goes into the ground.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe tracing equipment to locate the main gas supply pipework under the ground at the back concrete area to the 3 x gas meter manifolds.

We found all the original common galvanized steel gas pipework for the building to be in very bad condition, badly corroded and we advise the gas pipework under the ground is urgently upgraded with new copper pipework and fittings.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the common gas pipework under the ground and 18 x gas meters on 3 x separate manifolds are replaced with new copper pipe and fittings. We also found the outlet pipework for units 14,16,18 is badly corroded where it goes into the concrete slab and ground and high readings were found on the gas detector. Once we turned on the gas supply to the building we found unit 3's gas meter was ticking over rapidly and was unable to leave it turned on, further investigation work are required to gain access to unit 3, test the outlet gas piping and rectify the gas supply to unit 3. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked drain in the rear common courtyard.

Urgently attended the property, gained access to the rear common courtyard / clothes line area and found the surface water drain for the paved area to be blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to the common courtyard to clear the blockage in the surface water drain.

CCTV camera surveyed the common pipework and found debris and dirt causing the blockage, we also confirmed the surface water drain is a common sewer overflow relief gully.

Used the jet blaster and drain camera simultaneously to clear out all dirt and debris from the common sewer piping which has blocked the gully as it is being used as a storm water surface drain.

Flow tested downstream from the sewer gully - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further blockages from the common sewer pipework in the common courtyard, the sewer surcharge gully needs to be raised 75mm above the finished floor level as per AS3500 Australian plumbing standards. 

As the paved clothes line area requires a surface water drain, stormwater drainage needs to be installed under the pavers and the surface drain needs to be connected to the common stormwater. Once we have returned to the property and CCTV camera surveyed the common stormwater pipework and located the closest stormwater drainage, we will submit a separate quotation to lift pavers and install a new surface water drain connected to the common stormwater pipework and re-instate the pavers.

Attended the property, gained access to the carpark and found the sewer pit in car space 21 to be overflowing with sewage.

Lifted pit lid and drained the pit of sewage and grease into buckets.

Once drained, we opened up the inspection opening on the sewer junction and used a high pressure water jet blaster to clear a large amount of grease in the sewer piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the sewer piping and found tree root infestations growing in the earthenware sewer piping causing the blockage.

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree roots from the sewer piping.

Cleared out all tree root infestations, camera surveyed the line which is now all is clear and currently flowing away but if repairs are not carried out, further blockages will reoccur.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent common sewer blockages caused by tree root infestations, we advise the common sewer pipework is relined. Once we have reviewed these works with our relining team, we will submit an urgent quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

Reinstalled inspection opening, pit lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Re-installed pit lid and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent gas leak at the rear bin area.

Urgently attended the property and gained access to the left side passage near the rear bins.

Used gas detector to locate high readings of gas where the left side original meter manifold is located.

Excavated the concrete slab and found the main common gas supply pipework under the ground to be badly corroded and leaking.

Exposed the leaking gas pipework and found the leak using bubble leak spray.

Used Denso tape to wrap the corroded galvanized steel pipework as a temporary repair to isolate the gas leak.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe tracing equipment to locate the main gas supply pipework under the ground from the rear meter manifold to the front boundary regulator.

We found all the original galvanized steel gas pipework for the building to be in very bad condition, badly corroded and we advise is urgently upgraded with new copper pipework and fitings.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the affected corroded gas inlet pipework at the rear left meter manifold is cut out and replaced with new copper pipework and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly to repair the affected area of gas leak only.

To prevent major gas leaks at the property  and as a full proof solution, we advise the common gas pipework and 2 x meter manifold galvanized steel pipework is replaced with new copper pipe and fittings.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Investigate urgent water leak in units 3A and 3B.

Urgently attended the property on the 20/10/23 gained access into unit 3A and found water leaking through the bulkhead ceiling. We found water damage to the entire bulkhead and damage to the grouting on the common bathroom wall.

Gained access into unit 3B and found water constantly dripping through the bathroom ceiling from above.

Gained access into unit 4B flood tested all waste fixtures in the bathroom and no leaks were found. Isolated the water supply, pressure tested hot and cold water supply and no drop in pressure was found.

We were unable to access the common service riser as the riser has been tiled over in a previous bathroom renovation.

Dye tested all bathroom waste fixtures and no leaks were found. Following extensive texting no water leaks were found within unit 4A.

Returned to the property on the 31/10/23, gained access into unit for 4B, engaged pipe location leak detection.

Lay drop sheets in the bathroom, disconnected and removed toilet, excavated tile and common wall, exposing burst pressurized, hot water copper pipe.

Turned off the hot water supply and repaired burst hot water copper pipe work.

Turned on the hot water supply and tested all works carried out.

Re-installed toilet and temporary cover hole within common bathroom wall, cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further resultant damage repairs required to be undertaken in units 3a, 3b & 4b. Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 8.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 8, found water leaking behind the fridge in the kitchen and water pooling on the kitchen floor.

Inspected the common ceiling cavity and found water leaking through the waste pipe penetration from the en-suite bathroom above.

Gained access into the en-suite bathroom and carried out extensive testing.

Isolated the water supply, carried out pressure testing on the shower breaching piece which got a drop in pressure. 

Repaired leaking shower rose connection, re-pressure tested breaching piece, hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found within unit 8.

Flood dye tested the shower recess and found dye leaking into the kitchen below confirming the waterproof membrane within the shower has failed causing the leak.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in the en-suite bathroom to rectify the water leak in unit  8 - We advise a building contractor is engaged to remove the tiles within the shower recess, 1st course of wall tiles, install new waterproof membrane and re-tile shower recess and 1st course of wall tiles.

After the waterproofing and tiling works have been completed, we advise the resultant water damaged gyprock wall in the kitchen is repaired and painted.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

4.5 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework, downstream unit 2's toilet and reinstate 3x junctions using robotic cutter. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 21.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 21 and found water leaking through the bathroom ceiling.  

A section of the bathroom ceiling and cornice that had collapsed. We removed a section of the falling gyprock ceiling and cornice to make the bathroom safe.

Inspected the ceiling cavity and found water leaking through the concrete slab from unit 27's bathroom above.

Gained access into unit 27, isolated the water supply, carried out pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. Following extensive pressure testing no burst water pipes were found within unit 27.

Dye tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Removed 2 x tiles and excavated a hole in the front face of the bath to inspect under the bath.

Flood tested where the bath meets the common wall tiles and found water leaking under the bath and into unit 21's bathroom ceiling below confirming the water leak.

Installed a cover over the hole in the front face of the bath, cleaned all areas where work had taken place place in units 21 and 27 and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak - We advise to gain access into unit 27, cut out faulty sealant where the bath meets the common walls and re-seal using high grade flexible sealant. Also to repair the front face of the bath and install 2 x new white tiles matching existing tiles like for like. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Once these works have been completed we advise unit 21's bathroom ceiling and cornice is repaired and painted. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Urgent quotation - Relining & excavation works in the driveway

Following the recent storm water blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we locate multiple areas of collapsed, broken and defective original earthenware storm water pipework where tree root infestations are aggressively entering the pipework which is causing blockages within the driveway.  There are major cracks within the concrete driveway caused by broken storm water pipework which is currently leaking in the ground. 

This quotation is to saw cut and excavate the concrete slab in the driveway in front of garage number 4, cut out and replace collapsed earthenware floor drain junction with new PVC pipework, fittings, reline approximately 13 meters of earthenware pipework from down-pipe connection beside garage door downstream covering all root infested and dislodged pipework fishing reline into storm water tank, reline approximately 5 meters of earthenware pipework. Relining from down-pipe connection on the side of the building down to main line connection covering all root infested and dislodged joints, reline approximately 2.5 meters of earthenware pipework. Relining from secondary floor drain down-to main line connection sealing all dislodged joints, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of driveway disruptions. 
  2. Barricade around work area.
  3. Saw cut concrete slab in front of garage number 4, excavate the concrete and ground exposing collapsed floor drain junction.
  4. Cut out collapsed earthenware pipework and junction.
  5. Install new PVC pipework, junction and fittings.
  6. Bed pipework with blue metal, back fill trench and re-instate concrete in the driveway.
  7. Use high pressure jet blaster, sanding pads and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  8. CCTV camera inspect before relining.
  9. Reline approximately 13 meters of earthenware pipework. Relining from down-pipe connection beside garage door downstream covering all root infested and dislodged pipework fishing reline into stormwater tank, using an approved 2 part Epoxy Resin and Installed as a continuous seamless Inversion liner using Australian watermark approved products.
  10. Using Robotic cutter reinstate 2 junction connections.
  11. Reline approximately 5 meters of earthenware pipework. Relining from down-pipe connection on the side of the building down to main line connection covering all root infested and dislodged joints, using an approved 2 part Epoxy Resin and Installed as a continuous seamless Inversion liner using Australian watermark approved products. 
  12. Reline approximately 2.5 meters of earthenware pipework. Relining from secondary floor drain down-to main line connection sealing all dislodged joints, using an approved 2 part Epoxy Resin and Installed as a continuous seamless Inversion liner using Australian watermark approved products. 
  13. Flow test all works carried out.
  14. Bed, pipework in the driveway, backfill trench and compact ground.
  15. Install rio bars, steel and re-concrete affected area of the driveway.

  17. Clean all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.
  18. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in in the common commercial shop hallway outside shop 1 & 2.

Gained access to the common hallway outside shops 1 & 2 and found water leaking from the buildings hot and cold water riser pipework and service riser.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 102, opened the access panel for the riser and located water on the concrete slab and no leaks from higher up.

The bath is adjacent to the riser, inspected under the bath through the panel vent and found water to be pooling under the bath.

Dye tested the bath waste and the silicone seals where the bath lip meets the wall tiles. From dye testing we found the faulty seals around the bath edge causing water to leak under the bath.

We found the bath/shower seals to be cracked and the bath is not recessed inside the wall. There is also water damaged to the timber framing supporting the bath.

We located the 3 x shower wall and tiling around the bath to be in very poor condition with large gaps in the grouting, mould and tiles popping off held with silicone. 

Returned to the property and gained access into unit 102.

Cut out the faulty sealant where the bath meets the common wall tiles and vertical wall.

Cleaned and primed affected areas in preparation for resealing. Installed new high grade flexible sealant to all affected areas in the shower bath area and vertical wall.

Used aqua vacuum and removed build up of water under the bath.

Cleaned all areas where work had take place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Due to movement in the bath and as the bath is not recessed inside the wall, we consider the resealing works carried out to be a temporary repair.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 102 - Due to the poor condition of the bathroom, we advise the lot owner engages their own building contractor to remove entire bathroom wall tiles, remove bath, supply and install new steel bath recessed inside the wall, install primer, 2 coats of waterproof membrane and re-tile the shower walls matching existing tiles as close as possible to match.

Following the recent sewer clear out works and our CCTV camera survey, we located tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer line in multiple areas on the main sewer lines.

We advise a building contractor is engaged to to carry out repairs on the external brick wall, pointing and window frames on the front face and inspect unit 4's balcony membrane to prevent further leaking into the wall cavity.

Once the external wall, balcony and guttering works are completed, we advise the bedroom wall, ceiling and cornice in unit 2 is monitored using a moisture meter.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Please attend and investigate a possible further secondary leak into the unit below being unit 36, unit above is unit 38.
Unit 36 recently has a leaking issue with their own bathroom and their contents insurer has been handling these works. Please contact them for information when sourcing and identifying another further leaks.
Matthew form National Leak Detection 1800 346 353
The owner of unit 36 is Marianne 0408 246 391

Kellie Davison
0401 318 609
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 36.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 36 and found wet carpet in the main bedroom adjacent to the bathroom and shower recess. Pulled back the carpet and found water seeping out of the concrete slab and wall.

Flood dye tested shower and all waste fixtures in the bathroom - no leaks were found.

Pressure tested, shower breaching piece and no leaks found.

Removed base timber from linen cupboard to expose the common service riser and no leaks found from the common internal bathroom stack pipework.

Gained access into unit 38 above and inspected the bathroom.

Isolated water supply carried out pressure test on the hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes are found within unit 38.

Following testing in unit 38 with located the shower tap spindle to be leaking constantly, which was causing water to leak behind the tiles and into the wall. Repaired leaking tap spindle and re-sealed affected area to prevent any further water leaking into the wall. 

Whilst inspecting and testing unit 38, we found the silicone seals and grout in the shower recess to have gaps and cracks causing water to leak in behind the tiles and into the substrate. As the bathroom in unit 38 has been renovated, we will submit a quotation for the lot owner’s consideration for the sealing and grouting repairs required in unit 38’s shower recess.

We contacted unit 36 2 days later, who advised there was water still leaking in the unit after the taps were repaired in unit 38 above.

Returned to unit 36, carried out pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply and no drop in pressure was found. 

Carried out further dye testing on the shower recess with red dye. As the leak has slowed down and was not constant, we advised to monitor overnight to see if red dye leaks from the bathroom door.

We contacted unit 36, who advised the water leak had stopped, then started again during the night. No red dye leaked and she used several towels overnight to dry the floor to prevent water entering the bedroom.

Returned to the property on Saturday, isolated the hot water supply over the weekend. The occupant advised over the weekend the leak has dried out completely, confirming the leak is from the hot water supply in unit 36.

Returned to the property engaged pipe location leak detection. Pressure tested the hot water and got a drop in pressure indicating a burst hot water pipe in unit 36.

Use pipe locating equipment to locate the hot water copper pipes within the kitchen and bathroom walls. 

Used the listening devise and located the loudest noise in the shower wall low down where the pipe comes out from the slab.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to rectify the burst hot water pipe in unit 36 - Leak detection has advised to excavate affected tiles and shower wall, repair burst section of pipework, patch render wall, re-waterproof and re-tile using white tiles. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent blockage we cleared in the common tradesman's toilet and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original common earthenware branch line downstream from the common toilet located under the concrete slab.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 meters of root infested earthenware sewer pipework, downstream from the common tradesman's toilet, sealing all root infested and dislodged joints, using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Gain access into the tradesman's toilet. 
  2. Disconnect and remove common toilet to access the common sewer branch line.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  4. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining work

  1. Reline approximately 2 meters of root infested earthenware sewer pipework, downstream from the common tradesman's toilet, sealing all root infested and dislodged joints, using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  2. Re-install existing common toilet sealing to the ground.
  3. Turn on the water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  4. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  5. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  6. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  7. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate water leaks in unit 114.

Attended he property, gained access into unit 114 and found water damage on the internal walls behind the shower recess in both main and ensuite bathroom.

Found the bathroom tiling to be original and the bathrooms to have a flat floor level.

Carried out a pressure test on the shower breaching piece, hot and cold water piping in unit 114 and no drop in pressure was found.

Inspect grout and sealant in both showers and found missing wall and floor grout and no sealant around the perimeter of the shower tray.

Performed a dye test on the ensuite shower tray and located dye to leak through the wall into the bedroom carpet adjacent indicating faulty waterproof membrane under the tiles.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak below unit 1 in the common walkway passage.

Attended the property on 12/9 and located water leaking from the concrete slab around the common stack pipe penetration below unit 1.

Gained access to unit 1, stepped out the leak and found the common stack pipe in the laundry behind the washing machine and laundry tub. After inspecting unit 1, we found water leaking from the ceiling in the laundry around the common stack pipe indicating the leak was coming from higher up. At the time of inspection we were unable to gain access into unit 3 & 5 and requested contact details to gain entry.

Returned to the property on the 14/9,  Gained access into unit 3 and found no water leaking onto the laundry floors around the common stack pipe, no leaking taps in the laundry. Dye tested unit 3's laundry and shower waste drains and found no dye to be leaking into unit 1 from the concrete slab indicating the leak is not coming from the common stack pipe. Carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing in unit 3 and found there to be no drop in pressure.

Gained access into unit 4 and inspected the renovated bathroom and laundry, found there to be no leaking onto the laundry floor and no leaking taps. As unit 4 was not prepared for our attendance, we re booked to return the following day and carry out pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply. Returned to unit 4 on the 15/9, isolated the hot and cold water supply and carried out extensive pressure testing and found a drop in pressure on the hot water supply, indicating a burst pressurized pipe.

Returned to the property on 20/9, engaged pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water service within the laundry and bathroom walls and located the hot water pipework where it comes out of the concrete slab  in units 4 to the bathroom and laundry fixtures. Our leak detection specialist could not locate the exact position of the burst pipe within the concrete slab and advised that the we excavate the common walls in unit 4 behind the washing machine to locate where the pipes come out from the concrete slab into the wall.

Gained access into units 4 on the 22/9, disconnected the washing machines in the laundry to access the common wall. Excavate the wall around the hot water pipework where it goes from the wall into the concrete slab and found no water leak or burst pipes in the wall. We found the hot water pipework enters the concrete slab in unit 3's wall behind the washing machine. Gained access into unit 3 on the 26/9, removed the laundry tub and excavated the common wall, located the pipework where it goes into the concrete slab, cut the copper pipework and carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the pipework in the concrete slab to confirm the burst pipe is located in the concrete slab from the laundry to the common stairs and meter cupboard.

We advised the occupants in unit 4 to isolate the hot water in the common meter cupboard when the taps are not in use to reduce the water leak and prevent further damage.

As the burst copper pipe is located in the concrete slab pipework from the laundry to the common stairs meter cupboard and isolation valve, a hot water rerun is required to delete the burst pressurized copper pipe in the concrete slab.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 4 - We advise the burst pressurized hot water copper pipe is deleted within the concrete slab and a new hot water service is re-run from the common stairs hot water meter cupboard, through the bedroom wall to the laundry and bathroom pipework in the laundry wall behind the washing machine. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Please note - The burst pipe leak has caused damaged to unit 1's laundry ceiling light and they cannot turn the light on as it trips the power. We advise an electrician is engaged to inspect the laundry of unit 1 and carry out repairs.

Once the hot water pipework repairs are undertaken in units 3 & 4 and we know the full extent of the damage, we will submit a quotation for any resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate high water usage at the property.

Attended the property on 2 x occasions and inspected the main water meter at the front left passage.

On inspection we found the meter to be still and not ticking over. We found the smaller dial slightly moving at a constant pace and comes to a stop indicating no burst pipe.

Walked around the property and checked all common external areas, hose taps and drains, found there to be no visible water leaking. 

When we returned to the property, we Inspected the main water meter again and found the dial to be still and not ticking constantly.

Inspected the main water meter at intervals and found the smaller dial to stop most times after use.

Following investigation and testing, we found there to be no burst pressurized water pipe at the building.

The excessive water bill may have been caused by a leaking water fixture in one of the apartments and the faulty fixture has now been repaired.

We advise the next bill is monitored to see if it is excessive or back to the approximate cost of the previous bill.

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared in unit 7 and our CCTV camera survey, we found major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer line from the base of the stack outside unit 7 and in the main line downstream.

This quotation is to reline approximately 14 meters downstream from the common sewer stack pipework outside unit 7's bathroom, sealing all tree root infested and cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin and re-instate junctions using robotic cutter.

The following works will be undertaken:

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak into unit 26 from the bathroom ceiling.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 26 and found water damage to the bathroom ceiling where the drain pipes for unit 34's bathroom are cast into the concrete slab.

Gained access into unit 34's bathroom above and found the bathroom to be in original condition.

Pressure tested the shower breaching piece and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found.

Blocked off the bathroom floor waste drain and filled drainage pipework cast into the slab with red dye to test all pipe joins including that which had been previously sealed with epoxy. 

Flood tested the original bathroom floor tiles and waterproof membrane around the floor drain with green dye and flood tested bath and shower wall tiles / silicone seals with clear water. After extensive flood testing in unit 34's bathroom, no water leaked at the time of our investigation.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 44 and inspected the external wall and windows from the balcony. There are gaps around window and signs of water leaks on outside wall from little roof above unit 44's balcony.

Used moisture meter to confirm the external walls are dry indicating the leak is not coming form unit 44.

Returned to unit 34, made a hole in the side of the bath, used the inspection camera and found it to be dry, after flood testing of the shower/ bath and plug and waste pipework, no water was found to be leaking under the bath.

After extensive pressure testing of the water supply in unit 34, we found a leak on the cold water bath tap and toilet tee which is tracking back into the wall.

Turned off the water supply, pulled apart the cold water bath tap and repaired leaking teflon joint on the screwed tee which connects the toilet supply, installed sealant behind cover-plates to prevent water leaking into the wall and re installed taps.

We advise the water leak in unit 26 is monitored and if any further water leaks through the bathroom ceiling, further testing and investigation works will be required to be undertaken.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 44 - We advise a building contractor is engaged to seal the external window frames and mortar joints. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Attended the property on Friday and inspected the water hammer noise in unit 4.

After extensive testing, we can confirm there is loose pipework within the cavity behind the bathroom/laundry.

The occupant strongly advised, he would rather accept the hammer noise then undertake large excavation works damaging tiles in the bathroom and/or laundry.

We temporarily connected the washing machine to another tap under the laundry tub and the occupant was willing to test over the weekend to see the outcome.

We made contact with the occupant today, who advised the noise is still present after the temporary connection, but bearable if the bathroom door is closed.

Once we moved the washing machine connection to the tap under the laundry tub the hammer noise in the hallway and ceiling has since changed.

We have limited the noise by installing water hammer arrestors and there is a short cycle on the machine where it still makes a hammer in the loose pipework within the cavity that can be heard from the bathroom side.

Cost of further works up to date - $340.00 plus GST

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 4, cut a neat hole in the side of the laundry tub down low, install the washing machine tap/hammer arrestor on the water point and connect washing machine water hose. 

Cost for further works - $390.00 Plus GST

Description:
Water Meter Separation - Apartments 801, 716, 715, 701 & 601

JOB DESCRIPTION
Residential apartments 801, 716, 715, 701 and 601 are currently metered under a single water meter. Now that the apartments are under Strata Sydney Water have advised that they do not meet Metering Requirements for internal meter installations and/or AS3500.1:2015 Section 15.1. An Accredited Metering Supplier (Itron) will be required to complete the commissioning process once
the site is compliant with Sydney Water Multi-Level Metering Requirements and the Australian Standards.
Treat Plumbing was engaged to conduct an audit of the existing Hydraulic system that services the five apartments and to prepare a Scope of Works and costing to prepare for the installation of separate meters.
Invoice Description:
Attended the property on 2 x occasions and met with the building manager Darren.

Gained access to level 6, 7, 8 and the common roof plant to locate the cold water pipes for unit 601, 701, 801, 715 & 716 in the common hallway ceilings.

Removed downlights in the common hallways and inspected the pipework, locating pipework for each unit within the gyprock ceiling.

Gained access into units 601, 715 & 716 to inspect the ceiling cavity.

As per Sydney water Multi leveling Metering requirements, we advise to alter the existing common cold water pipework and Itron EverBlue water meters are installed, the new meters will be located in the Level 7 locked service cupboard and the level 8 roof plant room. 

Please see attached quotation to install individual cold water meters for units 601, 701, 801, 715 & 716 and alter the cold water pipework in the common hallway ceilings on level 6, 7 & 8 roof plant to allow individual cold water meters to be installed.

The quotation also includes separating the hot and cold water pipework in units 715 & 716 by cutting holes in the gyprock ceiling of unit 715 and installing new hot and cold water pipework within the ceiling cavity. To separate the hot water supply, unit 716 is required to install a gas Rinnai hot water heater on the rooftop wall in the external plant room connecting to the hot, cold and gas pipes in the adjacent kitchen.

Mapped out the new proposed cold water pipework, and supplied drawings to the building manager Darren.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Common stormwater repairs to the common driveway pits and main stormwater tank in the carpark driveway.

Following our recent stormwater clear out works within the driveway carpark we found the common below ground stormwater tank on the right side of the property urgently needs to be cleaned out of debris which is causing the pump to slowly discharge stormwater to the street. We also found the stormwater pipework connected to the stormwater tank is at a higher level than the driveway surface water pit drains causing the driveway pits to hold water and block up during heavy rain as the system is unbale to cope with the high volume of water. The Stormwater pits within the left driveway need urgent repairs as there are large holes around the PVC pipework connecting to the pits and when the pipework fills up water leaks from the pits into the subsoil below the bitumen driveway causing sink holes and undermining within the bitumen driveaway.

This quotation is to engage a sucker truck contractor to suck out all the dirt, silt and rubbish from the common storm water tank, service the common stormwater pumps, lower the common stormwater pipework causing the driveway surface water pits to fill up, repair all the surface water pits in the carpark driveway sealing the pits and filling in the base of the pit to prevent water leaking into the subsoil and to flow test the common stormwater pipework and ensure full capacity flow to the street.  

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of carpark closures.
  2. Gain access into the car park and engage sucker truck contractor.
  3. Suck out all dirt, silt and rubbish from the common storm water tank using sucker truck.
  4. Clean out the base of the storm water tank using high pressure hose.
  5. Remove the stormwater pump, clean out check valves, check impellers for any debris and service pumps. 
  6. Zip tie loose float cables that are hanging and adjust float levels to suite the pump activation level.
  7. Flow test common stormwater pumps and ensure discharging to the street.
  8. Excavate the bitumen and trench where the inlet to the stormwater tank connects to the closest surface water pit.
  9. Cut out and remove original earthenware pipework which is at a higher level. 
  10. Excavate the side of the stormwater tank and the surface water pit and lower the pipework to ensure fall to the common stormwater tank.
  11. Re-concrete around the common stormwater tank and surface water pit sealing the pipework into place.
  12. Repair 7 x surface water pits in the carpark driveway sealing the pipework connected to the pits and installing concrete at the base of the pits to prevent water build up in the base and prevent water leaking into the subsoil.
  13. Bed pipe, back fill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500.
  14. Installation of hot mix bitumen to the drive and road.
  15. Flow test all common stormwater pipework within the carpark driveaway and ensure full flow capacity to the street.
  16. Clean all areas where work has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 405.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 405 and found water damage to the common wall adjacent to unit 404.

Used moisture meter to locate high readings of moisture within the common wall.

Tested all fixtures within unit 405s bathroom and no leaks or faults were found.

Sucked out water from under the bath using aqua vacumn to prevent further damage.

installed new access vent on the front face of the bath.

Description:
URGENT QUOTATION - Burst pressurized common hot water copper pipework within the concrete slab unit 4.

Following extensive testing in unit 4 with pipe location leak detection, we located a burst pressurized hot water copper pipe within the concrete slab.

This quotation is to re-run a new hot water copper service from the kitchen to the bathroom deleting the burst hot water pipe within the concrete slab.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Lay drop sheets in unit 4's kitchen, bathroom and hallway.
  2. Remove toilet and vanity basin from bathroom.
  3. Excavate the tiles and wall in the bathroom and locate hot water line that goes to kitchen behind the toilet.
  4. Excavate the tiles and wall in the bathroom and locate hot water line that goes to the basin hot tap.
  5. Turn off the hot water supply and drain the water from the line.
  6. Test pipework to make sure the right line is being deleted.
  7. Remove skirting around the hallway walls to the kitchen cabinetry. 
  8. Excavate and chase the hallway walls in preparation for new hot water pipework.
  9. Run new pipework out the basin wall into the hallway then around the skirting to the kitchen cabinetry.
  10. Cut holes in the kitchen kickboard and secure new pipework under the kitchen cabinetry.
  11. Excavate around hot water copper pipework under the kitchen sink and external wall.
  12. Connect new hot water pipework at the basin and kitchen location.
  13. Turn on the water supply and test all works carried out.
  14. Repair tiles behind the toilet and vanity basin.
  15. Reinstall toilet and wall hung vanity basin.
  16. Turn on the water supply on to the bathroom fixtures and test all works carried out.
  17. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 3 and the common area.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 3, found the bathroom waste to be blocked and surcharging out of the overflow relief gully.

Removed inspection opening lids on the main boundary trap in front of the garages and found that boundary trap and sewer pipework for the whole building to be blocked.

Set up high-pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high-pressure water jet blaster extensively downstream from the boundary trap to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera and located tree root infestations entering the original earthenware outlet of the boundary trap to Sydney Water’s main located under the road approximately 10 meters. CCTV video link -  https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NJBIG

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera extensively to clear out all tree root infestations entering the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main.

Cut out section of waste pipework outside unit 3, used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out multiple areas of tree roots entering the main sewer line.

Repaired waste pipework, flood tested all waste fixtures in unit 3, main line and boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note if urgent repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested pipework further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages and flood - We advise the original tree root infested earthenware pipework is relined completely sealing the line as a full proof solution. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

If the owners corporation does not have the funds to undertake the relining works, we advise the tree root infestations are cleared out of the common sewer line on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months. We will submit a seperate quotation shortly for the option for preventative maintenance.

As per Quotation 20889 - Relining works on the common sewer lines

  • STAGE 1 - Relining works under unit 1's bathroom

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Gain access into unit 1 and lay protective sheeting on the floor.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the sewer pipework in preparation for relining. 
  3. CCTV record sewer line before relining.
  4. Reline approximately 2.5 meters of cracked and dislodged earthenware pipework relining from connection on inspection shaft upstream covering cracked toilet elbow sealing all dislodged joints, using watermarked approved Liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  5. Using robotic cutter reinstate 1 Junction connection.
  6. Reline approximately 2 meters of root infested earthenware pipework relining from inlet on gully upstream covering root infested section, using watermarked approved Liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.

  8. Flow test pipework after relining.
  9. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  10. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  11. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  12. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

  8. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to unit 3 and found the bath / shower waste to be slow draining.

Used the drain camera to CCTV camera survey all the common waste stack and branch pipes on the external wall, the sewer vent and in ground common sewer drainage -  All common pipes were found to be clear and no blockages were found.

In the bathroom of unit 3 which has recently been renovated we found the bath / shower waste to be connected to the tiled floor drain which used to be a shower.

Following testing of the bath waste, we found the bath waste pipework is sealed with silicone where it meets the floor grate and when the bath is draining under pressure there is a leak. There is also no fall on the flexible bath waste where it joins the old shower waste drain which is causing blockages.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 3 - As the bathroom has recently been renovated, we advise the lot owner of unit 3 engages their own plumber to undertake repairs to the faulty bath waste piping.

Description: JOB: U4 Plumbing Issues The following work needs to be carried out: inspect and quote on the plumbing issues with unit 4 Site contact: Graeme - 02 9328 1916
Invoice Description:
Attended the property and gained access to unit 4 to investigate toilets blocking.

Flushed all toilets on the top level bathrooms with toilet paper and located a blockage in the pipework causing the toilets to fill up.

Cut the silicone at the base of the toilet in the main bathroom and removed the toilet to camera survey the common pipework.

After camera surveying the common sewer pipework, we located incorrect fall in the sewer which is causing the toilet paper to catch on the pipework bends.

Flushed the toilet in the ensuite bathroom whilst the camera was in the pipework to confirm the toilet paper and incorrect fall is causing the blockage.

Camera surveyed approximately 3-4 meters of pipework which is slowly draining and holding water from the upstairs toilet pan connection along the kitchen/ hallway ceiling to the vertical stack.

Camera surveyed approximately 13 meters from the downstairs toilet to the boundary trap and found no causes of blockages in the common sewer drainage under the floors unit 4.

Re-installed toilet and sealed to the bathroom floor using high grade sealant.

Whilst testing the sewer pipework on the upstairs levels we ran the shower to flow test the drainage within the ceiling cavity, after flow testing the shower drain, we found water leaking through the kitchen ceiling bulkhead and downlights.

Inspected the shower recess and located missing grout and sealant - To repair the leaking shower recess, we advise the shower floor and wall tiles are re sealed by a shower resealing contractor.

Returned to the property removed cover plates and button kit for the 2 x top level toilet cisterns and found the cisterns water level could not be raised to allow a larger flush.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to cut a series of holes within the ceiling of unit 4's kitchen and hallway to locate the sewer drainage and inspect the cavity and vertical stack dropper to see if the drainage can be lowered to create more fall. We will submit a quotation for the further investigation works required to be undertaken in unit 4.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage on the Cooyoung Crescent side of the building.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 4.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 4 and found hot water leaking from the external wall behind the kitchen into the garden area.

Isolated the water supply from the heater, carried out extensive nitrogen pressure testing on the hot water supply.

Following pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe within unit 4.

Advised the occupant to turn the hot water supply off at the hot water isolation valve when not showering to prevent further water damage.

Returned to the property, excavated a hole in the external brick wall behind the kitchen where the brick vent was located.

Exposed the original hot and cold water pipes which run from the kitchen wall into the concrete slab. Carried out further testing to locate the burst pipe to be within the concrete slab. 

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water service within the kitchen to the bathroom. 

Our leak detection specialist could not locate the exact position of the burst pipe within the concrete slab and advised that the only way to undertake repairs is to rerun a new hot water pipe and delete the burst pressurized pipe within the concrete slab.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken in unit 4 - We advise the burst pressurized hot water copper pipe is deleted within the concrete slab and a new hot water service is re-run from the kitchen to the bathroom. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.
