Description:
We need a plumber. There is fluid leeching out of the steps near entrance to our block. 

It's a bit smelly.
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage near the entrance.

Urgently attended the property on Friday 1/9/23 and found the common sewer line to be blocked and leaking out of the concrete slab on the left side near the entrance.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening lids, used high pressure jet blaster downstream the inspection opening lid on the left hand side of the property but after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage due to the height change and offset bends in the sewer system.

Used CCTV drain camera and pipe locating equipment to locate the common sewer line to be at the bottom of the stairs. Excavated section of concrete next to the step with a jack hammer and excavated the ground 300mm exposing original earthenware pipework, gained access to the pipework.

Returned to the property on Saturday 2/9/23, continued to use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out multiple tree root infestations which was the cause of the blockage.

Flow tested the common sewer line - All clear and in good working order.

Returned to the property on Monday 4/9/23, back filled trench and re-concreted affected area.

After we had cleared all the lines, we undertook an extensive CCTV camera survey on the sewer and storm water system. Following our CCTV camera survey and investigation works we found  there is a floor waste/surface drain next to the entrance which discharges into the sewer and the two upstream connections are installed into the stormwater system. We consider around 10 to 15  years ago they had some work done to the building entrance and while completing those works the plumbers got the sewer and stormwater mixed up. Please see CCTV video link of the cross connection of sewer and storm water - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NE4FU

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the cross connection - We advise to remove affected tiles near the entrance, saw cut, excavate concrete slab, excavate a trench across the tiled entrance way to the earthenware sewer line which can be connected into the sewer pipe which is currently picking up the stormwater pit and connect to the common sewer, backfill, re-concrete and retile. The connection on to the stormwater line can be excavated and a stormwater pit installed in this location instead which would still pick up the ground water.  We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Invoice Description:
Investigate overflowing sewer on side of the building in courtyard area of unit 3.

Attended the property, found the common sewer line to be blocked and surcharging sewerage out of the common overflow gully in the courtyard area of unit 3.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening on the common stack pipe, used high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering  the original earthenware pipework downstream from the sewer stack pipe in multiple locations which was the cause of the blockage.

CCTV video link downstream sewer stack in the courtyard area of unit 3 - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NEZ6Q

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Flow tested common sewer line - All clear and in good working order. Please note if the tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further sewer blockages and floods will re-occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline approximately 11 meters of root infested earthenware sewer pipework, relining from the sewer stack inspection opening downstream to vertical shaft connection sealing all root infested and dislodged joints, using water marked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin and reinstate 1x gully connection using robotic cutter. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate bathroom leak and sewer smell.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1102 and located wet carpet at the entrance to the bathroom.

Lifted the water damaged carpet and found water leaking from the bathroom tile bed and door angle.

Pressure tested the shower and bath breaching pieces and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found.

Dye tested the shower recess and found red dye to leak from the tile bed into the hallway where the wet carpet is located indicating water has leaked through the waterproof membrane outside the bathroom.

Inspected the sewer smell in the laundry.

Removed floor waste grate and found the laundry floor waste to have no water seal and no fixtures charging the floor waste.

Used electric eel down the laundry floor waste pipework and found it to be clear and in good working order.

Poured a bucket of water down the floor waste drain which sealed the trap and advised the residents if the smell returns the floor waste needs to be charge with water to eliminate the smell.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 1102. To prevent water leaking from the shower recess, we advise a building contractor is engaged to remove the floor and first course of wall tiles in the bathroom, install new water proof membrane and retile the bathroom floor and first course of wall tiles.

Once the waterproofing and tiling repair works have been completed, we advise the resultant damage carpet in the hallway is steam cleaned or replaced.

The top floor apartments have recently experienced a drop in the water pressure and the temperature fluctuates unexpectedly, going suddenly cold and
then really hot.

Please make arrangements with the site contact before attending as other committee members may need to be in attendance.
Invoice Description:
Investigate low water pressure at the property.

Attended the property, gained access into the rear yard and located the common hot water heater.

Inspected the heater valves and found the original pressure limiting valve on the inlet supply to be set at 450kpa.

Gained access into unit 10 on the top floor, tested the water pressure in the bathroom and found the hot water pressure to be 300kpa.

Tested other bathroom fixture taps and found the pressure would drop in the shower to 150kpa very quickly.

Went to the heater and adjusted the pressure limiting valve to 600kpa which made no difference in pressure.

Made contact with unit 11 who is also on the top floor and booked them to return for further testing.

Returned to the property the following day, gained access into unit 11 and tested all bathroom fixtures.

Found the pressure fluctuates in the bathroom hot taps when other fixtures within the bathroom are being used.

Tested the water pressure in unit 11 and found the water pressure to be 300kpa.

Tested the buildings cold water pressure and found it to be 350kpa, indicating that the original pressure limiting valve does not need to be there on the common heater water supply.

Isolated the water supply to the heater, cut out and removed the pressure limiting valve and installed new pipe and fittings connecting the hot water supply.

Turned the hot water back on tested all works carried out - all in good working order.

Advised unit 10 & 11 to test the pressure over the course of the night and advise if the pressure has been resolved.

After speaking with the residents, we confirmed the pressure in the top units has been rectified and there were no further hot water fluctuations.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access into unit 6 and the owner advised of a leak in the ensuite bathroom ceiling from the exhaust fan.

Removed the exhaust fan cover and found a small oil stain. Disconnected the fan to inspect inside the ceiling cavity and no leaks were found. The owner advised the leak only occurred once and the ceiling fan was connected to the vent pipework.

There was no water stains on the ceiling or common drainage pipework within the cavity and the leak is coming from the extractor fan ventilation pipework.

Tested the extractor fan, found the bathroom fan and the kitchen fan above the cooktop to be connected. If the outlet is blocked this can cause condensation within the vent pipework.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 6 - We advise a mechanical air contractor is engaged to inspect the bathroom and kitchen ventilation ducting and carry out repairs to prevent condensation build up within the pipework which is leaking from the bathroom ceiling vent.

Gained access and inspected unit 10 and found it not to be above the leak.

Gained access into unit 11 and located the powder room toilet and floor waste to be directly above the fan and the laundry is in the adjacent room.

Ran all waste fixtures and flood tested the powder room toilet and laundry floor tiles and waterproof membrane - No leaks were found in unit 6 ceiling below. Pressure tested the hot and cold water piping and main and ensuite shower breach in unit 11 and no drop in pressure was found.

When flood testing on unit 11's upstairs main and ensuite shower recess, we located water leaking into the bedroom from the ensuite shower recess indicating faulty water proof membrane in the ensuite bathroom.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 11 by a building contractor - As the water proof membrane has failed within the upstairs ensuite shower causing water to leak into the bedroom adjacent, we advise the entire bathroom floor is excavated, rewater proofed and retiled to replace the faulty waterproof membrane. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common storm water line located in the pool area

While on site completing relining of the sewer system in the pool area we tried to put a hose down the storm water drain which immediately overflowed. We then removed the water and inspected using our CCTV drain camera. Following our CCTV camera survey we found 2 x sections in the original 100mm earthenware storm water line which are badly broken causing blockages. We also found tree root infestations, a large amount of sand and the earthenware pipework to be in bad condition with hair line cracks for approximately 15 meters.

This quotation is to reline approximately 15 meters of broken and tree root infested 100mm earthenware storm water pipework downstream from the downpipe using our watermark approved epoxy relining system and reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter completely sealing the line.

The following works will be undertaken:

Preparation:

  1. Carefully remove broken sections from the pipe and of the sand and debris.
  2. Clear lines using high pressure water jet.
  3.  Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS3500.
  4. Record footage of lines before relining.

Pipe relining:

  1. Barricade around work area.
  2. Reline 15 meters of broken and tree root infested 100mm earthenware water pipework located under the concrete slab in the pool area using our watermark approved epoxy relining system
  3. Reinstate 2 x junctions using robotic cutter
  4. Flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line for the pool bathrooms.

Following the recent blockage we cleared on the common sewer line for the pool bathrooms, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework upstream and downstream from the reflux valve. Also tree roots entering the 2 x common branch lines connecting each common toilet.

This quotation is to reline approximately 5.5 from the top of the floor waste in the bathroom to the reflux valve and to reline approximately 3.5 meters from the plastic section after the reflux valve down to vertical shaft sealing all root infested joints. Remove 2 x common toilets, reline approximately 2 meters of earthenware pipework relining from top of toilet down to previously relined mainline and reline approximately 1.5 meters earthenware pipework relining from top of toilet down to previously relined mainline.

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of water disruptions.
  2. Set up safe working area around common toilets
  3. Gain access into x 2 common bathrooms at the pool.
  4. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  5. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Turn off the water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 5.5 meters of root infested earthenware pipework relining from top of floor waste in common toilet down to plastic reflux valve using watermarked approved products.
  3. Using robotic cutter to reinstate 3 junction connections.
  4. Reline approximately 3.5 meters of root infested earthenware pipework relining from plastic section on reflux valve downstream to vertical shaft connection using watermarked approved products.
  5. Using robotic cutter reinstate 2 x junction connections.
  6. Reline approximately 2 meters of earthenware pipework relining from top of toilet 1 down to previously relined mainline.
  7. Reline approximately 1.5 meters earthenware pipework relining from top of toilet 2 down to previously relined mainline.
  8. Re-install 2 x common toilets sealing to the ground.
  9. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  10. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  11. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  12. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  13. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of all relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. Invoice Description:
Investigate water leaking into the fire stairs on B2.

Attended the property on the 7/8/23, gained access to B2 and found water pooling at the base of the fire stairs.

Used wet vac to remove a large amount of pooling water and dried the concrete slab at the base of the fire stairs.

Once dried, we located water leaking through the fire stairs wall from the external garden areas. 

Adjacent to the fire stairs is B2 external garden and unit 1's backyard. Left an access note on unit 1 to return on a dry day and carry out flood testing in the backyard and on B1 garden adjacent to the fire stair wall.

Found there to be a large amount of soil built up around the fire stair wall and the soil to be holding water.

Returned to the property on the 14/8 gained access into unit 1 and inspected the back yard around the fire stair wall, found the soil in the backyard to be holding water and also water leaking from the cavity wall and unit 1's courtyard floor tiles at ground level.

Gained access to B1 external garden area adjacent to the fire stairs above the retaining wall level.

Used a hose to flood test the fire stair wall on B1 and excavated a series of holes in unit 1's backyard on B2 below the floor level of the fire stair concrete slab.

After flood testing on B1, we identified water leaking into the fire stairs at the base, water pooling in unit 1's backyard where the holes were excavated around the fire stair wall within the soil and water leaking out from the cavity wall weep holes where the soil level was above.

Please see attached videos of flood testing the external areas on B1 & B2 - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N8U6S

We inspected the common stormwater drainage pits and found them to be blocked and full of leaves. We inspected the common stormwater downpipes on B1 level and found them not to be connected into the stormwater and discharging onto the ground around the building.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken by Treat Plumbing- We advise the common stormwater pit and pipework on B1 & B2 is cleared out of debris blocking the pits and the pipework is cleared out using the high pressure water jet blaster and drain camera. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the stormwater clear out works required to be undertaken on B1 & B2.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken by a building contractor - We advise the external soil level in the backyard of unit 1 on B2 and the external area on B1 around the fire stairs is excavated to a level below the concrete slab level and the large amount of soil is removed from the property. Once the soil level is below the concrete slab level, subsoil drainage needs to be installed around the perimeter of the building and the fire stairs, a trench needs to be excavated around the building and fire stair wall, the wall needs to be waterproofed, then geotech fabric, aglines and blue metal installed in the trenches and the agline drainage connected to the common stormwater system. Also the downpipes on level B1 need to be connected the common stormwater pits. Due to the large scale of works, we advise a remedial building contractor is engaged to undertake these works.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken pace and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property on the 11/8/23, gained access into unit 807, found the hot and cold water isolation valve within the laundry to be faulty and would not isolate the water supply. 

Advised residents of water disruptions, returned to the property, shut down the hot and cold water supply located on the riser and drained the water from the line.

Gained access into unit 807, disconnected the hot and cold water isolation valves and replaced with new.

Turned on the water supply, tested all works and found the hot water isolation valve to not turn off the water supply. Returned to the property on 14/8/23, laid drop sheets in unit 807, removed affected tiles and laundry tub. 

Used jack hammer to excavate the laundry wall exposing faulty hot water isolation valve and pipework.

Shut down the hot water supply located at the riser and drained the water from the line.

Cut out faulty hot water isolation valve and pipework. Installed new hot water isolation valve, pipework and fittings connecting onto existing hot water supply.

Turned on the hot water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Patch rendered wall, re-installed existing laundry tub connecting drainage.

Re-tiled and grouted affected area and re-sealed where the laundry tub meets the tiles using high grade flexible sealant.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in the common driveway.

Urgently attended the property, found the common sewer line to be completely blocked and surcharging sewerage onto the neighboring property.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection open lid on the common stack pipe between to the 2 garages in the driveway and boundary trap, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream the stack pipe to locate a collapsed section of original earthenware pipework located under the concrete driveway. We continued to camera the rest of the common sewer line to locate major tree root infestations to be entering majority of the main sewer line and outlet of boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main.

CCTV video link of collapsed pipe downstream sewer stack located rear right driveway - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N81SG

CCTV video link of tree roots in the common sewer line - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N8UBW

CCTV video link of tree roots entering the outlet of the boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N8UYA

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the original earthenware sewer line and outlet of boundary trap downstream to Sydney Waters main. 

Flow tested common sewer line which is currently clear and in working order. Please note if the collapsed and tree root infested common sewer pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will re-occur.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and cleaned all sewerage using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to saw cut and excavate a section of the concrete driveway, cut out collapsed section of earthenware sewer pipework, install new section of PVC pipework, re-instate concrete and reline all tree root infested common sewer pipework. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the works with our relining team.

This URGENT quotation is to repair the burst hot water copper pipe within the common laundry wall of unit 3 behind the laundry tub.

  1. Gain access, lay drop sheets in unit 3.
  2. Turn off the hot water supply to the unit and drain the water from the line.
  3. Excavate splash-back tiles and remove the laundry tub.

  7. Turn the hot water supply back on, testing of all works.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent after hours sewer blockage we cleared in unit 3's bathroom and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework at the base of the common sewer stack which was the cause of the blockage.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework downstream from the base of the common sewer stack outside unit 3's bathroom, sealing all cracked and tree root infested pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  3. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Turn off the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework downstream from the base of the common sewer stack outside unit 1=3's bathroom, sealing all cracked and tree root infested pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  3. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  4. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  5. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  6. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  7. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent blockage in unit 16's bathroom.

Urgently attended the property on the 31/8/23, gained access into unit 16, found the shower and basin to be completely blocked. When unit 18 above used there shower, black coloured waste was surcharging out of the floor waste and was flooding the bathroom.

Used electric eel downstream from the floor waste in unit 16's bathroom and after multiple attempts we were unable to clear the blockage.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment into unit 16's bathroom.

Used the high pressure jet baster and aqua vacuum downstream the floor waste but we were again unable to clear the blockage.

Removed common service riser in the bathroom, removed inspection opening on the common 80mm cast iron stack pipework, used CCTV drain camera and found the original cast iron stack pipework to be very badly corroded and a large amount of rust and hair causing the blockage. CCTV video link of blocked stack with rust and hair -https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-N8DNR

Used high pressure jet blaster extensively downstream the cast iron stack pipework and we found black coloured waste water to be flooding out of unit 11 and 7's floor waste in their bathroom. Following extensive jet blasting we were unable to clear the blockage in the common stack pipework.

Used high pressure jet blaster downstream unit 11 and 7's floor waste and aqua vacuum but were again unable to clear the blockage.

Cleaned unit 7, 11 and 16's bathrooms using disinfectant.

Returned to the property the following morning on the 1/8/23 with 2 x plumbers, gained access into unit 8's garage and removed inspection opening to access the common stack pipework.

Used high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively upstream from the stack and downstream from the stack in unit 16's bathroom to clear out a large amount of rust and hair from the common cast iron waste stack pipework.

Gained access into units 16, 11 & 7 flow tested all fixtures within the bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

Following testing we located a leak on the cast iron stack pipework within unit 7's common service riser where a previous plumber has made a hole into the common stack to clear a previous blockage. Used epoxy resign to carry out repair to the leaking common cast iron stack pipework.

Cleaned all areas as best as possible in units 16, 11 and 7 using aqua vacuum and disinfectant. 

Please note - We found the original 80mm cast iron waste stack pipework to be badly corroded and in very bad condition which was the cause of the blockage. Further works required to be undertaken to rectify further common sewer blockages in units 3, 7, 11, 16 & 18 - We advise the corroded common stack pipework is relined completely sealing the corroded cast iron stack pipework and all joint using a watermarked approved 80mm liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin. We will submit an urgent quotation for the relining works once we have reviewed the job with our relining team.

We advise a carpet contractor is engaged to steam clean or replace the damaged carpet in unit 7.

  10. Use CCTV drain camera to ensure the blockage has been cleared.
  11. Back fill trench with sand and re-instated pavers in unit 115.
  12. Gain access into unit 3.
  13. Lift tiles on the balcony to locate the floor waste drains.

  17. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following our CCTV camera survey we found major tree root infestations entering the original 150mm earthenware boundary trap and outlet pipework, tree root infestations entering approximately 2 meters of original 150mm earthenware sewer pipework on the right hand side of the property and also tree root infestations within Sydney Waters main sewer line. 

We will contact Sydney Water emergency crew who will attend the property and clear the tree roots from their sewer main free of charge.

  • OPTION 2 - Boundary trap reline (urgent works)

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clear out the boundary trap in preparation for relining.
  3. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining 

  1. Turn off the building water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline using inversion method approximately 4.5 meters downstream the boundary trap, sealing cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reinstate 3 x junctions using robotic cutter.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

Please note - If option 2 is approved, we will clear out the tree root infestations from the right hand side of the property with jet blaster and CCTV drain camera free of charge. 

Total cost of works for option 2 -  $6,980 + GST

 

 

 

  • OPTION 1 - Clear out all tree roots from the common sewer lines using high pressure water jet blaster & CCTV drain camera

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 202.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 202 and found water leaking from the gyprock ceiling above the shower in the bathroom.

Cut a hole in the water damaged ceiling and located water leaking from the pipe penetration through the concrete slab from unit 302 above.

Gained access into unit 302 and found water damage and rising dampness along the internal wall between the bathroom and the kitchen.

Cut a hole low down in the common service duct in the kitchen to access the pipework penetration where the water was leaking.

Inspected inside the cavity and found water pooling on the concrete slab around the pipe penetration and no water leaking from above.

located the shower recess, basin and toilet along the internal wall and a cavity behind where the plumbing and in wall cistern is housed.

Carried out pressure testing on the hot and cold water pipes and shower breaching piece, no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipe.

Removed the toilet, made a hole and inspected the cavity built out in the bathroom behind the plumbing fixtures.

Located red dye pooling within the cavity, indicating water has leaked through the waterproof membrane into the cavity where there is no water proof membrane.

The water pooling inside the cavity has caused rising damp within the besa block wall and damage to the gyprock sheeting in the kitchen attached to the besa block wall. The water leak has also caused damage and mould to the fibro walls in the bathroom behind the tiles.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 302. to prevent water leaking from the shower recess, we advise a building contractor is engaged to remove the floor and first course of wall tiles in the bathroom, replace the damaged fibro wall sheets, install new water proof membrane and retile the bathroom floor and first course of wall tiles.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 8 from unit 10 above.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 8 and found water leaking through the laundry ceiling from unit 10 above.

Gained access into unit 10, inspected the laundry and found water leaking on the floor tiles. Tested all laundry fixtures and no water leaks were found.

Tested pipework in the bathroom and located water leaking from around the hot and cold shower taps inside the wall, causing damage to the wall. Repaired the hot and cold shower taps to stop the leak inside the wall.

Isolated the water supply, carried out pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply for unit 10 and found the common cold water isolation valve to be faulty and the hot water isolation valve on the heater to be leaking. This was causing the pressure tests to fail.

Isolated the buildings cold water supply and replaced the common cold water isolation valve top and the hot water valve on the heater for unit 10.

Turned the buildings water supply back on and carried out extensive pressure testing on the hot and cold water for unit 10.

After extensive pressure testing we located a drop in pressure on the hot and cold water supply.

Laid drop sheets in unit 10, excavated the common wall under the laundry tub to expose the hot and cold water piping. We found there to be a burst pipe on the cold water piping in the common wall under the laundry tub. Cut out burst cold water copper pipework and installed copper pipework and fittings connecting onto existing cold water supply which rectified the leak within the wall.

After testing the hot water we located a 2nd burst common pipe within the concrete slab causing water to leak from out of the slab where the pipework is encased.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 10 and engaged pipe location leak detection. Used pipe locator to trace out the hot water supply, leak detector and listening device to locate the burst hot water pipe to be within the concrete slab between the laundry and bathroom.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to rectify the burst pressurized hot water copper pipe within the concrete slab - We advise to remove the vanity basin, removed affected tiles and excavate the bathroom wall in the shower and behind basin exposing hot water feeds, re-run approximately 30 meters of new hot water copper pipework surface mounted to the external wall connecting the laundry and bathroom, replace damaged tiles matching existing as close as possible to match and re-install existing vanity basin. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak from the bathroom of units 2 and 5.

Gained access to unit 2's bedroom and found it to be riddled with mould.

Used the thermal image camera and moisture meter and found high readings of moisture. We found a large amount of condensation on the window. 

The tenant advised when he moved in 6 months ago it was mould free, but said over the last 3 months it has gone really bad. He said he never opens the window up to ventilate the room. 

The bath tub is adjacent to bedroom. We pressure tested the bath breach which held test. Removed tap flanges and found it to be quite wet inside the hob indicating the taps had been leaking. 

Gained access into unit 5 and found the unit to be in poor condition. We found mould all along celling in bedroom and bathroom. There was no mould on the bedroom wall as she has her window open all the time so it's well ventilated. 

We found the carpet adjacent to shower is all wet. We pressure tested shower breeching piece which passed test.

We found the common shower recess and internal wall tiles to be in poor condition. Dye tested the shower recess and no dye was found to be leaking. As the shower recess and internal shower wall tiles are in poor condition, we advise the shower recess and internal shower wall tiles are excavated, rewater proofed and retiled.

There is water damage to the paint low down on the hallway wall adjacent to shower and also damage low down on laundry wall indicating water is leaking from the internal shower walls and common shower recess. 

There is no shower screen keeping the water in the shower recess and water is leaking straight out the door onto the hallway carpet. 

Attempted to nitrogen test the hot and cold water supply in unit 5 but all taps are leaking and we could not get an accurate pressure test.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken to stop water leaking from unit 5.

1. All taps are required to be serviced in unit 5 by the lot owners plumber.

2. The shower recess and internal shower wall tiles are excavated, re waterproofed and retiled by a building contractor. Please note - The common shower recess has been previously replaced but is in very poor condition. All shower walls are original but are on internal walls.

3. A new shower screen is required to be installed to prevent water leaking out of the bathroom.

4. As there is a large amount of mould on the bedroom and bathroom ceiling, we advise the roof and gutters need to be inspected by the buildings roofing contractor. 

Once these works have been carried out, we advise the carpet outside the bathroom is steam cleaned or replaced by a carpet contractor. 

Also all mould with in the bedroom and the bathroom is cleaned and removed.

Please note - Unit 5 is being kept in very poor condition by the tenant, the unit is extremely unhygienic and there is mould throughout the bathroom and kitchen which looks as if it has never been cleaned (photos attached).

In unit 2, we advise the bath taps are serviced at the lot owners cost.

The window in the bedroom is left open for ventilation and all mould is cleaned off the bedroom ceiling and walls.

Emergency after hours call out on the 23/7/23 - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 20.

Urgently attended the property after hours, inspected unit 20 and found the kitchen sink to be surcharging sewage.

Removed inspection opening lid on the common sewer stack pipe in the driveway below unit 20 and camera surveyed the common sewer line.

Found 2 x sections downstream in the common sewer piping where tree roots are entering the common sewer pipework causing the blockages.

Used CCTV drain camera upstream to find the common sewer pipework to be also blocked with rust and congealed fat.

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and drain camera simultaneously to clear out multiple tree root infestations from the downstream inground sewer piping.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out rust and congealed fat from the upstream stack pipework to the kitchen.

Reinstalled inspection opening lid on the common stack pipe and flow tested all fixtures in unit 20's kitchen - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further common sewer blockages in unit 20 caused by tree root infestations entering the inground common sewer piping, we advise the affected areas of faulty common inground sewer pipework is relined. We will submit an urgent quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 15 from the balcony into the living room.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 15 and found water damage to the flooring in the living room in front of the balcony doors.

Used thermal image camera and moisture meter to located high readings of moisture in the floorboards, skirting and external wall.

Removed water damaged skirting board from the wall to inspect the substrate which was damp.

Used a hose to water test the balcony door frame and balcony tiles adjacent to the water damage.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 15 -  As the water proof membrane on the balcony, balcony door flashings and seals have failed, we advise a building contractor is engaged to inspect the balcony doors and balcony tiles of unit 15 and undertake repairs to rectify the water leak.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

The plumber has recommend we report as it may be a deeper issue with the draining in the building. "
tenant unit 16- Christopher on 0410 448 242

 

W.O. Issued by : Gosia Mcdonald
Email : Frank.Tallaridi@bcssm.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked drains in unit 16.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 16, found the kitchen and laundry waste pipework to be completely blocked.

Disconnected waste pipework under the sink, washing machine from the laundry and attempted to electric eel the pipework but was unsuccessful due to a large amount of solidified grease within the common waste pipework.

Gained access to the garage and located the common sewer pipework connected to unit 16's kitchen and laundry waste fixtures.

Set up a ladder in the carpark, cut a hole in the sewer pipework and CCTV camera surveyed the common sewer line to find it to be completely blocked with grease.

Engaged a second plumber, set up the high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment within the car park.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively and CCTV camera simultaneously to cut through the grease up 2 levels, to the common branch and horizontal pipework for unit 16.

CCTV video links of grease in the line causing the blockage - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NGPR9 & https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NGP9F

Installed kitchen and laundry fixtures in unit 16, ran hot water through the pipework and carried out jet blasting from the garage below. Once the pipework was partially clear we tested everything in unit 16 and advised the resident they could use their kitchen and laundry fixtures.

Returned to the property the following day with 2 plumbers, cut out common sewer pipework in the garage and installed an inspection opening within the pipework to allow further jet blasting.

Used the jet blaster upstream from the inspection opening in the carpark up 2 levels to the common branch line connecting unit 16 clearing out a large amount of grease remaining in the pipework. CCTV camera surveyed after removing the grease to ensure the pipework was all clear and in working order.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place using disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

We advise a notice is sent to all residents advising to not pour oil down the kitchen sinks to prevent common sewer blockages and floods.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the 1st junction upstream from the boundary trap to have tree root infestations entering the original 150mm x 100mm x 45 degree eartanwere junction.

This quotation is to install 150mm x 100mm x 45 degree satellite junction reline repair sealing the tree root infested junction upstream from the boundary trap and install 100m - 150mm sectional pipe relining repair to seal diameter change to stop roots growing between the two pipes.

The following works were undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  3. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Turn of the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Install 150mm x 100mm x 45 degree satellite junction reline repair (complete Y junction) sealing the tree root infested junction upstream from the boundary trap using Felt liner with 2 Part Epoxy Resin.
  3. Install 100m - 150mm sectional pipe relining repair to seal diameter change to stop roots growing between the two pipes, using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
Can you please attend 2 Military Rd, North Bondi.
Unit 3 has a blocked toilet and they have had a plumber investigate, issue is not within unit. Please attend site ASAP to investigate further.
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 3.

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 3, found the toilet to be completely blocked and surcharging raw sewerage.

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer stack outside unit 3 and found the in ground sewer pipework to be blocked.

Set up high pressure jet blaster truck and equipment. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster downstream the sewer stack outside unit 3 to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera and found tree root infestations entering the the original earthenware pipework at the base of the stack which was the cause of the blockage.

Used high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the common sewer line downstream and boundary trap shaft - All clear and no further faults were found.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, flow tested all fixtures in unit 3's bathroom and common sewer line outside - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested pipework further sewer blockages will occur in unit 3's bathroom.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages in unit 3's bathroom - We advise to reline the base of the common sewer stack outside unit 3, sealing all tree root infested and defective earthenware pipework. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further woks required to be undertaken.

Description:
Flooding in basement
please make arrangements to meet with Lisa who has advised of a flooding issue in the basement.

Site Contact Person : Lisa Nicholson - Rep
Phone : +61 410655630
Email : administrator@businessbites.com.au

W.O. Issued by : Frank Tallaridi
Email : Frank.Tallaridi@bcssm.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate flooding in the basement restaurant.

Attended the property, gained access into the basement restaurant and found the drains had previously surcharged and to be partially blocked.

Lifted lids on the sewer pit and pump station in the bin room and found grease, fats and oils to be blocking the pumps and float switches causing them to not operate properly.

Engaged a second plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses down into the basement restaurant.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster upstream from the sewer pit, flushing out the grease from the pipework to the restaurant fixtures.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster to clean the pumps and pump floats removing grease build up causing blockages. 

Tested all fixtures within the basement restaurant and found them to be clear and running to the sewer pit and pump station.

High pressure hosed down the pit and pump station testing the pumps and released the grease and water from the sewer pit.

Whilst we were at the property, Lisa the restaurant owner rang the contractor who cleans the grease arrestor. Our plumber and Lisa both advised the contractor both the sewer pit and grease arrestor pit need to be cleaned out during the regular maintenance to remove grease build up within the 2 x pits.

Cleaned all areas where grease had surcharged using disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following our recent inspection in units 14 & 16, we found the original 100mm cast iron waste pipework connecting unit 16's toilet to be corroded and leaking through the concrete slab which is causing water damage to unit 14's bathroom ceiling.

This quotation is disconnect and remove unit 16's toilet, reline the corroded and leaking common 100mm copper waste pipework from the outlet of unit 16's toilet to the stack junction and re-install existing toilet. 

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Lay drop sheets in unit 16.
  2. Disconnect and remove toilet to access the common waste pipework. Please note, the original toilet is concreted to the floor and when we remove the toilet will break.
  3. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  4. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Install sectional pipe reline downstream from unit 16's toilet waste to the stack junction sealing over leaking. corroded, common 100mm copper waste pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  2. Once cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  3. Re-install existing toilet connecting water and waste.
  4. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  5. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  6. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  7. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Description:
URGENT QUOTATION - Common underground sewer repairs in the garage of unit 43 and driveway area.

Following the recent blockage we attempted to clear from unit 43's garage affecting unit 25 and our CCTV camera survey, we found the common sewer pipework to be collapsed under the garage concrete slab and bitumen driveway.

This quotation is to excavate approximately 2.5 meters of concrete and bitumen in the garage and driveway, expose the collapsed common sewer pipework, cut out and replace the affected piping with new PVC pipe and fittings and use the high pressure water jet blaster downstream to further clear out the blocked common sewer pipework, backfill trench and re-instate concrete and bitumen.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of water disruptions. 
  2. Set up barricades around work area.
  3. Gain access and temporarily remove objects and belongings out of unit 43's garage.
  4. Saw cut and excavate concrete slab in garage 43 and bitumen within the driveway.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 12a.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 5.

Attended the property on the 11/7/23, gained access into unit 5 and found water damage to the timber bulkhead above the shower in the bathroom.

Cut a hole in the bulkhead and found no water leaking at the time of inspection. There are water stains indicating water has leaked previously and the moisture meter indicated high moisture levels.

Gained access into unit 8 above and found the bathroom to be renovated and in good condition.

Flood tested the shower recess and dye tested all bathroom waste piping - No leaks were found.

Pressure tested the shower breaching piece and hot and cold water piping and no drop in pressure was found.

Ran the washing machine on a cycle and found no water to leak into the bathroom ceiling below.

Inspected the wall cavity behind the shower recess and toilet in-wall cistern, found it to be all dry and no signs of water leaking or water damage.

Returned to the property the following day, gained access into units 5 & 8 to carry out further investigation.

Tested all bathroom and laundry fixtures, flood tested all waste piping and we were unable to replicate the water leak into the ceiling cavity of unit 5.

Spoke with the occupants in unit 5 who were unable to advise the actual date of the water leak.

Called the occupants in unit 5 over the next 2 days who advised the water leak has not returned and the timber bulkhead has dried out.

We consider the water leak to be a one off leak, as no water leak was found and the timber bulkhead is dry, no further plumbing works are required to be undertaken at this time. 

We advise the bulkhead is monitored over a 1 month period and if no further water leaks are found, we advise the resultant water damaged bulkhead in unit 5 is repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 5.

Installed a temporary cover over the hole made in the timber bulkhead, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description: It is reported that there is another water leak in the bin room. You did replace faulty RPZ and isolation valves in late June. Please attend asap to investigate this new water leak. Please also check the pumps as there are reports of low water pressure. This has happened in th epast when you have turnd off the water. Previously you have Inspected the carpark and found the cold water pump to be on but not active. Adjusted the pump settings to manual then back to auto to reset the pump and found the water.
Invoice Description:
Attended the property on 2 x separate occasions to inspect the garbage room leak and cold water pressure pumps.

Gained access on the 6/7 into the bin room and found a water stain below the newly installed RPZ valve. Dried up the valve and located a small leak from the pressure vent port.

Gained access into the garage and located pump 1 to be in use and both pumps set to Automatic.

Watched the pumps over a short period and found pump 1 to be actively turning on and off when the buildings cold water pressure drops to 350kpa and then boosts the system to 550kpa.

Returned to the RPZ in the bin room and the leak has not returned.

Returned to the property on the 10/7 and inspected both the bin room and the cold water pumps.

At the time of inspection there was no water stain below the RPZ and the devise was not venting.

Inspected the cold water pumps in the garage and found pump 1 to be in use and constantly running at 550kpa.

Turned pump 1 off and ran pump 2 on manual and found it was unable to boost the water pressure to 550kpa indicating a fault with the pump. We advise pump 2 is urgently replaced.

Reset both pumps and set both to auto - Monitored the pumps over a short period and found both would activate at around 300-350pka and the boost the water pressure up to anywhere around 400-550 kpa causing fluctuations.

Please see video -  https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NGYN8

We found the 2 x cold water pumps are causing fluctuations in the buildings cold water supply, the single stage pumps when turning on are causing an instant spike in pressure, as well as fluctuations as they turn off at all different pressures.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent fluctuations in the buildings we advise a pump contractor is engage to upgrade the cold water supply common cold water pump system and a multistage pump control panel system is installed to drive the pumps constantly to maintain a constant pressure throughout the pipework. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place.

Following the recent blockage we cleared in unit 4 and our CCTV camera survey, we located major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework on the left hand side of the building.

This quotation is to reline approximately 2.5 meters of tree root infested pipework downstream from the common sewer stack outside unit 4's bathroom and also reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested pipework approximately 5 meters downstream on the left hand side of the building.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation 

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.
  3. Record sewer line before relining.

- Relining works

  1. Turn of the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Reline approximately 2.5 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework downstream from the sewer stack outside unit 4's bathroom, sealing all cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  3. Reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested earthenware pipework 5 meters downstream from the sewer stack outside unit 4's bathroom, sealing all cracked pipework using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property.
  7. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

  5. Remove associated rubbish and debris from the property.

Removed inspection opening on the common sewer stack outside unit 4, used CCTV drain camera to locate the common in ground original earthenware sewer pipework to be blocked with major tree root infestations. Laid drop sheets in unit 4 and removed toilet to access the common branch line.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and ran equipment into unit 4's bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera downstream the toilet waste to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original eartanwere branch line under unit 4's bathroom.

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the original eartanwere sewer pipework at the base of the sewer stack outside unit 4's bathroom, tree roots entering the inlet junction connection to the overflow gully next to the stack and tree roots entering approximately 2 meters of earthenware pipework on the main sewer line downstream.

Re-installed toilet sealing to the ground using high grade flexible sealant.

Flow tested toilet and common sewer line outside - All clear and in good working order. Please note - if the tree root infested common earthenware pipework is not repaired, further common sewer blockages will occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to remove affected pavers outside unit 4's bathroom, saw cut and excavate the concrete slab, ground, cut out tree root infested earthenware pipework at the base of the stack, overflow gully, install new PVC pipework, fittings, gully and inspection opening raised to the surface in preparation for relining. Reline approximately 3 meters of tree root infested pipework downstream from unit 4's toilet using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin and also reline approximately 2 meters of tree root infested pipework on the main line using watermarked approved liner with a 2 Part Epoxy resin, back fill trench, re-instate concrete and pavers. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Investigate leaking common gas piping.

Attended the property, gained access to the rear of the building where the common gas meters are located and found Jemena had isolated the gas to unit 5’s meter.

We also found non-compliance certificates stating the outlet gas supply for units 1,4,8,9 & 10 needs to be rectified within 7 days.

Excavated and exposed the pipework for unit 5 in the ground and found a large hole in the galvanised pipework due to corrosion, which was causing the leak.

We made contact with unit 5, who advised they do not have gas appliances and there is no need for their gas to be connected. We installed a cap on the outlet of the meter and isolated the gas supply so it cannot be turned on.

Walked around the building and attempted to gain access underneath from the garages to locate where the galvanised gas pipework runs to each unit. Following our inspection, we concluded there is no access under the building.

Left access request notes with the affected units in order to carry out further testing.

Returned to the property, gained access to unit 1,4,9 & 10 and used bubble leak spray and gas detector on the exposed pipework within the units, under the cooktop and bayonet connection. No gas leaks were found to be internal.

Please note, at the time of inspection and testing we were unable to gain access into unit 8 to test the gas appliances within the unit, after not being able to contact unit 8 several times, we have left unit 8's gas supply off for safety reasons and left a note on the door advising to contact Treat plumbing. Once we are able to gain access into unit 8, we will provide a quotation for gas repair works to reinstate the gas supply to unit 8.

Turned off the gas supply at the meter to units 1,4,9 & 10 and isolated the gas supply at the appliances within each unit.

Performed a pressure test on the gas piping and located a drop in pressure on units 8 & 10 only. All other units held test.

Inspected the condition of unit 10's gas outlet pipework and found the original common galvanised steel pipework to be corroded and leaking is required to be upgraded and replaced with new copper piping and fittings.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 10 - To rectify the gas leak, we advise to re-run a new copper gas service from the outlet of unit 10's gas meter approximately 12 meters in length connecting unit 10's gas cook top. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

1 As Inspected: *** The following opinions are based only on visual inspection.
1 1. The external damage appears to be only on decorative add-ons which have no structural, nor water proofing value. The resident reported that these are damaged by birds picking on them. A)We do not have facilities to access them close-up. B)It is doubtful the damage of these items would be causing leaks into the building.
1 2. We walked all around the unit with the resident and there is no visible evidence of mould.
1 3. Visual inspection of the balcony by the bedroom does not show evidence of any cracked / broken tiles and no evidence of any significant cement-set grout deterioration, however moisture level  readings are higher near the doorway than elsewhere. The unit (possibly all the units) suffers the common design / build fault of the balcony floors being level or higher than the interior floors and to
compensate the builders have allowed significant fall to the centre drain. The drain appears full size (around 80mm) on the floor waste however the actual outlet is only around 30-40mm. If this outlet or pipework below it are blocked or hindered, flooding of the balcony will occur during freak deluge storms. The current moisture readings at the damaged timber floor are low, which could indicate that it's been some time since any significant water ingress. Other typical ingress points may be the sliding door seal / flashing / drain / possible rusted lower channel, the floor / membrane (if any) of the balcony which is located directly above the damaged area of u70, or even the roof / guttering. 
None of these can be established without physical destructive works and flood testing, bearing in mind that no amount of flood testing can emulate the conditions which occur during storms of deluge proportions.
1 4. The gap on the balcony by the living room is a construction / expansion joint, which appears to be void by the sealant being weather damaged or physically removed. It should be attended.
1 Note: It would be a good idea to have your plumbers inspect the floorwaste drain for blockages and install suitable lid/grate.
1 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 To patch repair, fill, stain, lacquer, paint, as applicable the moisture damaged areas along the sliding door area wall and floor skirtings in the bedroom.
1 To water test and clear as accessible the bedroom sliding door frame drain track and apply a transluscent sealant to the external interface of the door frame to the wall.
1 To fill the void construction joint on the balcony floor by the living room balcony with polyurethane adhesive sealant.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared and our CCTV camera survey we located tree root infestations entering the 150mm earthenware boundary trap and outlet pipework to Sydney Waters main sewer connection.

This quotation is to carefully remove tiles and dig down to vertical shaft inspection opening under pavers to gain access into the vertical pipe leading to the Sydney waters boards main sewer, reline approximately 6 meters of 150mm root infested earthenware pipework from PVC section on boundary trap shaft downstream to vertical shaft down to boards main sewer connection, backfill trench and reinstate existing tiles. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of building water shut down whilst the relining works are undertaken.
  2. Gain access into unit 2.
  3. Carefully remove tiles and dig down to vertical shaft inspection opening under pavers to gain access into the vertical pipe leading to the boards main sewer.
  4. Clean line using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining. 
  5. Inspect line using CCTV camera.
  6. Shut down the buildings water supply and drain the water from the line.
  7. Reline approximately 6 meters of 150mm root infested earthenware pipework from PVC section on boundary trap shaft to vertical shaft down to boards main sewer connection.
  8. Inspect line using CCTV camera and record all findings onto USB.
  9. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  10. Bed pipework, backfill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500.
  11. Re-install existing tiles.
  12. Clean all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property. 
  13. All relining will be undertaken as per Australian Relining Standards AS-3500.
  14. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation of the relining works undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in units 37A & 38A.

Urgently attended the property, found the carpet in the common hallway outside unit 38A to be water damaged.

Gained access into unit 38A, pressure tested hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found. Flood dye tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Gained access into unit 37A found major water damage to the bedroom carpet.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure test on the hot and cold water supply. Following pressure testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe within unit 37A.

Used pipe locating and leak detection equipment to pin point the burst hot water pipe to be behind the kitchen service riser and cabinetry.

Laid drop sheets in unit 37A, excavated, removed riser panel and tiles locating burst pressurized common 25mm hot water copper pipework.

Urgently shut down the buildings hot water supply and drained the water from the line. Cut out burst pressurized 25mm hot water copper pipework and installed new section of 25mm copper pipework and fittings connecting onto existing hot water supply.

Turned on the buildings hot water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 37A - We advise the resultant water damaged kitchen service riser and tiles are repaired. We will submit a quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 37A.

We also advise a carpet contractor is engaged to steam clean the water damaged carpet in unit 38A's bedroom and common hallway outside unit 37A.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 4.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 4 and found water damage to the timber bulkhead in the bathroom.

Attempted to remove the bulkhead which caused it to collapse from the water damage and break the light cover on the wall.

Inspected inside the ceiling cavity and located water leaking around the floor waste and basin waste penetration from unit 7 above.  

Gained access into unit 7 and found the bathroom to be renovated.

Pulled out the washing machine and located water on the floor tiles under the machine.

Located a leak on the hot water connection to the wall tap. Tightened the hot water connection to stop the leak and dried the floor.

Dye tested the shower recess with red dye and the bathroom floor tiles with green dye.

Following dye testing, we found green dye immediately leaked from the bathroom floor tiles through the floor waste penetration into unit 4's ceiling below indicating faulty waterproof membrane in the bathroom of unit 7.

As the bathroom in unit 7 has been renovated, we advise the owner engages the building contractor who renovated the bathroom and undertake repairs to rectify the faulty waterproof membrane.

Once the waterproofing repairs have been rectified, we advise the bulkhead in unit 4's bathroom is replaced. We will submit a quotation for the bulkhead repairs and painting required to be undertaken in unit 4.

Screwed back timber bulkhead and secured it to the frame, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 3.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 3 and found the toilet to be completely blocked. Used drain cleaning equipment downstream from the toilet but we were unable to clear the blockage.

Gained access under the building, removed inspection opening lids and found the common sewer line to be completely blocked.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

We also found a hole in the side of the plastic inspection opening under the building where tree roots are entering the pipework.

Flow tested toilet in unit 3 and common sewer line which is currently clear and getting away. Please note - if repairs are not undertaken to the common sewer line, the tree roots will grow back and further common sewer blockages will occur,

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to prevent further common sewer blockages - We advise to reline approximately 12 meters of tree root infested original earthenware sewer pipework downstream from the inspection opening under the building, cut out and replaced broken inspection opening lid and replace with new inspection located under the building. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Investigate water damage to the living room wall adjacent to the main bathroom.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to 7,9,11 & 13 and inspected the irrigation pipework within the external garden areas and carparks.

Found mostly all of the irrigation pipework within the garden beds to broken, disconnected, open ended and not in working order.

Walked around the property and traced the irrigation garden pipework back to the water source which is located at the back, the front of each building and the carpark.

Dug around the garden in multiple locations to find the solenoid valves and pipework to be faulty and require replacement.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access, traced the water source back to the control panels located in the carpark and tested the water supply.

Turned on the water supply to work out whether the pipework was in good working order or needs repair / replacement.

Following our investigation works, we contacted our irrigation specialist and met with him at the building, to advise on further works required once the water source had been rectified to each garden.

Returned to the property and met with our irrigation specialist. After inspecting the garden irrigation pipework and the controls in the carpark, he advised new solenoid valves need to be installed in the gardens and a 'turn on repair method' should be used in the gardens to repair and connect the damaged irrigation pipework.

Further works required to be undertaken by Treat Plumbing - We advise the potable water pipework form the carpark to the external gardens is restored, new isolation valves and irrigation boxes are installed within the gardens and the pipework is turned on to the valves. We will provide a quotation shortly for the further works required by Treat Plumbing to install new isolation valves, irrigation boxes and reinstate the irrigation pipework to the external gardens.

Once the potable water source is restored to the garden valves, we advise the buildings irrigation contractor is engaged to install new solenoid valves and repair and connect all damaged irrigation pipework in the garden areas and commission the pipework, solenoids and controls so the irrigation around the buildings are self sufficient.

Description:
Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer pipework

This quotation is to reline approximately 12 meters of 150mm root infested earthenware pipe using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin from the boundary trap to Sydney Waters side entry main.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations and debris in preparation for relining. 
  3. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  4. Reline approximately 12 meters of 150mm root infested earthenware pipe using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin from the boundary trap to Sydney Waters side entry main.
  5. Reinstate junction using IMS robotic cutter.
  6. Once the liner has cured, remove the relining equipment from the common sewer pipework. 
  7. Inspect line using CCTV camera and record all findings onto USB.
  8. Turn on the buildings cold water supply and flow test all works carried out. 
  9. Leave work clean and tidy.
  10. Provide CCTV video of the relining works undertaken to the owners corporation.

  8. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  9. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

  1. Use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the outlet pipework in preparation for relining.
