Common waterproof flood testing in units 503,502 & 202.

Attended the property, gained access into units 102,202,402,403,404,502 & 503, inspected the balcony, bathrooms, laundry and ceiling cavity where water damage appears.

Carried out flood testing to the waterproof membrane in units 503, 502 & 202.

Carried out inspections of the water damaged ceilings in units 102, 402 & 403.

After extensive flood testing of the balconies, bathrooms and laundry floor tiles we found:

  • Unit 503

Main bathroom flood test - Flood tested the main bathroom floor tiles and found water had leaked out the doorway caused by insufficient fall in the floor tiles, water also leaked under the tile bed and waterproof membrane into unit 403's ceiling causing water damage to the gyprock ceiling in the hallway.

Repair recommendations - As the bathroom floor tiles have insufficient fall causing water to flow away from the drain and outside the bathroom door and water is leaking into unit 403's ceiling from faulty waterproof membrane  - We advise the bathroom floor tiles, tile bed and waterproof membrane is excavated and new waterproof membrane, sand cement bed and tiles are installed with correct fall to the bathroom floor drain. We will submit a quotation shortly for the works required to re-waterproof and tile the bathroom floors in unit 503.

Ensuite bathroom flood test - Flood tested the ensuite bathroom and found water had leaked under the tile bed and waterproof membrane causing wet carpet in the hallway. We also found water damage to the bathroom ceiling of 403 directly below 503's ensuite bathroom floor waste penetration.

Repair recommendations - As water is leaking under the bathroom floor tiles and waterproof membrane causing wet carpet in the hallway outside the bathroom door - We advise the bathroom floor tiles, tile bed and waterproof membrane is excavated and new waterproof membrane, sand cement bed and tiles are installed with correct fall to the bathroom floor drain. We will submit a quotation shortly for the works required to re-waterproof and tile the bathroom floors in unit 503.

Balcony flood test - Tested the balcony and found no water to leak whilst at the property. There is a large amount of water damage to the gyprock ceiling in the bedroom of unit 404 below the balcony, the water damage appears to be entering unit 404's ceiling cavity from along the concrete beam where the door frame and tile joint is located in unit 503's balcony above.

Following extensive flood testing of the balcony in 503 no water was found to be leaking into unit 404's bedroom, we consider during heavy rain and wind there is water leaking either from the balcony sliding doors and flashings or the balcony floor tiles and grouting, causing water damage to the ceilings in unit 404 below. We advise a building contractor is engaged by strata to excavate the balcony floor tiles, tile bed and waterproof membrane, install new waterproof membrane, sand cement bed and tiles are installed with fall to the drains. 

Laundry flood test - Tested laundry and found no water to leak through into unit 403 whilst at the property.

Kitchen leak - Found wet carpet in the kitchen / living room adjacent to the benchtop and sink. Inspected under the cabinetry and found a small drip on the water tap from the dishwasher after it had been disconnected. Installed a cap onto the tap to stop the water leak.

  • Unit 403.

-Following our inspection in unit 403, we found mould growth within the laundry gyprock ceiling which is caused by moisture and poor ventilation in the laundry when the dryer is being used.

Repair recommendations - To prevent mould growth in unit 403's laundry ceiling, we advise the buildings mechanical exhaust contractor is engaged to repair the affected mechanical venting in the laundry to improve airflow and reduce moisture in the laundry when the dryer is used.

  • Unit 502 

Flood tested main bathroom, ensuite bathroom and laundry no leaks were found in unit 402. 

We found a number of the balcony floor tiles in unit 502 to be cracked and also missing grout which is causing water to leak below the tiles and into the tile bed. 

There is a large crack within the concrete slab below the balcony and water has previously leaked through the crack causing damage to the bedroom ceiling in unit 402.

Following extensive flood testing in the main and ensuite bathrooms and laundry in unit 502, no water was found to be leaking into unit 402. 

Repair recommendations - As a number of the balcony floor tiles are cracked which is causing water to penetrate the concrete slab into unit 402's bedroom, We advise a building contractor is engaged by strata to gain access to unit 502 to excavate the balcony floor tiles, tile bed and waterproof membrane, install new waterproof membrane, sand cement bed and tiles are installed with correct fall to the drains.

  • Unit 202

Balcony flood test -  Carried out extensive flood testing to the balcony floor tiles within unit 202's balcony and no leaks were found in unit 102 whilst we were at the property.

The concrete expansion joint within the balcony floor tiles is faulty where the sealant is worn and cracked allowing water to leak through the sealant into concrete slab expansion joint.

Inspected the bedroom ceiling cavity in unit 102 below the balcony and found a large crack within the concrete slab where water is leaking and causing damage to the gyprock.

Repair recommendations - We consider the water leak in unit 102's bedroom to be caused by faulty water proof membrane under the balcony floor tiles and tile bed, We advise a building contractor is engaged by strata to gain access to unit 202 to excavate the balcony floor tiles, tile bed and waterproof membrane, install new waterproof membrane, sand cement bed and tiles are installed with correct fall to the drains.

Flood tested the main and ensuite bathrooms and laundry in unit 202 and no leaks were found in unit 102.

  • All units

To prevent water leaking under the tile bed in 6 of the lots, we advise to re-seal the the shower recess, bath edge where it meets the wall tiles and perimeter of the bathroom and laundry floor tiles. We will submit a quotation shortly for the re-sealing works required to be undertaken in the 2 x bathrooms and laundry.

To prevent mould growth, poor air quality and high levels of moisture in the laundry and bathrooms, we advise a mechanical air contractor is engaged to clean and maintain the buildings common exhaust system.

Description:
Urgent quotation - Common sewer repairs located in the driveway & right rear of the building

Following the recent common sewer blockage we cleared our CCTV camera survey, we located the common 150mm earthenware boundary trap in the driveway to be collapsed, blocked with sand and debris. We also found the common earthenware over flow gully outside unit 1 at the rear right of the building to be collapsed, cracked causing sand and debris to enter the sewer pipework.

This urgent quotation is to reline from top of boundary trap down around to vertical shaft before Sydney Water main,  reinstate 1 x junction using robotic cutter and reline vertical shaft from newly installed liner down to Sydney water main located within the driveway. Also to saw cut and excavate the concrete and ground located at the right rear of the building, cut out collapsed and cracked earthenware overflow gully, associated pipework, install new PVC piping, fittings, overflow gully, flow test all works, back fill trench and re-instate concrete. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of water building water shut down.
  2. Advise residents of driveway closure whilst undertaking the relining works.
  3. Barricade around work area in the driveway.
  4. Clear lines using high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera in preparation for relining.
  5. Use mechanical milling equipment to prepare lines to AS-3500 and record footage of lines before relining.
  6. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  7. Reline from top of boundary trap down around to vertical shaft before Sydney Water main using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin.
  8. Reinstate 1 x junction using robotic cutter.
  9. Reline vertical shaft from newly installed liner down to Sydney water main using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin. This repair is recommended to ensure the pipework cannot move any further and cause blockages.
  10. Turn on the buildings cold water supply, flow test all relining works undertaken.
  11. Provide CCTV video to the owners corporation for the relining works undertaken.
  12. Barricade work area located at the rear rear of the building 
  13. Remove old hot water heater to the side before excavation works takes place.
  14. Saw cut the concrete, excavate the concrete and ground exposing collapsed and cracked earthenware overflow gully and pipework.
  15. Cut out collapsed earthenware sewer pipework, fittings and overflow gully.
  16. Supply and install new PVC piping, fittings and overflow gully.
  17. Flow test all works carried out.
  18. Bed pipework, back fill trench and compact ground as per AS-3500.
  19. Install rio bars and steel in preparation for concreting.
  20. Re-concrete affected area.
  21. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.
  22. Once the concreted has cured, return to the property and clean all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

PLEASE NOTE - We highly recommend epoxy resin over Silicate resin due to the high volume of tree roots in the pipework. (We only Use Epoxy Resin).  All work is completed strictly to the Australian code of practice AS3500.  Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty, a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer and with a free annual inspection the duration of the guarantee. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Please attend to the reported blocked drain in Unit 5 of which a bad smell is coming from.

**Please contact Annie -
0407 363 139 for access.
Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access to unit 5 and located a sewer smell in the bathroom.

Inspected and tested the common sewer drain by flood testing using the bath and no surcharging was found.

Removed inspection opening lids on the external soil stack and used CCTV camera to survey the main sewer line and no blockages were found.

We found leaking sewerage at the base of the external soil stack adjacent to the building entrance door, we found the common PVC connection into the in ground sewer drainage is faulty causing the sewer leak. The pavers need to be removed, the ground excavated and the sewer pipework repaired and connected to the common external stack pipe. We have sealed the pipework with a temporary sealant to temporarily stop sewerage leaking at the entrance.

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify the sewer leak we advise to excavate the pavers and soil, cut out a section of drainage and connect the pipework, re-instating the ground and pavers at the front entrance door. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Investigated the crawl space under the bathroom and found there to be no access to the bathroom drainage pipes.

Under the floor space, we located an open ended drainage pipe which is connected to the kitchen sink waste and leaking down into the subsoil. Repaired the common pipework sealing the connection with sand cement.

After flood testing the bath we identified the floor waste piping in the bathroom to be dry. Flood tested the waste piping for the bath which charges the floor waste and found the common floor waste to be leaking and not holding water as it should.

CCTV camera surveyed the common floor waste pipework and found a crack within the gully causing the gully to loose its water and stay dry.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken -  As the original common earthenware sewer gully is cracked under the bathroom floor of unit 5 and there is no access, we advise the faulty common earthenware floor waste gully is relined. We will submit an urgent quotation for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked storm water in the driveway.

Attended the property, found the common storm water pit to be blocked and the pump to no be in working order.

Removed pit lid, cleaned out a large amount of dirt and debris from the common storm water pit.

Remove submersible pump and cleaned out dirt from propellers and serviced pump.

Re-installed, pump and tested - Following testing we found the pump to be in working order but the pump out line to be completely blocked.

Set up high pressure jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively but we were unable to clear the blockage and our jet blasting was getting stuck within the pipework.

Cut out pump out line at the front of the property, used CCTV drain camera and found the common storm water pipework to be completely crushed and requires urgent repairs.  CCTV video link of crushed common storm water pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NRYZA

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise to re run new PVC pump out line approximately 10 meters and delete squashed pipework under the tree. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 909's balcony.

Attended the property, gained access to unit 909's balcony and found water had leaked from the balcony ceiling where it joins to the beam.

Gained access onto the roof and inspected the small ledge and parapet wall on the other side of the glass balustrade above the concrete balcony roof.

There are some cracks in the parapet wall render and faulty seals which could be allowing water to leak into the concrete substrate.

We also found bubbles in the torch on waterproof membrane where water has leaked under the membrane.

The concrete slab roof falls to one side causing a pool of water in the corner which does not fall to the surface drain.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise a builder and waterproofing contractor are engaged to gain access to the small roof above unit 909's balcony and carry out repairs to the render and affected torch on waterproofing membrane.

Access onto the small roof ledge required a harness to inspect the failed waterproof membrane.

Cleaned all areas where wok has taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in the hair salon.

Attended the property, gained access to the hair salon and found water had leaked in the same location as the previous leak.

At the time we attended the ceiling was dry and there were no water leaks. The hair salon owner advised the leak only occurs during heavy rain events.

Gained access into the buildings common laundry and store room above the leak and found damp cardboard above the area.

Above the leak is the buildings common service riser with stormwater, sewer, electrical and cold water which go up each level to the roof, 8 levels.

Gained access onto the roof and used the hose to flood test the stormwater downpipe, roof drain and sewer vent.

During the water test, we inspected all previous plumbing repairs, altered stormwater drainage and sewer pipes within the common service riser outside unit 1C and within the laundry store room - No leaks were found to be coming from the previous repair works.

After flood testing the roof top for 3 hours, we eventually found water leaking from an electrical conduit within the concrete slab between the laundry store room and unit 1C, we were unable to pin point the location of where the water is entering the conduit and found it to be coming from the roof water testing.

Please see attached videos of water leaking from the electrical conduit - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NRBKT

                                                                                                                 - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NRRH3

Further works required to be undertaken - As the water leak occurs during heavy rain events, we advise an electrician is engaged by strata to locate the electrical conduits outside unit 1C and a roofing contractor is engaged by strata to inspect the buildings roof, waterproof membrane and flashings around the sewer and stormwater drains above the 103 service riser and carry out repairs to stop the external water leak.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate common sewer blockage at the rear of the building.

Attended the property, found the common sewer line to be blocked, sewerage and sand to be surcharging out of the boundary trap located at the rear of the building.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and drain cleaning equipment extensively but we were unable to clear the blockage and our jet blasting equipment was getting stuck at the base of the boundary trap.

Used venturi pump to pump out the sewerage from the base of the boundary trap and common sewer line.

Once we had pumped out the sewerage and sand, used CCTV drain camera to locate the base of boundary trap to be collapsed causing sand and major tree root infestations to enter the pipework. 

CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-NRBT1

Flow tested common sewer line which is currently clear and getting away. Please note, if urgent repairs are not undertaken further sewer blockages will occur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the collapsed and tree root infested boundary trap is excavated and replaced with new 150mm PVC pipework and fittings. Also to reline the tree root infested earthenware outlet pipework downstream to Sydney waters main completely sealing the pipe to prevent further common sewer blockages. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the repairs required to be undertaken.

Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 11.

Urgently attended the property on the 25/5/23, gained access into unit 11, found all waste fixtures in the main and en-suite bathroom to be blocked and flooding out of the floor waste causing water damage to the carpet in the bedroom.

Quotation - Relining works on the common sewer line

Following the recent sewer blockage we cleared causing sewerage to flood in unit 2's bathroom and our CCTV camera survey, we found tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework on the right hand side of the building which was the cause of the blockage. We also found the junction to be collapsed on the main boundary trap shaft.

This quotation is to install a 2 meter sectional reline on the main earthenware sewer line sealing over tree root infested section of pipework using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin. Also to install 1 x 150mm x 150mm x 85 degree satellite junction repair (complete Y piece) on the boundary trap shaft using felt liner with 2 part epoxy resin.

The following works will be undertaken:

- Preparation:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line in preparation for relining.

- Relining:

  1. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  2. Install a 2 meter sectional pipe reline on the main earthenware sewer line sealing over tree root infested section of pipework using a watermarked approved liner with a 2 part epoxy resin
  3. Install 1 x 150mm x 150mm x 85 degree satellite junction repair on the boundary trap shaft (complete Y piece) using felt liner with 2 part epoxy resin.
  4. Turn on the buildings water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  5. CCTV record footage of both relines and provide to owners corporation. 
  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  7. Remove asscoiated rubbish from the property.
  8. All works to be undertaken as per AS/NZS3500 standards.
  9. Remove associated rubbish from the property. 

PLEASE NOTE - Our products come with with a 25 year Workmanship warranty and a product life expectancy of 50 years guaranteed by the manufacturer. We only use Epoxy products which have been tried and tested for the duration of our workmanship warranty.

Investigate no hot water at the property.

We found 1x rennai 200i flashing 10 - Blocked flue and 1 x rennai flashing 11- gas supply. Re-set heaters at the power supply and found the same faults. 

Inspected flue system and found the outlet at the wall in the driveway was mechanically sucking in air not expelling air. 

Removed flues at the top of the heaters and found air pushing back into the heaters. 

Checked gas supply on the heater faulting gas and found there to be sufficient gas supply to the heater. 

We looked around the hot water plant room and found the mechanical vent in use. Pulled power supply to the mechanical vent to stop it from working and found this to eliminate the flue sucking air backwards. 

Tried running the rennai with no flue connected but found the same faults - Blocked flue 

As the building has no hot water, we advise Rennai or a hot water service contractor is urgently engaged to inspect the hot water heaters and carry out repairs. 

In conjunction, we advise a mechanical air contractor is engaged to inspect the mechanical vent and advise why this is connected to the hot water heater flues and why the flues have air pushing back down towards the heaters. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty tree root infested common sewer pipework is relined to prevent further sewer blockages within the common sewer pipework. We will submit a quotation shortly for the urgent relining works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent common sewer blockage.

Urgently attended the property on the 15/6/23, found the common sewer line to be blocked and flooding sewerage when in use.

Removed inspection opening lid on the main boundary trap located at the rear of the property and found the boundary trap to be completely blocked with tree root infestations.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively downstream from the boundary trap to clear out a large amount of tree root infestations entering the deep boundary trap and outlet pipework to Sydney Waters main (boundary trap 4 meters deep).

Once we had cleared and released the common sewer line, we then used CCTV drain camera to locate multiple areas tree root infestations also entering the original earthenware sewer line outside unit 1's courtyard on the right hand side of the property and outside unit 2's courtyard on the left hand side of the building.

Returned to the property the following day on the 16/5/23, used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out major tree root infestations entering the common earthenware sewer line outside unit 1 on the right hand side of the building outside unit 2 on the left hand side of the building.

Flow tested common sewer line on the left, right and to the rear boundary trap - All clear and in good working order. Please note, if repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested common sewer pipework further sewer blockages and floods will reoccur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify further blockages, we advise the tree root infested boundary trap & outlet pipework to Sydney Waters main is relined. We also advise the tree root infested original earthenware pipework is relined outside units 1 and 2 completely sealing the line using watermarked approved liner with a 2 part Epoxy resin. We will submit a quotation shortly once we have reviewed the relining works with our relining team.

If the owners corporation does not have the funds to undertake the reline sewer repair works, we advise the tree root infestations are cleared out of the common sewer line on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months to prevent common sewer blockages. We will submit a separate quotation shortly to undertake preventative maintenance clear out works.

Following our inspection at the property, we gained access to the lower level hot water plant room, the gas meter room and the roof space to inspect the common hot and cold water supply and gas meters. We also camera surveyed the common stormwater pipework from the lower ground courtyard and the common sewer pipework at the left and right sides, inspecting the common pipework which runs to Craigend street.

- Lower level hot water plant room and cold water pressure pump:

  • 2 x  Rheem 260 Litre hot water tanks installed 2004 & 2015 and no service history.  
  • Hot water plant isolation vales are original gate valves, do not work and require replacement.
  • Gas isolation valves located on the 2 x hot water heaters do not work and require replacement.
  • 2 x TPR valve for hot water heaters are in good working order.
  • 1 x Hot water circulating pump connected to the flow and return hot water pipework.
  • 2 x Asbestos flues have been replaced with metal flues.
  • Hot water pressure pump in good working order.

Recommendations - We advise the 2 x common hot water heaters (dated 2004 & 2015) are replaced with new 260L Rheem heavy duty gas hot water heaters and the faulty water and gas valves, circulating pump and associated pipework is cut out and replaced. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

- Gas meter room located at the top of the Craigend street stairs off lower courtyard:

  • Gas meter connections are galvanized steel, all other gas pipework is copper.
  • 14 x Gas meters have no meter bars and are hanging by pipework.
  • Bubble leak sprayed manifold and no gas leaks were found within the gas meter room.
  • The gas meter set up currently does not comply with AS 3500 plumbing codes. 

Recommendations - We advise the gas meters are mounted to the external wall using meter bars and the galvanized steel inlet and outlet pipework is cut out and replaced with new copper pipework and fittings to comply with Australian plumbing codes. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

- Roof space:

  • Found 2 x old asbestos water tanks in the roof space not in use.
  • Original screw gauge copper cold water supply pipe runs up the building into the roof space then runs down the building to unit fixtures.
  • Water hammer within the cold water pipework in the roof space which makes a noise when the cold water pressure pump kicks in and when plumbing fixtures are being used.

Recommendations - We advise the loose hot and cold water pipework within the roof space is clipped to the battens using brackets and fixings to prevent water hammer noises at the property. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required within the roof space.

We advise strata engages an asbestos contractor to remove the 2 x asbestos water tanks from the common roof space.

Common Storm water from courtyard.

  • CCTV camera surveyed PVC storm water from kerb and gutter on Craigend street and found piping to be in good working order - No faults were found.
  • CCTV camera surveyed surface drain in the courtyard and found to be in good working order - No faults were found.
  • CCTV camera surveyed earthenware surface drain located at the top of stairs at the Craigend Street entrance, upstream to downpipe was clear and in good working order. Downstream from the surface drain approximately 2 meters we found a small break in the pipework. Further down, we found the pipework to be blocked and could not use the CCTV camera to survey the stormwater pipework which runs from the stair surface drain into the garages then to Craigend Street.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the original earthenware stormwater pipework is cleared out using the high pressure water jet blaster from the surface drain at the top of the stairs to the street, access into the garages is required. Once the stormwater pipework is clear and the condition of the original pipework is known, we will provide a quotation to rectify the pipework to prevent stormwater blockages. 

- Common Sewer left and right side of the building and under the garage floor.

  • Right side sewer stack pipes have been replaced with PVC pipe and fittings.
  • Left side sewer stack pipes are original cast iron.
  • CCTV camera surveyed the sewer drainage and found the pipework to be original earthenware with multiple areas where tree root infestations are entering the pipework. 
  • Boundary trap is located in the council footpath on Craigend Street.
  • CCTV camera surveyed boundary trap and vertical shaft which has previously been re-lined to Sydney water main. The relining works previously undertaken a long time ago is warping, in very bad condition and hasn’t bonded with earthenware piping. Tree root infestations are entering the pipework and boundary trap and to prevent further blockages relining repairs will be required. 

Recommendations -  We found tree root infestations in the main common sewer line that is required to be cleared out using the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera. Once we have undertaken clear out works we can provide a quotation to reline the main common sewer line to prevent further blockages reoccurring. We will submit a quotation for the sewer and storm water clear out works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Urgent Quotation - Replace cracked shower breaching piece within the common shower wall in unit 3

Attended to unit 3 to service the hot and cold shower taps to stop the shower from leaking, within the common wall and found a large crack on the cold water side of the shower breeching piece causing the tap to not close the water off. 

This quotation is to excavate the common shower wall around the shower breaching piece, cut out the faulty breeching piece, copper pipe and fittings within the common wall, replace breaching piece, render and re-tile the common shower wall in unit 3.

The main cold water isolation valve for unit 3 does not isolate the water supply and is also required to be replaced.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down
  2. Gain access into unit 3 and lay drop sheets in the bathroom.
  3. Isolate the buildings cold water supply and replace main isolation valve with new top assembly.
  4. Turn on the buildings cold water supply and test all works carried out.
  5. Isolate the hot and cold water supply to unit 3.
  6. Excavate the common shower tiles and wall to expose the faulty breaching piece.
  7. Cut out faulty breaching piece and install new breaching piece, copper pipe and fittings.
  8. Turn the water supply back on testing all works.
  9. Patch render the common shower wall in preparation for tiling.
  10. Install primer and 2 coats of waterproof membrane.
  11. Re tile the common shower wall with wall tiles as close as possible to match.
  12. Grout wall tiles using additive.
  13. Clean all areas where work has taken place.
  14. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked storm water at the rear courtyard.

Attended the property, gained access to the courtyard at the back of the building and found the storm water drainage connecting 2 x downpipes to be completely blocked.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure jet blaster truck and ran equipment to the rear courtyard.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively to clear out dirt and debris from the main storm water line.

We used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream from the 2 x downpipes to find major tree root infestations entering the base of the downpipes causing the blockages.

Following extensive jet blasting works we were only able to clear 1 of the downpipes and the main storm water line, but the base of the 2nd downpipe near the laundry is completely collapsed and we were unable to get our small puncher head on the jet blaster through the collapsed section of pipework.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - We advise to saw cut and excavate the pavers, excavate the concrete and ground, cut out collapsed earthenware storm water pipework, install new PVC pipework, fittings, backfill trench and re-instate concrete and pavers. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked sewer in units 5 & 6.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 5 and found all bathroom waste fixtures to be blocked and holding sewerage.

Investigated unit 6 courtyard where the common sewer is located, opened sewer lids and found the main sewer to be blocked and holding sewerage.

Flow tested common sewer pipework and boundary trap - All clear and in good working order.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent sewer blockages reoccurring, we advise the tree root infested boundary trap and outlet pipework to the main is relined. We will submit a quotation for the relining works once we have reviewed the job with our relining team.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leaking into unit 1302.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1302 and found water damage to the kitchen flooring adjacent to the bathroom and island bench.

Found water damage to the gyprock ceiling in the downstairs bathroom below the laundry, cut 2 x holes in the ceiling to inspect the air-condition drainage and no leaks where found.

Lifted one floor board in the kitchen adjacent to the bathroom door and found the concrete slab to be dry. Inspected the island bench kickboards and dishwasher - all dry

Tested all fixtures in the downstairs bathroom and no leaks where found.

Tested all fixtures in the upstairs main bathroom and no leaks were found. Installed sealant behind the shower taps.

Found water damage to the gyprock ceiling and wall in the upstairs laundry which is above the downstairs bathroom and corner to the kitchen.

Inspected inside the roof cavity in the laundry and found the box gutter or common stormwater drainage pipework. Flood tested roof and flashing above and no leaks where found.

Installed waterproof membrane over the affected areas of roof flashings above the leak.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 1302 and used thermal image camera within the unit.

Identified high readings of moisture and water damage in the laundry ceiling upstairs. 

Removed access manhole cover in the laundry and inspected inside the ceiling cavity. Found traces of water leaks below the concrete beam and roof / courtyard wall flashings.

Inspected the roof courtyard , wall / roof flashings and vent shaft above the affected area.

Returned to the property, cleaned all affected areas and installed high grade sealant and water proof membrane over the affected areas of wall joints, roof flashings and vent shaft.

Returned to the property once the waterproofing had dried, supplied and installed a metal flashing over the vent shaft to seal the wall joint adjacent to the laundry of unit 1302.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further work required to be undertaken - We advise unit 1302 is monitored during heavy rain events to see if any further water leaks occur.

Invoice Description:
Investigate 2 x blocked drains in the lower car park.

Remove pit lid grate and found the submersible pump to be faulty and not in working order. Disconnected the pump, found the base of the pump to be completely rusted out and requires urgent replacement. 

Used CCTV drain camera and found the common storm water outlet pipework to be completely blocked with dirt and debris between the 2 x common storm water pits.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access into the car park, isolated the power supply and disconnected the faulty submersible pump. 

Cleaned out dirt and debris from the base of the common storm water pit. 

Supplied and installed new submissible pump, non return valve, pipework and fittings connecting onto existing common outlet pipework. Turned on electrical supply and tested all works carried out.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment into the car park.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera extensively to clear out a large amount of dirt, tree roots and debris from the common storm water line between to 2 surface pits.

Flow tested the common storm water pipework which is clear and in working order.

Once we had cleared the pipework, we used CCTV drain camera to locate a broken section of earthenware storm water pipework under the concrete slab in the cark park between car spaces 8 and 15. Tree root infestations are entering through the broken original earthenware pipework and if repairs are not undertaken tree roots will again grown in the common storm water line and cause conintal blockages.

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common storm water blockages - We advise to reline the broken and tree root infested section of common earthenware storm water pipework.  We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken. 

Re-install pit lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Quotation - Preventative maintenance jet blasting and CCTV camera survey works on the common sewer Piping

Following the recent sewer blockages we have cleared out our CCTV camera survey we located multiple areas of tree root infestations entering the main original earthenware boundary trap, outlet pipework to the Sydney Waters main in the road and upstream to the car park and tradesman's toilet.

This quotation is to carry out preventative maintenance using high pressure jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the main original earthenware boundary trap, outlet pipework to the Sydney Waters main in the road, common sewer pipework upstream to the car park and tradesman's toilet.

As major tree root infestations are entering the common sewer pipes aggressively we advise these preventative maintenance clear out works are undertaken every 6 months to prevent sewer blockages and floods at the property. Please note, we last undertook these clear out works on the 4th November 2022. 

The following works are will be undertaken:

  1. Remove inspection opening lids on common sewer piping and main boundary trap.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out tree root infestation from the main boundary trap and outlet pipework to Sydney Waters main under the road.
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out tree root infestation from the common sewer pipework upstream to the car park and tradesman's toilet.
  4. CCTV camera survey common sewer pipework and ensure all tree roots have been cut out of the common sewer pipework. Following our CCTV camera survey if any broken or collapsed pipes are found we will report back to BCS with CCTV video.
  5. Flow test common sewer piping to main boundary trap and ensure all clear and in good working order.
  6. Reinstall inspection opening lids and clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.
  7. Removed associated rubbish from the property.

After the laundry waste has been repaired, we advise the lot owner engages their own painting contractor to repair and paint the resultant water damaged internal laundry wall.

We will submit a quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Urgently attended the property on the 5/5/23, gained access into unit 12 and found there to be no sewer smell at the time. The occupant advised the smell is always around the kitchen area.

Re-installed trap, flow tested the sink and no further blockages were found.

Returned the keys to the managing agent.

To prevent the sewer smell from returning, we advise all plumbing fixtures in unit 8 are flushed out regularly to stop the sewer traps from drying out.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property to inspect the common drainage for the building. 

We cut holes in the base of 6 x common down pipes, inspected and CCTV camera surveyed the 6 x separate down pipes to locate the faults in the common storm water piping.

Downpipe A - Downpipe A is located at the middle left of the building and access is from unit 2 only. We cut a small square out of the downpipe and put the drain camera down to inspect the inground drainage. We found the connection between the downpipe and PVC adapter had a gap in it, during rain this would Leak underneath the building.

Further works required to be undertaken on down pipe A - To prevent further storm water water leaking under the building, we advise to excavate the base of the down pipe and install new PVC piping and fittings. Also to flush out the common storm water piping with the high pressure water high blaster.

Downpipe B - Down pipe B is located at the back left of the building, we CCTV camera surveyed downstream and found that it holds water for 1 - 3 meters.

Further works required to be undertaken on down pipe B. We advise the storm water piping is flushed out with the jet blaster and a PVC inspection opening is installed for future access to the down pipe and inground storm water piping.

Downpipe C - Down pipe C has a faulty connection between the downpipe and PVC connection. In heavy rains this would leak badly underneath the building. The connection is above the slab and need a to be rectified to stop further leaking, CCTV camera surveyed downstream and found water holding in the pipe.

Further works required to be undertaken on down pipe C - To prevent further storm water water leaking under the building, we advise to excavate the base of the down pipe and install new PVC piping and fittings. Also to flush out the common storm water piping with the high pressure water high blaster

Down pipe D - We inspected down pipe D which has a new down pipe and connection to the in ground drainage. Camera surveyed the in ground drainage which is holding storm water due to back fall in he common storm water piping.

Downpipe E - Following investigation and camera survey works we found downpipe E is the cause of the leak at the bottom of the stairs, downstream from the downpipe I found this to be the only inground pipework that had not been upgraded to PCV. Following our CCTV camera survey we found the earthenware pipe was collapsed. The pipe is in such bad condition that it has broken in half. During any rain the water will leak into the garden bed and through to the bottom of the retaining wall. 
Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the stormwater on the front left of the building is upgraded and replaced with new PVGC piping and fittings through the garden bed, then core hole through the retaining wall, surface mounting new PVC piping it to the brick wall next to the stairs and replacing the piping through the council footpath and discharge to the kerb and gutter. 

Down pipe F - CCTV camera surveyed down pipe F and found downpipe F is clear from the branch line to the main line, it holds water due to backfall in the branch line.

We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further storm water works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Hi Team,

u7: Catriona 0450 892 167; u4: 0414506366.
"I have been informed by our tenant that there was a leak in the bathroom as well as the bedroom, the water has seeped through the ceiling from the unit above ours,"
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent water leak in unit 4 from unit 7 above

Urgently attended the property after hours on Saturday 1/5/23, gained access into unit 4 and found water leaking through the bathroom door frame, bedroom ceiling, cornice, wall and door frame from unit 7 above.

Gained access into unit 7, tested all fixtures within the bathroom and kitchen and no visible water leaks were found.

Isolated the water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply. Following extensive nitrogen testing we got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water copper pipe within unit 7.

We advised unit 7 to turn off the hot water supply when not showering to prevent further water damage into unit 4 below.

Returned to the property on the 3/5/23, engaged pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water supply within unit 7's bathroom. Used leak detection equipment and leak detector to pint point the burst hot water copper pipe to be located within the common shower wall.

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken to rectify the burst hot water pipe in unit 7 - We advise to remove the affected tiles and excavate the common shower wall, turn off the water supply. cut out burst hot water copper pipework, install new section of copper pipework, fittings, turn on the water supply and test all works, patch render shower wall and re-tile matching existing tiles as close as possible to match. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 7.

After the plumbing works have been completed and we advise the resultant water damaged bathroom and bedroom ceiling is repaired and painted in unit 4. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the resultant water damage repairs and painting works required to be undertaken in unit 4.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Please contact tenants of Unit 2 & 8 and carry out the investigation for the ceiling leak (mould issue) of unit 2.
Charles 0404 796 938 (Unit 2), agent Rhiannon 0434 981 004; Aili 0486 027 395 (Unit 8); Committee member James who knows the history of this unit's issue 0409355975.
History of Unit 2's leak/mould issue:
- previous owner had done the renovation of kitchen, removal of existing fitting, tiles and replace, plumbing alteration is not approved; bathroom renovation, removal of existing fitting, tiles and replace. Plumbing and waterproofing is not included; internal painting of unit.
-please check walls of unit 2, moisture detector and pressure test unit 8 bathroom and visually inspect grout, and check the roof space for any leaking into the walls.
-there is mould report attached which shows there was no moisture in the ceiling; the carpet in this unit was wet for a while due to the water leak from the bathroom but now no longer wet.
-the kitchen wall behind the shower has moisture in it and it was investigated by the agent's plumber, no leaks in unit 2 pipes were found.
-there is moisture in the walls between the kitchen and hallway to bathroom. not sure if it is also in the opposite wall as per agent's plumber (not clear);
-there is a possibility that the walls are still drying out due to the wet carpet or the leak from previous.
Please also determine who's responsible for the leak as committee members claim it will most likely the lot owner's.

W.O. Issued by : Lisa Lin
Email : Lisa.Lin@bcssm.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage in unit 2.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2 and found water damage to 3 x internal walls in the kitchen and hallway adjacent to the shower recess.

Used moisture meter and found high readings of moisture within the internal walls. The high readings were located from the shower rose height and lower, above the shower rose height to the ceiling we found low readings of moisture and no water damage.

Isolated the water supply to unit 2 and nitrogen pressure tested the hot and cold water supply and shower breach and no drop in pressure was found indicating no burst pipes in unit 2.

Gained access into unit 8 and inspected the bathroom above the water leak. Used moisture meter on the adjacent walls and found low moisture readings. Carried out a dye tested on the shower tray and no dye was found to be leaking.

Due to the low readings of moisture higher up within the water damaged walls and our investigation works in unit 2 & 8, we found the leak was not coming from unit 8.

As no water leaks were found, we found the water damaged walls in unit 2 were caused by a previous leak which has since been repaired.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 2 - We advise the water damaged internal walls are left to dry and are monitored to see if the moisture returns. If the water damaged internal walls dry out then we advise the water damaged walls are scraped back repaired and painted.

Please note - We cannot advise who is at fault for the testing/report or the resultant water damage repairs required to be undertaken as we were not called out to the previous leak that caused the water damage.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water leak in unit 105.

14/3 - Attended the property, gained access into unit 105 and met with the site contact from Aquaproof.

Inspected the bathroom ceiling cavity and no leaks were found at the time of inspection.  Aquaproof advised the leak was coming from around unit 108's floor waste penetration through the concrete slab. A stormwater downpipe is located directly behind the floor waste pipe and we were advised the leak only happens in heavy rain.

Gained access to the roof and camera surveyed the stormwater downpipe looking for any cracks or breaks in the pipework which could be causing the leak. No obvious defects were located from our camera survey.

17/3 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 111, 108 and 105 and found no water damage to the ceilings which would indicate where the leak is coming from.

29/3 - Returned to the property, gained access into unit 105 and no leaks were found, occupant also advised it hasn't leaked. Gained access into unit 108,  tested the washing machine and dye tested all waste fixtures within the unit 108 and no dye was found to be leaking.

Accessed the roof installed a plug in the downpipe and flood tested the stormwater drainage 1.5 meters down from the roof penetration testing the water proof membrane around the downpipe penetration - no leaks were found. 

4/4 - Attended the property after heavy rain gained access into unit 105 and found the leak had stopped and all penetrations to be completely dry.

26/4 - Attended the property, gained access to units 105, 108, 111 and the roof.  Flood tested the roof and downpipe for over 2 hours in attempt to replicate heavy rain. After flood testing no water leaked from the common stormwater downpipe or the roof top waterproof membrane above the affected area.

After extensive testing of the common stormwater downpipe, roof waterproof membrane and bathroom waste fixtures in unit 108 we were unable to locate the water leak. We have ruled out all common plumbing fixtures within units 105, 108 & 111. During each inspection we have never been able to locate the cause the leak and the leak has not been present over the course of any our attendances.

If the leak reoccurs we advise a remedial building contractor is engaged to undertake further investigation works.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent sewer blockage in unit 1.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found the toilet to be surcharging sewage all over the bathroom floor when other units above used their waste fixtures.

Removed a service riser access panel in unit 1's bathroom giving us access to the common service riser. We located an inspection opening on the common sewer stack pipe.

Removed the inspection opening lid and found the common stack and sewer piping to be completely blocked.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses into the bathroom. Used the high pressure water jet blaster to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the in ground common sewer piping and we found thick tree root infestations to be the cause of the blockage.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and the drain camera simultaneously to cut out the tree root infestations from the common sewer piping.

Used pipe location equipment to locate the faulty area of common sewer piping to be under the concrete driveway outside of unit 2. We were unable to push the camera downstream past 15 meters due to multiple bends in the common sewer piping.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further sewer blockages and floods in unit 2, we advise to excavate the concrete outside unit 2, cut out a section of tree root infested common sewer piping, junction and install 2 x inspection openings raised to the surface, undertake further jet blasting and CCTV camera survey of the common sewer piping, backfill the trench and reinstate the concrete. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken. 

Once these works have been completed and we have access to the underground sewer piping, we will then engage our relining team to inspect the common sewer piping under unit 1 and outside in the common area. Once our relining team has inspected the common sewer piping, we will then provide a further urgent quotation to reline the faulty tree root infested common sewer piping.

Reinstalled inspection opening lids and access panel lid in unit 1's bathroom

Cleaned all areas in unit 1's bathroom where sewage had surcharged using disinfectant and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent water leak in the common entrance.

Urgently attended the property after hours on the 23/4/23 and found water leaking through the gyprock ceiling and downlights located in the common lobby at the front entrance next to the lifts. 

Inspected the common ceiling cavity and found water leaking through the concrete slab.

Traced out the above unit to be unit 1A. We were unable to gain access into unit 1A on our inspection and left a note on there door.

Returned to the property, gained access in unit 1A, isolated the water supply and carried out extensive pressure testing. Following extensive pressure testing no burst pipes were found within unit 1A.

Flow tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Inspected the common service riser outside unit 1A and found damage to the carpet outside the riser. We found water leaking from a faulty inspection opening cap. Repaired leaking inspection opening cap but we still found water leaking through the common hallway ceiling below.

Laid drop sheets in the common area cut out a larger section of the common area gyprock ceiling to locate a leaking section of 100mm common waste pipework. 

Cut out section of leaking 100mm common waste pipework and installed new section of PVC pipework and fittings connecting onto existing common waste pipework. 

Flow tested all works carried out - AL in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property. 

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the resultant water damaged gyprock ceiling in the common entrance ceiling is repaired and painted. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Contact poerson Alex 0423 216 699 /02 9362 1700
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak at the front of shop 1.

Attended the property, gained access into shop 1 and found water leaking at the front corner of the shop from the gyprock wall.

Gained access to level 1, where the gym is located and accessed the front awning above the council footpath.

We found the front awning to be full of debris, rocks and rubbish blocking the outlet to the downpipe for the awning. Removed debris from the outlet pipework clearing the blockage.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, gained access onto the awning and cleaned all debris, rubbish and rocks from the awning which is causing blockages to the outlet downpipe.

Used high pressure water jet blaster to flush out the awning downpipe and test to see whether water is leaking into shop 1.

Following the flushing of the downpipe we found water to leak from the gyprock wall within shop 1 at the front where the awning downpipe is boxed in behind.

Cut a hole within shop 1's gyprock wall to inspect the downpipe.

We found a common square copper downpipe with several offsets high up near the awning outlet which are leaking from the joints and corrosion within the copper pipework.

We also found the awning downpipe is not connected properly to the original earthenware drainage under the ground.

Camera surveyed the drainage and found it to be clear for approximately 6 meters, then holding sand and water from the downpipe flushing with the high pressure jet blaster.

We then inspected the kurb and gutter and found all original stormwater outlet holes within the kurb and gutter have been deleted when the council footpath and gutter has been replaced. 

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the water leak into shop 1 - We advise the square copper awning downpipe is cut out and replaced with PVC pipe and fittings. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for further works required to be undertaken.

Installed an access cover over the hole, cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Work Details: The owners have had a plumber attend to a blocked toilet, they have cleared a small blockage,
however there are tree roots further down the line.
Can you please call Andrew on 0403 730 184 to arrange your attendance to clear the blockage
as the toilet is surcharging
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent sewer blockage in unit 2

Urgently attended the property after hours on the 25/4/23, gained access into unit 2, found the toilet to be blocked and surcharging sewerage in the bathroom.

Removed external inspection opening and found the common in ground sewer pipework to be blocked.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment outside unit 2.

Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively upstream from the inspection opening on the main line to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line. 

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer pipework upstream towards unit 2's bathroom and downstream on the main line in multiple areas. We found there are sections of the main line that has previously been relined. 

Used high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out as many tree roots as we could and prevent further flooding in unit 2's bathroom.

Flow tested unit 2's toilet and common sewer line outside which is currently getting away.

PLEASE NOTE - Following our CCTV camera survey, there is still further tree root infestations that require cleaning on the main line downstream from unit 2. Once the further clear out works have been completed and the main line is clear, we can then provide a quotation with a scope of works to reline the tree root infested common sewer line as a full proof solution. We will submit an urgent quotation for the further works required to be undertaken.

Re-installed inspection opening lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 1.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and found water damage to the bulkhead in the bathroom and the popcorn / gyprock ceiling in the kitchen.

Gained access into unit 2, pressure tested the shower breaching piece and hot and cold water piping and no burst pipes were found.

Inspected the original, common shower / bath walls and found faulty seals where the bath meets the wall tiles and behind tap flanges allowing water to leak into the wall and under the bath.

Further urgent work required to be undertaken - As the shower / bath walls with faulty seals and grouting are located within the original bathroom, we advise to reseal where the bath meets the common wall tiles and behind the tap spindles. 

Inspected the kitchen and found water damage and swollen timber underneath the kitchen benchtop around the sink which shows signs of water leaking when the kitchen is in use. There is also water extensive water damage to the kitchen cabinetry below the sink.

AFTER HOURS CALL OUT

Water Leak Unit 8 into Unit 3 below AHES - 1.4.2023 job called into Peter As approved by the Strata Committee, please attend site to inspect, repair and report on water leak from Unit 8 into Unit 3 below that is getting worse. Contact - Unit 8 - Joe Barton 0438 988 269 Contact - Unit 3 - Julie Stocca 0417 435 664 Please provide your findings to the Strata Manager Thank you AHES 1300 267 181
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out on the 1/4/23 - Urgent water leak in the bathroom of unit 3.

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access into unit 3 and located a water leak coming from the ceiling and internal bathroom wall adjacent to the kitchen.

Gained access into unit 8 and found no water damage, removed boxing in the kitchen which houses the common sewer stack and found water leaking from the ceiling around the sewer penetration from unit 13 above.

Gained access into unit 13, inspected the common sewer stack and found it to be dry above the waste fixtures. Carried out dye testing on unit 13's bathroom and kitchen fixtures. Attempted to pressure test the cold water supply but found the cold water isolation for unit 13 to be faulty and was unable to carry out an accurate pressure test.

Returned to the property on the 3/4/23, Isolated the buildings cold water supply and replaced the faulty cold water isolation valve in the kitchen for unit 13. Pressure tested the hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found. Gained access into unit 8 and no dye was found to be leaking.

Returned to the property on the 5/4/23- Gained access into unit 3 and found faint yellow dye on the kitchen ceiling and wall indicating a leak from the common copper sewer stack and waste pipes, confirmed the yellow dye to be coming from the toilet waste. Excavated a section of the internal wall between the kitchen and the bathroom where the toilet waste branches into the common stack, tested the toilet several times and found water leaking from the wall close to the concrete slab below the toilet branch line. Excavated more and attempted to seal the burst copper waste pipe with high grade sealant on the common sewer stack pipework.

Returned to the property on the 12/4/23, Gained access into unit 3 and found the leak has slowed down but not stopped completely, we were unable to gain access into unit 13, so we left an access request note on unit 13s door.

Returned to the property on the 18/4/23 - Gained access to unit 3 and found further water damage to the bathroom ceiling and bulkhead in the kitchen, we also found the yellow dye had expanded indicating the leak was coming from the toilet waste. 

Accessed the roof cavity to confirm the roof is all dry and there was no leak coming from the tiled roof down the vent piping when it rains.

Gained access to unit 13 excavated more of the internal wall and found the toilet waste was still leaking slightly.

We were unable to carry out a temporary repair on the outside of the sewer stack pipe due to the location which is tight up against the wall and there is no room to install sealant to cover the burst pipe without excavating the entire wall and concrete slab.

Removed inspection opening lids on the copper sewer stack and used high grade sealant to seal the hole from the inside of the sewer waste in attempt to plug the burst copper waste pipe.

We have asked unit 13 not to use the waste fixtures in the bathroom or kitchen for 3 hours to allow the sealant to dry. We also had to replace the outlet rubber on unit 13's toilet to stop the toilet from constantly running into the sewer stack.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the burst section of common copper sewer stack and common branch line to the toilet is relined. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the urgent relining works required to be undertaken.

Once the re lining works have been completed and we know the extent of the water damage in unit 3, we will submit a separate quotation for the resultant damage repairs and painting works required in the kitchen and bathroom of unit 3.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate flooding in the garage.

Attended the property, gained access into the garage below street level and found sewerage had flooded the garage after heavy rain.

Lifted the lids on the sewer pipework, CCTV camera surveyed the pipework and found no blockages within the sewer which could be causing the garage to flood with sewerage.

Investigated the common sewer and stormwater pipework at the property and used CCTV camera to survey the common sewer boundary trap to Sydney waters sewer main.

Using the camera we located a faulty reflux valve between the common boundary trap and sewer main in the street which is accessible from a pit at the front stairs entrance.

The reflux valve pit is approximately 3.5 meters deep, the lid to the reflux valve has a hole in it and the internal reflux flap is missing.

We consider during heavy rain events the Sydney water sewer main is overflowing with stormwater runoff and the missing reflux valve is allowing the backflow of sewer into the carpark.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the reflux valve lid and internal flap is replaced within the reflux valve pit to prevent sewer backflow into the carpark during heavy rain events. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Investigate water overflowing in the carpark.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise a pump company is engaged to replace the 2 x stormwater pumps, all outlet pump out pipe pipework and fittings in the visitors carpark stormwater pit.

Investigate urgent water leak on the footpath outside 16-24 Parramatta Road.

Unfortunately due to multiple services located under the councils foot path, we cannot undertake this job due to the location of the burst pipe. A civil plumbing contractor is required to be urgently engaged by strata complete the excavation and burst pipe repairs.

Further URGENT works are required to be undertaken by a civil plumbing contractor. To  rectify the urgent water leak, we advise to obtain road opening council permits, traffic control, saw cut concrete footpath, excavate concrete and ground exposing burst copper pipework, isolate the buildings water service, drain the water from the line, cut out burst copper pipework and install new copper pipework and fittings, turn on water supply, test all works, bed pipework, backfill trench and temporary repair the councils footpath using bitumen.

Invoice Description:
Investigate low water pressure at the building.

Attended the property, gained access and found low water pressure throughout the building.

Gained access to the buildings cold water supply pumps and found the pumps to be ON, but not operational as the pressure gauge was at 150kpa.

Turned off the power supply at the control panel to re-set the pumps.

Description: Water leaking in a new location in the bedroom near the door
Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent water leak in unit 1.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 1 and the occupants showed us water leaking in the bedroom in a new lactation to the previous burst pipe we previously repaired.

Turned off the hot water supply in the storage room, nitrogen pressure tested the hot and cold water supply and got a drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst hot water pipe within unit 1.

Returned to the property 29/3/23, engaged pipe location leak detection to trace out the hot water supply in unit 1.

Used a listening device and leak detector to pin point the burst pressurized hot water pipe to be located within the internal shower wall.

Returned to the property, on 30/3/23, laid drop sheets in unit 1, removed affected tiles and excavated the internal shower wall to locate the burst pressurized hot water copper pipework. Once we opened up the wall, we also found the cold water pipework to be badly corroded and soldered onto of the hot water pipework.

Turned off the hot and cold water supply, cut out burst hot water pipework and corroded cold water copper pipework, install new copper pipework and fittings, turned on the water supply, tested all works, patch rendered shower wall and covered hole with plastic to allow the occupants to shower.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property. 

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to remove the shower screen, re-tile affected area of shower wall using tiles as close as possible to match, re grout using additive and re-install existing shower screen. We will submit a quotation shortly for the tiling repairs required to be undertaken.

Left the excavation open in the rear yard for further works required to maintain the original existing stormwater pipework.

Contacted Woollahra council members who advised of appropriate steps and the application process in order to work on the existing stormwater pipework for 83 Moncur street which is located inside the neighbouring property of 28A Spicer street.

Description:
leaking pipe on side of building causing subsidence and sand slip for this building and building next door. video added

Reported by Mariella 0425 223 132

Engineer bloke - Billy 0416 377 469
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leaking into the neighbouring building site.

Attended the property and met with the engineer from the neighbouring building site who asked us to camera survey the leaking stormwater pipework at the rear left side of the property to see if the pipework is collapsed or in working order. He has also asked us if we can seal around the leaking sewer stack at the rear left of property.

  • Left side

Used CCTV camera to survey the rear left side stormwater drainage from the kurb and gutter in the rear lane and found the storm water line to be blocked with large amounts of debris and building materials.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster, used jet blasting equipment upstream from the gutter to remove a large amount of debris clearing the pipework under the left path from the rear downpipe to the lane.

Once clear we found the rear left downpipe discharges to the rear lane kurb and gutter and is in good working order.

We found the middle left side downpipe not to be connected to the drainage pipe under the side path and runs under the building.

Camera surveyed the rear middle downpipe and found the drain runs towards the front of the building and the original earthenware storm water drainage was collapsed and blocked approximately 5 meters downstream under the building. 

Inspected the sewer stack where water was leaking from the base, installed sand and cement at the base of the open stack sealing the pipework to prevent water leaking into the adjacent building site.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken on the left side - We advise the left side middle downpipe is re run to the curb and gutter when the path is excavated by the neighbouring property builder.

  • Right side.

We inspected the right side path and found a blocked sewer gully which was causing the sewer to overflow down the right side path. We also found a corroded sewer stack which is leaking down the external wall of the building approximately 3 stories high.

Description:
Variation quotation - Rear stormwater downpipe and common gas pipework on the right side of the building.

After further excavation at the backyard, we found the rear roof downpipe to be discharging into the ground and there is no absorption trench in the back yard for the stormwater to run to. If an absorption trench was to be installed in the backyard major excavation works will be required to install an adequate sized absorption trench to cope with the amount of rainwater discharging from the back roof. We advise the rear downpipe is re-run, surface mounting the pipework along the right side wall to the front downpipe and which discharges at the curb and gutter at the street. 

After the right side concrete was excavated, we found the copper gas piping from the gas meters to the external wall to be installed just below the ground level and the gas pipe needs to be lowered 300mm below the ground level as per gas codes AG5601, so the new path can be concreted.

  • Part A - To surface mount 24 meters of PVC piping from the rear roof downpipe to the front right downpipe discharging the rear gutters to the front downpipe which connect to the street. 

This quotation is to surface mount approximately 24 meters of common stormwater piping across the right side of the building to the front downpipe discharging the rear roof stormwater to the street. 

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Use extension ladders the run pipework at a level above the bottom windows and door on the right side. 
  2. Supply and install approximately 24 meters of PVC pipe and fittings connecting the rear roof downpipe to the front right downpipe. 
  3. Install stainless steel brackets and fixings securing the pipework to the wall. 
  4. Alter front downpipe and install a tee junction  for the rear downpipe.
  5. Flow test all works carried out. 
  6. Remove associated rubbish from the property. 
  • Part B - Relocate existing copper gas pipes on the right side, 300mm below the ground as per AS5601 gas codes. 

This quotation is to cut out the existing copper gas piping and and install copper gas piping 300mm below the ground as per as3500, from the meter manifold to the external wall so the new path can be concreted. 

The following works will be undertaken: 

  1. Isolate the gas supply to all units. 
  2. Excavate a trench 300mm deep from the meter manifold to the external wall.
  3. Cut out copper gas pipework where it passes along the path above the ground level. 
  4. Supply and install copper pipe and fittings to connect the gas pipework to lower it below the ground level. 
  5. Backfill and compact with sand.
  6. Turn the gas supply back on testing all works.
  7. Remove associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate noisy pump on LG2.

Attended the property, gained access into the lower carpark LG2 and found the common submersible stormwater pump within the pit to be making a noise as it was running constantly and not turning off.

Lifted the faulty pit lid grate, isolated the power to the pump and removed pump from the pit.

Inspected the condition of the pump and found the float had broken off and the pumps bearings are in bad condition.

We also found the pump out line pipework to be connected with rubber fittings not glued PVC fittings.

Adjusted the float, cable tied the float to the pump and re installed the pump.

Tested the pump and found it was slowly pumping the water from the pit but shutting off. We found the pump is faulty and is required to be replaced.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - We advise the faulty trafficable pit grate lid grate is replaced, the faulty submersible stormwater pump, non return valve and pump out pipework is replaced with a new submersible pump, non return valve and PVC pressure pump out pipework. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas and removed associated rubbish from the property.
