Description:
Amended Quotation - Additional common plumbing works required to be undertaken

Following our inspection at the property, we found the common gas pipework for unit 2 & 3 to be original, rusted and requires replacement from the gas meter to the kitchen gas appliances, the cold water supply to have no individual unit isolation valves installed to isolate the water supply in an emergency without isolating the entire building. We also found the hot water heater for unit 1 shop to be located on the concrete path at the back which needs to be excavated and no isolation key to isolate the buildings cold water supply at the main meter.

This quotation is to install 2 x copper gas pipes for units 2 & 3 under the new concrete path form the meter to the external wall and cap off for future use. Supply and install 3 x cold water isolation valves at the base of the kitchen and bathroom riser pipes on the external wall and relocate the hot water heater for unit 1 shop from the concrete walkway mounting it to the buildings external wall.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Install approximately 6 meters of copper pipe and fittings for unit 2 & 3's gas supply on the left side, under the new path to the external wall of the building and cap off pipework.
  2. Install brackets and fixings securing the new pipework to the external wall.
  3. Cut out and remove old galvanised steel pipes under the ground and on the right side external wall where possible using a large extension that are not in use.
  4. Isolate the gas supply for unit 4's gas meter and install a new common gas isolation valve. 
  5. Isolate the water and electrical supply for unit 1's shop hot water heater located down the left side passage.
  6. Drain water heater, install mounting bracket and secure the water heater to the external wall off the concrete path.
  7. Connect water and electrical supply to the heater, altering the pipework. 
  8. Turn the water supply back on testing all works.
  9. Isolate the buildings cold water supply at the main water meter.
  10. Cut out copper pipework on the external wall for 3 x cold water risers. 
  11. Supply and install 3 x new 25mm cold water isolation valves and fittings at the base of the kitchen and bathroom cold water riser pipework.
  12. Turn the buildings cold water supply back on testing all works..

This quotation is to reline from the top of the boundary trap, downstream for 5.5 meters to Sydney waters main junction, reline upstream from the boundary trap junction for 6 meters and install 1 x structural fiberglass junction patch over the boundary trap 85 degree junction as per AS/NZS3500 standards.

The following works will be undertaken: 

  1. Advise residents of cold water building shut down.
  2. Use high pressure water jet blaster to clear out the tree root infestations and debris in preparation for relining. 
  3. Remove all water from the boundary trap using a wet vacuum, CCTV inspect drainage line prior to relining to ensure line clear.
  4. Turn off the buildings cold water supply and drain the water from the line.
  5. Reline from the top of the boundary trap, downstream for 5.5 meters to Sydney waters main junction using inversion relining method.
  6. Reline upstream from the boundary trap junction upstream for 6 meters using inversion relining method. 
  7. Install 1 x structural fiberglass junction patch over the boundary trap 85 degree junction that is severely cracked and tree root affected. This is required to legally cover tree root affected and cracked sections to meet with AS/NZS3500 standards.
  8. Once the liner has cured, remove relining equipment from the common sewer pipework.
  9. Used CCTV drain camera to inspect and ensure all in good working order.
  10. Turn on the buildings cold water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  11. Clean all areas where work had taken place.
  12. Remove associated rubbish and materials from the property.

Description:
Preventative maintenance jet blasting & CCTV camera survey works - Sewer piping every 6 months

We last cleared out major tree root infestations growing in the original earthenware boundary trap shaft and sewer piping in December 2020. As the original earthenware sewer piping and boundary trap has tree root infestations growing in multiple areas and to replace major costs would be incurred for a deep excavation, we advise preventative maintenance jet blasting and CCTV camera survey works are carried out every 6 months to cut out the tree roots from the original earthenware sewer piping and main boundary trap preventing sewer blockages and surcharges at the property. 

The following works will be undertaken: 

  • Remove inspection opening lids on boundary trap and sewer stack pipes.
  • Use high pressure water jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads to clear out all tree root infestations from the sewer piping.
  • Use CCTV drain camera simultaneously with water jet blaster, to ensure all tree root infestations have been removed from the sewer piping.
  • Flow test sewer piping to the boundary trap located in the driveway.
  • Re install inspection opening lids on the ground and on sewer stack pipes.
  • Clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.
  • Remove associated rubbish from the property.

  4. Flow test sewer piping to the boundary trap located in the driveway.

  6. Clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Invoice Description:
Investigate front sump room water leak.

Attended the property, gained access to the front sump room and found the floor to be full of water and the submersible pump operating constantly.

Found water leaking from the neighbouring property, both stormwater drains at the kerb, inspected the main water meter and found it to be running at a rapid pace.

Located the pump out line for the submersible pump to be draining into the common stormwater on the left side of the building which was blocked and surcharging.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear multiple blockages in the storm water piping on the left side to the street.

CCTV camera surveyed the storm water piping and found 4 x sections where tree root infestations are entering the storm water piping. 

Once clearing the common stormawater pipework on the left side we were able to stop the water leaking from the neighbouring property.

Used the CCTV camera to survey the common stormwater pipes under the ground to locate water constantly leaking into the pipework further up the building.

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe locating equipment to trace out the common cold water line and leak detector to locate a burst cold water pipe in the ground below the storage room 11, under the concrete slab.

Excavated the external grassed area behind the storage room, where the burst pipe was located under the building in attempt to locate the leak and try to install a temporary repair.

Installed barricades around the excavation until further urgent works are carried out.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To rectify the water leak, we advise to excavate the concrete slab in the storage room 11, repair the burst section of common cold water pipework and re-instate the concrete slab. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

Please note : Access into the storage room 11 is urgently needed for the burst cold water repairs to be undertaken.

Once the urgent burst pipe works have been completed, we will submit a separate quotation to rectify the blockages in the common stormwater pipework on the left side of the property.

Clean all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property,

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 102 and Shop 2.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 102 and found water damage to the hallway timber floors at the front door along the common wall of unit 103.

Gained access to shop 2 and found water leaking into shop 2 at the rear, through the concrete slab.

Left access request notes on unit 103.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 103 adjacent and inspected the bathroom.

Pressure tested shower/ bath breaching piece combo and no leaks were found. Dye tested bath waste piping and no leaks were found.

Following flood testing, we found the seals to be faulty and cracked where the bath meets the common wall tiles.

Excavated tiles on the side of the bath and used wet vac to remove water from underneath the bath cavity, installed access vents covering the hole within the tiles.

Cut out faulty sealant in the shower bath area, cleaned and primed all areas and installed new high grade flexible sealant where the bath meets the common wall tiles and vertical wall.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property. 

Following inspection and testing of the bath, we found there to be movement in the original bath and consider the sealant installed to be a temporary repair as the original bath is not recessed inside the walls.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 103 - We advise the defective bath is removed, excavate the the 1st course of shower wall tiles, install primer and 2 coats of waterproof membrane, install new bath and re-tile 1st course of wall tiles using tiles as close as possible to match. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 103.

Once the bath replacement works in unit 103 has been completed, we advise the hallway flooring in unit 102 is repaired by a flooring contractor.

Investigate common stormwater pipework in the passageway along the building.

Gained access to the side passageways along the left, right and rear of the building.

Found 2 x common stormwater downpipes at the rear on both corners to have holes at the base just above the ground.

CCTV camera surveyed the common storm water piping and found 2 x areas where tree root infestations are entering the common storm water piping. 

Once majority of the tree roots had been cut out we camera surveyed the piping, found collapsed storm water piping and large holes that are letting tree roots infest the storm water piping.

We used pipe location equipment to locate the where the storm water piping runs through the rear passageway and the 2 x affected collapsed sections of common stormwater pipework under the rear concrete passageway.

To rectify further storm water blockages we advise the common storm water piping is excavated and replaced with new PVC piping and fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further common storm water repair works required to be undertaken.

Inspected the passageway and found 2 x additional water leaks.

1. The metal downpipe connected to the rear Telecommunications House roof is rusted at the gutter nozzle, the downpipe angles are rusted and leaking and there is a hole at the base just above the floor.

2. The common cold water isolation valve in the rear passageway is leaking constantly onto the floor and requires replacement.

We advise, the leaking isolation valve and rusted common downpipe for the Telecommunications house are cut out and replaced with new pipe and fittings. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Thank you
Zac
Invoice Description:
Investigate loose external downpipe pipe and blocked gutters.

Attended the property, gained access and found the common cast iron pipework to come loose on the external wall. We also found the common gutters to be blocked with leaves causing the gutters to overflow.

Cleaned out the common guttering which we could reach from the stairs, removed leaves from the guttering to the rainwater head. Went to the supplier and sourced stainless steel brackets to suit the common cast iron pipework.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers and used the large extension ladder to access the loose cast iron pipework, blocked guttering and downpipes.

Supplied and installed 5 x stainless steel brackets and fixings securing the loose cast iron common pipework to the external wall of the building.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster and ran hoses to the top gutter and downpipe, cleared guttering of leaves and flushed out stormwater downpipe.

Used the jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and the drain camera simultaneously to clear out the storm water piping from the curb and gutter in the street and the downpipe to clear multiple blockages in the common storm water piping.

Once majority of the tree roots had been cut out, we CCTV camera surveyed the common piping and found collapsed earthenware storm water piping and dislodged joints with large gaps that are letting tree roots infest the storm water piping in multiple areas under the council footpath.

Further works required to be undertaken on the common storm water pipework - As the tree roots are entering the stormwater piping in multiple areas and the original pipework is badly dislodged under the council footpath, we advise the faulty common stormwater pipework is relined. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Further preventative maintenance works is also required to be carried out every 6 months to prevent stormwater blockages and floods at the property. We advise the common guttering, downpipes and stormwater drainage is cleaned out on a preventative maintenance program. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the preventative maintenance works to be carried out, as we have just completed these works the next stormwater clear outs are due in August 2023.

Cleaned all areas using the high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in Townhouse 124.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Description:
Please attend to the reported leak in Unit 8 possibly from Unit 12.
**Contact Details below:
Unit 8 - Sally - 0419 122 178
Unit 12 - Dianna - 0468 859 006
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 8.

Attended the property on the 7/2/23 and found water damage to the common service duct access panel in the bathroom.

Cut a hole within the common bulkhead and service duct to investigate the common copper sewer stack. Found water leaking around the common stack penetration from unit 12 above.

Gained access into unit 12 and inspected the renovated bathroom.

After thFound no silicone seals around the shower wall mixer and gaps in the cover-plate, allowing water to leak behind the shower wall tiles. Re sealed gaps behind the shower mixer to rule out any possible leak.

Flood dye tested the shower recess which is adjacent to the common service duct and no dye was found to be leaking into unit 10.

We are unable to access the common stack in unit 12 as the common service riser access has been built out with cabinetry and tiled over in the renovation works. We tried to remove the downlight within the ceiling bulkhead behind the shower but was unable to inspect inside the cavity bulkhead without causing damage.

Returned to the property on the 14/2 and gained access into unit 10 & 12 to carry out further testing. Dye tested all bathroom fixtures, carried out pressure testing in unit 12 and no leak was found to be coming from the renovated bathroom.

Unit 10 advised the leak was intermittent and only occurs 2 out of 5 days. Left access request note on unit 16's door to gain access.

Returned to the property on the 20/2, gained access into unit 10,12 & 16, Dye tested all bathroom waste fixtures in unit 16.

Excavated a white tile on the common service riser of unit 16, to inspect the common copper toilet waste branch line and stack and found the concrete slab to be dry.

Dye tested the entire shower recess with green dye and common floor waste / basin waste fixtures with red dye. After extensive dye testing in unit 16, we found red dye to be leaking into unit 8.

Returned to the property on the 28/2/23, gained access into unit 30's courtyard and gained access into the roof. Used CCTV drain camera downstream from the top of the stack on the roof to locate the original common internal copper stack to be in very bad condition and leaking. 

Further URGENT works required to be undertaken - To rectify the water leak, we advise to install 3 x reline satellite junction repairs on the 3 x leaking junctions on the common internal copper stack pipework connecting units 12 and 16. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further relining works required to be undertaken.

After the relining works have been completed, we advise to repair and paint the damaged bulkhead in unit 8's bathroom and to replace the resultant damaged tiles next to unit 16's toilet. We will submit a seperate quotation shortly for the resultant damage repairs in units 8 and 16.

Cleaned all areas where the work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

"Pipe that is supposed to lead water down to the sewer is filled with hardened soil which needs to be cleared professionally" Site contact: Emma 0478 542 218
Invoice Description:
Investigate common stormwater blockages at the building.

Attended the property, met the site contact Emma who showed us issues with the common storm water drainage and guttering on the left and right hand side of the building.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream the outlet of the strip drain on the left hand side of the building and found the original common earthenware storm water line to be completely blocked with tree root infestations.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment. Used high pressure water jet blaster extensively with tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to clear out the tree root infestations from the common storm water line.

CCTV video link downstream the outlet of the strip drain - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-B968G

Further works required to be undertaken to prevent further common storm water blockages on the left hand side of the building, we advise to Install a 2 meter reline of structural fiberglass liner over heavily cracked earthenware pipework located under driveway and also reline approximately 10 meters 100mm dislodged earthenware pipework relining from floor drain (left of the doors) covering dislodged 45 degree bend.  We will submit a quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Following our inspection with Emma on the left hand and right hand side of the building, we found the below further works are required to be undertaken:

- The base of the common downpipes not be connected into the ground drainage

- Missing mesh covering for the 3 x storm water pits and strip drains which prevent leaves and debris blocking the pits and strip drains.

- Base of the common stormwater pits to be holding water.

- The bottom level entrance floor to units 1-3 & 8-10 floods, as there is no current drainage pit and pump.

- Insufficient drainage near the clothier line on the right hand side of the building.

Further works required to be undertaken - We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the multiple storm water repairs on the left and right side of the property.

Please note - We also found there to be insufficient downpipes on the left and right side of the building to handle the volume of water during heavy rain and blocked guttering causing overflow. We advise the buildings roofing contractor is engaged to supply and install additional downpipes and clear out the guttering. 

Re-installed grate lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose.

Client has indicated repeated bursts of copper pipework since installation of new HWS; please advise if this may be contributing to issues.
Invoice Description:
Investigate water damage to the common wall in unit 2.

On the 17/1/23 we attended the property, gained access to unit 2 and found water damage to common wall in the living room.

Used moisture meter to identify high moisture levels of moisture within the water damaged rendered brick wall.

Gained access into unit 3 and inspected the kitchen which is adjacent to the water damage in unit 2.Used moisture meter to identify high moisture levels in the brickwork and paint stains on the wall.

The occupant in unit 3, advised there was a flood in the unit above some months ago and water leaked down his kitchen walls. He was not very co-operative and asked our tradespeople to leave. 

Left access request notes on units 8 & 9 above for further investigation works.

On the 25/1/23 we returned to the property, gained access into unit 2 and carried out moisture test on the common wall, used moisture meter and thermal image camera to determine the wall has slightly dried.

Attempted to gain access to units above and no one was home in units 8 & 9 at the time.

On the 24/2/23 we returned to the property, gained access into unit 2 and inspected the common wall damage in the living room. Found the common wall has remained the same and has not become worse.

Used moisture meter to identify lower levels of moisture, compared to the previous visits.

Following multiple visits with extensive investigation works, we consider the water damage may be caused by a previous one off flood in unit 9's kitchen, After gaining access into unit 2 & 3 several times over the course of 1 month, we found the water damage within the common wall in unit 2 & 3 has not grown in size and the moisture meter shows the level of moisture in the common wall is becoming less over time.  We advise the common wall in unit 2 is monitored and when the wall dries carried out it can be repaired and painted.

Whilst at the building we met with site contact Marike, who advised of a leaking hose tap in the common courtyard and a sewer smell and the front passageway to the building. Supplied and installed a new hose tap to prevent water leaking in the common courtyard and supplied and installed a new micro flap vent cap on the sewer vent causing sewer smells in the front side passage. 

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, gained access into lots 37 & 38, found the storm water had flooded from the garden pits connected to the common storm water main in the garden area which was causing water to flood the garages. 

Removed grated lids and found the 2 x large garden pits to be full of leaves, debris and the outlet to the pit has a large amount of root infestations.

Engaged 2 x plumbers, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment, Used the high pressure water jet blaster downstream the outlet of 2 x pits to clear multiple blockages in the common storm water piping.

CCTV camera surveyed the storm water piping and found multiple areas where tree root infestations are entering the storm water piping. CCTV video link - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-B9HJY

Used the jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads, CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out the storm water line and get the line flowing.

Once the majority of the tree roots had been cut out, we camera surveyed the piping and found collapsed PVC pipework that are allowing tree roots to infest 2 x separate outlets downstream from the garden pits in 37 & 38.

Cleared out as much as possible with the large tree root cutting heads to clear the common pipework, but there is still partial tree root penetration. 

We found the garden surface pits in 37 & 38 to be set lower than the overflow for the main storm water pit and when the blockage occurred the stormwater overflowed into 37 & 38.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken - To prevent further blockages and floods at the property, we advise the 2 x collapsed garden pit outlet pipes are relined, we will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the relining works required to be undertaken.

Following our inspection we found the base of the downpipe at the rear of lot 38 to be broken and requires repairs. Further works required to be undertaken to excavate the ground, cut out broken downpipe and fittings, install new section of PVC pipework, fittings, back fill trench and reinstate area. We will submit a separate quotation for the further works required ot be undertaken.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in Townhouse 16.

Attended the property, gained access to townhouse 16 and found water damage to the gyprock ceiling in the living room.

Inspected the main bathroom above, located the toilet and basin to be above the water damage.

Removed light fitting in the living room and cut a hole in the gyprock ceiling, used the camera to inspect inside the ceiling cavity where the water damage appears. 

Within the ceiling cavity we exposed the PVC waste pipes for the basin, floor waste and toilet penetrations exposing the timber floor.

We found a faulty PVC pipe fitting which has been previously temporary repaired with epoxy resin servicing the floor drain piping where it passes through the floor timber floor beams. 

Returned to the property, cut a larger hole within the ceiling cavity and exposed all the bathroom waste pipes.

Cut out and replaced the previously epoxy repaired PVC waste fitting and installed new PVC pipework and fittings. Flow tested all waste piping in the ceiling cavity - All in good working order.

Flood tested and dye tested the bathroom floor tiles around the floor waste and toilet waste where the pipework goes through the tiled timber floor.

After extensive dye testing and flood testing in the main bathroom and bathroom floor tiles, we found water to leak through the main bathroom floor tiles from the toilet waste penetration into the ceiling cavity below.

We consider the water leak has happened on a one off occasion where water has leaked onto the bathroom floor around the toilet waste tiles into the ceiling below.  We installed high grade flexible sealant around the toilet waste and floor tile to prevent water leaking into the ceiling below.

As a full proof solution, we advise the bathroom floor tiles are removed and the bathroom floor is re-water proofed and re-tiled. We submit a quotation shortly for the further repair works required to be undertaken.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise the resultant damage to the living room ceiling is repaired and painted, we will submit a quotation shortly for the repairs and painting works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place, installed a temporary cover over the hole made in the ceiling and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended site and investigated water leaking into loungeroom wall which backs onto bathroom and laundry. 

Used moisture meter and the highest reading is close to corner of shower / bath .

Pressure tested hot water pipes and pressure dropped from 880kpa to 640kpa in 20 minutes. 

Pressure tested cold water pipes this held pressure. Following extensive nitrogen pressure testing no burst pipes were found within unit 1.

Everything in the bathroom looks perfect,  grout , silicon seals , taps , tiling etc.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise to get the the builder that undertook the bathroom back to the property as the works were recently completed 1 year ago.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 6's garage.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 6's garage located at the rear of the building and found sewerage to be leaking on the garage floor.

Carried out further inspection to find the original 100mm cast iron sewer stack pipework to be leaking and the common tradesman toilet adjacent to unit 6's garage to be blocked and surcharging sewerage.

Set up the high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Removed inspection opening lid in the driveway, used high pressure water jet blaster extensively upstream from the inspection opening to punch a hole in the blockage and release the common sewer line.

Used CCTV drain camera to locate major tree root infestations entering the original earthenware sewer line which was the cause of the blockage. Used the high pressure water jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out the tree root infestations from the common sewer line.

Flow tested the common sewer line which is currently clear but if repairs are not undertaken to the tree root infested common sewer pipework, further blockages will reoccur.

Re-installed inspection opening lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and disinfectant.

Further urgent works are required to be undertaken - We advise to reline the tree root infested section of common sewer pipework upstream from the inspection opening in the driveway and cut out approximately 1.5 meters of faulty 100mm cast iron sewer stack pipework and replace with new PVC pipework and fittings in unit 6's garage. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Description:
Fix Overflow & Clear downpipe
Please attend site and fix waste water overflow at the side of Building. It has been overflowing on and off throughout the week.
Clear/Check downpipes from the gutters, particularly gutters from U4 rear balcony.

Site Contact Person : David Johnson
Phone : +61 402870631

W.O. Issued by : Krysten McDonald
Email : savanah.sione@bcssm.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate sewer overflow at the side of building and common stormwater downpipes.

Attended the property, tested the common sewer pipework and found it to be all clear and in good working order. No blockages or faults were found within the common sewer pipes.

Camera surveyed the common stormwater downpipes at the rear of the building and found the common stormwater piping to be blocked in the ground holding water and sand.

Returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, set up the high pressure water jet blasting equipment, running extension hoses into the backyard.

Cut open the downpipe drainage and cleared out the common stormwater pipework using the jet blaster and CCTV camera simultaneously from the rear downpipe, clearing out the pipework removing sand build up from the surface water drain.

Jet blasted downstream from the stormwater pit at the back right and found the stormwater discharges into an absorption pit in the backyard.

Inspected all the rear guttering and downpipe nozzles for the rear balconies and found the guttering to be blocked of debris.

Cleaned out all guttering and flow tested the common downpipes and storm water piping with the high pressure hose to ensure no further blockages - All clear and in good working order.

Installed new pipework at the base of the back downpipe connection where it goes into the ground.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate urgent blockage in the car park.

Urgently attended the property, gained access into the car park and found the common storm water drainage to be blocked causing the lower car park to flood during heavy rain.

Remove strip drain grate lids, cleaned out all leaves, dirt and debris from the base of the strip drain.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment with 2 x plumbers.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera downstream the outlet of the strip drain to clear out a large amount of dirt and debris from the common storm water line which was the cause of the blockage.

Flow tested strip drain and common storm water line - All clear and in good working order.

Supplied and installed chicken wire mesh as leaf protection. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further blockages, we advise the rest of the common storm water pits and drains are cleared out, clear out common storm water lines using high pressure jet blaster and drain camera on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked kitchens in units 7 and 9.

Urgently attended the property on the 20/1/23, gained access into unit 7 and found the common kitchen/laundry waste pipework to be blocked.

Disconnected the waste pipework, used electric eel to punch a hole in the blockage and release the line, used CCTV drain camera to locate the common stack pipe to be badly internally corroded which was the cause of the blockage.

Engaged 2nd plumber, set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.

Cut out the base of the common stack pipework, used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the rust from the common stack pipework. CCTV video link after upstream from the base of the stack - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-B9UB5

Re-connected common waste pipework, flow tested the kitchen and ran the washing machine at the same time in unit 7 - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place in unit 7.

Returned to the property on the 21/2/22, gained access into unit 9 and also found the kitchen/laundry to be blocked. The blocked stack connecting unit 9 is a seperate stack to unit 7. 

Disconnected kitchen waste pipework and used electric eel to clear the blockage within the common branch and stack pipework. We cleared out a large amount of rust from the common stack which was the cause of the blockage.

Re-connected kitchen waste pipework, flow tested the kitchen and ran the washing machine at the same time in unit 9 - All clear and in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place in unit 9.

Sewer line needs investigating for possible re-location.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, met with the site contact John to CCTV camera survey the common sewer line, inspect water leak on the eastern side of the building and loose downpipe.

The following works were undertaken at the property on the 14/2/23 & 16/2/23:

           1 - CCTV camera survey common sewer line

Used CCTV drain camera to inspect the common sewer lines at the property. Following our CCTV camera survey, we found the common boundary trap, shaft and sewer pipework to be collapsed, squashed under the large heritage tree located at the rear lane boundary, kerb and driveway carpark. Used CCTV drain camera upstream towards the building and no faults were found. The site contact John advised that the storm water line has been connected into the sewer line. Following our CCTV camera survey, we were unable to locate the location where the storm water has been connected into the common sewer line.

We met with our re-lining team at the building to inspect to see if the common boundary trap and sewer piping could be relined.  Our relining specialists advised that relining the common boundary trap would not be warranted as it is installed too close to the stump of the large tree and the root system is already lifting and squashing the pipework upstream and downstream from the boundary trap shaft.

CCTV video downstream the boundary trap located next to the large tree - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-B9KFC

Further works required to be undertaken to rectify the tree root infested and crushed common sewer line - As we have previously encountered sand stone rock under ground in this area, we advise a civil plumbing contractor is engaged to excavate the sandstone rock within the rear lane and building driveway / carpark to re locate the common boundary trap and common sewer drainage from the rear right side under the tree to rear left side of the property installing a new junction within Sydney water sewer main approximately 2.5 meters deep under the road.

           2. Leaking waste pipe on the eastern side of the building

Inspected the common storm water and found the left side of the building has overflowing gutters leaking water onto the main entrance pavers during heavy rain. Used CCTV camera to survey downstream from the inspection opening at the base of the downpipe and found the common storm water line under the pavers to be blocked by tree roots and debris entering the pipework where the original earthenware meets the PVC and next joint up. CCTV video link of blocked storm water pipework - https://office.aroflo.com/DocStorage/6QO-B9XH7

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment.  Used the high pressure water jet  blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out multiple tree root infestations from the common earthenware pipework causing the blockage. 

Flow tested the common storm water - All clear and in good working order.

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify further blockages, we advise to reline approximately 3 meters of tree root infested common storm water piping from the base of the downpipe. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further relining works required to be undertaken.

          3. Loose common downpipe at the front right of the building

Sourced new clips from the supplier, returned to the property with 2 x plumbers, used large extension ladder to access the downpipe and faulty clips, supplied and installed 3 x new downpipes clips matching colours, securing the downpipe to the wall using stainless steel fixings.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Work to be Done: Attention Treat Plumbing: please arrange a service call to Unit 812 to investigate the leakage in the batroom most likely emanating from the ac drainage. Access Instructions: please contact Peggy Mok

Peggy Mok Elanda Partners peggy@elandapartners.com.au 0405331616
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in the bathroom of unit 812.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 812 and found water leaking from the base of the common wall and laundry tub when the air-conditioning is being used.

Flow tested the laundry tub waste piping and no leaks were found, turned on the air-conditioning unit and found water leaking out from under the laundry tub.

Found the common floor drain tundish under the laundry tub that catches the air-conditioning drainage to be blocked.

Used electric eel to clear out the common tundish drain under the laundry tub, down stream from the air-condition drain.

Tested the common tundish drain and found the drain to be all clear and in good working order.

Returned to the property the following day and found water leaking from the common wall when the air-conditioning was in use.

Inspected the air-condition pipework under the laundry tub and found it to be altered during renovations and leaking from the common wall around the waste pipework and silicone seal where the new pipework has been installed.

Excavated the common wall below the laundry tub and found the pipework to be leaking from the PVC fitting and altered pipework inside the common wall. 

We found the water leak to be inside the common wall where the altered pipework joins the original piping inside the wall.

Cut out and removed faulty leaking PVC pipework within the common wall.

Installed new PVC pipework and fittings within the common wall joining the air-conditioning drain to the common tundish floor drain under the laundry tub.

Tested all new pipework and found the pipework to be in good working order.

Returned to the property and found the common wall to be dry and the leak to be resolved, patch rendered the affected area of common wall under the laundry tub.

Cleaned all areas where work has taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Please note - We found whilst the air conditioning unit is being used in unit 812, there is a large amount of condensation within the ceiling cavity of the bathroom, causing water droplets to form on the air-conditioning unit and dripping onto the ceiling.

There are cracks in the render allowing water to leak into the brickwork, there is also a air-condition conduit which is installed on the external wall for unit 1, the conduit has been installed and the building has been rendered after causing there to be open brickwork behind the conduit, water is leaking into the brickwork from behind the air-condition conduit causing the water build up within the brickwork.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked downpipe at the right side of the building.

Attended the property, gained access to the right side of the building and found the common downpipe to be blocked.

Cut out the base of the downpipe and removed a section of piping to access the in ground stormwater drainage drainage within the garden bed along the side of the building.

Once the pipework was removed, we found tree root infestations at the base of the downpipe where the PVC joins the original common earthenware piping.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment to the right side of the building.

Used the jet blaster with large tree root cutting heads and the drain camera simultaneously to clear out the tree root infestations from the common storm water piping.

Once majority of the tree roots had been cut out we camera surveyed the piping, found the original common storm water piping to have dislodged joints with gaps that are letting tree roots infest the storm water piping.

We used pipe location equipment to locate the dislodged section of common storm water piping within the garden bed.

Used the high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera simultaneously to clear out all the tree roots from the common earthenware pipework causing the blockage.

Flow tested the common storm water - All clear and in good working order.

Once clear, we installed new section of PVC downpipe and inspection opening for future clear out purposes, sealed the base of the downpipe where it connects to the in ground earthenware drain and reconnected the common downpipe.  

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify further storm water blockages, we advise the common storm water piping is excavated within the garden bed and replaced with new PVC piping and fittings. We will submit a quotation shortly for the storm water upgrade works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

We removed the tile grated lid from the floor drain and found sediment debris and sand partially built up at the base of the the drainage in the concrete slab.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked drains at the rear of the property.

Attended the property, found the common storm water pit and strip drain at the rear of the property to be blocked.

Removed grate lids and found the common storm water pit and strip drain to be completely blocked with dirt and debris.

Excavated and removed all dirt and debris from the common storm water pit and strip drain.

Used CCTV drain camera downstream from the outlet of the pit and strip drain and found the common storm water line to be blocked with dirt and debris.

Set up high pressure water jet blaster truck and equipment within the car park area.

Used high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear the outlet of the pit and strip drain downstream to the kerb and gutter in the street.

Flow tested the common storm water line which is currently clear and flowing to the street.

Please note - Following our investigation and CCTV camera survey we found that the inlet to the pit is picking up all downpipes at the property and is lower then the outlet of pit which is causing the inlet to hold water.

Re-installed pit lids, cleaned all areas where work had taken place using high pressure hose and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further storm water blockages, we advise to clear out all storm water pits and strip drains within the car park area, use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the common storm water lines to the street. We advise these works are undertaken on a preventative maintenance program every 6 months. As we have just completed these works, we advise the preventative clear out works are next undertaken in August 2023. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2 and found water leaking from the bathroom ceiling above the vanity basin causing water damage to the entire bathroom ceiling. 

Removed man hole cover and inspected the bathroom ceiling cavity and common waste drain pipes. We located water leaking around the bath and basin waste penetration from unit 5 above.

Gained access into unit 5 and flow tested all bathroom fixtures. Dye Tested the bath waste with red dye and the shower waste with green dye. Flood tested the original bathroom floor tiles around the basin waste penetration.

Carried out pressure testing on the hot and cold water supply, but was unable to get an accurate test on the cold water supply due to a faulty common cold water valve in unit 5.

Advised residents of a building cold water disruption, returned to the property, shut down the buildings water supply, gained access into unit 5 and replaced the common cold water isolation valve and turned on the water supply.

Carried out extensive pressure testing on the hot and cold water pipework within unit 5 and no pressure drop was found.

Laid drop sheets in the bedroom of unit 5 and excavated the internal wall to gain access under the bath to inspect the bath waste and hot and cold water pipes for the bath taps.

We located dye underneath the bath and wet concrete around the bath waste pipework. Tested the bath waste and found a leak on the original bath waste pipework where it passes through the concrete slab into unit 2 below.

Further urgent work required to be undertaken in units 5 & 2 - We advise to make a larger hole in the bedroom wall of unit 5, cut out affected area of bathroom ceiling in unit 2 to access the leaking pipework, excavate concrete slab from unit 2 exposing bath waste pipework, cut out the leaking bath waste pipework, install new bath waste, PVC pipework & fittings through the concrete slab connecting onto existing common waste pipework within unit 2's bathroom ceiling cavity. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further urgent works required to be undertaken.

This quotation is to carry out preventive maintenance clear out works on the common sewer pipework using high pressure water jet blasting with large tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera clearing out all tree root infestations from the common sewer lines.

Please note, we last undertook these clear out works in July 2022 and we advise the preventative maintenance clear out works are undertaken every 6 months to prevent common sewer blockages.

The following works will be undertaken:

  1. Remove all inspection opening lids on common sewer piping.
  2. Use a high pressure water jet blaster to clear out the common sewer piping.
  3. Use a high pressure water jet blaster with tree root cutting heads and CCTV drain camera to cut out all tree root infestation from the common sewer piping to the main boundary trap. 
  4. Flush out overflow relief sewer gullies using high pressure water jet blaster.
  5. CCTV camera survey sewer piping and ensure all tree roots have been removed and the piping is clear. Following our CCTV camera survey If any broken or collapsed pipes are found we will report back.
  6. Flow test common sewer piping to the main boundary trap. 
  7. Reinstall inspection opening lids clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose and disinfectant
  8. Removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Investigate blocked drains in unit 9.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 9 and found the shower waste to be partially blocked.

Removed grate lids in the bathroom and used electric eel to clear out the common waste pipework downstream from the shower and floor waste. 

Flow tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom - All clear and in good working order.

After flow testing the shower recess, we found the shower floor tiles to have insufficient fall to the waste drain. Water pooling on the shower floor is causing mould/moisture build up in the bathroom floor tiles. We also found the shower screen leaks rapidly onto the bathroom floor tiles from the door angles when the shower is in use. As the bathroom is renovated, we advise the owner of unit 9 engages their own contractor to replace the shower floor tiles, installing new tiles with correct fall to the drain and repair or replace the leaking shower screen.

Reinstalled floor waste grate lids and cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

PLEASE NOTE - We Inspected the kitchen waste pipework and found the pipework has backfall from the kitchen sink to the common branch line and waste stack. To rectify the backfall in the kitchen waste pipework, we advise the common branch line and waste stack junction is cut out and replaced to a height lower than the original branch line. As the original kitchen waste pipework has been modified, we advise the lot owner in unit 9 engages their own plumbing contractor to undertake the works.

investigate the mould in Unit 43
Please attend to to investigate the mould in Unit 43 as per the attached photos.

 

W.O. Issued by : Lisa Lin
Email : elizabeth.higgins@bcssm.com.au
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leak in unit 43.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 43 and found water damage in 3 x separate locations. Unit 43 is located below the floor level and is dug out of the subsoil. 

Following extensive investigation works and testing we found the below:

Leak 1 - In unit 43, we found water damage to the internal living room wall behind the entrance door adjacent to the bathroom. Water damage appears low down along the wall below the step up to the shower recess in the bathroom. Used moisture meter and thermal image camera to identify high readings of moisture. Inspected the original bathroom floor tiles and shower recess within unit 43, pressure tested the hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found. Flood tested the original floor tiles within the shower recess and found water to leak into the substrate and tile bed.

We found the original waterproof membrane within the shower recess to have failed causing water to leak below the floor tiles into the substrate and cause water damage to the internal wall. 

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 43 - To rectify the water leak, we advise to remove the floor tiles within the shower recess, first course of wall tiles, install new waterproof membrane, re-tile shower recess and first course of wall tiles using comparable tiles. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken in unit 43.

Leak 2 - In unit 43, we found water damage to the bedroom ceiling, used moisture meter and thermal image camera to identify high readings of moisture. Stepped out the location of the leak and found units 5 and 6 above.

Inspected unit 5 and found water damage to the corner of 2 x common walls in the living room, adjacent to the water damage is unit 6’s bathroom.

Gained access into unit 6, inspected the bathroom and found the shower/ bath to be above the water leak.

Undertook testing on the fixtures and hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found.

Flood tested the common shower wall tiles grouting and bath seals to find water leak under the bath from faulty sealant and grout.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken to the common shower / bath walls in unit 6 - We advise the shower / bath area is resealed and re-grouted, sealant is installed along the common bath edge and behind the tap spindles. We will submit a quotation shortly for the sealing and re-grouting works required to be undertaken.

Leak 3 - In unit 43, we found water damage to the common wall and wardrobe timber in the bedroom, water damage appears low down along the base of the common wall causing rising dampness in the bedroom.

Used moisture meter and thermal image camera to identify high readings of moisture.

Walked around the property and located a common storage room which is adjacent to unit 43 and below units 5, 6 and the courtyard. Gained access to the storage room from the builder renovating unit 2, and inspected the common brick wall adjoining unit 43. We found rising damp mould, wet subsoil and wet rock.

The water that is leaking into the storage room subsoil is coming from the retaining wall below the open courtyard outside units 1-6.

Flood tested the common stormwater drains in the courtyard outside units 1-6 and found them to be running clear. We found no water to be leaking into the storage room from the flow testing of the common courtyard stormwater drainage.

Further works required to be undertaken - We advise a building contractor is engaged to inspect the driveway storage room adjacent to unit 43 below unit 6. Clear the storage room of rotten timber and unused storage items, repairs are to be carried out to the external courtyard outside units 1 and 6 to prevent the subsoil ground water leaking into the storage room.

As the existing common stormwater drainage within the courtyard is original earthenware drainage, we advise the stormwater drainage in the courtyard is replaced if any large scale remedial works are carried out in the courtyard outside 1 and 6. 

Cleaned all areas where works has taken place and remove associated rubbish from the property.

After the 3 x separate leaks have been repaired, we advise resultant damaged walls and ceilings are repaired and painted.

  11. Clean all areas where work has taken place.

Description:
Water leak Flaot Centre
Good Morning,
can you please attend to the leak into the float centre.
It appears to be leaking from the light well above the float centre or the awning. The lot owner has advised that "Someone, assuming the builder has placed a catcher tray to collect the water in the ceiling . The tray is now full and we believe the water outlet is blocked at the front building awning due to leaves in the gutters, not allowing water to escape."
Invoice Description:
Investigate water leaking in the Float Centre and blocked roof awning.

Attended the property, gained access to the float Centre and found water damage to the ceiling tiles in the hallway passage and the gyprock ceiling in one of the Float rooms.

Lifted the ceiling tiles in the hallway to inspect inside the ceiling cavity and found water leaking from cracks in the concrete slab, outside the drip trays previously installed within the ceiling cavity to catch water leaking.

Disconnected the outlet drain connected to one of the drip trays and flow tested the PVC waste pipework and found it to be clear and in good working order. Inspected the common drip tray and found the spigot drain to be rusted and leaking, we installed high grade sealant around the spigot waste pipe to try slow the leak. Stepped out the location of the 2 x drip trays within the float center hallway ceiling and gained access to the residential building units on level 1. Found the external courtyard on level 1 to be located above and the floor drains for the courtyard to be blocked. Used drain clean equipment to clear the blockage in the courtyard floor drain and flow tested the common stormwater drain to ensure it was clear and in good working order.

Within the courtyard on level 1, we found the floor drains to blocked causing the courtyard to flood and faulty waterproof membrane around the blocked floor drain and common air-conditioning duct causing water to leak through the concrete slab into the Float Centre ceiling below.

Further works required to be undertaken - As the water proof membrane within the courtyard on level 1 has failed, We advise strata engages a building contractor to inspect the courtyard and undertake repairs to rectify the water leak.

Where the existing drip trays have been installed in the float center ceiling, are too small and no longer catch the water leaking into the hallway area. We advise to remove the existing drip trays and install 2 x larger custom made drip trays fixed to the ceiling below the water leaks. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

Used large extension ladder to access the front awning above the shop and found the awning gutter and downpipe to be blocked with leaves and debris.

Removed the leaves and debris from the gutter and cleared the roof awning. Set up the high pressure water jet blaster and ran equipment onto the awning roof. Used the high pressure water jet blaster to clear the blockage in the common storm water downpipe removing all debris and leaves. Flow tested the common storm water downpipe - All clear and in good working order.

Further preventative maintenance works required to be carried out every 6 months to prevent stormwater blockages and floods at the property from the front shop awning. We advise the common shop awning box gutter and downpipe drainage is cleaned on a preventative maintenance program. We will submit a quotation shortly for the preventative maintenance works to be carried out, as we have just completed these works the next stormwater clear outs are due in July 2023.

Following the awning blockage there is resultant damage painting repairs to the underside of the awning ceiling outside the Float Centre. Once all works have been completed, we will submit a quotation for all resultant water damage repairs and painting within the float center and also the front awning.

Cleaned all areas where work had take place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Invoice Description:
Attended the property, inspected the entrance downpipe at the rear and found it to be corroded where it passes through the awning. Measured the downpipe and went to the supplier to pickup materials.

Returned to the property the following day, cut out corroded downpipe where it passes through the awning and supplied and installed new a metal colorbond downpipe and PVC drainage inspection opening at the base.

Backfill trench and re-instated existing plants next to the entrance. 

Further works required to be undertaken - To rectify further storm water blockages we advise the common storm water piping connected to the front entrance downpipe is rerun approximately 12 x meters in length with new PVC piping and fittings surface mounting the pipework on the external wall to the rear downpipe outside Garage 9.  Also to use high pressure water jet blaster and CCTV drain camera to clear out the common storm water line downstream. We will submit an urgent quotation shortly for the storm water upgrade works required to be undertaken.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.

Invoice Description:
Investigate leaking sewer pipe above the storage area of lots 9 and 18.

Gained access into the carpark, inspected lot 9 and 18's storage cage and found water leaks dripping through the concrete slab penetration and then running off the 40mm bath waste piping. 

We located units 16 and 17 to be above the affected leak.

Gained access to unit 16, above and inspected the original bathroom. Isolated the water supply, carried out pressure test on the hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found within unit 16. Dye tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

Flood tested where the bath meets the common wall tiles and found water leaking into the storage room below.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 16 - We advise to cut out the faulty sealant where the bath meets the tiles and re-seal using high grade flexible sealant. We will submit a quotation shortly for the further works required to be undertaken.

We were unable to gain access into unit 17 on our inspection and left a note on their door.

Returned to the property, gained access into unit 17 and found water damage to the internal study wall adjacent to the bath.

Inspected the original bathroom, isolated the water supply, carried out pressure test on the hot and cold water supply and no burst pipes were found within unit 17. Dye tested all waste fixtures within the bathroom and no leaks were found.

We found a large amount of movement within the bath which is causing the seals to crack where the bath meets the common wall tiles. Flood tested where the bath meets the wall tiles and instantly found water leaking into the storage room below.

Further works required to be undertaken in unit 17 - To rectify the leak, we advise to remove the bath and replace with new bath chased into the wall as per AS-3500 plumbing codes. We will submit a separate quotation shortly for the bath replacement in unit 17. 

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

Attended the property to investigate water leaks units 2,5 and 9 following the engineers report.

WATER LEAKS FROM UNIT 3 INTO UNIT 2

Investigated water leaks from unit 3 into unit 2 from unit 3’s rear and front balconies.

Attended the property, gained access into unit 2, found water damage to the rear left bedroom ceiling and water damage to the front left balcony ceiling.

Removed light fitting in the bedroom ceiling of unit 2 and found water leaking through the concrete slab penetrating from the waste pipe of unit 3’s rear balcony.

Gained access into unit 3, inspected the balcony and found a planter box which has a metal flashing over it.  We found as follows:

1.         The occupant has put pot plants onto the metal flashing which is causing water to pool, leak down into the planter box and leak through the failed waterproof membrane within the planter box.

2.         The weight of the pot plants is causing bowing of the metal flashing and is pulling the flashing away from the wall resulting in a gap between the planter box and the wall from which water is penetrating into unit 2.

3.         We also found water leaking around the balcony drain, through the concrete slab into unit 2 below and consider the water proof membrane within unit 3’s rear balcony to have failed.

We cut out a section of water damaged villa board ceiling in the front balcony of unit 2 and found water leaking through the concrete slab around the floor waste drain from unit 3’s balcony above.

Gained access into unit 3’s front balcony and found as follows:

1.         Found an air conditioning condensation drain goes to the side of the surface drain which is causing water to pool on the balcony floor tiles when the air conditioning unit is in use.  Water is leaking through the concrete slab into unit 2 below.

2.         We consider the water proof membrane on the front balcony to have failed.

We advise as follows:

1.         The owner’s corporation engages a remedial building contractor to urgently provide a quotation to rectify the leaking front balcony, rear balcony and planter box.

2.         We strongly advise the pot plants are removed from the flashing on the rear balcony to prevent water leaking into the planter box and causing further water penetration into unit 2’s bedroom below.

3.         After works have been completed in unit 3, we advise the resultant water damaged bedroom ceiling and front balcony ceiling is repaired and painted in unit 2.  (These remedial works are in addition to the ceiling damage caused by the burst flexi hose a few weeks ago which is a separate issue).

Investigate water leak in unit 406.

Please Note - We inspected the hot and cold water isolation valves for unit 506 and found the butterfly valves to be faulty and are required to be replaced with new hot and cold water valves.  

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place.

To replace the metal floor drain the balcony floor tiles will have to be removed, a new custom floor drain installed and the balcony floor will need to be re waterproofed and tiled.

Once all works have been completed in unit 5,  we advise the water damaged balcony ceiling in unit 2 is repaired and painted.

Description: Urgent water leak unit 12
Invoice Description:
Emergency after hours call out - Urgent water leak in unit 12

Urgently attended the property after hours, gained access to unit 12 and found leaking water under the kitchen floors causing them to buckle.

Gained access into unit 8 below and found water leaking down the bedroom walls and water stains on the ceiling.

Isolated the hot and cold water supply, carried out nitrogen pressure test and got a large drop in pressure on the hot water supply indicating a burst pipe within unit 12. 

Returned to the property, engaged pipe location leak detection, used pipe locating equipment to trace out the hot water supply pipes and leak detector to locate the burst hot water pipe within the common kitchen wall.

Pipe location, leak detection advised to cut out the kitchen cabinetry and expose the hot water pipes within the kitchen wall behind the hot water heater. Found a small noise behind hot water outlet where it goes through the backboard in cupboard.

Returned to the property, gained access to unit 12 and laid drop sheets in the kitchen. Cut out kitchen cabinetry and excavated the wall chase to expose the hot water pipes within the wall. We did not find the burst pipe to be located within this part of the kitchen wall.

Further urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 12 - To rectify the water leak, we advise to delete the burst pressurized hot water pipe within the common kitchen wall of unit 12 and partially re-run a new hot water service from the kitchen sink to the bathroom wall. We will submit an urgent quotation to follow this tax invoice for the urgent works required to be undertaken in unit 12.

Once the urgent partial re re run is complete in unit 12, we advise the resultant water damaged bedroom ceiling and walls in unit 8 are repaired and painted. Once we know the full extent of the damage, we will submit a quotation for the resultant water damage and painting repairs in unit 8.

We advise the water damaged flooring in unit 12 is replaced by a flooring contractor. 

Clean all areas where work had taken place.
